We tend to use the M5 and/or the M15 timeframe, however the system works on all TF's 2. Which currency pairs does it suit? Any currency pair is fine. As with any system, it works best in a trend rather than a ranging market, but any pair will work. Gold and Oil work as well also. 3. So if you want to use Japanese Candles at home....fine.....just make sure that any charts you post to the thread abides by the rules. 4. Do these indicators repaint? No, none of the Genesis indicators repaint. It may seem that way if you have (say) an M15 indicator on your M5 chart, but once the period candle has closed, in this case, the M15, then the indicator paints to the chart permanently. Of course while the M15 candle is still in progress, the indicator may *seem* to repaint because the candle is not yet closed. This question has been addressed many times so you can search for more in depth explanation. 5. On the recent charts posted, I see no Arrows, but I see an extra Matrix. Why do some charts have no Arrows and why do some charts have this extra Matrix? Ok ,the 'extra Matrix' that you see on some peoples charts is actually the Arrow(s) represented in a Matrix, rather than an actual Arrow painted on the chart. If you put the Arrows AND the 'extra Matrix' on the chart, you will see that they match....perfectly. This 'extra Matrix' is named the ASCTrend and it can be found on the thread of Xaphod here. This very cool addition makes the charts cleaner and easier to read, and the code behind ASCTrend is much more efficient than the Arrow code is, so your computer will have less work to do. The Arrows still work just great, and ASCTrend works great too....you can choose which you prefer. 6. I have downloaded the zip file and installed everything, but one line (or more) of the Genesis Matrix is one solid colour, it never changes. What's going on? The most common reason for this is that you do not have all the indicators properly installed. The Genesis Matrix draws it's data from the indicators in the zip file, and it looks to the 'experts/indicators' folder to find the indicators it needs. If the indicators are not in the 'experts/indicators' folder, then the Genesis Matrix cannot display the data! The only other is a Microsoft permission problem that exists on Window Vista and Windows 7, I don't know about Windows 8. It's a common problem that Microsoft has inflicted upon us, and more information can be found here , which will help you out. The screenshot below shows the basic way I trade. Other people have other variations of trading the Matrix, but for those of you who don’t know me, this is a quick guide for what I look out for. Firstly, I trade only from The Frankfurt market open, which is 1 hour before London open…….until approximately 2 or 3 hours after New York open. I don’t trade the Asian markets as a habit, because they are too slow and prone to small movements, but if I see something juicy I might enter a trade. There are more pips available after I finish trading sometimes, but that is usually past 2am for me, so I am asleep!!! So….here we go….I will enter a Sell trade if all the following conditions have been met: The Matrix is all the same colour after the current candle is closed, ie, Matrix cannot repaint Stochastic if falling from a recent overbought state A Bear candle has opened under the Yellow 5 EMA The Arrow…..now I don’t always wait for the arrow because in a sudden PA reversal it may be late…but….if an arrow doesn’t arrive within the next couple of candles, I become concerned!! The trade exit. The exit is always harder than the entry because we want to stay in the trade for as long as it runs…..but we don’t know where the run will end!! So generally speaking, I will exit at a support/resistance line. This could be a pivot line, a previous high/low area, a round number etc etc. In this case, the exit was none of the above!! However, the PA began to stall and could make no further progress….and….a big doji candle appeared…..and….tha candles began to move above the Yellow 5 EMA…..and…..the Stochastic began to climb. That’s enough reason for me to exit the trade….or…..al least bring your Stop Loss down into a decent profit area so that some of your profit is protected. That way you will definitely make a profit, plus you will be in a good position if the bear run resumes. Edit: Stop Loss for shorts goes above the previous swing high, and for longs, below the previous swing low. Having said that, the Stop Loss is not there for you to sit and watch get hit if the PA turns around. It's there as emergency protection. The idea is that you recognise that the PA has turned and you need to manually exit the trade and consider entering the opposite way RJ

--- 帖子 #16 ---
Ahhhh....the SL placement.....lol....good point, I forgot to mention that in post #1. I'll edit that in a sec. SL for shorts goes above the previous swing high, and for longs, below the previous swing low. I don't use a set TP, although I have an idea in my head. For instance, if I enter a short just under the daily pivot, my initial target will be S1.....unless there is any other support line that comes along first. When (and if) S1 is reached, I will target S2, or some other support line that may come first.....like a round number or previous support area etc. % risk per trade is very much up to the individual. I like use 2% but others I know use 5%....others use 1%.....still others vary the %age depending on the PA. I don't there is a 'right or wrong' way to do it.....it's what you are comfortable with.

--- 帖子 #18 ---
Well, if it is a proper "signal", ie Matrix is complete the other colour, oh yeah....I will exit for sure.....in fact I probably already did! If the reversal is a strong one, I will look for the same conditions as in post 2 and enter. If the reversal is against the trend, I will probably wait and see if the trend resumes, and look to re-enter. Generally speaking, I start manually trailing my trades from about +20 onwards. So when a trade is in profit by at least 20 pips, I will move my SL to break even and eliminate the risk. As we get further on in the thread you will see this in action. Depends. If the counter move is just the market 'breathing', then I will let it go. If it seems like a full blooded reversal, then I will exit. It's a tough call and one that only comes with experience. It's combination of some Matrix signals, but mostly it depends on the Stochastic and what caused the reversal. Was it just a bounce of the Pivot like we have just seen? Was it because Bernanke was running his mouth? The reason for the reversal, if indeed it is a reversal, should let us know what to do. Sometimes, there are counter trend trades that I will will take. If we get a full opposite signal....ie Matrix + Stochastic + Yellow 5EMS + Candle opening clear under/over the Yellow 5 MA and there is no reason NOT to enter.....like a pivot/round number etc.....then I will enter the counter trend trade...BUT.....I will move my SL to break even pretty smartly to protect myself.

--- 帖子 #36 ---
A little bit more for the newer members about the current trade that Olivia is going to buy beers for!! Red line is entry as mentioned before. 1. PA hit the Daily Pivot and bounced off, as it often does 2. PA retested Daily Pivot and then broke through 3. PA went on down and Hit S1 (where it currently is. When PA broke through the DP.....it's time to bring the SL down into profit (just above the DP, which is now resistance) to eliminate risk from the trade. Now it's a free trade....yippee!! Now that PA is thinking about breaking thought S1, we need to be aware that it might bounce a little here, so we bring our SL down into more profit to about +30....which is mid way between S1 and the DP. So....worst case scenario is that we get stopped out for +30. Nothing wrong with +30 is there?

--- 帖子 #40 ---
One of my pet hates is a messy chart....it's just me....others can happily trade with many indicators on their chart. There is a very important indicator that I use, and it is the ATR indicator. The Average True Range. I have this on an M15 chart because I want to see more of the trend, and I can have the indi here without cluttering up my M5 chart. ATR indi's purpose it to show us how far the PA has come today, and how much more the PA is likely to move. For instance, if the Average True Range of the EU pair for today is 150 pips, and the movement today is already 145 pips (which the indi will show), then it might not be too smart to enter another trade on that pair today.....unless.....there is a very good signal to do so. And if there is, keep the SL tight...just in case. Below is a screenshot of what it looks like, but I'll let Olivia explain it because she is good with it, and I will get some more pips while she's yappin!

--- 帖子 #42 ---
Don't worry, mine are still moving nicely. This is the ATR indie I prefer, you can't change any of the inputs except the colour (which you'll need to do if you have a black chart) If you hover over the lines, you will see when the day starts that above the price is high 2 then above that high1 then below price you have low 2 and low 1 in that order. When price reaches one of the lines for instance, on EJ now, price has reached and gone through Low 2 and Low 1, it then brings the High lines down to show where (if it now turns around) price is likely to reach the other way. I find it very useful, the lines very often act in the same was as S/R do and of course can break through on a good day just as price breaks through s/r.

Hi Realjumper! Congratulations with the new thread! I think risk (or money management) is some of the most important elements of trading. Good money management and trade management can make something useful out of a poor system in the hands of a good trader, as long as the system is not a looser. But a good system can not make something useful out of poor money management. At least not if it is in the hands of a new inexperienced or "bad" trader. Because of that i would say that for new traders money management is just as important as the system itself. The reason i say "for new traders" is because experienced traders already know this. They would never become experienced if they use bad MM. Then they are out of the game already. Like the system itself, the MM do not at all have to be complicated and/or advanced. Both the trading system and the MM can be VERY simple and easy to follow and still be excellent. In fact when it comes to trading the simplest is often the best. The reason i am posting this is that i have seen a trend lately both here on FF and on other forums and websites that they post a system and the only MM they post is "use 5% risk pr trade", (or even more) and that is dangerous. I can say without a doubt that it does not matter how good the system or the MM is if a new inexperienced trader goes live with a new system he/she is still learning, and using 5% risk pr trade it is doomed to fail. A experienced trader can maybe do it and there may be some exceptions among new traders. I see Yelena claims to be a new trader and she is doing good using "high" risk, but as a general rule the combination of high risk, new trader, learning new system and poor MM will not end well. Again for experienced trades it is all very different. They know what to do when they run in to trouble. That is all i wanted to say about it. This is not a thread about money management but i advice new traders to learn as much as they can about it. Here is a short video that may help some people as a starting point. It is not a MM system but some info on how important good MM can be: Inserted Video

That's not repainting......that's the limit of bars back it counts. This can be changed, but the more bars back it counts, the more work for the CPU. Back testing should be done on a trading simulator, then you can go back a considerable time and trade as you normally do, but you can vary the speed.

Here is the EJ M5 chart. The green vertical line is Frankfurt open and there was a long trade opportunity just about straight after. You could argue that the stoch is very high and you would not take the trade....and that is a fair enough response. Lets come back to the stoch in a minute. We have a clear signal from Genesis we have a bull candle opening clear of the Yellow 5EMA.....we even have the arrow. All that might be a problem is the stoch. Now, regarding the stoch.....yes, it is quite high, but, it was way low just a few candles before. So the PA isn't overbought. It isn't perfect, but it's not bad. The clincher is the swing low, where our SL will be placed is just 10 pips. So, we would have to consider, is it worth the risk?......a 10 pip risk, when almost everything else lines up to tell us to take a long. Would you take it? It's up to you.....I would certainly take the trade because a 10 pip risk is worth it to me. If you would rather sit it out and wait....that's fine too

--- 帖子 #274 ---
The Genesis Matrix will give alerts when all 4 are the same colour and the current candle has closed. You just need to turn it on in the settings. Right click on your chart and go to 'Indicator List'.....select the Genesis Matrix from the list and click 'Edit'. Scroll down to the bottom of the sub window that appears (see the screenshot) and you will see the Alert Settings menu. If your settings match the screenshot, you will get an audible alert and a pop up window when the current candle closes and the Matrix is all the same colour.

--- 帖子 #348 ---

--- 帖子 #349 ---
Drag your mt4 platform over 2 screens....should have one screen filled with grey and the other with stuff on it...now move the windows you want to the grey area

--- 帖子 #350 ---
There are 2 steps to let you do that. The first is at the OS level. In Win 7, on the Display/Screen Resolution tab, select "Extend these displays" from the Multiple Displays drop down. In WinXP, I think a similar option is on the Display Properties/Settings tab. Once that's done, in MT4, drag the right border of MT4 onto the second display. You should end up with a lot of blank space in the main window. Then just position your charts as you wish.

Some traders may look at the angle of the stoch (i do some times) but it is not possible to say 45° (or 30 or 60 or some other) angle is good or bad because it depends on the setting of the stoch and even more how you are zooming/stretching the charts in/out and how big part of the chart your indicator window is and so on. So the angle have more to do with experience and comparing with earlier moves, how the stoch moves compared with the price of course and things like that. Arctic4x

--- 帖子 #414 ---
Something interesting here.... This first long trade just after Frankfurt open is almost a carbon copy of the trade I spoke of yesterday on EJ 1. Just as with EJ yesterday, the stoch is quite high, but everything else looks good. We have the Matrix, The Yellow EMA, the candle above the EMA and even the arrow.....the only possible issue could be the rather high-ish stoch. But......once again, the SL under the previous swing low was only 10 pips away. To me, again, a 10 pips risk is worth the risk. 2. PA got to R1, which is the first target, but couldn't progress from there, so exiting the trade for a nice little profit is in order. We can see that there was a complete rejection and consequent reversal from R1. 3. Because the reversal was so violent, the short signal is late. That's just too bad for us......using lagging indicators, we can't expect much better. Because the signal is going to be late, the SL placement is going to be a bit expensive.....in fact it is 25 pips away from the signal when it eventually turns up. So.....should we take the trade or let it pass because the SL is expensive. For me, I look at it like this: The previous long trade gave me +26 pip profit. The SL on this short is going to be a relatively expensive -25 if it gets hit. So, big deal.......I will take the risk, because if it gets hit, it will wipe out 25 pips of todays 26 pip profit........so if that happened, I would end up with +1 pip profit!! So......I am still in profit for the day.....so I enter the trade. 4. The trade goes well and hits the daily pivot and gives me +23 pips So, in all, I get a profit of +49 pips, and all I risked of my capital was 10 pips. Risk/reward of almost 5:1

Dakuki PM'd me in regards to the higher time frames trading. I cannot post a screenshot in a PM so I will post here. Maybe someone else can also benefit from this or maybe get a idea for their own trading. Here is my thought process: 1. Weekly chart: - I have a 5 and 8 EMA (no shift and typical) plotted that I can quickly gauge the trend. (The white arrows in my chart is where the 5 and 8 EMA cross) Remember the weekly trend is not going to change anytime soon as it is very very strong. This trend change was from late April. - You can also see Genesis is showing down. 2. Daily Chart: (This is my main trading time frame) - Then I go to Daily and look for a short entry. - As you can see we also had the EMA 5&amp;8 cross again to down side (positive sign) - Genesis also crossed down (This would signal a entry for me) (One note: I live in South Africa (GMT+2) and my broker is in Australia so the daily candle changes for me at 2am local time. Due to me also still having a 9-5 job I am not eager to stand up at that time) So the question comes in what do I do....... well that is easy. When I wake up in the morning I quickly look at the 4H and lower charts to get a entry with lower SL. 3. 4H Charts - As you can see we already had a signal on the 4H charts so you either wait for another signal on the 4 hour or you go to a lower chart for another signal. 4. 1H Charts - Now we are in business. - Stoch coming from high (positive) - Price moving below 5EMA (positive) - Genesis lining up (PULL the trigger) or let us take it one step further 5. 15 Min chart - Stoch already a bit low (negative but the higher time frames is backing me up) - Genesis lining up (WHY WOULD YOU NOT TO PULL THE TRIGGER HERE) So for +- 25 pips SL from the last Swing high, I got 242 pips profit. That is almost 1:10 risk to reward. Plan your trade....... and then trade the hell out of that plan.

--- 帖子 #457 ---
Attach multiple instances of GenesisMatrix to the chart. When you attach the matrix to the chart, click on the Inputs tab and change the TimeFrame.Period property to the higher time frame you want. You should only type in higher time frames relative to the chart you are attaching it to. A TimeFrame.Period of 0 means the current chart's Period().

--- 帖子 #515 ---
I see some confusion here regarding the stochastic. As I said earlier, it was first invented in 1950 and it still widely used in trading....not only FX trading, but any kind of trading and it a very useful indicator. At first, many people think that it is simply an 'Overbought/Oversold' indicator, and they get frustrated when they discover that it can stay 'Oversold/Overbought' for a long time and spoil their trades. That is not the fault of the stochastic, it is the fault f the trader who has not understood the stochastic. If it was nothing more than an 'Overbought/Oversold' indicator, we could just have a red/white colour, and that's it. But if you take the time to understand the indicator, rather than dismissing it because it doesn't do what you erroneously thought it was going to do, you'll discover that it is indeed a very useful tool. Best you research something and actually understand it, before dismissing it!! Take a look at the EU chart below from several days ago, it is a good example. I won't go into the trade entry because we know about that already. 1. So up to this point, the trade has been a success.....but, someone who doesn't understand stochastic will be saying "time to exit because the stoch says the pa is oversold." So what does that erroneous statement mean? It means that the trader thinks that the stochastic is nothing more than a 'Overbought/Oversold' indicator, and if they exit the trade based on that, they will miss out on many pips, as you can see. What I would do at that point, and I have mentioned this before, is to bring my SL down into a profit area *in case* the PA reverses. As we can see, the PA drops further. 2. We see here that the PA has dropped further, but the stoch is still saying 'Oversold'. So what? So, the fact that the stoch is staying well down is showing the strength of the bears.....it's showing that the PA intends to stay down here for the time being, it's showing that the bears are strong. Would I enter a trade with the stoch in that state? No, because it *could* reverse at any time. I will now bring my SL down some more. 3. You can see that just after #2, the stoch moved up out of the 'Oversold' area. Is that a reason to exit the trade? No, it's not, because the PA didn't indicate any reason to exit. Candles stayed under the Yellow 5EMA, trend hasn't shown any sign of reversal at all. So we can see that the PA continued down, while all the time the stoch stayed either 'oversold' or very close to it. The exit came after #3 when we can see the stoch suddenly climb *AND* the candles change and cross the Yellow EMA, which itself is now pointing up. What happened here is that the stoch help keep us in the trade, where many would exited and then got all upset because they exited too early. This is one of the strengths of the stochastic indicator. We have yet to touch on stochastic divergence and the way that stoch can keep you from entering a trade that looks good but stoch doesn't agree. You enter and you get burnt! Yes, you can see trades that sometimes turn out well despite the stoch not agreeing, but, they are not high probability trades. I am only interested in high probability trades. I'm not here to guess and gamble. If you wish to use RSI instead, that's all good, but please don't delete something when you don't understand it. Take the time, do the research and learn about the tool before you dismiss it out of lack of understanding. As I said, it has been around since 1950 and still widely used by all the big players

The Stochastic oscillator is a great tool for all markets in my view, as is RSI. For trending markets, my stochastic signal to exit the trade or set a tight stop loss is upon cross of zero line. For shorts, for example, the Stochastic will remain oversold or under zero for most of the move. When it finally crosses above the zero (center) line, it usually indicates the end of the move. The opposite is true for longs.

--- 帖子 #582 ---
Hey Gt, Within a chosen timeframe (say M5) every indicators 'repaint' although 'repaint' is not the right word in this case..... Most indicators (macd rsi stox ma.....) will be set to 'Close' in their respective 'Input' tabs and that means 2 things: 1) they will finally draw themselves on the chart by taking the last value reached at the end of the M5 period; once this value is known, the indicator value is calculated and drawn accordingly and this will not and cannot change (in the same way that once your M5 candle has finished, it is set in stone). 2) but ... during the 5 minutes of your M5 period, the indicator will constantly change up and down, reacting live to the PA (stick a 1-period MA on a M1 chart and you will see that happen with every tick); this is not 'repainting', this is normal behaviour for a graphical interface relying on constantly updating data. In the case of Genesis' Matrix, point 2) happens even more often because the matrix is made of 4 different indicators: during any M5 period, PA might move in a way that gets T3 to turn blue, then TVI might turn blue too while GHL stays red and when PA moves in the other direction the red/blue can/will change and this is normal behaviour as explained above. But, once that M5 candle has closed, the 4 different red/blue squares that make the new Genesis matrix will be set in stone and their respective colours will always stay as they are. The repainting problem was present in previous versions of the Symphonie matrixes (where an indicator would look back at previous candles and then repaint itself to kinda make itself look better by showing a good buy/sell signal early (sometimes way too early, and something that gets picked up quite early by trained/experienced eyes)). Xaphod (thanks again) then released an updated version of the Symphonie matrix where the last repainting indicator was replaced by a non-repainting one and I believe that this is what Genesis is now based on. So, unless you can post a picture showing that any dot on the matrix has changed colour after the close of its respective candle/timeframe (and proving me wrong and making me eat humble pie), please let's have no more of this repainting lark and let's concentrate on trading. Oli PS: good to see you all in this new thread: I had wondered where you'd all gone!

--- 帖子 #691 ---
Hi &amp; welcome Slim as it was your first post, I'll try to answer your points in as much details as I can... The difference between your 2 posted charts is that the top one shows the basic MT4 candlesticks/candles and the bottom one shows Heiken Ashi (HA) candles, favoured by RJ and others (a part of RJ's setup is that the HA candle following a Matrix signal must open clear of the yellow MA) . Below I've reposted an old Pdf of his (the Genesis matrix is now different but the trading principles are still the same: worth a good read and another read and...). Regarding your 10 pips profit/30 pips loss..... bear in mind that in here a lot of people will quote TP (Target Points) &amp; SL (Stop Loss) based on the M5 timeframe (TF): I don't trade the M15 TF but it makes sense that for a higher TF, the SL and the TP will have to be larger on most occasions. As for your 'failed' trade example here are my thoughts: .RJ and others always make the point of the importance of trading with rather than against pivot/support/resistance points/lines. For example, if the PA (Price Action) goes up towards the R1 resistance level and it fails there once and then twice, then they will more than likely enter a short trade if they get a valid sell signal around the R1 level. .in your case, the price was already nearly 2/3 up between the Daily Pivot (DP) support and R1, in what is known as 'no man's land': 1) there was at best another 15/20 pips to be had between your entry and a safe 'around-R1' exit so the 2310/15 area should have been in your thoughts as a possible exit level, or you should at least be putting your SL at B/E (Break Even) then. 2) using the same setup (Long heading towards R1), the previous entry where the previous yellow arrow was (2275), offered a better Risk/Reward (RR) setup: R1 at 2315 was a good 40 pips away and you could have hidden your SL below the previous low (2250 - 25 pips) or below the DP (2240 -35 pips) still maintaining a R/R above 1 at least. I know that the entry was outside 'recommended' trading hours but it's just to explain my point. 3) a third 'warning' would have been that the price had already been brought down from the R1 area and if it got rejected again, the likely rejection could be swift because of the potential Double Top forming at 2315. I say 'swift' for the following reason.... .at your entry point, nobody knows whether the price will get rejected again at R1 or not .plenty of speculative traders will join the Long bandwagon as we are going up again because they know that if we break R1 decisively then we could have a big move up (because all the people who were short approaching 2315 and hoping that the level will hold again, will have to cover their shorts fueling the move upwards even more). .the flipside of that is that when faced with a double top/R1 rejection again, the Longs will also exit their positions quickly and you get a swift move to the downside as everybody tries to exit at the same time and for those who don't exit quick enough, their SL is likely to get hit pretty quickly. All the best. Oli

--- 帖子 #693 ---
The current matrix limits the number of bars you can backtest to 1500 for the T3 line. The files attached will allow you to backtest the matrix further, up to the number of bars on your chart, if you wish. There is one additional parameter available when you attach the matrix to your chart: T3_8.BarCount with a default value of 1500. Change the 1500 to a higher number to allow the T3 line to display accurately further back in time. http://i50.tinypic.com/iege50.jpg Use the default for live and demo trading to prevent sluggish response. Use a larger value for backtesting only. Place the attached files into your MT4's \experts\indicators folder and restart MT4. Attach the new matrix, change this parameter for backtesting, and you're good to go.

For new(ish) traders.... Simplicity is key ! I've said it before on Symphonie's and I'll say it again here: on page one you have all you need. Download RJ's zip file, install everything on the instruments that you want to trade and don't add anything else. It's not that all the founders of Symphonie/Genesis are hiding anything, I genuinely believe that they trade exactly as described and that the only other indicator that they use is their experience (unfortunately we can't yet code that into an indicator lol). They have given us a whole strategy and I know from experience that it is sooooo tempting to want to add your own personal touch to it but without experience you will more than likely end up with a bastardised system that will cause more hesitations, more missed trades ...than the original. After all, the current version is the culmination of over 1 year of testing, backtesting, forward testing ... by at least a handful (5+) of people: do you really think that you can generate these 5+ years of manpower in a few days/weeks? As mentionned earlier, I think that Pivots are important too: the fact that RJ/Olivia/Yelena.... use them to filter out possible bad trades and to maximise gains on your winning trades should not be lost. Have a look at the current chart: it's an H1 eurusd chart using RJ's basic template from page 1; I use H1 to give you an overall view of the whole week just gone by..... Look at the huge amounts of times (blue rectangles) where the price bounced off either S1 or R1, almost every single day. Keep this picture in mind and now visualise 2 things that will increase your pips: 1) all the great entries (very little drawdown) that you could have had when Genesis gave either a buy/sell signal around those levels 2) if you were already in a trade heading towards either R1 or S1, what great places these 2 support/resistance levels alone would have provided to exit your trades and bank a really high % of the pips on offer. They say that a picture is worth a thousand words, so I'll shut up now. Oli

--- 帖子 #708 ---
Slim, let me add some comments. Matrix is a great combined indi but nothing more. You need to integrate it in a trading system which fits with your personality to have success with it. Matrix Pros : As said it is a combined indi based on 4 different indies. this combination reinforce each single indi and gives you more chance when you enter in the market. In other words higher rate of successful entries. Cons: As many indies it is a little lagging ( http://www.babypips.com/school/leadi...ndicators.html ) and its signal is a little late compared to the pure price action. Therefore if you want to use it an important condition is that price can move enough pips in your direction. How can we get it ??? Below some guidelines Time filter : choose the time during the day where volatility is higher (typically from London open to second half of NY session). Pay attention to FKT open because sometimes the price movement is denied by London open. Trade with the trend : This is obvious and you have heard it thousands times …trend is your better friend until it ends. Well how to understand where we are (trend vs. range : http://www.babypips.com/school/trendspotting.html )? Here some suggestions : Try to use a MA in the higher TF (I like SMA75 with EU) and look at the following conditions to spot a potential lasting trend: Price position (below/above MA) MA direction (raising or dropping) MA slope (Trend momentum) Stochastic oscillator : Once again higher TF give you the direction while the lower TF give you with the matrix the better entry point. RJ explains it very well in the pdf already posted. Let me add an advise. Don’t try to catch the perfect reversal point but wait for a clear trend in the higher TF before choose the direction … in other word wait for the crossover of stoch in higher TF and climbing over 30 level haeding up. This is the reason why some of us like to have a MTF higher TF stoch in the same window with the standard one.... this si their kompass. S/R : This is the basic knowledge you should have before trading. If the price is coming close to a S/R pay attention because all of us are waiting to understand what will happen and as rule of thumb …. Buy close support and sell close resistance. In reality it is a little more complex and I prefer to wait for a confirmation (Yelena calls it double top I call it 123 pattern). For intraday traders pivots play an import role from this standpoint and once again as rule of thumb if price is above daily pivot think about going long and viceversa. ( http://www.babypips.com/school/suppo...esistance.html ). Last but not least read in this thread the posts of very good traders you can learn a lot about trading. Concerning specifically your trades I see you use M15 TF. It is important to understand what kind of trades you are looking for (if you like scalping I think M5 is better but if you prefer let me say swing trading M15 could be ok … but this is my personal opinion). When you got in the market price action was in a narrow range (about 35 – 40 pips) between R1P and a support (besides there were some other long term S/R and fibo levels). As I said The lagging factor and the range killed you. In these cases you have two choices : 1 move to lower TFs for scalping or 2 wait (also not to trade is trading) … the second one is my best choice. Let me close with other two little advises : · MM (never overtrade) and always protect your precious capital with SL and moving it to BE as soon as possible. · Know yourself …. This is also an investment you can do for your life I am sorry for this long post and for my bad English, I hope this could help you and someone else here. Have a great future in this business Ciao wiz

getRDone, It sounds like you didn't get the files into the correct MT4 sub-folders. First, exit your MT4. The genesis.tpl file should go into the templates folder that is directly below the MT4 installations root folder. Overwrite the one that is probably already there from your first attempt. Restart your MT4, and you should be fine.

The only filter most of us use is checking the M15 stoch before going in and in a strong trend like on Friday, I would not go against the trend and take the first signal in the opposite direction, I would look for a retest of that area first. You couldn't have got much more of a trending day than Friday, in the image attached there were 2 counter trend signals on EU (during normal hours) at the horizontal lines, the first one although overbought the M15 stoch was peeking above the 20 line, but the weekly pivot was just 9 pips above the entry point so would have been no trade for me. The second one looked better but the pivot was again only 12 pips above the entry if you had taken a chance you could still have got out at BE. You will usually find there is some kind of filter like that, and it will keep you out of most, but obviously there will be some losses as well when everything looks good but still fails, those you would just have to accept.

Essentially, what you're asking for is the 'Holy Grail'....and it doesn't exist. There simply is no way to know whether a move is going to be a 100 pip trend, that may turn into a 500 pip trend over a few days, or whether it is a false start and will reverse after 10 pips. If we knew the answer to that dilemma, we would all be extremely rich people. This is the reason for Stop Loss and good Money Management

--- 帖子 #735 ---
I am learning discipline slowly Before I enter a trade, I look at the M5 chart with the M15 stoch on it and ask myself if I took a screenshot now, would I be able to look at it later and find a reason I shouldn't have gone in. Only these things are taken into account as well as the matrix obviously, the position of the M5 stoch, position of the M15 stoch, price above/below 5ma and clear of s/r above for a buy or below for a sell, at least far enough away that there is a good chance I can move to breakeven if needed. As far as retests go, if there is a clear rejection of a s/r line and price is not particularly trending I may not need to see a retest before going in, but if an M5 bar has managed to breach the line and close below it/above it, that to me is not a rejection so I would need to see a retest. I've found the trades I go into now are (to quote RJ) high probability trades and then I don't need to filter anything else because losses are kept to a minimum and when losses are kept to a minimum its surprising how quickly the pips add up. I trade at what most would call high risk, so losses have to be kept to a minimum. Thats why I look at 4 different currencies, so I can cherry pick what I class as the high probability trades from each of them or all of them.

--- 帖子 #744 ---
Hi handy, I don't believe that there is a recognised day start because of 'ego' as all 3 trading zones (Asia, UK/Europe, US) would like to believe that they are the important one lol This is just my personal preference, and others may disagree especially if their Pivots work well with their own timezone (that's definitely more important than my opinion lol), but I like the end/start of my charting day to be 22.00 UK/London time (= 23.00 Central European Time (Frankfurt) = 17.00 Eastern Standard Timetime (New York) for the following reasons): 1) this is the time when Forex trading becomes available again on most trading platforms and it gives 5 equal and complete trading days until most platforms shut down again the following Friday at 22.00 2) there is no Sunday data to mess up any MAs and Monday's pivots will take their clues from the previous Friday rather than from the 1 or 2 hours of low liquidity Sunday data. 3) 1 complete 24 hours day include the Asian + UK/European + US sessions in full. You certainly do not want your 'day' to include only a part of the UK/European/US session. If your are using MT only as a charting platform, then using Alpari-UK (there are others) does the trick, because they have set their servers at UK/London+2 exactly for the reasons stated above. Oli.

--- 帖子 #751 ---
Hi Mr Pippy, I don't think that there is a correct or an incorrect way to trade re-entries, either with a Matrix signal or an Arrow signal (or both). It really depends on your level of confidence in the strategy and your level of trading experience but sticking to 'standard' entries for a newer trader might be safer. As an overnight example in Crude Oil M5, the first entry (white line) had all the right criteria (even the M15 matrix was half short - 2nd matrix down) but: 1) the original arrow+matrix entry wasn't the cleanest one as it took a while to get going and had some drawdown 2) the following 3 re-entries (yellow lines) all were great trades with very little drawdown all yielding plenty of pips (100+ for the first one). It's also a good example showing that when an instrument starts to trend in one direction, then the Stox will go and stay in OB/OS condition for a long time. Also bear in mind that this is a 'good' example of re-entries: there are plenty of examples too where a matrix-only re-entry (without a new arrow) resulted in a bad trade. Oli

Something that has helped give me more confidence to take these trades (and to stay in them) is to add a 13 EMA to the chart. Make the color Magenta and make the line thicker than the 5 EMA yellow line. For example, put it on a 15 min AUD/USD and look at the last 5 arrows. 3 shorts and 2 longs. The 3 shorts would have won and based on the rules you would not have taken the 2 longs (both losers) because the stoch had not "recently" come from below 20.

--- 帖子 #831 ---
The entry is at the close of the bar where RJ have his line. That is normally more or less the same time and the same price as the open of the bar where you have your line and that is the time of entry. That means you read the stoch (and other indicators) at the last closed bar and that is where RJ have his line. So the line on your chart is not at the "wrong" bar because you enter at the open of that bar (the close of the previous bar) but you are busy entering the trade at that exact time so you read the stoch at the close of the previous bar where RJ have his line. The stoch and the other indicators will no longer be changing (repainting) at the closed bar. Your bar is still "live". English is not my language so i am not sure if that sounds logic but anyway both RJ's line and your line is correct because in forex the close of one bar is almost always more or less the same as the open of the next. Arctic4x

--- 帖子 #851 ---
Recognising the difference between a pull back and reversal, even a short term reversal, is not something for which there is a formula or a set of rules. Of course, if we get a complete opposite signal, then you can take as a prudent time to exit, but it may not have been the optimum time to exit. It's really one of things that comes with hours and hours of chart time and trading......and even then, mistakes still occur. Even if you exit a move early and the PA continues in it's direction after a pullback, it's not the end of the world. Some profit is better than no profit, and after a pullback you will nearly always a good Genesis signal to re-enter. If not.....watch and learn. )

Here is a typical illustration of the pivot test (ej m5)....bounce.....re-test and breakthrough that Olivia and others have been speaking of. Yes, there is a little slippage of the PA over the pivot, which is one reason why I'm not worried if pivots don't match perfectly.....a few pips either side is ok, imo. You'll very often see this not only on pivots, but on most other s/r lines, no matter whether they may be round numbers, fibs, trendlines or whatever.

--- 帖子 #1035 ---
I use Steve Hopwood's Multi Purpose Trade Manager, and then a variant of it that allows for ATR based jumping stops ... found here . So I use that to set ATR based SLs &amp; TPs, to set BE and to run jumping stops etc. It may not be the best way to do it for Genesis, but it works for me and just means I can focus more on deciding whether to enter or not. It also has a heap of other functions. The home of MPTM is now no longer on ff - google can help you find it. The best thing about MPTM is you can run multiple instances of it on one MT4 (each on a different chart), so you can have different settings for different timeframe trades, or in my case, I split trades. I then use a separate pair of scripts to automatically determine position size (based on ATR) when I enter - easier for me because my account is non USD, so the calculations are a bit slower when you're trying to do things quickly. If you do decide to use MPTM, make sure you read the manual and test it thoroughly on demo first.

--- 帖子 #1068 ---
GU: you already had the start of a downtrend with lower lows at B &amp; D and lower highs at A &amp; C + you correctly drew the down trendline. The daily pivot was 21 pips away and stox were fine but you were going against a new formed/forming downtrend. In that case, waiting for a break and M5 close above the trendline would have been a minimum. EU: same pattern...I couldn't draw A &amp; B on your chart but it's the opposite of the GU trade (higher highs at B &amp; D and higher lows at A &amp; C makes an uptrend) + if you draw a trendline from the low at 09.50 to the other low at 11.00, again you'll see that no candle broke and closed below the trendline. A quick filter that i've mentionned on Symphonie: a 13-period RSI with a line drawn at the 50 horizontal level. Look for your signal candle to close above 50 for a long (strength) or below 50 for a short (weakness). It's not a cast-iron filter but if you are going against the trend then you want to make sure that the countertrend move has some strength rather than just being a quick pullback-and-resume-the-direction-of-trend.

--- 帖子 #1077 ---
Capstone, There are 2 steps. First, drop the usual stochastic indicator from MT4 onto your chart with the following parameters: http://i46.tinypic.com/2nb94c7.jpg Second, using the Navigator, drag the MTF Stoch on top of the normal Stoch window you just added, and set the parameters like this: http://i45.tinypic.com/10ymaue.jpg That should give you the overlapping M5 and M15 stochs in one window. If you want to hide the slow lines, just change their color's on the Colors tab to None from the drop choices.

--- 帖子 #1078 ---
Yesterday, and in fact much of this week, has not been easy trading. I see the same type of panic/disappointment/frustration creeping in here with some people, and they are falling into the same old trap.......'let's add more indicators!'. Listen, the answer isn't in adding more indicators......the answer is in recognising that the market does not trend nicely every day. It has periods of consolidation/ranging. It also has levels of support and resistance, some of them, very, very strong levels. See on the Weekly chart below.....the EU pair is at an extremely important and strong level.....a level that hasn't been properly broken since about 2005. Of course the PA is going to have trouble here...it has happened before, this level is strong.....not unbreakable, but strong. We have had a great run down from the 1.30's to where we are now, but even then, there has been a couple of decent consolidation/ranging areas that we have had to work through. The answer is not in adding more and more indicators looking for the magic pill that will make you money no matter what the market does. The answer is in recognising how the market behaves, and when it is good to enter trades and when it is not. It simply is not possible to make hundreds of pips every day.....sometimes you need to accept the fact that today may be a day where the market is going to be difficult/dangerous and it's best to stay out.

--- 帖子 #1177 ---
For me....it's not an issue Oli. Someone has tried and tried to pin me down to specific numbers and their meaning on the stoch, but it's not an absolute science. For instance.....79 does not mean 'not overbought' and 81 mean 'definitely overbought'. It doesn't work that way. The 80 and 20 lines are just numbers that we use to measure the level, but they have no real meaning....imo. For that reason, it is impossible, and foolish, for someone to try and pin down an absolute with the stoch......and for the same reason, it's not a major issue which line you exclude. In fact it's better if you don't exclude a line at all because you're missing out on some of the value of the stoch indicator, but for the purposes of the M5 chart, it is handy to do so. I have the stoch in full (both lines) on other charts.

--- 帖子 #1202 ---
Olivia &amp; other... This is a TA pattern that happens in all TF and is fairly consistent: by consistent I mean that you should be wary of it and not trading it (at least not the breakout part). We had a well defined triangle formation/consolidation (between the 2 yellow lines) on AudUsd. Once a triangle has formed use the 'cycle lines' indicator from MT and place one end at the start of the formation (A 0%) and the other end at the apex of the triangle (B 100%) leaving just 3 equal lines inbetween showing 25/50 &amp; 75% of the time elapsed. If you get a break of either trendline around the 65% area, very often this will be a false breakout and it will reverse quite quickly. The way to trade it is to wait for a later break of the other side (E) and very often you will get a nice pullback for a much better entry at the retest of the top line (C) or the bottom line (D). The reason that I mention this pattern is that it was also accompanied by a Genesis Long signal at (E) at 14.15 UK time and the M5 stox was in a great position and the M15 wasn't far behind. The TP for such a pattern is the height of the triangle (28 Pips) added to the 1.0431 breakout point at (E) giving roughly 1.0459 (we hit 1.0455 so far).

--- 帖子 #1214 ---
A few more words (not mine) to ponder over the weekend and my annotations in italic..... The Stochastic Oscillator "doesn't follow price, it doesn't follow volume or anything like that. It follows the speed or the momentum of price . (That's probably why it's so well suited to Genesis - you want to get in a trade while the momentum is strong). As a rule, the momentum changes direction before price (that's why the Stox will generally turn early and why it's already on its way up/down by the time we get a Genesis signal). It is important to note that overbought readings are not necessarily bearish and oversold readings are not necessarily bullish. Securities can become overbought/oversold and remain overbought/oversold during a strong uptrend/downtrend. Closing levels that are consistently near the top/bottom of the range indicate sustained buying/selling pressure ( RJ touched on that last part a few times at Symphonie's) . Look for occasional oversold readings in an uptrend and ignore frequent overbought readings. Similarly, look for occasional overbought readings in a strong downtrend and ignore frequent oversold readings. (In a nutshell, in a strong uptrend, be careful if you want to sell when the Stox is OB but instead look to re-enter Long position(s) when the Stox is or gets near OS levels - similarly, in a strong downtrend, don't look to buy when the Stox is OS but instead look to re-enter Short position(s) when the Stox is or gets near OB levels). Should a security trade near support with an oversold Stochastic Oscillator, look for a break above 20 to signal an upturn and successful support test. Conversely, should a security trade near resistance with an overbought Stochastic Oscillator, look for a break below 80 to signal a downturn and resistance failure. ( This is the bread-and-butter setup used by most successfull Genesis traders in here - look for a test and retest of an important Pivot line and go with the next Matrix signal). Bullish and bearish divergences in the Stochastic Oscillator can be used to foreshadow reversals (more on that next week depending on time available and interest by members in here). Please feel free to add anything you like whether it be comments based on your experience or questions based on what you don't know. Oli

Another simplified Genesis Matrix. I struggle to look at the charts for any length of time due to being at work, so I needed a simplified version of this excellent strategy. Here's what I came up with. I removed all pivot indicators. I added 200EMA. Trade long above and short below. M5 AND M15 stochs must go below 20 for long, above 80 for short. M5 must then be angling up for long, down for short. Enter on Matrix signal with candle close on the correct side of the 5EMA. SL below/above the last fractal. TP = 2 x SL. I find this simplifies things significantly and suits my purposes. It might also be a good place for newbs to start. A lot fewer trades, but a simplified and reliable entry. Not trying to change the strat here. Just showing how I trade it [very successfully] in case anyone is interested! Cheers, Rob

You also posted on your chart something very important in terms of Money Management (MM) &amp; trading emotions that new(er) traders might have missed.: Target Point (TP) = 2 x SL (Stop Loss) - No intervention, you either get SL or TP 1) because your TP is twice the size of your SL, you can afford to be right only 1 out of every 3 trades and still be at breakeven.....(nice). It shows that with the right MM and Risk/Reward (RR) strategy, you can be profitable even if you only get it right less than 50% of the time. 2) this is probably even more important for new(er) traders: I am talking about emotions . On one side we have greed that will always want you to wait a bit longer because "you might just get an extra pips out of this trade" and on the other side we have fear that will make you increase the size of your SL because "if the market turns soon I might just be able to get out at breakeven". Both of these will more often than not get you less pips because you won't pull the trigger at the 'right' time in a winning trade and it will decimate your account by having too big a SL and/or increasing it as the trade turns against you. There is an old saying by a stock trader (Oscar) that I know that is very very true: "Stops(loss) &amp; Limits(TP) are IN, emotions are OUT". He means that when you enter any trade, not only should you know where your SL &amp; TP are but you should also enter Limit orders to make sure that when either of TP or SL is reached, the trade is closed automatically. Honestly, as a new(er) trader you will have a much better time trading if you do it like that because you will take the emotions out while the trades are progressing giving you more time to concentrate on the next chart where the next trading opportunity is developping. Oli

Yeah! When you first start out, all you can see is those HUGE moves/trends, so you naturally want to capture that. But you don't NEED to. I genuinely don't care if I make 20 pips and the rally goes on for another 120 pips [like EurUsd one day last week]. I have made TWICE what I risked. I am VERY happy! While on this subject, I would like to caution against counting pips. Pip counting is meaningless and only serves the ego. ALL that matters..... I'll say it again..... ALL that matters, is what you risk, versus what your potential reward is. Pip counting is TOTALLY pointless: Trader A makes 1000 pips in a week. Trader B makes 50 pips in a week. Who makes most money? Trader B of course! Why? Because trader A used 150 pip stop losses and 50 pip targets. Trader B used 5 pip stop losses and 50 pip targets. [I've made these figures extreme, in order to demonstrate my point!]. So, please guys, don't count pips, count R. That's risk reward. I switch off when someone posts that they made 100 pips today. Big deal. If you MUST count in pips, at least tell us how many pips you RISKED. Because if my imaginary trader risked 100 pips to make his/her 100 pips, the 20 pips I just made actually represent a return on my account which is DOUBLE his/hers!! [assuming same % risk] Not ranting here guys, just trying to assist! And make people think for themselves a little! Rob

--- 帖子 #1235 ---
Only being able to put in one trade at a time is a problem, can't you drop the lot size so you can trade another pair? Thats the first thing out of the way. I will say though, you are concentrating too much on the pivots and not enough on price action in my view. Yes you have to be aware of pivots but to say point blank you will take profit at a certain place because of a pivot is not right. Yes, if you have to go out and can't watch the trade, the safest place to set your take profit is just below/above a pivot level, but if you're watching the trade you should watch the price action and if it flies through it without looking back then you stay with it. The GU trade you talked about, although there wasn't a pivot underneath it, there was clearly an invisible line there that GU had been unable to break, so when it didn't break it again you should have quickly moved to breakeven when it started to move backwards. I have to agree with a couple of the others when they said to concentrate on 1 currency, especially if you can only trade one trade at a time. Each currency will have days where they move a lot and days when they don't, so just trade the one, whichever one you feel best on, AU usually trends quite well but it will have days that it doesn't, EU the same. GU I wouldn't touch yet until you've mastered one of the others because it can suddenly fly in a completely different direction. So if I were in your shoes (which believe me I have been) I would choose between AU and EU. One other thing, be aware of pivots, don't take trades that are obviously right on top of a pivot if you are thinking of selling or right below if buying, but if its far enough away that you can think to yourself you will have space to move to breakeven if necessary then take it. If nothing ever went through a pivot the market wouldn't move. It would be bouncing between the daily open and the next pivot line all day and go nowhere else and that would not happen. Don't restrict yourself to "I'm going to take profit at x point thats only worth 20 pips, my stop loss is 30 so I won't take it. Look at EU on 26th, how many pips could you have got if you had been able to take that trade and not restricted your thought process about how far it was going to go? I know what your problem is, and you won't believe me, but most of your problem is mental. You are restricting yourself, instead of gathering what pips you sensibly can, you are taking it as gospel that the pivot will not be penetrated and coming out too early way before anything else is telling you to come out.

I am not a new trader by a long way, but I still like to capture moves, I still HATE setting a take profit of 20 pips and it goes another 100 pips without me. I never take risk/reward much into account. If the stop loss for a trade is too big (more than 25-30 pips including spread on the M5) I don't take it, its as simple as that. I definitely don't care going for 1:1, 1:2 or whatever else, and I'll tell you the reason for that. I couldn't trade like you've set out, because to me, to let a trade go to nearly taking profit then watch it come back to its stop loss is a trading sin. We each have our ways of trading of course and each person must go with what feel, but the maths doesn't add up. If you have a fixed stop loss, so you always risk 20 pips and want to gain 40 then it starts to make sense. But if your stop loss varies which it does placing the stop loss under the swing high/low then it doesn't make sense. Olivierforex stated that it was good because "you can afford to be right only 1 out of every 3 trades and still be at breakeven" and I say thats not right. Trade 1: 25 pip stop loss reaches 50 pip take profit. Profit: +50 Trade 2: 40 pip stop loss gets hit Profit now: +10 Trade 3: 30 pip stop loss hit Profit now: -20 Do you see what I'm getting at, all the while there is a variable stop loss, the maths don't add up. The way a trader called Paulus does it, is to risk 5% of his account to gain 10% -15% that makes more sense but is much easier for him to work out "on the fly" because he uses a spread betting company that is a fixed lot size value whatever currency he trades try doing it when you're working on a different value currency at the same time as placing the trade and working out your stop loss, its a lot more to think about. The pip counting thing, we don't all have the same percentage risk, that is down to personal preference, as long as the pips are counted properly, for instance on each individual trade, not adding on if the trade is added to then its fair enough. I count pips myself as my way of knowing how I well or badly I traded on a particular day, my actual risk in % terns is nobody elses business but my own, but in pip value it is never more than 30 pips including spread max on M5. EDIT: Just one more thing I've thought of and then I'll stop rambling. Just about every day RJ and I will have a competition on who gets the most pips. We both count pips in the same way, not adding to them when adding to a trade, just purely on individual trades. Now if he gets 200 pips and I get 100 and the same time roughly was spent trading, I take it that he has traded better than me that day. I don't think to myself but what was his R:R on those trades, I care who managed to steal more pips away from the market.

ALL that matters..... I'll say it again..... ALL that matters, is what you risk, versus what your potential reward is. Position size is what you mean equal to, risk size... Potential reward is unknown, risk is...provided you put a SL. After 1oo trades or better , 1000 trades, then you can compare R winners to R loosers...that ratio gives your expectancy for your system based on samples....that sounds more like business, or bad business ...same like in any other business... Any expectancy above R 0,50 is good business in my book...meaning, you make, on average, half a dollar, per dollar risked..or better. The distribution is different for any winning system...some loose 10 times in a row, then make a big winner....others win 50 percent of the times but make a bit more on the winners...whatever increases your account...and another variable is the ammount of opportunities you get to play your game.... Life is limited...some edges are tiny, but get repeated very often...that´s how big boys make money with their robots...other edges are better, but play out very seldom... Hi Cody, Sorry I didn't explain properly what I meant &amp; I've just realised my mistake....if you put a M15 MTF stox on a M5 chart then for every 14 minutes and 59s the M15 stox is 'laging' &amp; won't be painted until the M15 bar closes, at which point M5 &amp; M15 will be 'level' again. I thought that Yelena used a modified version that shows you live where the M15 stox is likely to be painted (the blue bit) but after rechecking the charts I realised that it was taken at the end of the hour when M5 &amp; M15 are always 'level'. You see that problem even more if you have an H1 Stox on an M5 chart, as the H1 stox 'lags' for 55 mins. Cheers

--- 帖子 #1337 ---
Something we haven't yet spoken about that the newer members might be interested in is the meanings of Stochastic Divergence. RSI and CCI can show divergence, as can MACD and TVi and many others. Personally I think oscillators do the best job, (stoch, rsi etc), but that's just me. I'm not going to get right into the subject here, but if you go here there is a nice easy to read but comprehensive tutorial on divergences. Divergences don't always work, so they are not an entry signal.....(because we do not predict where the PA is going on this thread, because we don't know!)....but they are a great 'heads up' as to what *might* happen. Do not form a directional bias in your mind because of this, just bear it in mind *in case* in works out, then you might be able to get a good entry to the action. So, below is the EU H4 chart, which is showing a Hidden Bullish Divergence.....meaning that the PA might have a run up from here over the coming sessions. Just something to bear in mind, but not to form a bias in you mind....fwiw

--- 帖子 #1338 ---
It is so confusing getting to grips with Regular and Hidden divergence. Was looking for divergence on the highs of oscillator on your chart until I finally spotted it on the lows. Have made several attempts to devise an easy aid to memory. After review of the tutorial have put together this aid to memory. Regular Divergence: Warning of possible Reversal in direction of Oscillator. Hidden Divergence : Possibility of Continuation in direction of Price. Bullish Divergence look at the Lows.(Price and Oscillator) Bearish Divergence look at the Highs.(Price and Oscillator) Hope it helps and does not add to the confusion! EP

--- 帖子 #1377 ---
Point 1: notice how we hit the down trendline to the pip...this tells me that the bears are in charge because there wasn't even any overspill above the trendline and we retraced fast and we made a new lower low at Point 2. Of course I didn't know at the time if the price would bounce of the trendline or go through it but when the Long signal was generated (1st blue arrow) there was only 8 pips left before we'd reached that trendline and that is not enough for me (to quote RJ, it wasn't a high probability trade and therefore I didn't enter a Long despite the fact that the Stox were in good places). Point 3: we were still in the downtrend with 0-2 making lower lows and 1-3 making lower highs. Once we retraced from 3, I drew my second down trendline between 1 &amp; 3 (I would not consider a Long until we at least Closed a M5 candle above it). Point 4: once we got to that point I started being open to a possible Long setup later because: a) for the last 3 hours the price had been going up and down around the DP and that is showing at least indecision between Long &amp; Short. b) we now had 5 different candles that had tested 1.2254 and that level had held (was support slowly starting to come in around that level after the earlier bounce at 1.2248? Higher support levels are the first steps in an emerging uptrend). Point 5: at 12.40 we get a COMPLETE Long M5 Genesis signal with 4 blue dots + Arrow (yippee, I like to have the Arrow on the same candle as Genesis - not a Genesis rule, it's just me) + the next candle 'opens clear' of the yellow MA + (M5 blue / M15 yellow) stox are pointing up from recent OverSold (OS) levels and they are NOT in OverBought (OB) territory yet + the H1 stox (red) is at least flat now + that M5 candle closed at 1.2269 ABOVE the DP at 1.2265. Last but not least, there was still that trendline I talked about earlier to consider (the one between points 1 &amp; 3). Although it doesn't show it using HA candles, the 12.40 M5 candle also Closed above that trendline (please see yellow circle in the green insert). With all this in my favour I entered a Long position + I felt that I had a good Risk/Reward scenario in this trade: 1) I could put my SL either below the 1.2254 level (mentioned in Point 4) risking 20+ pips or even below the low at 2 (1.2248) risking 30+ pips. 2) the reason that my R/R was good is that at 1.2269 , the R1 area at 1.2305 was 36 pips away giving me a 1 to 1.5 R/R (not the best but acceptable). Last couple of points: a) if you look at the green insert again you could have had an extra confirmation if you were even more cautious: the M5 candle that followed the break of the 1-3 trendline (yellow arrow) was technically perfect to add to the Long cause because: 1) it retested the 1-3 trendline, went below it, at which point buyers stepped in as it was potentially the last chance to 'get in' for a Long ride. 2) not only did it again Close above the trendline, it also closed as a bullish candle (the close was higher than the open) and it had that long rejection-of-the-old-trendline tail. It doesn't alsways work like that: if you had waited, we could have had this candle go straight up and give you a much worse entry and even stop you from entering altogether if it had closed too near the R1 area to still offer you a good R/R ratio. It has been mentioned before: consider R1 (and the other pivot levels) as areas rather than a straight line so look to take profit a few pips before it especially if you haven't had the best of day so far or if the previous PA has not been too friendly. Yes it might just go straight through and you could miss out on more pips, but you are not the only trader eyeing these levels and if the price retraces, you don't want to be the last one to get out and get the worst price too to close your trade. Oli PS: feel free to add anything...there is no such thing as definitive PA/TA analysis as we all see different things in the same chart. Edit2: EurUsd2 should be the picture now showing and it's a bit clearer! Edit 3, also important ...when we got the first Long signal, all the dots on the M15 matrix (below the M5) were red! When we got the Long signal, 2 out of 4 dots on the M15 Matrix had already turned blue (much better than none lol) and the signal was generated at 12.40, meaning that when the M5 candle closed at 12.45, so did the M15 candle (so what you see is what it was then - M5 signals generated on the xx.10 xx.25 xx.40 xx.55 candles have added strength in my view if the M15 matrix is also starting to change colour then).

--- 帖子 #1402 ---
For anyone struggling a little bit with this, I think that you should do the following with the pairs that you are monitoring: 1) have 1 chart with all you need for Genesis trading in terms of indicators 2) have a separate chart where you do basic TA at least so that you don't overcrowd Genesis charts with other stuff (i do that). Lines (up &amp; down trendlines, support lines, resistance lines, pivot lines...) are really powerful for 2 reasons: 1) a lot of traders use them ----&gt; they will enter or exit their positions around them 2) unlike most indicators which are lagging (they take their value from past data), lines are not lagging and that is their biggest strength in my opinion. As soon as you have 2 tops or 2 bottoms, draw a line between them (as shown in the example today - Euro M5 TF - the blue arrows are the 2 anchor points for each trendline) and watch the PA if/when the price returns to that line and you will learn a lot in a short period of time. As we've seen earlier today on more than 1 occasion, broken trendlines accompanied by a Genesis signal can serve as an extra confirmation to a more reliable entry. And of course the opposite is also true: if you get a Genesis signal and price sits a few pips away from a trendline, be careful (a Genesis signal is not a guarantee that price will break through).

Dan, As RJ has said, the closed candle is the entry point. Some of the charts posted, though, deliberately show a vertical line drawn on the bar prior to the actual entry, so as not to obscure the detail of the entry bar to the viewer. There isn't a fixed standard of how to indicate an entry point, but that may also explain some of what may appear to be "early" entries.

--- 帖子 #1437 ---
Quite a few people have pm'd me over the last couple of days about a higher low/lower high and they are unable to see them properly. Just to help you out while just starting trading, if you put the zigzag indicator on your chart it does help to see them at a glance and if you are having trouble with false signals, don't put a sell in until the high before the signal is lower than the high before it, and don't put a buy in until the last low before the signal is higher than the previous low. If you are getting lower highs and higher lows then price is ranging. Take that into account along with pivots, stoch and the genesis matrix and you will find you will not go too far wrong. All this will do is help to keep you trading with the immediate trend of the M5. BUT don't forget, the trend has to end sometime. Edit: The zigzag will repaint as price moves through where it thought was a high or low, just be aware of that. Its not too much of a problem though as you are waiting for the signal from genesis afterwards, but just so you're aware of it.

--- 帖子 #1473 ---
I have lately adopted a trade management strategy that has really helped my trading alot and I am finally showing showing some nice profits with symphonie/genesis. Its not a perfect strategy but its one that suits me and I just thought I would share for people who might be struggeling. I use to always watch my trades and it made me insane. Always closing early to see it run or not closing to see it go from profits to stoploss. What I do lately is I start of with my stop loss at swing high/low. If I enter a trade I try to go for 2-1 reward/risk. So if stop loss is 15 pips my target will be 30 (or nearby pivot/sr/roundnumber) Once my trade goes 1/3rd I take 1/3rd profit and I move my trade to BE. I get stopped out alot, but atleast I have a stress free trade with small profit. Today was a great example how it worked perfectly. My first trade EU didnt make the 2-1 target but I got small profit and then stopped out at BE. My second trade, GU made it all the way to 2nd target. Now the trades werent perfect setups (according to me) so I didnt take 2% risk like always but only 1% If I took 2% i would be up 4% already but half of that is already double my daily target Also I attached my demo balance chart to show how much it has helped me. Like I say its definitely not perfect and you miss alot of good trades when stopping out at BE, but for a bad and nervous trader like me finding my feet its working pretty good. Ive mentioned before, currently I am more concerned not loosing a trade that I am with winning one.

Yes, it utilizes fixed % risk. If you use 2%, 5% or whatever, it's up to you. Pip value $4 on eur/usd if the SL needed is 20 pips your lot size would now be 1 standard lot, or 10 mini lots. pip value $10 on eur/usd. it seems clear that using fixed lot size with variable stop loss can hold your profits over time according to monte carlo simulation. any thoughts?

--- 帖子 #1515 ---
Yes that is the good old "Two Percent Rule". The good thing about it is that it is very effective when it comes to the power of compounding profits. But that is also the bad thing about it because if you run in to a longer period of big draw down it is harder to get back to the high of the equity. You get what is called "negative compounding". That is easier if you use fixed lot size for risk. You get back to break even faster and easier. I will make a short example for one loosing trade and one winning trade. Just remember the more losers you have in a row and the deeper the DD gets, the harder it is to get back. To make a extreme example: If you loose 50% of your acc you have to make 100% profit to get back to break even. Anyway the example: For simplicity this is a R/R 1:1 system. You risk 2% of your $1000 acc. That is $20. You loose so your acc is now $980 You win the next trade and now you make 2% profit.2% of 980. That is $19,6 so now your acc is only $999,6 If you used fixed lot size for both trades (example $20 risk every trade) you would be back at BE. I am not sure if i explain this very well because English is not my language but anyway there are both advantage and disadvantage using the good old "Two Percent Rule" I am not saying one thing is better or worst than the other but it is important to study MM so you know the differences. Arctic4x

--- 帖子 #1520 ---
I understand what you are saying, but that's not exactly what I am trying to say. The point is adjustable lot size in relation to the size of stop loss needed for each trade . The 2% risk (or whatever number you want) remains the same, always. Doesn't matter if the SL is 20 or 50 pips. If you can enter a trade with a smaller SL, you can up your lot size, but still within your pre-determined risk profile . example: $10000 account, risk 2% per trade - fixed 50 pip stop loss risk = $200 lot size = 0.4 standard lot ($200/50 pip SL=$4/pip) now, just for sake of argument, imagine this trade yields 50 pips, so its 1:1 but, what if you could safely enter this trade with only a 20 pip SL? if you kept your lot size the same (0.4 standard lot) your gains would still be $200, or 2%. on the other hand, if you adjust your lot size in relation to your SL within your risk profile you would have: SL = 20 pips risk = still 2% ($200) lot size = 1 standard lot ($10 pip) if the trade yields 50 pips you would have now $500 in profits, instead of $200 using fixed lot size. Both methods had the same total % risk. The variable was the size of SL needed

There´s a big problem with scaling down...although it´s common, even used by good pros. It goes against the golden rule: keep winners big, loosers small. Scaling out makes sure, that when you get stopped right away, and like everyone else you will sometimes, you get the full punch... on the other side your best winners are always half... I know it helps our mind tremendously....esaing the initial stress...but in the long run, it goes mathematically against your bottom line. Try keeping a record, both ways, and compare after 20 trades or more....whichever way you do it. The only way it could work, is if you consider both trades as different systems, one that takes profit fast...the other let´s profits run. BUT, does the fast profit system, all by itself, work?...if not...then it´s an ilusion...ans you use the other to pay for the expenses of the looser... Of course, if you get out on the first systemat 2 R or better, and let the second one run for another 10 R...then you are talking business... Numbers don´t lie...make sure you keep track, of every trade...excell is great...make satistics...compare...then make your own conclusions...after that you know if it works... Like I said, treat both as 2 different systems...and watch closely, see if they make $ individually, otherwise, one is supporting the other one. My humble recomendation. Best of success to you...

--- 帖子 #1539 ---
[quote=cuchuflito;5894716]There´s a big problem with scaling down...although it´s common, even used by good pros. It goes against the golden rule: keep winners big, loosers small. Scaling out makes sure, that when you get stopped right away, and like everyone else you will sometimes, you get the full punch... on the other side your best winners are always half... I agree. Van Tharp in "Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom" says the same thing. He interviewed dozens of traders, and asked them to look back at their trades. If they had kept a full position all the way to their target, if their bottom line would have improved. And every one of them agreed it would have. He stated that the psychology of traders requires the need to be right, otherwise they get discouraged and don't perform as well. So in that context, taking part of a position off early, moving the stop to break even, and having a "free" trade is beneficial to them. They get to be right more often, but ultimately their bottom line is affected and they make less profit. Again, every individual trader has to do their thing and trade the way that makes them comfortable, and our egos play a huge role in that, but not always to our advantage.

I'll sleep when I'm dead Wiz!! I do tend to enter ahead of time if the Matrix and all other signals point the same way.....*and*......I have the luxury of a tight SL. Be aware though, that in super high impact news like NFP there will almost certainly be some SL sweeping going on a minute or two before the official release. The other thing to be aware of is that if get it wrong, and the movement is (say) a violent 100 pips spike, then there can easily be a 60 pip or more slippage in the SL.......so our SL of (say) -20, could easily end up at -80......which is going to spoil your day!!! So I don't try this with super high impact news, you have to pick and choose which ones you're going to have a go at. The safest thing to do is as you mentioned, let the dust settle and then enter a minute or two after the release.
