--- 帖子 #1586 ---
Entries are clear, by now , guess for everyone . Exit, as RJ says, is harder. Good traders just "know" from market "feel". Others like me, need some extra tools. I want to share an effective stop trail that I learned years ago... (TP: just like RJ says, easy enough.) TRAIL: Once in the trade open a new, separate chart with 3 Indies. Alligator AO AC from B. Williams. They come standard in MT4. (By the way, I´m an "expert" in B. Williams, read the books, know them by heart since the beginning in the old days.: don´t try it, it hardly works, although very popular!!!) The rules: 1 Stop: last pivot as per Genesis rules. 2 Stop: trail the farthest Alligator line, as the market goes your way. 3 Stop: keep an eye on the AC, as son as it goes 3 bars in the opposite colour to your trade, trail the second Alligator line. 4 Stop, as soon as it goes another 3 bars against you move to the closes t Alligator line. 5 Stop (might come before the latter), as soon as the AC goes from positive to negative, or viceversa (against you), trail 1 Bar plus spread till stopped out. 6 Stop: If the market runs strongly in your favour, as soon as both AC and AO have more then 5 bars in the same colour, trail also 1 bar till stopped...this doesn´t happen too often, but when it does it´s a running swing... ADVANTAGES: -reduces the size of loosing trades. -keeps you on board, often till the end of the swing or very close, or your preset TP. -mechanicall, no emotions. DISADVATAGES: -not perfect like all trailing systems. -will kick you out in bumpy swings, sometimes sooner than necesary. DISCLAIMER: please backtest thoroughly, it works for me, might not work for you

--- 帖子 #1601 ---
[quote=olivierforex;5898801]Thanks for the extra explanations, all is clear bar the above: 1) do they have to start at the same time? NO, provided you do get 5 together.. 2) or can one start before the other, in which case the first one might get to 7 or 8 before the 2nd gets to 5+ YES 3) we are talking about the opposite colour (so if we're short, we look for 2 x 5+ green bars? WRONG here´s the confusion: The crossing of the middle line is clear, and those AC bars will be opposite coulour to your trade, so if short, they will be green and viceversa. The other rule (which is a Bill Williams original), is: if both AO and AC have a 5 bar (minimum ) run on the same coulour of your trade , THEN you also apply the 1 bar rule. Why?, in those rare occasions, the market should be flying in your favour....and won´t last too long (of course maybe), so the idea is to stay close and protect your (hopefully) huge gains. The other rule is from someone else, I did not invent either....have a look on any TF, it´s a pretty effective trailing method. Original basic B Williams, is just follow the red line till you get a close aginst it...you can change to the closer Alligator lines if the market starts separating too far from them, ie. it´s flying your way steeply. Doing this will keep you going in long trends, but, will give up a lot of pips in shorter swings...as always, imposible to find the perfect solution...they are all a compromise... Cheers

--- 帖子 #1623 ---
There was no entry available at London open, unfortunately. The stochastics were way too high (both M5 and M15) and there was no decent pullback to give an entry until after NFP. Of course, with hindsight, an entry earlier on at London open would have been great, ignoring the stoch and everything else. This time you would have got lucky. But ignoring the rules and entering low probability trades will burn your account.....of that you can be certain. It is pointless to look back and lament what could have been, if you ignored the rules ect etc etc. That does no one any good, and it will lead you into taking risky trades and eventual failure. Also, you don't need to ride 100 pip+ trends. Those moves are nice when they come, but if you develop that mindset, you will start to ignore the smaller trades and dismiss them as 'not worth the effort.' The reality is though, that collecting 3 or 4 25-45 pip moves per day, every day, will build you account faster than you thought possible. When nice big runs happen along, great....it;s a bonus, but that's all it is. The rules of the system, once learned and practiced will keep you from entering low probability trades. High probability trades are what we are interested in, and if that discipline means that from time to time we let what would have been, with hindsight, a decent trade go by, then so be it. The times that happens is rare and not important. Entering a low probability trade is stressful, and it's a silly thing to do which is born out of greed. Fear and greed will kill accounts, and they are products of each other. Discipline is the cure!

--- 帖子 #1689 ---
Re. your "recoloured" candles... No indicator in the current matrix repaints so you must have the "alert on bar close" set to 'false' in the Input tab which means that you get an alert every times all 4 dots change colour within the same candle. Set it to 'true' and you will only get an alert if all 4 dots are the same colour at the end of your chosen TF candle. Oli

First of all, thanks for your quick respond Olivier. I kinda meant something different tho. The option you mentioned was set to "True". --- 帖子 #1692 ---
Robert, You are right. This is not repainting. The M5 candle is still open, so the M5 matrix, living on the M1 chart, will color the number of M1 bars back to the beginning of the M5 bar. So up to 4 bars may flip because the M5 is changing. Once the M5 candle closes, there will be no further changes in any bars on the M1 chart. Interpreting the color changes of a higher time frame can be tricky, but just remember that the 4 (or 5 just at close) bars painted on the M1 is still just 1 bar if you were looking at an M5. But looking backwards, what you're seeing is what the matrix, in all time frames, looked like at the close of the highest time frame bar.

metworth, Those signals are coming from two different indicators. The first, beginning with "genesis" is coming from the genesis matrix, without a stop loss/or time frame. Since the arrow is a secondary signal, which isn't really needed to be present for a trade entry, I suggest you turn that property back to false.

--- 帖子 #1718 ---
Angela, As bubola and RJ have suggested, make sure your MT4 is up to date. Second, got to the Tools/Options/Charts tab of the MT4 main menu, and make sure the Max bars in chart is a reasonable number (like 5000). Having a large number here can slow down the initial load, but after that things should be OK. Beyond that, the only time I've had a problem with system response was when one of the Genesis indicators was not present in the experts\indicators folder. Follow the instructions here and see if it helps. If it doesn't, I would try creating a new demo installation in a folder that isn't inside the Program Files or Program Files (x86) folders. (Vista has some issues with "permissions" that can cause unusual behavior on some systems. ) Then install the Genesis indicators from Page 1 and try again. Large numbers of indicators (&gt;500) in the experts\indicators or a very large history file or a large number of trades in a profile can slow a system way down or crash it. A fresh install of MT4 should use about 17,000-23,000 KBytes of memory (as shown in Task Manager/Processes tab). If you're using &gt; 100,000 Kbytes for an install, it's probably time to clean things up a bit. Hope this helps. --Cody

Angela, In case you didn't see my previous response, it is here . The arrow indicator is included in the zip file on page 1. --- 帖子 #1753 ---
Nothing specific unfortunately, other than lack of an obvious trend of course! You can see that since Monday we have been bouncing up and down between these lines.....that it to say that we are stuck in a range. If you look at a Daily chart, you can see a similar pattern. Which way it will break out, no one knows......but on the H1 chart below, you can see that there really isn't a trend to trade, so we need to be mindful that any trades we enter will probably be relatively short term trades and not run too far before turning around. When he have an obvious trend we can ride it a long way, even re-enter other trades in the same direction (scaling in), but with these days of being stuck in a range, that isn't possible......but because our system is good at what it does, we can pick our entries pretty well.

--- 帖子 #1781 ---
These are the principles of H1-M5 trading: 1. you first want confirmation of the trend/direction in the higher TF (H1): this is because a trend in the higher TFs will generally be stronger, last for longer and give you more pips than a M5 trend (the downside of H1 is that you will need wider SL, you will get fewer signals and probably will have larger drawdown too....) 2. once you have a new signal in H1, the trend will have turned and you will already be quite a few pips away from the previous top/bottom, but that's ok - it's better to miss on a few pips than be trading in the wrong direction. 3. then at some stage you will get a pullback (because price rarely move continuously in the same direction) - you will not take that M5 signal because it is in the opposite direction of the newly formed H1 signal. 4. after that, you will get a new M5 signal that will be in the same direction of your original H1 signal &amp; you will take it because now H1 &amp; M5 are pointing the same way. Below was a good example posted by Evaluator on the Symphonie thread a couple of month ago (20th June). Find it in your chart on the H1 TF, mark it, then look for the next M5 signal going the 'wrong' way and finally for the good M5 signal(s) after that, that have good pips and little drawdown, because they are in the same direction as the main trend. http://www.forexfactory.com/attachme...1&amp;d=1340297129 And this, from him too, the same explanation in a graphical way: http://www.forexfactory.com/attachme...3&amp;d=1332454036 ........ important : in ranging markets, higher TFs like H1 can be a killer because often they will signal the changes of trend too late and by the time you enter, the market is already turning round the other way ... (there is no such thing as a free lunch in forex). Oli.

--- 帖子 #1796 ---
If you look at a decompiled source of the arrow indicator, it is mathematically identical to the ASCTrend indicator, including the use, internally, of the Wiilliams Percent R indicator, and drawing the arrow. DPO is conceptually much easier to understand, but the math is different and doesn't call the iWPR; this version doesn't draw an arrow. But when the DPO indicator crosses it's 0.0 line, you will find that's where the arrow indicator will paint an arrow on the chart. DPO is looking at the current close compared to the SMA moving average of the last 14 Closes that have have been shifted 7 periods forward. There. Isn't that simple?

--- 帖子 #1813 ---
From the snap shot that you posted earlier, no. You were missing files out of your experts\\indicators folder. Loading a template onto your chart, in that case, would have just shown the indicators of the template that you *did* have in that folder. Which is pretty much what your pic shows. Additionally, if you close MT4 at that point, the template will be updated to only expect the files you have. On the other hand, once all of those indicators have been properly placed into their folder, and the template from the Genesis zip download is reloaded into the templates folder that is directly under the main MT4 folder, attaching that template will give you what you want. MT4 tries to be helpful by updating the template and profile when you close it, but in some cases, that can just confuse things. Hope this helps explain how things are related. --Cody

--- 帖子 #1873 ---
Hi Dmitry, HA candles have 2 uses within Genesis trading: 1) once we are moving in a direction, they can keep you in the trade longer because they do not change colour as quickly as a normal candlestick (ie you're less likely to close your trade on a minor pullback) 2) specific Genesis use: once you get a signal, Genesis likes the next HA candle to 'open clear of the yellow MA'; because of the way HA candles are calculated, a 'clear open' shows extra strength/momentum in the direction of your trade (I believe that RJ will not take a trade unless that criteria is met).

--- 帖子 #1940 ---
The dangers of predictions and bias. I was just reading on another thread, doesn't matter which one, where a poster has a strong Bull bias and cannot see past this. The Bear run we have had since 1.2440-ish, he deems to a 'correction' to the bull run. Because he has convinced himself that we are in the early stages of a complete long term reversal of trend, he bought at 2370 on the 6th of this month. He bought again at 2410 on the 7th. He bought again at 2350 on the 8th. That makes him about -320 pips as we speak......and he is still convinced that the bull run is under way. Now, maybe he's right.....maybe the bull run is underway and maybe this bear run is a correction. I don't know..... and neither does he or anyone else . The point is that we have been selling this bear run and making good pips, while he has been buying into a selling market.....it's called 'catching the falling knife', and right now he's getting cut pretty bad. If he is right, and the market does go up, we will buy it on the way up too. So by the time he gets back to break even, we will be a couple of hundred pips (at least) ahead. This is why I am not interested in predictions on this thread, and this is why we take trades according to what our system tells us, and not according to what we, or anyone else thinks!! No predictions and no bias. It's good for your account

--- 帖子 #1988 ---
its the supertrendline (STL) the 2nd row of the symphonie matrix, which is also the 2nd row of Genesis. both are CCI's the differences: 1. STL considers the threshold of the cci in the symph matrix. it does not in Genesis. 2. STL has 60 for setting, Genesis has 20. the main function of the the STL is for exits (exit #2 of symph thread), stay until the color changes. if you look at his picture, you'll see that Genesis gave you better exits and better entries (2nd row of Genesis vs STL) the STL is meant for days when PA refuses to pull back, like last week's friday trade. however, that occurrence only happens once a month nowadays. Genesis is meant for the intraday trader to get the meat of the daily ranges and not get out at +3 just because one has a bias or blindly following the cci. we've spent a long tie with symph and realized along the way that the most profitable exits are via the pivot points. i.e for yesterday's short, yesterday's low. you can liquidate 50% at the first pivot. then lock the remainder at +3. that way, the trade will never become a loser. happy weekend.

--- 帖子 #2000 ---
Hi Olivier, Yeah, the arrow indicators appear and disappear until the TF's candle closes (e.g., sometimes you see a 5 min short signal arrow printing on the 5 min TF only for the PA to reverse long and erase the arrow.) That's why it's important to wait for the candle to close to consider the signal valid. There should be a way to get the arrow to print only after the candle actually closes. I'll take a look at the source code if you or anyone else is interested. For now, If you're using the 15 min MTF arrow on the 5 min timeframe, I would only consider the 15 min arrow valid when the 15 min candle actually closes and not before (although you can take the M15 arrow printing early as a possible sign of trend reversal as long as it's in agreement with every other genesis signal/MTF stochs/5 EMA/SL risk-reward/PA failure at pivots). Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #2005 ---
genaja, Here is the Symphonie SET Candles indicator adapted for Genesis, as well as a modification of the original. Put all of these indicators in your MT4 experts\indicators folder, close and restart MT4 (if it was running), then load either SET or ESET onto any chart, any time frame. The original Symphonie_SET_Candles indicator was a predecessor of the Symphonie Matrix and painted the price candles based on the agreement (or not) of the Emotion and Sentiment indicators. Despite it's name (the T in SET stands for Trendline), the trendline indicator of Symphonie was not used in the rules for painting in v3. Genesis_SET_Candles_1.00 duplicates this behavior exactly, and all this indicator does is paint the candles of the main chart according to whether the bottom 2 lines of the Genesis matrix agree. If both are red, the candle is red, if both are blue, the candle is blue, and they are mismatched, the candle is yellow. If you use this (I won't), interpret the signals carefully. Blue candles only mean that 2 of the 4 lights in a column of the Genesis Matrix are blue, NOT the entire 4 indicators of the matrix. Genesis_ESET_Candles_2.00 takes the concept a step further, and uses all 4 lines of the matrix to determine how to paint the bars in the price window. If there is a full Genesis Signal long, the price bars are blue; if there is a full Genesis Signal short, the price bars are red. If there is disagreement in any of the matrix signals, the price bar is yellow. I won't be using this one either, because you lose 2 important features: the color of the price candle and the ability to use the Heiken Ashi candles. One of the recommended entry rules is an opening of the Heiken candle clear of the EMA5 line. Note that if you are loading the ESET_Candle_2.00 indicator, there is really no reason to load the Genesis Matrix on the same chart. If you load both, you double the computation needed per tick, and gain no additional information from that. Personally, I'll stick to the Genesis Matrix, which is at least the grandchild of the Symphonie_SET_Candles, and in my opinion, improves on it. The Matrix summarizes the information concisely, doesn't obliterate the Price Action information in doing so, and preserves the ability to use the Heiken Ashi. Which is sort of appealing to both my Right Brain and my Left Brain. --Cody

folks.. With your system in here where your almost getting a signal on every dip's and curves by basically trading off the 5ma with some confirmations to go with it your at risk to end up with some loss trades no matter what.. now some of these signals occur during ranging market and there is no way and no one including the OP here can help you to filter that.. looking at higher tf or pivots watch and etc won't help you either, it helps as much it hurts to miss opportunities.. so simply ask yourself, if the philosophy of my trading style is to catch every move of the market, wouldn't i fall into some losses or at times into strings of losses at some point and time? the answer is clearly Yes. so you either bear with losses to continue trade the same mentality to catch almost every move, or you simply take step back and let go of the first move off the range or a stall market and then to trade the dips after you seen the first move.. thats your only filter, which will cost you to miss some moves, getting less signals.. but its better than trading inside range and getting hammered for however long it might take. there is no filter for what your looking for.. the only filter is to change your trading philosophy. This post by no means is meant a negative affect on the thread or a attempt against the op or the contributors in here, it's just simply stating fact to make aware of what your trading and what you can choose to do.. this system could be profitable.. but, for who? certainly not for the one who gets discourage by losses and looking for new filters or questions after each loss, in reverse should simply take and accept the losss and move on and to set eyes on the long term results (not easy to do but doable, in fact its necessary to achieve success in this business).. but others who can bear with losses and got mass of trading experience who can read between the lines at times and cherry pick (which that i can tell you for sure is not easy and consistent) could be profitable. Anyways sorry to stick my nose in, only meant good and wish the best of luck to all. Dean

--- 帖子 #2074 ---
I have mentioned it to Gtudor already, but anyone using TMA Slope, please be aware that it repaints up to 20 bars! That's not to say that it can't be useful if you are checking it 'live', but it's absolutely meaningless if you do any backtesting (with 20 bars repaint, this is the sort of indicator that looks like the 'holy grail' on backtest - it actually calls turns in markets even before any consolidation takes place). Oli

--- 帖子 #2145 ---
For me it depends on the R/R ratio that presents itself in the 'next' trade because I try to consider each trade in isolation (I try not to get influenced by any ongoing trade(s) but that's not always easy - emotions always try to come into play lol). As I trade many instruments the risk in each trade is always quite small to allow me to have many running ones at the same time if the opportunities present themselves. But yes I'll have a maximum overall risk figure because it is not unknown for markets to turn on a dime and hit all your SL one after the other. What RJ mentionned also makes sense: if your first trade is already protected at B/E then you can almost consider the next one as the only one running as far as risk is concerned. One thing that is imperative for me if I'm running more than 1 trade is to place the SL even before I enter the 2nd/3rd trades for extra safety.

--- 帖子 #2271 ---
I have been randomly backtesting in the trade simulator that you can download from page1. This is how I have been backtesting with good results, I have come out a winner almost every day I trade! First I randomly pick a day in the past few years on the 5min chart. I then fast foward to around 2H before London Open and apply the matrix and start trading, I usually take the pre Frankfurt trade and trade through London session, sometimes into New York. I use a 30 pip stop loss on default and manually scale in from there. I like to dynamically reduce risk by dragging my sl behind the PA. Once I am up 25 pips or so I lock in 10 pips of profit and let the trade run. If I find myself in a loosing position and the 5min signal turns against me I will almost always cut the loss, if the 15min goes against me I have to take the loss. I will always cut the loss at -30 as a worst case scenario but usually end up taking around 10 to 20 pip losses. This is also a great way to practice and get use to recognizing patterns.

--- 帖子 #2345 ---
I've come to the conclusion that it's broker dependent, especially because the level at which those two arrows appear on Magdalen's chart are so close. I'm using Pepperstone , and I also have no arrows on the EurUsd chart at that time. I do have a long arrow at 1330, but nothing after that. Reloading the chart (only that 1) , restarting MT4, deleting and reloading the indicator, and trying 2 alternate indicators all give the same result for me: no arrows in the area they appear on Magdalen's chart. Olivia and I investigated a similar phenomenon a few weeks ago with the Gann Hi-Lo, and at that time I was using an Alpari account. Again, the cause was broker data, not the indicators. The indicators are driven by price quotes, and it is the broker's discretion as to when those ticks are sent out. MT4 "ticks" are not like stock ticks. They don't indicate an individual buy/sell. They are simply when the broker chooses to send a change in price. True ECN's are going to send those faster. I don't think you need to worry about the indicator's accuracy for this.

Now that I am thinking of it, I believe the problem was that the arrow I was using was the one you could alter max bars, to backtest purposes. after installing arrow.mq4 you provided it seemed the arrow reverted back to the one you cannot alter max bars displayed. weird, huh?

--- 帖子 #2376 ---
Ah, that explains it. The #MTF arrow uses iCustom to call arrow. The parameter list passed to iCustom has to be the same as the number of extern variables you see when you attach Arrow to your chart. Either none of them or all of them have to be listed, and in the same order. If you were using an arrow with a different number of parameters, iCustom (and therefore #MTF arrow) would get confused. When you added the arrow.mq4 file to your folder, MT4 recompiled that when you reopened it (happens automatically), so #MTF arrow could now find all of arrow's body parts with nothing left over. Edit: If you want to use the other arrow that has the MaxBars parameter, redownload that file and rename it to something else, move it to the indicators folder, restart MT4 and load that onto your chart.

While I am study this thread I want to make one notice concerning ATR indis. As we know its calculated on average range from last period. Thanks to Cody, we know that “lfl-atr projections” is using an averaging of last 7 days. The problem could be with calculation because of different time of brokers servers. Instead of 5 normal daily candles per week we can have 6 candles. So sixth candle is significally decreasing an average true range. Also as we know new day at the market starts with Sydney. And if your brokers starts much more later after Sydney it is also can influence on exact ATR number. So, to get as much as more real ATR numbers we have to use broker with 5 daily candles per week and we have to be able to adjust starting time for ATR calculation. It’s all my thoughts about ATR and may be I am wrong, just want to share it. By the way, good explanation video about “lfl-atr projections”: Inserted Video

I assume that you mean these 2 lines: [i] ExtMapBuffer1 = iCustom(NULL,TimeFrame, "arrow", SoundAlarm, EmailAlarm, 0, y); [i] ExtMapBuffer2 = iCustom(NULL,TimeFrame, "arrow", SoundAlarm, EmailAlarm, 1, y); I assumed that they had something to do with a 'physical' arrow on the chart when in fact they meant 'arrow.mq4' as in the indicator. And that brings another issue to the fore, that some people might have experienced or aren't aware of: .when you download a whole set of indicators, often with a template attached to it, you should keep the indicator's names exactly as they are because the template will look for them and need them to be unchanged. .it's a similar setup with the GenesisMatrix: it is made up inside of separate indicators and when loaded unto a chart, these will be 'called' to make up the lovely 4 rows of dots that we all enjoy; if one of these needed indicators is labelled differently, GenesisMatrix won't find it and you'll have a row of dots that's always the same colour.

--- 帖子 #2478 ---
Pivot stuff (if you didn't know it or have never noticed - check with FXIPivots as they keep previous days levels on the chart): 1. because we had a 'big(ish)' day yesterday in EU, all the pivots will be further away from the DP than after a small day (a day with not much movement). A better example is Monday 6th August when R1 was a huge 150 pips away from the DP (because we had such a huge move on Friday 3rd August). 2. because yesterday was an 'up' day, R1 &amp; R3 will be further away from the DP than S1 &amp; S3 ( R1 is 72 pips away from the DP but S1 is only 45 pips away from it). Similarly, after a 'down' day, S1 &amp; S3 will be further away from the DP than R1 &amp; R3 (this does not apply to R2/S2 though because of the way they are calculated - these 2 are always the same distance from the DP)

Yeah, that is our good friends at Metaquotes giving us the finger. You can get it to work if you are prepared to take some extra steps. Set proxy server to 127.0.0.1 Log out of MT4 and close MT4 Modify Spread in symbols.sel file Restart MT4 and login with any accountnr/pwd Simulate to your hearts content You may need to find and convert/import history data if your installation does not have enough. Required Programs: MT4i Spread Controller. Does most of the above work for you. Requires site account registration to download. http://www.mt4i.com/appstore/app.asp...ort=popularity SpreadChanger program to modify symbols.sel file with spread of your choice: http://www.jeremywhittaker.com/2011/...lly-change-it/ SpreadChanger script to modify symbols.sel file with spread of your choice: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...14#post4175914 If you are at MT4i you may be interested in trying out their MT4 trading simulator: http://www.mt4i.com/appstore/app.asp...ort=popularity

This is my view regarding Stox in order of importance (this is the case on both your red lines/entries): 1) I like the Stox to have been OB/OS (above 80/below 20) to at least show some potential exhaustion of buying/selling pressure in the previous move. 2) I then like my Stox to be pointing the right way (UP in your cases) 3) Only then do I look at the Stox level: I'll be more cautious if we approach or are already around 20/80 but that won't necessary put me off a trade; as we can see in your examples, the Stox can remain OB/OS for a long time while price is still going in the same direction (see potential in 1)). --- 帖子 #2601 ---
Believe it or not, there is a lot more information hidden inside the basic ATR indicator. In fact, I took the basic calculation for ATR (which is nothing more than an average of the candle's High-Low) and tweaked it through several versions until I came out with an indicator that outputs seven (7) different modes, or signals. So, from the ATR, you can extract at least seven (7) more characteristic, or behavioral outputs that tell you a bit more than just the High-Low average to be expected. The ATR (my version is called something different) can be a really good Timing Indicator, which is something that most traders have yet to discover. Its value as a Timing Indicator is probably more than its value as a Magnitude Indicator. However, you have to observe it in the right chart time frame, in order to see its true value and worth as a tool for Timing the move of the market (not its direction). It is not a directional indicator by any means. Gee - maybe I should spend some time on this subject just a bit somewhere on the forum. Regards, StealthTechnology

You are really looking for the next DP leg in the Harmonic pattern. After that, you will note that for this pair the Genesis Matrix will enter a another 'period' of less than feel good moments given the whipping action that will take place relative to its signals. That's because the market does not always fit a Standard Harmonic Ratio Pattern. Sometimes those ratios go beyond the simple Fibonacci tool that ships with the trading platform and you really have to dig into the Fibonacci Ratios to be able to calculate the next relevant set of ratios . This is the part about Fibonacci Ratios that they do not teach at most Trading Bootcamps. And, yes - it is fun and it feels good when the market remains inside a Standard Harmonic Patter, because those patterns are more well known to most traders. However, it is the Non-Standard Harmonic Ratios and Cycles that most traders don't follow and don't seem to understand very well. Yet, those are the dominant frequencies within the range of all Fibonacci Ratios (Non-Standard Ratios). Anyway, I'm going to keep reading (I'm trying to get caught-up in this thread) to find out how that DP leg turned out: 1) Did the market remain in a Standard Harmonic Pattern allowing the Short trade from Point "D" to Point "P" (the Projection point)? 2) Did the market turn Non-Standard and begin spewing less well known Harmonic Ratios to the upside, forcing the market into a brand new bullish trend? Ahh...ok, I see what you're saying now. The way I handle such situations is to wait for the retest of the pivot. It always happens (well not always, but mostly), and enter on the rejection of the retest. We have spoken about this before on this thread. You'll see most strong S/R lines retested and that is the time to enter. You might consider the stoch to be too high at the re-test, but you have to remember that the re-test is all part of the same move, therefore the entry is valid.

--- 帖子 #2858 ---
Geoff, I'm not surprised that the signals are earlier, since you're reducing all 3 smoothing periods from 12 to 3 or 5 to 3. Just be aware as you use this that you're reintroducing a lot of noise. The only way I can reproduce your screen shot is to load the indicator, change the input parameters, then recompile the source code while the indicator is attached. Odd things happen, you're right. Simply attaching it and changing the inputs to 3 doesn't cause this. But in any event, flipping the time frame to anything else and back will tidy it up. I can't tell if this is an issue with MT4 or the indicator. I've looked at the code, and it seems fine. If your intention is to simply discard the the histogram information and turn the indicator into something like the top row of the matrix, try this one, instead. The defaults here are the same as the top row of the Genesis Matrix. You can change the inputs as you were doing, but you won't need to change the display to a fixed minimum or maximum value. --Cody

--- 帖子 #2859 ---
You need to reset the buffers that have already been used. Ex: Inserted Code if (tvi_sig&gt;=0) { Buffer1[i]=tvi_sig; Buffer2[i]=EMPTY_VALUE; } else { Buffer1[i]=EMPTY_VALUE; Buffer2[i]=tvi_sig; }

--- 帖子 #2911 ---
This is the way I see it: it would be foolish to think that data will always be kept secret until its release time and sometimes it's bound to ... ahem ... leak in advance. But also think about all the trading/investment companies that spend huge amount of money on research: they will have their own data and I'm sure that more often than not their estimate will be similar to the data being released. So what do they do: they can't telegraph their knowledge and move the market too much in advance so they will slowly accumulate a position over time (overnight) but very often the basic PA leading to the data release will be misleading (last night was a good example: since 3am UK time we have been making lower highs and lower lows giving a 'start of a downtrend?' look to the casual/untrained eye). A decent set of short-time indicators might reveal the 'true' picture and be placed the 'right' way come data release time; of course it doesn't always work like that but a nice and fruitfull exercise is to keep track of how your own indicators were placed before major data release and look back on it week after week, month after month and see if you get a pattern. If you do, that's an extra valuable edge in your trading arsenal.

--- 帖子 #2992 ---
If the M15 Stox stays stubornly OB, you will see an obvious uptrend on your chart and then you will look for the M5 stox to go back down in OS territory (yellow arrows) and then look for a new M5 Genesis long signal with the M5 stox still in a decent position to re-enter (yellow vertical lines). But care is need because the more powerful M15 stox being in OB condition could dictate the next proper move in the opposite condition. So pick these carefully: the best ones will be if you can hide your stoploss not too far below to still give you a good R/R ratio (yellow horizontal lines). Also on 1st page link ( Stochastic Indicator (more info) : http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...20#post5883620 Oli

--- 帖子 #2997 ---
Hey Bugs, good to see you back. You're right, this was a fine short entry with nice double/treble top/rejection of R1. SL would have been about 25 pips but that's maybe too much for some? This is what I would have looked for before I entered: .the 2-3 support bounces before entry were around 2537 giving you only 10 pips before a possible bounce &amp; the previous ones weren't far away either (2526/2528) so keep that in mind (there might only be 10/20 pips in it). .happy with that and a 25 pips SL? Then you enter and now you need to nurture that trade and look for signs that the 10/20 pips might be all you gonna get (the DP is a long way away at 2499). A) M5 stox was already quite low when you entered and within a few candles it was OS ---&gt; be careful and keep a close eye on the trade. B) The first sign of trouble was the positive stochastic divergence at (1) Price made a new low but the stox was already rising a bit (even if the stox had stayed flat and not risen, that would still have been a positive divergence) ---&gt; be more careful C) Then you had a 2nd positive stox divergence at (2) (price stayed flat but the stox was already rising ---&gt; by now alarm bells might start ringing, so either take your 10 pips or at least put your SL at B/E. Last but not least, with one broker I got my entry signal at the same time as you (late), but with another one (Alpari UK) I got it a few candles earlier (where the yellow vertical line is). Food for thought, although on this occasion it didn't make any difference as the entry price would have been very similar. Oli

--- 帖子 #3010 ---
Hi Arctic, We now know that Bugs' trade was a 'failed' trade. I'm a great believer that winning trades make you concentrate more on your growing bank account (we're only human after all) rather than the reasons why the trade was successful. Using failed trades to improve your trading and your understanding of Genesis shortfalls (indicators can't do everything for you) is as important if not more.... Look at Bugs chart and the area in blue before the reversal happened (1): with normal candlesticks you can't really deduct too much regarding PA and if anything it's looking progressively more bearish especially with the last candle. Now look at the same area with HA candles (2): you have 4 dojis one after the other and as we know dojis represent at least indecision in the market (some say it's the first sign of reversal) because the market goes one way, then the other and finally we end up where we started (the HA candles have no or very little body). Now, you add this to the warnings I expressed in a previous post because of the 2 positive stochastic divergences and you have at least a case for tightening your SL (possibly to B/E). I have to declare that I'm not the biggest fan of HA candles (I even prefer bars to candlesticks as they show better the overall structure of a market - candlesticks can be 'distracting') but HA have been put in the Genesis system after careful thoughts and lengthy testing and not because people wanted to make it more complicated for non HA lovers, so I use them with this strategy. The Heiken Ashi Basics file comes from the PDF part of a different strategy but I've only kept the HA bits so as not to introduce yet more new stuff... Oli.

--- 帖子 #3040 ---
Another reason to spend time @Genesis: there's more smart ladies in here than on other threads Another quick word (bet it won't be quick by the time I've finished typing) on standard Stochastic: if you set the '%D Period' to 1 (rather than Genesis 3) it does not change the curve of the Stox at all, all it does is hide the dashed (Signal) --- line behind the Main line and it will show as (11,1,3) on a chart (the same effect is achieved by selecting 'none' for the colour of the Signal line). I know that it's not standard Genesis but I've seen a few people using it like that too: + cleaner stox window with less lines + keeping only the Main line gives a smoother stox curve +/- it tends to get into OB/OS a bit later (can be good or bad) - you lose the info about the crossing of the Main &amp; the Signal line

Hi, and welcome on board. As you have some trading experience (equities) I think you will pick this up without a lot of difficulty. Big E was/is a nice guy and his thread was great......it got a bit cloudy when Big E got sick, but early on it was really good. As Olivia said, going through the Symphonie System will just confuse you. It's inherent problem is the repainting of indicators, and scattered TA and predictions by various people that detract from the system. Some basic TA is good, but when it becomes predictions I get very upset because for every prediction that says the PA *will* go up, I'll produce another that says the reverse. The reality is is that *no one* knows where the PA is going next, which is why the professional analysts cover their bases by giving a myriad of reasons as to why the EU (for example) will go up to 'x' level, but, if the 'y' level below gets broken then the 'z' level below becomes a reality. It's all bullshit.......no one knows where the PA is going!! So, what we needed was a robust and reliable system that reacts as early as possible to the markets movements reliably, without cause us too much whipsaw (or choppy-ness). The team has come up with the system and Genesis is it!! For other reading material, I see you have done the babypips school and read High Probability trading.......that's all I have done too. I read another book that is now a downloadable PDF (free) and it is about the mental state, the emotional side of things. I can't for the life of me remember it's name but it will come to me and I'll find the PDF and post it. Many people have read it and speak highly of it.......I didn't like it at all, but many do. I don't believe in reading too many other threads. In my time I have found that it is best to choose a thread/system and completely immerse yourself in that thread/system to get the best out of it. I see a lot of thread jumpers, and I was one of them, but it doesn't work. When you find something that you think suits you, immerse yourself in it and learn every tiny thing you can about it if you want to get good at it. It's like learning another language.....the best way to do is to go to that country and be totally immersed in it......the learning curve is so much quicker. Hi RJ and team please allow me to share just a little bit of my trading experience to a newer bee than me newbie.Before forex I have traded stock intraday for almost 10yrs quite profitably and I watch the price and volume only without any chart or indicator.Move on to forex almost four years ago due to its 24hrs trading. Volume in forex differ from one broker to the other so its very hard for me to gauge the bull/bear strength initially.BUT I found out the next best thing to gauge the bull/bear strength is by watching the price and indicator divergence/convergence.For those who forget there is a BID/ASK and DONE/Executed of price. Divergence between price and indicator happen because in a downtrend more of the price is DONE at ASK price rather than BID price,vice versa for uptrend.It shows the weakening of the bear and that more buyer is willing to buy at ASK price.That is why you see price keep on falling but the indicator keep rising.It does not mean price will change direction immediately .IT may move sideway or continue down once bear find renewed strength.SO how to trade this set up profitably?There are many ways some example are price nearing pivot,support/resistance or already hit its daily range will increase your chances of a winning trade.The more confluence the better.AND divergence will almost always happen near the swing high/low ,so if it turn out to be winner your r/r will be very good.It can also be use to exit trade. As for me I prefer the M5/15 time frame cause the impact is almost immediate and the stop can be as low as 7pips including spread.You will have 50/75% success rate initially trading this set up alone. But with lots of practice you can hit 85/90% success rate. Since we now trade Genesis, we can wait for the signal to enter once divergence is spotted.Its much safer and to keep you more discipline in following system rule. To all newbie including myself,you only need to master one or two set up to make pips/$ daily. Do not try to add more indicator ,moon wave ,microwave etc..to complicate yourself.This system has been tested for 1yrs before releasing to the general public. Thanks to RJ and team for sharing this great system for free for all of us to profit from it.

--- 帖子 #3133 ---
Hi Hubby, I agree with you that looking for price/indicator divergences before an entry is very important on the M5 TF where we don't have the luxury of a bigger SL. Regarding Volume in MT4 this is what I believe is true but if someone knows otherwise, feel free to correct me: .the 'volume' indicator doesn't really show volume at all and it should be at least renamed to something else. . it only tells you how many times the price has changed in your current bar and that's why: 1) when you look at a M1 chart you can see on occasions a very big difference on the 'volume' level between one broker and another (for this reason, 'better' brokers that report even the smallest of tick moves are likely to show higher 'volume' than the others). 2) you can't rely on it much because a 5 pip/tick move in a low liquidity period like the Asian session will be treated in the same way as a 5 pip/tick move during the Europe session. In other words, during Asia you can move EurUsd by 5 pips with x amount of € or $ but you will need many more € or $ to move it by the same amount during the Europe session. So in a nutshell, the 'volume' indicator in MT4 doesn't tell you at all how many € &amp; $ have actually changed hands on each candle. Some people are happy with the 'approximation' but as Genesis doesn't require it, you might as well not cloud your judgement with it.

I notice a lot of confusion and errors going on lately regarding market open times, and frankly, I am amazed that people are getting wrong because it's just so simple to get it right. There is a session open and close time indicator posted by ForexFactory on the home page!!!!! All you have to do is make sure that the clock at the top of this page matches you local time, and then the session times provided by ForexFactory will be accurate. Then, download the Market Open Times indi posted on Post #1 of our thread, and adjust it until it matches the FF session times. Then you will have the session times marked on your chart. Not rocket science is it? You have to check the settings when daylight saving times come and go of course.......but hopefully people will be able to figure that one out without too much difficulty

--- 帖子 #3332 ---
Here is an updated version of the MTF arrow, the source of which was provided by futurespeter. This version adds some features listed below, and also corrects a bug that would cause the MTF arrow to draw incorrectly when first attached, under some circumstances. The following changes have been made and are available from the Inputs tab when you attach the indicator: 1. externs UpArrow and DnArrow The symbols displayed for the up and down arrows Changed the Default from 108 (solid circle) to 233/234 (small solid arrows) Pick anything sensible you like out of the WingDings character set. 2. extern ArrowSize to change the size of the displayed arrow Default is 0 Too large a value and the arrows overlap 3. extern TimeFrame.Period to match the Genesis extern name; 0 = current Period(), can assume any valid number of minutes for a chart period Leave as 0 to use TimeFrame.Auto 4. extern TimeFrame.Auto Behaves like GenesisMatrix to auto select the period for the mtf arrow Automatically adjusts the higher time frame when you flip periods on the chart Valid input: 0, 1, 2 Default of 1 to automatically select the next higher time frame; ( although M15 and M30 both -&gt; H1) Set to 0 to manually define the period with TimeFrame.Period, above. (Which will prevent an adjustment when you flip chart periods) Set to 2 to automatically select the second highest time frame 5. extern SoundAlarm Changed default to false This indicator uses the arrow indicator found in the Page 1 zip file. Both of these indicators must be present in your MT4 experts\indicators folder for it to work.

--- 帖子 #3449 ---
To add to this, IMO one of the best things you can do is take a screenshot of every single entry you take. In my case, I take one of the m5 chart alongside the h1 chart so I have some context when I look back. Then on weekends I sort them into two folders - winning trades and losing trades. The power of sitting there scrolling through your own winning trade after winning trade or losing trade after losing trade and being able to pick out common elements is something I've found quite handy in identifying my trouble areas. Of course, there will always be some that should've been winners but became losers and vice versa - but in general, I've found it very handy in identifying any common elements in my good and bad entries. May help anyone who is still trying to figure out where they're going wrong.

--- 帖子 #3514 ---
You've answered your own question. Three of the four indicators of Symphonie repaint closed bars. The second row occasionally, the bottom two rows, frequently. The bottom 3 rows of Genesis are driven by different indicators that give very similar signals to the Symphonie indicators, after they repaint, but none of the indicators in Genesis repaint. The confidence in knowing that an entry signal of closed bars is not going to suddenly reverse itself at some point in the next 5 bars is significant.

--- 帖子 #3515 ---
There has been a couple of questions lately about 'repainting'....and both Cody and I have said that the Genesis Matrix does not, an can not repaint. For those that are too tired to read Post #1, I'll paste the pertinent part here for you: " Genesis matrix, where all 4 indicators do not repaint once the current candle has closed " And for those who might wish to argue the point, be sure to understand that until the current candle is closed *nothing* is painted permanently......not even the candle itself!!!

--- 帖子 #3521 ---
Yes, that's more or less what I do when the PA obliges. When the PA gets to a S/R line (could be a pivot, round number or whatever), I manually bring my SL up to a decent profit area, hopefully allowing enough room for a small pullback to re-align Matrix etc. If a new signal (or a re-entry signal as I like to describe it) spawns, then I will scale in a new trade. As that new trade moves into a respectable profit, I will bring it's SL up to +1, and I will also bring the first SL up to the same level. It doesn't always work out as planned, but it often does and then it pays handsomely!! Of course, a decent trend helps!!

--- 帖子 #3556 ---
I don't really have a hard rule about that, it depends on the behaviour of the PA. On my EA trade, it took about 2 hours to gain 17 pips so to, I deduced that it was going to be a long hard slog to gain a decent profit, so I set the SL to BE at about that level, or slightly less, and I'm happy for it to get hit if need be. When we have a decent trend, I might move to BE at (say +25). It all depends on how the PA behaves. As a guide, if the PA is quite choppy, then moving to BE early will see it get hit, so you may need to allow the PA more 'breathing space'. On a strong trend when the PA doesn't really pullback, you can perhaps shift to BE a bit earlier. It's a judgement call so I can't really be more specific than that.

--- 帖子 #3578 ---
Hi daujones, A few things: 1) the M1 Stox was completely OS on the first 2 sell signals (2 &amp; 3) and it had already gone to OB territory for the long trade 5 (it had already risen ). 2) if you're trading the M1 charts you should at least have the M5 Stox (blue line roughly) on your charts too (in the same way that we have the M15 Stox on our M5 charts), to give you an idea of what the higher TF is doing. This would also have stopped you from entering the long trade 4 as the M5 Stox was well OB 3) The long trade 1 was the best as it had M1 and M5 stox both going up from recently OS territory 4) Similarly trade 6 was looking good as both M1 and M5 were falling from OB territory but this trade didn't work out. Why? One reason could be that thoughout your chart, the M15 Stox was constantly rising (green line), favouring the higher probability Long trades.... Moral of all this: always keep an eye on what the higher TFs are doing and this is even more important if you are trading the M1 TF that is notoriously noisy and prone to false/bad signals. Oli

--- 帖子 #3645 ---
What you need to understand is that Stochastic is more than a 'yes or no', indicator, which are the only two options available to the matrix. Given that this is the case, the line would have to be drawn as to where to make the matrix change colour.......for oversold conditions it could be on the 20 line.....what about 18?....what about 10?.....what about 2?. Then we have the same problem with the overbought postions. Where are you going to draw the line? What if the stoch doesn't reach the line? Even if all the above cold be sorted, how would we use the matrix to show divergence? Clearly it would be impossible. The idea is not new, and Cody is already way ahead of you on this. I think your chart won't mind giving up a bit of space for the stochastic......people have been doing it for 60 years, I think you'll get used to it!!!

--- 帖子 #3651 ---
I thought I posted this, but it seems I didn't. This is the #MTF Stochastic with the following changes: Added extern NextHigherAuto; if the TimeFrame extern is 0 (current period) NextHigherAuto will automatically set the indicator to the next higher time frame. This is useful if you flip timeframes. The MTF stoch will adjust automatically If TimeFrame has a value other than 0 that matches the number of minutes of a valid MT4 chart, NextHigherAuto will set the indicator to the next higher time frame from that. This will not adjust if you flip timeframes, but can be useful if you want something besides the immediate next higher time frame's stoch to be displayed. Added externs HidePctK and HidePctD; these will control which of the stoch lines are displayed. The default value is false for both, so both lines are displayed. Place this file in the experts\indicators folder of MT4, and restart MT4. As before, to create a Stochastic window on your chart that displays your current time frame and the higher timeframe's stochastic, drag the MT4 stochastic from the Indicators branch of the Navigator onto your chart, then drag this indicator from the Custom Indicators branch of the Navigator on top of the Stochastic window.

--- 帖子 #3674 ---
The stochastic wallabie is just 3 timeframe stochastics overlaying each other, then a line is created which is the average of those 3 timeframes. All indicators that take into account a higher timeframe will change all the while the candle of the higher timeframe is still open. From what I can tell from the video that comes with it, they are mainly looking for divergence with it.

--- 帖子 #3713 ---
When you enter a trade from a good signal here.....and there's at least one every day....when the trade get's to +15 or +20, bring your SL up to +1 (plus the spread).....now the trade is free.....the risk is removed and you can manually trail the trade (but not too close) as it makes it's way to your target. As long as your trade is protected by a SL at +1, then there is no reason to exit it until it gets to your target or knocks you out for +1. Either way, you lost nothing.

Hey Matrix, When using M5 and M15 Stox, I always first look to see what the M15 is doing and I will wait until it has gone into OS/OB territory and is joined in the same area by the M5 Stox (the 4 yellow circles). The trades (my comments are based on your chart and on all the indicators that you are using): 1) M5 and M15 Stox rising from OS + Genesis Long signal + bounce off S2 + M15 Matrix already has 1 blue dot (you know that the M15 TVI would have been blue then because it was the 3rd blue already : 3 x M5 = 1 x M15). All good + small SL (&lt; 20 pips) -----&gt; Take the trade. 2) M15 coming down from OB, M5 doing the same, PA rejection of WeeklyPivot (WP), Genesis short signal... so all good to take a short? Yes &amp; No as there are a few close-by 'issues' and this is where you have to weight the + against the - and make a decision: .the 60 SMA providing support? .S1 that was twice resistance could now be support (green arrows) .the M15 matrix is still ALL BLUE (X) 3) I wouldn't have taken this trade for 3 reasons although it turned out to be another really good one: .M15 Stox still in OB territory . M5 Stox very close to OB and did not go into OS territory again beforehand .WP that got rejected earlier was only a few pips away. I hope that helps.

You shouldn't get angry and bad trades are not always mistakes: even with a really good setup your SL can get hit before the market turns your way (that is just the way trading is). Trade 3 was one of those examples: it had a lot going for it and all the reasons that you mentioned in favour of the long trade were valid. At that point the market presented every traders with the same question: is EU about to turn back down and shall I take the next short signal, or will the next long Genesis signal be a good opportunity to re-enter the newly-formed long trend? In that situation, when M15 Stox is staying OB (showing long strength), I like to see the M5 Stox resets itself &amp; go all the way down to OS territory first before I consider a Long re-entry. On this occasion, M5 Stox didn't go OS so I did not enter but this post about RJ's long EA trade is a very good example of what I look for for a re-entry continuation trade (the M5 Stox is in blue, M15 is yellow &amp; M30 is orange) http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...43#post5980543

--- 帖子 #3738 ---
maybe this will help: 1. beginning of day, look at CSM to choose pairs to play. if you don't want to then just open EU and EJ since they have the cheapest spreads . (planning your entry) 2. look at the fxpivots: wide = high probability of range bound = activate scardie cat mode narrower or pivots much closer together (than yesterday, especially the day before) = high probability to trend; breaking 3 pivot prices in 1 go = activate patient mode (planning your exit) exception: today we have EU interest rate announcement and the fxpivots are wider than yesterday's. TP: pivot prices SL: swing high/low emergency exit strategy 1: SMA60 cross , and if you want to wait for M5 bar to close below/above SMA60 that is opposite your position. that's right, oli! i use it as filter for entries because PA bounces off of it. if it breaks it then the direction has changed. if it chops through it then PA is ranging. plus it provides support/resistance for re-entry positions. emergency exit strategy 2 (SL / trailing stop loss): M15 opposite arrow comes sooner than your swing high/low. which actually makes SL a lot more affordable. (without filtering pairs to use) there were 3 consecutive days in April and May that SL's were hit simultaneously in EU and EJ. those were heavily ranging days like monday's 25 ATR for EU. however, the losses were less than 30pips total per day. often SL is between 9-19 pips including regular spread. 30 pips is 3% of your running balance if you expose 1% per trade. therefore, you don't exit prematurely or let your losses run loosely (assuming you are trading with the trend).

--- 帖子 #3748 ---
Dee50, The Detrended Price Oscillator explanation of the arrow is the easiest to understand. There is one discussion of it here , and another description here . In general terms, the arrow is a good signal for a pending change in trend. Genesis usually signals 1-2 bars earlier, which is why if the arrow doesn't appear, it may be cause for watching a trade more carefully. Trades can be taken regardless of whether an arrow appears at the same time as the Genesis signal. In my mind, there is more confidence if the arrow is there at the same time, but that won't stop me from taking an entry. Hope this helps. --Cody

--- 帖子 #3862 ---
The most common reason for your computer hanging is that you are missing some of the indicators needed to drive the matrix. Please check the troubleshooting link on the first page to see if that helps. Use a fresh download of the zip on page one and only use those files. Also, check that you have fewer than 300 ex4 files in your experts\indicators folder. And that you have the latest build of MT4 (432 or higher) running on your machine. If that doesn't help, please post a screen shot if you can. --Cody

--- 帖子 #3863 ---
Try this one, james. This is a simultaneous display of the arrow on multiple time frames, in a format that matches the primary Genesis Matrix. The two most important inputs are: HTF_ARR.Period and HTF_ARR.Auto. The higher time frame will auto-select the next higher time frame if you set HTF_ARR.Period=0 and HTF_ARR.Auto=1. This is useful when you flip time frames, because the time frames of the arrow matrix rows will auto-adjust. You can also fix the second row to a specific time frame by entering a valid minutes of an MT4 chart in HTF_ARR.Period. The second row will not adjust when you flip time frames, in that case. Place both indicators in your MT4 experts\indicators folder and restart MT4. -Cody

--- 帖子 #3978 ---
And my M15 Arrows are the same as RJ....it's all down to the broker and very often the datafeed doesn't need to be that different for discrepancies to appear. Bear in mind that any indicator is simply a mathematical formula attached to the movement of price (open/high/low/close) and then 'translated' to an easy to understand graphical way (the colourful Arrows for example). A broker having a candle Close at say 1.2780 will return a slightly different 'indicator' value than one having a Close at 1.2781: and if that value is close to the level where the indicator turns from green (50.0001) to red (49.9999), one broker will have the arrows but another one will only have it one candle later, or even not at all (if the price reverse sharply). And this is not really about good &amp; bad brokers because sometimes a split second can make all the difference: if the last tick is at 13.34.59.9s, with one broker it will register on the 13.30 candle and with another it will register on the 13.35 candle (both candles will have a different Close and a different Open ---&gt; different indicator value ---&gt; Arrow appears/doesn't appear. PS: this wasn't addressed to you Cody (despite the quote), cuz I know that as a programer you're well aware of the price/indicator relationship

--- 帖子 #4018 ---
The ruling was a positive one for the Euro. However, the general sentiment in the market was that the GCC will rule in favor of the ESM so therefore most of the result was already priced (60-80%) and that's why the Euro didn't move a great deal other than those volatility swings during the broadcasting. The recent rally was to price in the ESM ruling as well as aspirations that the Fed will announce QE3 tomorrow. Even if they do announce QE3 tomorrow I'm sure the the USD denominated currencies will move a decent amount against the USD, however, if QE3 is rejected tomorrow expect the USD denominated currencies to drop like crazy as most of the longs over the last week will start to take profit and the USD long interest will increase in the market. Today's PA after the ESM ruling is a very good example in being very careful when trading news or such events. You have to try to understand to what degree the market has priced in a particular expected result leading up to the actual event. I've noticed even when trading things like NFP if the number is only off by a very small amount the pair does not exude a lot of volatility. Ex. last weeks NFP number was off the expected number by a pretty good chunk and that's why the rallies on that day were quite sizable. Just something I've noticed and learned a long the way.

--- 帖子 #4019 ---

QE3 has been hovering around the market for a long time, but the threat of a downgrade had an immediate impact.......and then, the pricing in of the German court decision, as you said, accounts for the rest of the movement. The eur/usd rally has been spectacular from the 1.22's, but it is quite overbought on all charts up to (and including) the Daily. As we know, this can remain overbought for a long time, but it's just worth keeping in the back of your mind.

--- 帖子 #4022 ---
Just thought I'd share a train of thought with some who are new to trading this system. One thing we have to know is that this system is designed to recognize momentum and give signals based on that. For us small traders trying to trade in markets dominated by highly capitalized institutional traders, the only thing we can really try to do in order to be successful is to try catching the momentum that is created by the smart money in the market. Many of the senior traders here mention time after time that it is a very good idea to trade with the dominating trend for the day etc. It's usually never a good idea to try catching a market turn or top or bottom. Genesis gives you signals most of the time when the market has moved into a particular direction, that means momentum is flowing that way. Combining that with the properly aligned Stochastics and you get very high prob. trades.

It's like when you see a car coming down the road and you want to cross in front of it because it is indicating that it will turn left before it gets to you. Do you accept the indication and just cross right in front of the car?......of course not.....you wait for confirmation that the car is going to turn before you step off the curb......the indicator might have been on by mistake or never cancelled from a previous turn. Either way, it's not worth risking you life on!! Since Frankfurt open I have entered no trades. --- 帖子 #4076 ---
Hey Pattie, It's a lot harder now than it was a few years ago to get into FX trading because the volatility (= the amount of pips available) just isn't there at the moment so take comfort in that. At least as far as EU is concerned (but this applies to many other FX pairs), it has been a lot more difficult recently (&amp; certainly since the start of 2012) to get pips out of the markets. This is a EU chart showing the range of pips that we get on a Weekly basis (from High to Low): as you can see we have been for the last few months near the very low of the range with Weekly candles barely larger than 155 pips (bottom line) which is ...erm...nothing really and it's very hard to get good trending move. The top of that range (middle line) is around 630 pips and 90% of EU Weekly candles fall between these 2 numbers and as you can imagine you'll get a lot more pips per trade in a week when the movement is that high. Will we ever see the highs of 2008 when we had Weekly candles well above 1000 pips, with 1 week topping out at 1350 pips! It's a shame that Genesis wasn't around in those days, but hopefully these days will return soon...

TF M15 (you get to avoid those wide spreads ) 2. the M15 genesis signal must spawn on the M15 candle at news time or right after the HIN. 3. TP pivot price or round number that is bearing sentiment. mr krugger ( http://www.jkonfx.com/ ) always gets the sentiment price correct, but not when to enter (sorry jon. anyway, you look like prince william ) of course if TP is not met, exit when PA signals an exit when does one enter? on a compelling HIN + genesis signal. compelling = interest rate, NFP, FOMC, speeches by central bank heads, large buying/selling of a large private/public entity, china news... 4. SL on the bottom (for long positions)/ top (for short positions) of the M15 candle that spawned the news or a proximic pivot price where price is expected to bounce off in the event that top/bottom is too expensive. i have many screenshots of such trades, but these ones are of recent memory and you can still feel the joy/frustration as you watched the price whipsaw like hell. and you can differentiate why on one trade a pivot price was used as TP and round number on the other. on regular HIN, like GDP, unemployment, CPI, trade balance/deficit, ISM, etc. ..... --- 帖子 #4139 ---
Last night I had a friend call around who is also a trader, but his learning curve is a little behind mine so he came for some help. I could see what the problem was, and I have been guilty of it myself in the past, and still do fall into the trap occasionally if I don't remind myself. I expect that that most people have done this: They see the market open at Frankfurt and they watch the candles take off in a direction. They think, "Ok, if this continues I will enter here." Then a couple of strong candles in the same direction form and the trader thinks, "hmm....that push was pretty strong, perhaps it's a fake out. I won't enter yet, but I'll wait to see if this is confirmed with a further push, then I will enter." There is a further push, but it's a bit stronger than the trader expected and the move has now gone 45 pips. The trader now thinks, "shit....perhaps the move is almost over and anyway, London is nearly online and I have seen these Frankie moves reversed by London, so perhaps I'd better stay out. But the PA continues. London comes and the PA continues. Our trader thinks, "ok....alright....if London confirms this, I will definitely enter." The PA continues quite strongly. Trader thinks, "shit.....now the move is 75 pips.....perhaps I'd better not enter now as the move must be getting exhausted." The PA continues and finally the trader enters. 12 pips later the move finally pulls back and stops our trader out, and he/she is real pissed off. What's worse, is that when our trader looks at the indicators right from the start of the move, the entry was so obvious that he is now totally pissed off and in a bad mood so no more trades are take today!! Sound familiar???? So, last night, after discussing this at length with my friend I chose a random currency pair that I do not trade or even look at. Then I deleted all the candles, all the arrows and the 5ema. The candle window was completely black....nothing.....nada. Then, I scrolled back in history and chose 2 consecutive days, and we traded with just the Genesis Matrix and the Stochastics. When there was an entry, I put out red vertical line and the same for the exit. At the end of our 2 days trading.....trading only the recommended hours....I turned the candles back on and we went through the trades. The results were: 5 trades entered 4 trades won 1 trade lost The lost trade was -5 and the 4 winners totaled 45 pips. So, just using the Stochastics and Genesis we made a profit. The exits could have been better had we seen the candles, but that's not the point......the point is that we could turn a profit without even seeing the candles, arrows or 5ema. The analogy is this: As a pilot can fly by looking out the window (VFR), he can also fly by never looking out the window but looking at the instruments (indicators) instead (IFR). When it is a dark and stormy night and visibility is poor and there are crosswinds and windshear present as the pilot makes his landing approach, he will be flying IFR and will be using the aircrafts and the airports signals to effect a pin-point accurate and safe landing (ILS). IFR flights and ILS landings happen all the time. In fact it is the safest and preferred way to fly. Looking out the window sends false signals to the pilots brain, especially when flying in cloud and many crashes have occurred in this way. Our pilots have been trained to use and believe in the instruments because they don't lie. Our pilots all over the world do this every day and keep us safe. So, what I just proved to my friend, was that by getting mesmerised by the watching the candles (VFR) can and does lead to poor decisions at best....and a total disaster at worst. But, but just using the basic instruments (IFR) we could trade (fly) profitably. Now I'm not suggesting to delete the candles etc as I did, but what I am saying is that we need to watch the indicators and have faith in them FIRST......and seek additional information from the candles, arrow, 5ema. All I used was the Genesis Matrix and the stoch......the with IFR, we made a profit. My friends VFR made a loss. Guess what is stuck on a sticky to the top of his monitor now?...yep.....a reminder to fly IFR!!!! So to finish, there is no need to add a zillion other indicators to the charts as I keep saying. They won't help you, all they will do is create more things to check and cause doubt, especially in the case of repainting indicators. By adding all this crap to the charts you are just showing that you have little understanding of the system, and so you create a mongrel system that will fail.....yes it will. Flying IFR with VFR to assist continually and consistently turns a profit.

--- 帖子 #4145 ---
That is so true....The 'problem' with people's perception of Genesis is that its graphical &amp; visual simplicity hides the complexity behind it. I'm sure that most people look at the matrix and count it as 1 indicator (4 dots either blue or red - easy) when in fact it is none of that. If I'm correct, bar the CCI line, the 3 other matrix lines (TVI/GHL/T3) are 'made' of at least 2 indicators (if not more) running in the background. So at a stroke you already have a minimum of 7 'decision makers', add the Stox (5 &amp; 15) + the Yellow MA + the Arrow &amp; the odd Pivot line &amp; you are talking about at least 12 different indicators all needing to be pointing in the same direction to give you valid signal. How many more do you really need? But having said that, yes you can add more indicators as extra 'filters' and for sure they will stop you entering some Genesis bad trades but the flipside of that is they will also keep you out &amp; make you miss some good trades. It's a balancing act and I decide to include something extra in my trading only by doing a lot of backtesting and this is my method: .on the M5 TF I will mark down on my chart all the Genesis trades for a minimum of 1 month. .for each of these trades I will write down what my Potential New Filter (PNF) was telling me and you have 4 possible scenarios: 1) PNF agrees with a Genesis good trade: that will be marked as +0 (the PNF didn't add anything). 2) PNF agrees with a Genesis bad trade &amp; that trade would have been a 20 pips loss: that will be marked also as +0 (the PNF didn't add anything). 3) PNF disagrees with a Genesis good trade and it would have stopped me from entering a good/valid trade: if that trade 'showed' me a 'realistic' 30 pips, I mark this as -30. 4) PNF disagrees with a Genesis bad trade and that trade would have been a 20 pips loss: that will become +20 (the PNF stopped me from entering a bad trade). I then add it all up and if: .it is a negative (-) total or very close to zero then the PNF gets discarded as it hasn't added anything of value: it's only taking some of my attention away from the other stuff. .it is a big positive number &amp; I will include it in my forward live trading for a month and see if the backtesting results match the live difference in outcome. It's only then that I decide to keep it or not. So if you have anything 'new' to add to Genesis' core rules and you have done some proper (and I really mean proper lol) backtesting to backup your claims then I'll happily listen. If not, I think RJ will show you the door lol

--- 帖子 #4155 ---
If I could add a little more perspective on RJ's comments. As a broad generisation, the vast majority of experienced traders I have met over the years, virtually all have echoed RJ's perspective on trading, it is all about : - PA (Trend) - S&amp;R - Momentum Or as Corey Rosenbloom wrote in his book "The Trading Course: Technical Analysis, High-Probability Set Ups, and Execution Tactics", Trading is as simple as pick a timeframe, you are comfortable trading, assess the trend, then take the next timeframe down from that, then wait for pullbacks, and trade with the higher TF trend. Inexperienced traders spend huge amounts of time searching for another indicator that is going to give them that perfect system "the holy grail". My issue is experienced traders have huge amounts of chart time, that enables them analyse markets with clarity that allows them to make clear trading decisions. Inexperienced traders, feel they need to add another indicator to confirm what their other indicators say, which leads to confusion, delay in making decisions, and the consequence of possibly (or probably in my case) missing the trade.

--- 帖子 #4236 ---
In a decent trend, that is often the case. If you had exited the trade, then that gives you a chance to re-enter. Or, if you had your SL in profit and you didn't exit, you can now scale in another trade in the same direction. With a good trend, this can be done several times and really do some damage to the broker. We spoke about this not too long ago and it's a great way to maximise the profit from any given move. It's not quite that easy if the market is not trending though

--- 帖子 #4264 ---
There's a tendency on demo accounts to let trades run because it's not gonna cost you anything if it goes against you... This is not addressed at you personaly Sify but to anyone on demo: I know it's not 100% possible but try to treat your entries &amp; exits with the same care that you would on a live account. And also, as important, get used to closing trades for +10-15 pips at the time when the opportunities present themselves: .if the trade carries on your way it still doesn't cost you anything apart from less demo-profit. .it's a great exercise in discipline that will be invaluable when you switch to live account (otherwise, if you're not mentally prepared for taking 10-15 pips, your brain (greed) will want you to hold on for a bit longer " because you might get another 5 pips out of that" and then the market retraces and it's either +0 @ B/E or even a loss).

Does anyone use 'shared pivots' where EU responds to EJ pivots and vice versa. Today, for example : 1: only EJ hit the resistance but both started falling. 2: EU was bouncing off S1 for 2 hours but both responded the same way. 3: EJ bounced off S1 and this stopped EU's fall. 4: EJ's drop was stopped when EU hit S2 Yesterday's movements for both pairs were bounded by EU's daily pivot at the bottom and EJ's R1 above. There are examples of this almost every day and they can be used as targets, entries or warnings in the same way as normal pivots. They may help to shed light on some otherwise unstructured trading days. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hi Oli Thanks for the reply. Pivots often agree very closely between pairs but when pivots are wide (large range on previous day) I often see this shared pivot effect. They occur because high activity on one pair tends to drag the others. What is certain is that there is more logic behind pivot-sharing than, say, Camarilla's which simply divide the previous days range into 9 mathmatical zones which are closer together near the pivots. Any pivot system will work provided enough people use it, but most people use standard pivots. As I type this both EU and EJ's falls have been interrupted by AU's S1 level.

hello to everyone im new to this thread but i like it and i want to try it.I have a question about the moving average.Can someone explain what does the shift 2 stand for?.Thank you

--- 帖子 #4399 ---
The moving average line is plotted on the chart 2 intervals to the right of the actual time for which it was calculated. If you go to the most recent bar on your chart, you'll see that the EMA5 is shifted 2 bars to the right of that. The most famous indicator that uses shifted plots is probably Bill William's Alligator.

--- 帖子 #4400 ---
In the settings for a moving average you can set the shift, setting it at 2 will shift the moving average forward 2 candles, the primary reason for shifting it is in order to become try to become a leading indicator.
