I am not typing much here. But I will try explain a trade I took friday. I will also try tell why I did it. Its all about how to read a chart. I use the 1 hour timeframe to give me the bigger picture, and then I trade from 5 mins. Lets start analysing the 1 hour chart. LOOK at 1-2-3 where I have the turquis line. Its all strong RES levels. then all off sudden at 4 price broke out to upside. then from X to A we have an impulse leg. Impulse leg is where structure break. Then look at the area marked 5 and 6. that is first time price went back to "OLD" price level where we saw strong RES. Broken RES will quit often now be support. We also see divergense on all indis in this area, so maybee we have a trade setting up in this area. NOW I go to my 5 mins to see what goes on. Can I find a reason to take a long here.??? I have removed the HA candles just so it is a bit more clear to see. LOOK at where I marked 1 and 2. Here we have Bullish Divergense. Look at the 15 mins MTF stoch. Price go lower but stoch did not go lower. SO now we have regular divergense on higher timeframe (1HOUR) and Bullish divergense on my trading timeframe. --- 帖子 #4459 ---
One option is to split your trades ... Close half your trade at 10 - 15, set BE on the other half, and then let the other half continue ... Has pros and cons ... Pro - there'll be times the remaining half trade gallops away and you make more pips than if you'd fully exited at 10 - 15 Con - there'll be the other times the remaining half hits your b/e and you make less pips than if you'd fully exited at 10 - 15 Only time and experience will tell you whether full exits or 50/50 will make you more pips in the long run - just need to figure out which one would work best for you.

--- 帖子 #4477 ---
If you are using the M15 Stox, you should start 'thinking' about a 'potential' Short once the M15 Stox gets into OB territory (yellow rectangle) and then look for a M5 Genesis short signal (+ good M5 Stox position) later on to corelate your M15 Stox. Important: I am not predicting anything, I'm just putting myself in 'possible' Short alert mode: as we know, price can carry on moving up and the M15 Stox can stay in OB territory for ages. But look at the price movement leading to the yellow rectangle: yes it is up but not by very much (less than 20 pips and it found Resistance at the DP 100.84). Also note that the first short didn't work too well (although you would have still survived with your SL above the highs) but when the 2nd one came we also had a Stox Bearish Divergence (price flat - Stox down) and that gave a great signal (I know, it's outside Genesis trading hours but it's a good example of M5/M15 Stox dance &amp; Divergence) Compare that to the Orange rectangle when the M15 Stox has gone into OS territory: not the same scenario because the price has followed the Stox down by a lot more (60 pips) so you now have a downtrend and that tells you to be more careful about taking an opposite position. In those situations it's generally a good idea to wait for at least a retest/confirmation of those levels first before attempting a Long.

also, keep in mind that the holy grail is trade management (keeping losers small and riding winners). The focus should not be on trying to totally eliminate losing trades because it is impossible to avoid them. You can only learn how to select good trades that have a "pretty good" chance of working out...but the money will be made over time in how you manage each and every trade.

--- 帖子 #4577 ---
Just to clear this up.....my understanding is that instead of using the Matrix at the bottom of your chart, you are using the GMTS-Dash as created and supplied by Xaphod. I am completely fine about this because the Matrix displays it's data according to TVi, CCI, T3 and GHL indicators. In exactly the same way, GMTS-Dash displays the same data sourced from the same indicators, just that it displays it's data in the form of arrows in a box at the top left of the screen, whereas Matrix displays it's data as red and white squares at the bottom of the window. The advantage of using the Matrix is that we get to see the history of the indicators and we get to see the 4 colours lining up as the move deveops..or not! The advantage of using the GMTS-Dash is that at a glance multi timeframes status can be viewed which may give more validity to any move in a lower time frame. The downside, as far as I know, is that the GMTS-Dash can only show the 'here and now' status and the history and the developing move cannot be seen at all. To be honest, I haven't tried the GMTS-Dash, but I'm going to do so now just to make sure that I'm seeing this correctly. Perhaps Xaphod or Cody would like to comment. If you go to the Genesis Tools thread of Xaphod, you will find the GMTS-Dash there and it comes with a great PDF which explains everything. So that's that! The Ichimoku cloud I would ask you to remove please because that indi sets up a bias and is not helpful or necessary to make successful trades with Genesis. As Olivia points out, if you want to trade with it, that's great.....just make sure you don't have it on your charts when you post trades please. Sorry to be so harsh, but there has to be a line in the sand. Thanks for understanding. The Coral I can let slide because it is just a coloured 60 MA which, as you say, Yelena and Minako both use, and I have seen others use. Really it's not necessary and personally I think it is a waste of time, but I will let that one slide......but that is the limit to how far I will let things go. Moving Averages are lagging indicators.....the bigger the number, the bigger the lag. Thats one reason why MA cross systems never work. They look good in a trend, but they will keep you from getting a good entry in ranging markets.....and markets range more than they trend.

--- 帖子 #4657 ---
Wasn't in the yen-cross trades, but this is a good reminder to have stop losses on at all times. Actually, what I do is set an automatic SL of 30pips that is triggered when I enter a trade, and then I adjust it to the last swing high/low +/- 5 pips when I get a moment. I use 30 pips because anything more than that (25 pips to swing H/L + 5 pips buffer), I would not enter a trade. Unless I'm entering more than 1 trade at a time, I would have adjusted the SL within a minute after my entry. Just makes me feel safer, in case a phone call or interruption happens before I get a manual SL in.

--- 帖子 #4659 ---
Here is a true story for you. A while ago a trader placed a fairly sizeable long trade on the UJ pair and didn't set the SL because the phone rang. The phone call was about a huge earthquake that had happened in Japan and because that trader has friends in Japan, he listened to all the details. Then he turned on the TV to see it all live and watch tsunami etc, and then tried phoning friends in Japan. Suddenly he remembered his trade and rushed back to the desk expecting to see a decent profit as the Yen weakened due to the earthquake/tsunami etc......but what he saw was a huge spike down as speculators rushed to buy the Yen as the earthquake/tsunami meant that a lot of money would be repatriated to Japan. The loss to that trader was in excess of $6k!! The moral of the story is to set your SL and forget about everything else.....even if the house is on fire....SET THE SL!!!! Oh and by the way........that trader was me.

--- 帖子 #4683 ---
Sorry for all these posts. I don't mean to bombard, and will be off. Just happen to have a few things I thought I could answer today (relieve burden from the team plus help me learn/reinforce my thoughts as well). I try to look at what PA does in two separate blocks. The busy block (FF open to London close, the period we mostly trade in as the range is usually wider), and also the quiet block (the other times). More frequent than not, the quiet block can retrace the PA of the busy block, setting the market up for more continuation trades. And the quiet block price action can be rejected by the following busy block, unless there is a strong up/down down in the US stock market. Obviously not the case that as often recently. Hope this makes sense. Again, nothing is certain. Just how I try to make sense of things. If of no use, the Genesis team can throw it out (help me also to know if not useful)

Lets put it this way, I would never trade against a strong H1 stoch. I have all my stochs showing %K and %D lines, including the stoch-MTF. I treat them the same as your standard MA-cross strategies. If you trade with H1 &amp; M15 &amp; M5 stochs all crossed in the same direction, with M5 &amp; M15 tape all heading on the same direction, during main trading times, away from major news, you would struggle not to make money. It may get you into moves a little late. But my theory on trading, is you should not try and get the exact pivots right, just aim for the "meat in the middle". I usually get in a little late and get out a little too early. But make money (small bits) regularly. Some talented traders have an inate ability to identify major market turns. That talent has missed me by completely !!

The main reason you get such a sharp/faster move from one of the Stox is that not only is the 'price field' set to 'Close/close'(0) but you have also set the 'MAmethod' to LinearWeightedMA (3) which is even faster than ExponentialMA (it should be set to Simple SMA - 0)

--- 帖子 #4813 ---
Set 'TimeFrame' to 0, set 'NextHigherAuto' to true. That way if you switch time frames whilst looking at your charts, the mtf stock will automatically switch to the next higher time frame. By placing a value other than 0 in the 'TimeFrame' field negates this action.

--- 帖子 #4923 ---
The fact that NY was about to open could also be a con in my book, and in this case it appears to have changed direction right on market open. One recurring theme in this thread is in situations like that to wait for a double bounce before going countertrend ... e.g. if you'd got that signal after a second bounce off of the daily pivot there is more chance it would carry on upwards - as long as all the other signals were in line. Of course, it's never straightforward - there are also times where it bounces once and shoots straight up. But in this case, the PA wasn't looking strong enough to suggest that either - generally if it's going to go straight up it would look very much like a "V" (i.e. sharp slope upwards).

--- 帖子 #4927 ---
At the risk of sounding like a broken record myself, do not take a buy trade if price is making lower highs and lower lows unless there is the presence of divergence or something else strong that says it will turn around, wait until price has made a higher low, you don't have to wait for a higher high, just a higher low. Going the other way, do not take a sell all the while price is making higher lows and higher highs unless divergence, wait for a lower high. This is especially important on the M5 chart. You have got to be working with the trend of the moment or you will lose.

In your screenshot, you have pricefield=1 for the Stoch-MTF.mq4 and pricefield=0 for the #MTF Stochastic v2.1.mq4 . That is why one shows divergence and the other does not.

--- 帖子 #4940 ---
The Stoch-MTF draws the line to the last lower time-frame candle. It gives a more accurate real-time representation. The #MTF Stochastic draws the line to the first lower time-frame candle. It looks better in hindsight . It also gets the crossover wrong.

--- 帖子 #4948 ---
Oli, what is in your opinion the right ratio between psych and tech? ciao wiz

--- 帖子 #4949 ---
There's no answer to that. It really depends on the individual trader, how advanced they are in their trading career and where they are financially at a given time.. It's a ratio that will change as one progresses through trading and dare I say, through life. All things being equal, this ratio will/should gradually increase in tech's favour throughout a trader's journey. That's why 'rules based systems/strategies' (like Genesis) are well suited to remove the emotions out of trading because the decision-making process does not have too many grey areas (unlike fundamental-analysis-trading that can always be viewed from 2 completely opposite angles). Having said all that (lol), many people can still benefit from a good read and take many clues about attitude/discipline/belief... from some of his books, so enjoy!

--- 帖子 #4950 ---
Another comparison, I once read was: You can give an experienced trader an extremely profitable strategy and they can lose money, and you can give a very average/barely profitable system to an experienced trader, and they can make decent profits. I think a major differentiating factor, is experienced traders understand the complexity of the markets, inexperienced traders, are just hoping to find the holy grail of an arrow or a cross on an indi, will give them money. Take for example Yelana's trades about a week ago, trading her correlated pairs, with a stunning trade, then on Friday RJ noted GU was retesting multi-day highs, and with strong stoch divergence, made a very nice trade. How often do we see inexperienced traders post a 5M chart, and ask "why the trade didnt work", or "is this a good entry", only for experinced traders comment, "did you look at the H1 chart..." Re psychology, to me trader psychology, can be translated into an undertstanding of probabilities, and trust in their extensively tested trading system.

--- 帖子 #5015 ---
I don't know if I agree with all of this, but it's not far off the mark. Pasted from: http://newtraderu.com/?p=1823 If you truly are serious about being a trader then there are seven things that you will have to accept. You will have to accept that over the long term at best only 60% of your trades will be winners. It will be much less with some strategies. Accept that the key to being a successful trader is having big wins and small losses, not big bets paying off. Big bets can lead quickly to you being out of the game after a string of losses. Accept that the best traders are also the best risk managers, even the best traders do not have crystal balls so they ALWAYS manage their capital at risk on EVERY trade. If you want to be a better trader then you need to accept that trading smaller and risking less is a key to your success. Risking 1% to 2% of your capital on any single trade is the first step to winning at trading. Use stops and position sizing to limit your losses and get out when your losses grow to these levels. You must accept that you will have 10 trading losses in a row a few times each year. The question is what your account will look like when they happen. You have to accept that you will be wrong, a lot. The sooner you accept you are wrong and change your mind the better off you will be. If you really want to be a trader then you are going to have to accept the fact that trading is not easy money. It is a profession like any other and requires much work and effort and even years to become proficient. Expect to work for free and pay tuition to the markets through losses until you learn to trade consistently and profitably. Trading is about math, ego control, risk management, psychology, focus, perseverance, passion, and dedication. If you are missing one, you may not make it. Trade wisely my friends.

--- 帖子 #5056 ---
Actually, I like the "7 Things Each Trader ... " link RJ posted. Yes, it is opinion, and it is NOT the only thing that matters in trading, but it is hard to find arguments against it being sound concepts to follow. Eg you may not lose 10 in a row, but you better be prepared for it, less hubris leads you to an overly large risk per trade (tail events do happen more frequently than statistics suggest - eg why Black Scholes don't work or read The Black Swan by Nick Taleb). The scientific research "Traders aren't wired like us", on the other hand (taken at face value based on the story, and not the complete research which wasn't made available), is most likely flawed as it uses a sample size of only 28, doesn't discuss over how many years the research was undertaken (people behave differently in bull vs bear markets, financial traders probably behaved differently pre vs post QE, and probably differently since the Greenspan put vs the Volcker era), which nationality the traders were (cultural differences), or even what age/sex they were. Or what type of traders they are (day, swing, position etc), and how they trade. Or whether they are trading with own money or client/firm money, and how they are incentivised (a good year by taking a lot of risk = $$$ for retirement vs a bad year = zero bonus or looking for another job). And all these influence how a trader is 'wired'. And you can't get a good enough representation with a 28 sample size. I'd much rather take the sound advice and opinion of an experienced and successful trader (or a fundamentalist like Buffett), than a piece of research that might be seriously flawed (eg efficient market hypothesis).

What I do is take .gif snapshots of the trade setup as it is unfolding. I also snapshot the higher timeframe charts. Then, I go back and look over each chart with a "fine tooth comb" and try to think up any conceivable filters that may potentially separate the winners from the losers. The vast majority of the time the filters are utterly worthless. However, every now and then I find a "gem" that enables me to take better trades. How do I know that it is a gem? Because it worked on historical trades? Absolutely Not! It is a gem because it works on trades that occur during a forward test.

Hi Iwan, r u using FXI pivot as your pivot indicator? if your broker is NOT GMT+2 it will give slight discrepancy in the chart from where the pivot should be to confirm the pivot points you can check www.actionforex.com I am using the other pivot indicator (SDX-Tzpivots) since you can adjust the GMT setting but it does not show historical (previous days) pivots I adjust it to GMT+2 and found it would nearly match the ones in actionforex In your case when using SDX-TzPivots with GMT+2 setting, the GBP/USD yellow EMA is still above pivot while the AU yellow EMA is below DP. you can find the indicator in this thread (click the paper clip button on top right corner of the thread page) and 2nd thing, why wait until you hit SL to exit? Iwan, Look at the M15 Stox and see how more powerful moves tend to happen when it goes into OB or OS territory first (yellow circles + arrows). Your entry: yes M5+M15 Stox in good positions and heading the right way, but your next question should be: "where is my M15 Stox coming from or has it visited OS or OB last ?" It wasn't coming from OS territory (white circle) and this is your warning that this next move might not be a powerful one. Your exit: Spot on. The next Short signal (yellow vertical line) was great with M5+M15 heading the right way then your question: "where is my M15 Stox coming from or has it visited OS or OB last ?" and the answer was that it was coming down from OB territory last (blue circle) so really an exit then &amp; there for a few pips was called rather than waiting for the SL at -25+pips (assuming that you had it below the recent lows - green line).

Potential Target Point Projections for contracting triangles: 1) calculate 'height' of triangle (41 pips) 2) add this number of pips at the point of breakout to either side: Up: 1.0260 (also 80%ATR 1.0249 &amp; R2 1.0255 - surprise?) Down: 1.0270 (also 80%ATR at same level) More conservative TPs would be 61.8% (Fib) of the height (ie 25 pips either side)

--- 帖子 #5345 ---
Although I'm new to this system I've been trading since the 90s and very successfully for the last 4 years with stocks. Genesis is a natural fit for me with forex markets and it has been going very well. I aim for 2-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio...but not on every trade. If my equity is at new highs then I will take a 1-to-1 trade no problem. However, when I get into a drawdown I get defensive and much more selective with my entries and trade management and focus more on waiting for high quality setups with a 2-to-1 RR to climb out of drawdown. You have to be adaptable and not see it as a black or white thing. The goal is to minimize losses and maximize profits. Press your winners and cut your losses. However, I keep a running tally of how many trades i've taken with RR less than 2-to-1 versus those with RR greater than 2-to-1 and I will get more selective if the metric drops to an uncomfortable level. The minimal RR I will take is 1-to-1 and if I do take a 1-to-1 trade then I'm typically extra careful, depending on the size of the stop, and ready to bail on the trade if the price action starts to get dicey.

--- 帖子 #5348 ---
I've noticed quite a few traders asking ,"What risk to reward ratio do you aim for?" (or shoot for) 1st of all, this is highly dependent on many factors. Your risk tolerance level, personality, account size, sobriety level, etc. 2nd of all, all of the traders on this thread use different R:R levels, some don't use any, it's highly personal. 3rd, and this is very important, is use of the word "aim". You may attempt to attain a profit that was 2X your risk. It doesn't mean you'll get it. You take what the market gives you and move on. And last, don't expect peple here to teach you how to trade. Go through the Baby Pips school, check some other threads and forums, but this thread is not a How To Trade thread. Some of the traders here have been quite generous with their time but frankly when I come here and I see posts like "Where should I put my stop?" or "When should I exit?" or my personal favorite, "How much profit have you made with Genesis?" I'm gone.

--- 帖子 #5369 ---
Hi Al, It means 'what was the most pips that I could have got from that trade from the entry/signal point to the end of that move' (if I had a 'perfect exit'). This is work that is only done once a move has finished. Obviously we never/rarely get a 'perfect exit' but for the instruments that I trade I keep a note in my journal of the pip-size of all the moves. So I have an idea what the average/maximum/mininum move might be: it's just simple math/statistic, again to try to squeeze a bit more out of each trade if I can. For example if the 'average/median' for an instrument is say 35 pips and I see that the next pivot is at 40 pips, then I'll be a bit more conservative and won't be afraid to close before the pivot if I see 'hesitation'.

--- 帖子 #5383 ---
Also, if you had looked to the left when you took the AU trade you would have noticed that it was in the middle of chop (i.e., sideways price action). The trade worked out but you may want to "look to the left" before taking a trade to make sure that you're not entering in chop. Sometimes the Euro/London Open will break a market out of chop..but it's still much more of a gamble to enter in chop because you're basically saying that "I believe that this is the trade that will breakout of the range"...now is that a bet you wanna make? if so, then take the trade. If not, then pass on the trade and wait for a breakout or enter on the breakout.

Excel but paper works fine too. Type of work I did at the end of the day or weekend for new instruments/strategies. A good example showing that even with the HTF M15 Stox on the floor the price can carry on going in the same direction for many more pips: .OB/OS Stox on their own aren't a reason to exit a trade (although you should be careful when entering as it's unlikely to be a HPT). .Continuous OB/OS should first be seen as a sign of strength(OB)/weakness(OS) rather than an immediate hint of trend reversal. .Waiting for decent PA first (the usual HL or LH) + the powerful divergence is good practice for a TRT (TrendReversalTrade)

Your original entry was against the downtrend but you got the rest of Genesis spot on. 4 things: 1) a more cautious trader might have waited for the PA to at least turn a bit and show a Higher Low (HL) 2) by the time you got your HL and the next Genesis signal (vertical blue line), M15 Stox was still fine and rising but M5 Stox had already been in OB territory ---&gt; more caution, it's not looking like a HPT 3) 3 or 4 candles later, you get a M5 bearish stox divergence (white lines) ---&gt; even more caution (maybe tighten SL to BE or take some profit) 4) you then get a Short Genesis signal (yellow line) For Short: M5 stox great, just been in OB + bearish divergence Against Short: M15 stox hasn't reached OB territory and was still pointing up at the close of the 10.10 candle - S1 support close by. While it's not a perfect Short, there are even more things now that are against your original Long position ----&gt; close now for 1-2 pips or definitely SL@BE

--- 帖子 #5635 ---
Goodmorning to everyone, I receveid some PMs from people asking for some clarifications. I think it is more helpfull to share my answers with all in order to sort out any doubt. 1. What does it mean YES/NO about the arrows in the statistics? If an arrow (both M5 or M15) was already appeared when Genesis signal come on it is YES viceversa NO. 2. When M5 Arrow is YES and M15 is also YES, means that both TF arrow appear together at time of entry? NO, it doesn't. In this case both M5 and M15 arrows were already on the chart when we had a Genesis signal. This is the typical trend day when we scaled in new positions in the same direction of the trend. 3. When do we enter? Following the arrows or Genesis signals? We always enter in a trade according to the rules in post#2. Arrows are just confirmation signals. If M5 arrow doesn't appear within 3-5 bars begin to be concerned. 4. When M15 arrow appeared would you entry or wait for the next genesis signal to enter? Arrows are only a confirmation signals. Perticularly M15 arrow can help to highlight the higher probability trades in the M5 timeframe. Numbers say that if you enter the first Genesis signal in the same direction of M15 arrow you can get high succes rates. 5. How can we backtest the system with the arrows? You'll have to leave 'arrow.ex4' in your experts folder because MTF Arrow is calling it. But you can remove it from your chart and try this arrow instead. You can change the number of bars it looks back and it should make no difference to mtf arrow

--- 帖子 #5690 ---
This is why I manually trail my trades......I will do a live one next time I see a good set up early on in the session. Just briefly, taking EA for example...if you took the trade as the PA left the pivot and had your SL below the swing low, then as the Pivot got hit, move the SL to BE. Now the trade is free...the risk is removed....you can't lose from here on! As the PA moves up from the PA and heads to R1, bring up the SL to (say) +10. Now you will get 10 pips no matter what. As the PA moves up towards R2, bring the SL to just under R1 (+15 more or less). When R2 is hit, ATR is 2 pips short of the max.....so now you either take your profit, or you move the SL again and aim for S3. Given that ATR is maxed out.....although it could go higher, I would take my 50 pips and look for another set up. It's just a matter of not being greedy. If your trade is at (say) +15, and it reverses and hits your SL at BE.....so what? You lost nothing.....don't cry about the 15 you have had because you haven't got it!!!!! But......what a shame to cash it in at +15 and then watch it go to +50, no? But don't worry.....we have all been there, and we all revisit that dilemma from time to time!!

--- 帖子 #5759 ---
Hi Profitpips but this is for everyone. I know that this will be bread'n'butter for a lot of you but enough questions still pop up to make me think that some will benefit from a 'refresher'... This is the sort of process that should be going through your minds when you contemplate a counter-trend trade as this chart is a very good example: 0. first sign that the uptrend (purple arrow) might be over: we have a LH (Lower High); very aggressive traders might consider a short scalp trade at this point (not me). To me, at this point the 'advantage' is still with the Longs as it was the prevailing trend then. 1. second sign: we have a LL (Lower Low) as we have gone below the first support (blue line) and we have also broken below the recent trendline (green line). Many traders (me included) will now be looking at their indicators and consider a possible Short (it might not happen - and this stage we didn't know). 2. third sign: we now have a 2nd LH and I would be assessing my RRR and looking at where to place my stop (above T) but also mindful of the second possible support level (yellow line). On most occasions I would enter on a Genesis signal with good Stox positions &amp; all the rest. 3. fourth sign: we now have a 2nd LL + the second support has been breached so it's looking good for Shorts but hang on, the price is not making much progress so should I be cautious? Yes because of that (it doesn't hurt to be cautious) but a BIG 'NO' because when checking the higher TF (M15), we can see (I checked back) that Genesis M15 also went short on the big red arrow so now we have M5 AND M15 Short. 4. fifth sign: this is the 'killer' trap for Longs: yes we had a new Long M5 signal (dotted line) but this is now against the M15 and should be avoided for all the reasons detailled above (+ no Higher Low (HL) &amp; no Higher High (HH) to even hint at a new change in trend). 5 ---&gt; 8 no reason to even consider a Long as we are making a succession of LLs &amp; LHs.

--- 帖子 #5794 ---
Ok. If trading was as easy as spending a handful of months on learning currency trading, and one month on a system (any system), then we would all be rich beyond our wildest dreams, would we not? Trading is not easy, and it certainly isn't a get rich quick scheme. Traders that we have to compete against include the major banks and hedge fund managers etc etc etc, and those people have studied their craft for years, and been mentored by some on the best in the business. They trade accounts so large that it would make your eyes water!! It simply is not possible to compete against those professional and highly trained and skilled traders by spending a handful of months learning the market and one month on a system. Going to your local tool store and buying the latest welding equipment and a DIY on Welding book, and spending a handful of months learning to weld, will not get you a job in any engineering plant, let alone on a North Sea oil rig where the big money is made. Obviously you will be competing against some highly skilled and experience welders and you cannot compete. But, by spending a lot of time.....a LOT of time, learning how the market moves and what moves it, and then applying a good system, you stand a chance of making it. As I said, trading is not easy....it is very difficult. It is unreasonable to expect consistent profits until you have invested considerable time in learning this craft. Perhaps you are not suited to trading....perhaps you underestimate what is required of you to succeed in this business. Only you will know these things, and this is not an occupation that is suited to everyone, any more than being a welder suits everyone. Most people spend 3 years or more of intense learning, practicing and screen time before they 'get the hang of it'.....most welders (and other trades) spend 3 or 4 years learning the basics too. Trading is no different to learning any other trade/skill. it takes time.

--- 帖子 #5813 ---
You can't, simply because one (EA) is just the mathematical calculation derived from EU/AU: by the time one of these 2 moves, EA is simultaneously updated too. If EU &amp; AU move in the same direction (up) &amp; roughly the same amount of pips, it doesn't tell you anything about EA (it won't move much), it only tells you that the US$ is weak against both the € &amp; the Australian$ You can use EA as hedging against certain positions in EU &amp; AU but that's it and it's certainly beyond the scope of what we discuss here under the Genesis banner.

I was going to post your definition of repainting is incorrect, which would have highlighted that very fact. Repainting is were an indi changes colour/reading, after the relevant candle closes. --- 帖子 #5978 ---
That really depends on the size of his account: 23% on a small account is not that much but on a big account it is a lot harder to achieve because in real terms if you trade with the same leverage, the size (in $/€/£...) of the SL &amp; DD gets really big. On a £1000 account, with a £1/pip leverage/trade size, a fairly standard Genesis SL of 20/30 pips per trade (£20/30) is only 2/3% of the account and if you get 230 pips (£230) per week (46 pips (£46) a day - not uncommon in Genesis trading) you get your 23% per week. But as I've said earlier, it's a lot harder to achieve with a bigger (£10000 account) because you are now risking 10 times as much in SL &amp; DD and that will invariably impact your decision making (although technically the % are still the same, so it shouldn't make any difference ... but it does and herein lies the big connendrum between trade-size/leverage/fear/greed/...)

--- 帖子 #5979 ---
Exactly right Oli. Making 23% or more per week on a small account is easily do-able depending on the size of the account. Also, provided the daily goal (say) 50 pips/day is maintained, and the profits compounded and lot size increased in scale, then the account can grow by a huge amount, but still keeping the daily goal of 50 pips the same. Of course as the account grows, and the lot size traded grows, soon we are looking at some pretty big numbers......$2500 at 5 lots x 50 pips....a nice trade, no? But, a SL of 25 pips at the same rate = $1,250 loss. And right there is where the problem comes in. Our fear/greed emotive setup see's a $1,250 loss when the SL is hit and we might think "#@&amp;% and ?%@#&amp;^ that's a huge loss today.....and tomorrow we might lose the same amount......and maybe the next day too. Now we are freaking out at all this money we have lost. But wait a minute.....maybe we're looking at this all wrong. After all, out target of 50 pips per day hasn't changed......our (average for this example) SL of 25 pips hasn't changed. So we lots 75 pips over 3 days.....pah.....big deal.....who cares? After all, we're normally banking in excess of 250 pips per week......what's a 75 pip over 3 losss?? The loss is nothing to worry about......but when we convert that 75 pip (over 3 days) loss to actual money, we freak out at the $3,750 loss. But, if we are trading 5 lots according to the accepted rules of MM, our account will be in the region of $75,000. So the loss is inconsequential. Even more importantly, the loss is the SAME PERCENTAGE of out account as it always was. And there we have it, instead of looking at the money (like us humans tend to do), we *need* to have the discipline to look at the percentage of the account as it grows, and as it steps back in the event of a loss or series of losses. Forget the $$$$'s.......and to some extent, forget the percentage.....focus on the target. As the account grows, increase the lots size to maintain the win/loss percentage, but focus on the daily target. If the daily target is 50 pips, at the beginning of the table you can see that the weekly gain is just $312......the weekly loss would be less than half that even if we lost every trade that week. BUT.....by week 20, our weekly gain is in the region of $18,500.......and out loss would less than half that even if we lost every trade that week.......BUT, look at the account size, $78,000. So a weekly loss of (say) $6000 is not going to have a huge impact on our $78,000 account. A $6000 loss sounds big.......but it's always been the same when you look at the number of pips gained or lost. Our silly emotions of fear and greed convert that win/loss to $$$. Imagine if we could blank out the $$ profits on our brokers dealing platform and only ever see pips....if we could resist the urge to convert pips to $'s, and only do the conversion every 6 months, I think trading would be a lot easier for a lot of people Fear and Greed.......SUX!! NOTE: The first 2 weeks in this spreadsheet should be less than 0.1 lots for good MM, but that is not possible on the broker that this spreadsheet was produced for.....so don't get too hung up on those first 2 weeks.

--- 帖子 #5980 ---
Interesting spreadsheet RJ. It's easy to get carried away with the compounding factors based on the analysis of making the 50 pips a day, everyday. Even when we make the adjustments and say we go for 20 pips a day we can end up with sizeable accounts in theory. However, just like you were saying about "Greed and Fear", he doesn't respond to the theory of the spreadsheet. Sticks his head up at in-opportune times and creates havoc for the in-experienced and experienced for that matter. There is a big difference in the mindset from trading a .1/.2 Lot to a 10/15 lot, traded with a 25 pip stop. Where we would have let it run to the S1 pivot before, we start questioning the trade at the slightest hint of a retrace and take 10 pips instead of the 30 pips that was on offer. We would have achieved the 30 pips had we stuck to the rules. So start small with a max of 2% risk on each trade (ideally smaller), and get in the mindset of trading the system the way it should be traded with your intended targets no matter what. No increasing stops because the trade is going against you!!! Once your bank is in a position for the larger trade sizes you should have formed the neural pathways required to manage your trades as per the rules you have been applying all along. Before you know it you should be placing less emphasis on the size of the trade as opposed to managing the trade as per the Genesis method. It has become a new habit. Now all I have to do is practice what I preach!!!

--- 帖子 #5981 ---
That's where it comes down to having a trading plan.....and trading the plan rather than trading by fear. The size of the account doesn't matter.....as per the spreadsheet, we are aiming for 50 pips/day and the risk is (more or less) *always* the same %age (apart from the week 1 and week 2 ). I will always let the trade run to S1 (for example) because once my SL is at BE....there simply is no losing from here on in.....the risk is removed. 8 times out of 10 it will get to S1 or beyond......on the other 2 occasions it will come back and knock me out for +1. Yes.....I could cry about "oh shit....I wish I had have taken the profit at +25 instead of +1 that I have now"......but that is greed. If we give in to that....soon, we will be aiming for +25. What happens when it turns around at +20 and knocks us out for +1? Will we then adjust our target to aim for +20?? What happens when it turns around at +15.....+10....+5???? Now we are solidly in the grip of fear and greed. My personal way is to aim for the pivots or other s/r lines as we all know. If I get knocked out for +1....so be it. I go and make some coffee and look for the next opportunity and I don't give the past trade a second thought.....because....many time when I am aiming for (say) S1.....the PA might go to S2 or S3. Those wonderful trades more than offset the times where I get knocked out for +1. So it's all 'swings and roundabouts' for me.....the point is, I have a plan.....and I stick to the plan. The minute you start changing your plan out of fear and greed, is the day you are looking down the barrel of the 95% who lose!! Discipline and patience are the keys.....along with a good system and a good plan. You must stick to each of the above. Of course the spreadsheet doesn't allow for losses and it doesn't allow for +20 days or withdrawals. The point of the spreadsheet is to show what is possible with modest pippage, discipline, patience and a good system.

IF H1 PA is up only take M5 long setups as per RJ's post 1 rules.. It's good advice for newer traders: look ahead when a 4 dots signal is about to appear, switch to H1 TF quickly and look at the slope of the yellow MA: 1. if it's going up, only take Long trades 2. if it's going down only take Short trades 3. if it's flat, we are most probably ranging Nothing stops you from taking opposite counter-trend trades but at least that way you'll know when you're counter-trend trading and that you should be more cautious and not hesitate to take quick profit or bring your SL to B/E quickly

--- 帖子 #6038 ---
I'm going to disagree with you both on this point. What you're essentially saying, if I'm reading this correctly is that if the H1 matrix is (say) indicating long, then take all long signals on the M5? Is that right? If it is, then it's wrong. That is essentially the 60 - 5 method on the Symphonie thread, and that was developed by Yelena. Where it falls down is that there are 12 x 5 minutes candles to every 60 minute candle, and the M5 trend can turn LONG before the H1 trend picks it up. The time gap between M5 and M60 is simply far too great and losses are inevitable. The Genesis team discussed this, and both Cody and I independently had dismissed the 60 - 5 method for that exact reason. The 15 - 5 method that was posted a few pages back after some considerable testing and data collecting was found to be much more reliable and consistent. That's why the team pursued the idea and published the PDF which is available via the links on post #1

--- 帖子 #6046 ---
I'm sorry, but it's not exactly the same. Any higher TF MA only takes into account price at close (normally), or in this case, the high, low and close prices. The lower timeframe uses all the intervening bars, which under extreme cases could spike to the moon and back. Your M5 MA(60) would look very different to your H1 MA(5) in that case. Again, I'm being pedantic. For this case, it would most likely yield the same interpretation of H1 PA.

Let me just add that "continuous weakness/strength in OS/OB territory for M15 Stox" is something that is not always easy to gauge even for seasoned traders, well at least for me. It's one of those things that is more easily identifiable with hindsight or after the fact and that's not much help in live trading lol The tell-tale sign (and the one that would have kept me out of a short trade) is that although it was still below 20, the M15 Stox had been continuously rising since the lows and was approaching the 20 level when the M5 signal came (ie, not yet ripe for a Long but caution at least for a Short) And if we carry on down in UC, the 80%ATR is nicely positioned at 9316 for a possible retest of today's low area

--- 帖子 #6215 ---
I performed a pivots review of EURUSD (actually I performed this analysis for all markets I trade) for the period 10/15/2002 thru 9/28/2012 (so about 10 years) and discovered the following: ~The Low &lt;= S3 5.56% of the time ~The Low &lt;= S2 16.56% of the time ~The Low &lt;= S1 42.60% of the time ~The High &gt;= R1 44.97% of the time ~The High &gt;= R2 18.27% of the time ~The High &gt;= R3 7.19% of the time What does this mean to me? Shorting below or near S2 and Buying above or near R2 is a low-probability play. My procedures were taken from this article (I believe Dmitry first posted the link to the article, but I can't remember): http://www.investopedia.com/articles...#axzz282lnHUbg I hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #6216 ---
.As we don't reach S1/R1 more than half the time, for trades taken around the PP, it should be a good idea to have your TP (or a part of it) a few pips before S1/R1 (as suggested previously in here)... .As we don't reach S2/R2 between 80 &amp; 85% of the time, opposite direction trades initiated around these levels on a Genesis signal should have a good statistical chance of success (even more so at S3/R3) but bear in mind that by the time we've reached S2/S3/R2/R3 we will have a definite trend in one direction and despite the stats you will be countertrend trading...

--- 帖子 #6217 ---
I will also add that my analysis of all my other markets revealed roughly the same statistics (i.e., pretty close) as EU.

--- 帖子 #6256 ---
Ok.....I have sat in the background on this issue today to see how you all feel and what you think. Most of you understand why outside indies are not allowed here, but Marty also makes some valid points. It's true, this is not a system for newbies......but by that (and perhaps I should amend Post #1 to make it crystal clear), I meant that this is not for newbies *to fx trading*. Many newbies think they can go to post 1 of any thread, download a system and start printing their own money!! In fact I expect many people here now thought that at one time too......I know I did. But if that was allowed to happen here, newbies would lose, if they were dumb enough to use real money. If they just demoed, they would still lose and become disheartened and/or bombard the thread with newbie questions....hence, the link to the school of pipsology on Post #1. As we can see, using stochastics is not an easy thing to master, but many here are now doing very well with stoch and they are appreciating it's value and simplicity. That is something that a newbie (to fx trading) will never get his/her head around. So, this system is not for them. The reason why no other indicators will be allowed is simple. The system works, and it works well as it is. If someone with a year or two of struggling to be consistently profitable comes here and uses the system as is, they will be on the path to consistent profitability. However, if I wasn't so strict on the indi issue, by now people would see charts with various THV indicators, Coral, all manner of MA crosses, SAR, Inchimoku clouds, harmonic patterns etc etc etc......and then this thread would look like any other here at FF.....and the very people we are trying to help would see this thread as just another mongrel system that is complicated and open to all sorts of predictions and interpretations. Who will win?......the brokers, that's who!!! When people become consistently profitable with Genesis, they may well add their own indies to make the system even more profitable....and that's great....I love it. But hopefully, by then, they will realise that others who are joining our thread are in the same position that they once were themselves. And what do they need? They need a consistent, easy(ish) system with pages and pages of examples with all the same charts, and a group of profitable Genesis traders to help them to become profitable. And that's the reason why outside indicators have to be kept off the thread. I hope that clears a few things up.

--- 帖子 #6296 ---
I am also in the US. Here is what i did for this situation. I found it to be the most transparent and legal. Register with the NFA (National Futures Association) as a Pool Manager. You do not need to be licensed to do this with less than 14 participants and less than $400K in the pool. Then find a broker who will let you run the pool. This way everthing is taxed seperately, kept seperate, split correctly, and kept clean. Also, if this works for you, word will spread and you will have other offers. This way you will be prepared as it grows. I do not know anything about the other "trade copier" programs or anything, but I do know that if something goes wrong as a result of the trade copier, you are in trouble. I would rather be with a good broker who has the sytem set. That way I know it is all working and I have a registered broker to fall back on. FWIW, "CYA" will be your friend for life, but friends who lose money, often turn in a second. Trust me on this. Good luck with your venture! Know this, your emotions will change when you trade because of "the boss" It come out in you pulling a trade exit earlier than you normally would at first, but it will have an effect. Make sure you exit startegy is as planned and as mechanical as your entry.

--- 帖子 #6306 ---
Thanks RJ. I like trading gold, especially bullish moves when the USD is weakening. Gold is traded in USD so when the dollar weakens, it gets cheaper for the rest of the world. That pushes the price of gold up in dollars. At the same time, because the $ is weakening, and $ being THE world currency, risk aversive traders move their money into gold, pushing the price up further. This means that you do get exaggerated moves in gold and so make it worth trading even with the higher spread. I never traded gold with TF lower than 1 hour before, early days, but it does seem to be working with Genesis 15 minute charts.

In the appendix (entitled The Genius of W.D. Gann: An Interpretation ) to Tony Plummer's Forecasting Financial Markets , the case is made that the elusive secret to Gann's trading success, which he never revealed explicitly, is to be found in Gann's The Tunnel Thru the Air . To me, the key is to be found in the many references to the gospel's words "I tell you the truth, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven." His mother told him that the Bible said, 'A little child shall lead them,' and that anyone who would harm little children, can in no wise enter into the Kingdom of Heaven." And becoming like little children is the same as ridding yourself of acquired personality. So there you go: In heaven, as in trading, personality is an obstacle. Also verified by science.

--- 帖子 #6551 ---
1. Trade with what you can afford to lose and not miss throwing away. 2. Have a great system (thanks RJ et al), and a good plan. 2. Treat trading as a game you have to play well; the better you play, the more you win. 3. Close the terminal window of your MT4, dont take a look at the 'money'; focus on the screen and 'playing' your game. 4. Since its a game, have all your gaming buttons and 'shortcuts' at your finger tips..no need having 5 steps to close a position and open one simultaneously. You need to have the option of reacting fast to the 'action'. 5. At day or week's end, be happy with the money you made; and/or research and be determined to be a better player (especially with losses). As with all games practice WILL make perfect.

Thanks....the translation is (more or less): Nyse Euronext will require the application of the so-called Rule 48 in the opening phase. The decision is aimed at curbing excess volatility that could occur after two days of forced closure due to the passage of the hurricane Sandy in New York. The Rule 48 includes the ability of market makers in the market to temporarily halt trading in case of excessive volatility. It is therefore the possibility of suspending trading also by other criteria than those used by automatic blocks. The Rule 48 has been invoked for the last time Sept. 6, 2011.

Hello insainty, The more experienced traders have unique ways of trading with the Matrix, as well as using the 'standard' model. The 'standard' method is found in mostly RJ's posts. The '3' MTF arrow strategy you're referring to was initiated by Yelena (who I'm expecting back from holidays soon); I suspect this trading style (which seems similar to how Martyfish trades); basically surfing the waves of Higher Time Frame Momentum; is profitable but isnt really the basic Genesis M.O. The Basic M5 Genesis Method: * 4 'Lights' * great M5 and M15 stochastics (OB/OS (showing trend strength or exhaustion), direction, divergence) * watch your P,S,R lines and look left * SL: swing Hi/Low +/- 'x' * TP: next line or PA stall or Genesis signal in opposite direction etc etc from 5-15 PDF.. * Execute on the open of the next candle after the signal. Thats bare-bones of it really.. Keep reading through it should be clear as you go along..

--- 帖子 #6729 ---
For the new(er) traders: when you apply any indicator to a chart, that indicator does not 'know' if it is being applied to EU, GU, Gold, Crude Oil, etc.... The indicator's code does some math, returns a value and the clever people like Cody/Xaphod transform it into an easy-on-the-eyes/brain graphical format (the 4 dots...) for us. If an indicator (or a set of indicators) works on one instrument, it ought to work on all. That's the principle at least, but we all know that each instrument has its own characteristics, its own way of moving, its own 'life', so there will be some where Genesis is as good as the original (for example on EY, UC, CY - I believe that Genesis was mainly tested on EU but I'm happy to be corrected on that) and some that aren't as good and require additional filters, but overall, because it's only math running in the background, a sound, well-tested set of indicators like Genesis should (and does) work across all instruments, from FX pairs to commodities, to indices.... I trade both WTI &amp; Brent but with other non-Genesis indicators due to the larger size of the stops (higher volatility) extra filters are needed. At times it can feel like GU on steroids lol

I am used to enter in a trade with two units (short and long unit), once I am in profit and price touches my first target I get out short unit and move in BE the second one ... now I am relaxed because I have made some profit and I have a free risk trade in my hand. In this situation it is simpler to let PA acts and look at it without emotional involvement.... and this is the best scenario to made the right decisions. ciao wiz

Thankyou Wiz, I did use to manage my trades in a similar way. Like many traders I used to, and still do, determine my stoploss based on S/R, which is usually the last swing high/low. Also, like many traders, I used to aim for R:R of 1:1, ie. setting take profit level equal to SL. Nowadays, unlike many traders, I realise that using S/R for stop levels is sound, but basing TP on the size of the SL is absolutely ridiculous. From what I have seen with trading Genesis so far, it certainly looks feasable to take profit on half the position at DP levels or with your Exit 2 from the PDF and maybe letting the other half run to obvious strong S/R or opposite signal. --- 帖子 #6794 ---
How about with these updated settings lol: .slim down the body of the HA candles to 2 (as before) .remove the wicks/tails of the HA candles by setting their colours to none (255,255,255). .set the charts' properties as defined in the other box + set to 'bars', not 'candles' I believe that you now get the best of both world: 1) you can see the actual tops/bottoms of the normal candles (because the HA wick/tail has been removed) so your trendlines and areas of S/R will be as intended. 2) you can instantly see if it's an up or a down candle (the centre line + the 2 little open/close side bits will both be either white (up) or red (down)). 3) you preserve the body of the HA candle to see if it 'open clears of the yellow MA' or not.

--- 帖子 #6804 ---
If you really can't get to grips with HA candles, then don't use them. I find that they cut out a lot of noise that is associated with Japanese candles, and Japanese candles tend to give a bias as far as formations go...eg bearish engulfing, morning star, even star, inside bars etc etc etc......all these things instill bias which is what we are trying to combat here because bias is a BAD thing!!! But like I say, if you have tried and cannot get to grips with the HA candles, then use the Japanese candles. It took me a while to forget about Japanese Candles after 3 years of learning everything about them, but eventually HA candles make life so much less complicated for me. I have to say though, that for longer term analysis, most f which I don't post here because it's not relevant to the Genesis system, I do in Japanese candles....but I'm talking about H4 and Daily charts where 'noise' isn't an issue anyway.

--- 帖子 #6808 ---
That's right....a solid downtrend. Of course there will be RETRACES along the way, but there RETRACES are not reversals and the start of an uptrend....they are RETRACES and they are dangerous to attempt to trade unless you have quick fingers!! I know what you're thinking..... "how do I tell the difference between a retrace and a genuine trend reversal?" The short answer is "You can't!" You would need to be looking at higher timeframes and other things to determine if the trend has genuinely changed. Doing what you're attempting to do is to get in right at the point of the trend change.....and eventually, if you persist, you will get the super-early entry into the trend change......IF your account survives that long!! Picking tops and bottoms of trends is a fools game and many people have lost a lot trying to do that. When the trend genuinely changes, you'll see it. You won't get in at the point of the reversal, but you'll do ok....we all do. But until that reversal comes, it is safer to trade with the trend that to try and go against it.

--- 帖子 #6812 ---
They do happen, but admittedly they are rare. The main point is to prevent people rushing into the trade too soon. If people wait for the signal candle to close.....they will see the next candle open clear of the yellow ma nearly all the time. That's a good thing. If people get in on the signal candle and it hasn't yet closed, it can go the other way and cost them! Maybe it doesn't seem that important, but to my way of thinking it is a nice safety feature that does no harm

I actually find your chart hurts my eyes to try and look at it. It really is horrible. Why have you got your stochs taking up nearly half the area? Your candles are all squashed up and with the thick MA's and arrows superimposed over, I'm surprised if you have any idea what is going on. Yesterday was not a good trading day. I did not have a single trade on my real money account. The market was basically ranging and when that happens signals tend to occur at the top/bottom of the range. Personally, I prefer to wait for a break-out of ranges, a retest of S/R as R/S and then take a signal in that direction. There was only one good move with EU yesterday. That was the move down not long after FF open. From yesterday's posts some made some good money off of that move, but that ship sailed without me. The top blue box is the Asian range. Price broke above it at FF open, but only by 3 or 4 pips, so not much of a breakout. Genesis signalled a short 20 minutes before London open (first vertical line), but it was only 7 pips above the bottom of the Asian range. So I didn't take it. It moved well, so with hindsight you may say that I was wrong not to take it, but that's the way I trade. It keeps me out of a lot of losers. If there had been a retest of the breakout level and a new or continuation signal, I would have been in, but it didn't happen. C'est la vie. The second vertical line is a buy signal. The previous 3 candles suggest that price is stalling and stoch has flattened off close to the 80 level. Against the big move direction, this is not a HP trade. 3rd vertical line a short signal, 7 pips above S1 - nuff said. Although this trade did go more than 10 pips in profit, so it would have given the opportunity to move SL to BE. 4th vertical line. Much the same as the previous long signal, but possibly a little stronger as price had made a higher low. 5th vertical line. Looking left we see a higher low and a lower high. This market has no direction at all! As well as that, price is only a few pips above S1. Would have worked out quite well thogh as 20 pips would have been on offer at 1 time. 6th - I would hope no explanation needed! 7th - PA showed signs of stalling previous 4 or 5 candles. Braciola, I feel that you are one of those people who have started with Forex either because you believe all the hype and think that it is a way to get rich quickly, or you have financial difficulties and think that this is the solution with a few indicators. It doesn't work that way. The most important thing is to be able to read the charts. The most important aspect being sentiment. Think of it as a battle between the Bulls and the Bears. A battle that goes on forever with one side advancing, the other retreating. Sometimes their respective strengths are balanced, other time one has obvious control. When the charts indicate that one is control, that is the time to jump in. If strengths are looking balanced and you can't decide who is in control - STAY OUT OF THE MARKET. It worries me that you are trading with money that you cannot afford to lose and that you have not spent enough time studying charts to be able to have a clue what is going on. Sorry to be harsh, but until you know what you are doing, trade with a very small account.

--- 帖子 #6914 ---
I agree with you on this. I have not taken one single trade today. The EU and UC trades at the Frankie open were the only two of my markets that were high-probablility. However, I didn't take EU because the trend was weakening on my HTF chart and I didn't take UC because there was not enough profit to my first target. Knowing when to sit on your hands and determine when a market is offering you a high-probability setup is one of the most important traits that you can develop as a trader. Think of it this way: You are paid to sit at the computer all day and only place a trade when you see one that's high-probability (and by high-probability I mean "only" a 50% winner). I've been batting around 50% winners with close to 3-to-1 RR (real money trades) because I only take the creme of the crop trades and I will cut my losses quicker than a pitbull on a ham sandwich (which also means I miss out on some ultimate winners). Run the mathematical expectancy on my numbers and you will see that it's very high. This leave me with only 4-8 trades per week, but I'm gradually increasing my position size as I take from the "house" (minus the vig of course). I only increase my position size out of profits and never out of my own capital (i.e., be conservative with "your money" and only get aggressive with your risk after you have a substantial profit cushion).

--- 帖子 #6915 ---

If you are trading a real money account and getting frustrated with not getting enough trades, take the mediocre trades on a demo account and watch it drop. Eventually you will be satisfied with only taking the high probability trades.

--- 帖子 #6985 ---
ATR != ADR ADR = Average Daily Range. ((Daily High - Daily Low) for N days)/ N TR = True Range = MAX[ High(today) - Low(today), Close(yesterday) - High(today), Close(yesterday) - Low(today) ] ATR = Average True Range = (TR for N days) / N The results are usually similar. Are you using the same period? One can set the period for the ADR in the dashboard via the parameter: ADR.Days What value is period parameter set to in the LFL-ATL indicator? The default value is probably 14. The ADR calculation in the dashboard is simple and based on daily candles, so it is dependent on your brokers server time-shift.

Yes, you should be using the same number for both if you want comparable data. Given that the LFL-ATR is in popular use here, setting the ADR to 7 would be a reasonable choice. For the ADR, the most popular settings probably are 5 and 20. The former being a week and the latter about one month. I do not think one can consider any one setting more correct than another. Use whatever you think gives a good estimate for your trading strategy.

In the book on my profile he talks about this.....he says that he has a friend who people used to ridicule because on the trading floor, he entered very few trades while they were entering a lot of trades. Some winners, some losers. But, when the friend did enter a trade, he was super focused and the trades nearly always worked out, and they decent trades. His win/loss rate was in the region of 90%.......so he may have taken fewer trades, but 90% of the trades he entered were winners, and some were big winners. That's they key.....not to jump in and out of the market winning a few and losing a few because you know who the big winner really is don't you?......yup....the broker, because he wins every time you enter the market! I try to do what the friend above does.....only enter the high probability trades and let the rest go. If they turn into the big move, I will find an entry later perhaps and get some of the move. If not, I'll be happy for those who made money and I'll be happy that I lost nothing. Remember that spreadsheet I posted before?........50 pips a day is all it takes to make a very large account. Even 20 pips will make a large account over 12 months. We don't need the BIG moves.....we need *consistent* high probability trades that return us a profit.

Hi all, first post - I've coded Genesis into an EA. It is not profitable yet, but I see promise - it needs more filters for higher probability trades. Rules: Entry: Matrix signal, Stoch signal, EMA Signal, Candle agreement Exit: SL: Previous Swing H/L, Trail to BreakEven @ +X (20), TP: I have tried a number of combinations with varying success depending on the specific PA If SL is to remain at previous swing H/L, the Entry is what must be improved in order to increase win %. Potential Filters to Add to Entry: 1. Adding a higher TF for agreement - causes a later entry but helps to avoid whipsaws - would prefer to not do this unless required - seems a proxy for adding a directional bias 2. Adding Pivots / other S/R and allowing trades only when signal occurs near and in opposite direction and/or far away and in same direction 3. Other... Looking for input from Genesis veterans regarding potential Objective filters that may be added to produce better entries. Frequency of trades isn't an issue, only win %. I can figure out the best exit once the entry is optimized.

I look at all time frames for divergence but for M5 trading in particular, I look at M5 and M15 charts for divergence that I can use in my intraday trading. H1, H4 and Daily divergence I tend to keep in the back of my mind as possible trend reversal points, but I don't really apply them to my intraday trading. But.....congratulations on your trade

Ok can I add my two-pence worth. In a strong trending market, stochastics become very difficult to interpret, any time frame. Particularly a weak setting like 11,3,3. So it is probably not totally an effectively "tutorial", taking a market which is not appropriate for stoch readings. Thats why we have tapes and arrows to determine trend - trend is stronger than momentum !! If multiple HTF trends allign, pay attention to that, and less so to stochs. In a range bound market stochs are KING !

--- 帖子 #7271 ---
Another thing with trading without a SL. The unexpected can happen sometimes and you could find yourself without an internet connection and unable to exit a trade. A few years back a ship's anchor ripped out some undersea cables and we had very bad internet connections for quite some time. Its also a good idea to set a TP even if its way beyond your wildest expectations. If you find yourself without internet and with only a SL in place, the chances are that it will eventuially hit the stop even though going into profit many times. I also had the misfortune to have a 5000 Pound plus account with MF Global when they went into recievership. I didn't have any open trades with them at the time, but I know that traders were unable to manage open positions, not sure if SL and TP were honoured though. Hopefully I will eventually get my money back, but it all takes time and it seems that the receivers like to make it excessively complicated. So always set a SL, even if it's 100 pips away. Better than losing xxxx pips if the unthinkable happens. The beauty of MT4 is that when you see that you may be getting a trade signal soon, You can open the trading window and set the SL and TP in advance. You are then ready to push the button if you get the full signal when the candle closes.

--- 帖子 #7272 ---
I look at how strong the trend is: is it a gradual one with visible retracements along the way or is it a cascade-type one where you'll be trying to catch a falling knife. If it is the former and you get a nice base/consolidation area around S3 then it can be tradeable if/when all else is pointing the same way (in those cases, consider also a H1 Stox) and you have a good RRR between your SL &amp; the next pivot line. In today's examples (EY &amp; CY) we are only a few pips below where we were 7 hours ago (not a cascade style downtrend) but I'd be wary that we haven't hit the 100%ATR line yet. Either way, they are rarely HPT, and also remember that although it is not showing on Genesis indicators, there is also an S4 further down ...

--- 帖子 #7297 ---
Right, let me revisit that post so that there is no confusion where I stand and also bearing in mind that we have experienced and new(ish) traders in here. This only referred to gaining much needed experience and discipline with manual SL &amp; TP when trading a live microlots account. My view: your (fixed) SL is your best friend ("Stops are IN, Emotions are OUT ") because until you really know what you are doing trading-wise, if you don't have one, you will eventually ignore your 'mental' SL for 2 reasons: 1) habit: every trade that goes against you with serious drawdown but that eventually gets back to BE or even profit will re-inforce the feeling that you don't need a SL because ... "I know what I'm doing/markets always turn around right?/I'm a lucky type of trader/SL are for sissies/etc....." (delete or keep (lol) as appropriate). 2) surprise: this is not an 'if' it is a 'when' .....at some stage in your trading career, if you don't have a SL in place, you will be in a trade that goes so fast and so deep against you that you will simply freeze, unable to click 'close trade' and your trading account will be gone (and although you won't feel that way at the time, count yourself lucky if it happens early in your trading career as your account will likely still be quite small, but it's best that it doesn't happen in the first place lol). Do you really think that you will be able to react more rationally than a guy with years of experience in the Chicago trading pits when faced with a 1000 points drop in the Dow Jones in minutes? (For those not familiar with indices, 1 S&amp;P points = roughly 10 Dow Jones Points = roughly 10 Forex pips) And I make no apology if I sound like your Grandad

1. Do you have the problem when you have only the genesis matrix on the chart? Ie have you localized the problem to the matrix indicator? 2. Reduce the 'max bars in chart' value. 'Tools-&gt;Options-&gt;Charts-&gt;Max bars in chart' then restart. This will reduce the time spent by the indicators drawing the history when you change the TF. If you for example have 200000 bars in the chart, the expect processing that amount of data to take some time.

When the market is ranging, it is a tussle between the bulls and the bears with neither side seemingly able to take ground. PA entered the range with the Bulls being very strong, bears fought back but were unable to keep the bears at bay and were over-run and price continued up. Price reached and breached R2, where the bears once again launched an offensive. But they could only manage to take the price back down to the top of the range before the bulls regained domination. The bulls took the price up again to where the bears last made a stand. Note that the bears took 8 candles to regain the ground to the top of the range. The bulls only needed 4 candles to take that ground back. At times like this, you often find that the bearish sentiment totally collapses So I think it was quite reasonable for you to take the trade.

--- 帖子 #7416 ---
Hi Frenetic, Yes, I have to agree with you. When there is a strong trend in the higher tf, there are many opportunities to trade against that trend in the lower tf. A trend in a lower tf is simply a retrace, not a reversal in a higher tf. When taking the trades in a lower tf, it's always a good idea to be aware of this and maybe exit when the retrace appears to be running out of steam

--- 帖子 #7417 ---
That's the thinking that led to the 5-15 method to be developed. Yelena developed the 60-5 method for the Symphonie system, and the Genesis team discussed this. We agreed that in a strong trend, and we're talking several hours to several days, the 60-5 method works well. But, the difference between the H1 and the M5 (60 - 5) was too great much of the time and good moves were missed completely. That's what led us to comprehensive testing of the 5-15 method and we found that the results were much more profitable than 60-5.

Hi Cody, just a question about the MTF Arrows 3.00 Does is wait for all 3 arrows to confirm then it stays on the chart, or when will it not stay on the chart, as I've seen an instance this morning on EURUSD with EURO open that it showed the third arrow, and then poof all was gone?

--- 帖子 #7438 ---
The MTF Arrow will paint 1 arrow for each 5 minute 'segment' of the 15 minutes. When the M15 candle has closed, the arrow (3 arrows on an M5 chart) will be painted for ever......or not painted for ever. As stated several times on this thread and on Post#1 NOTHING in Genesis repaints once the candle that created the signal has closed. So, when the M15 candle is closed, if the 3 arrows are on the M5 chart, they are there for ever.

Hi Mark, With the EJ earlier, looking to the left it's quite obvious that the market is ranging. More recently it was in an even tighter range. When price breaks out of a range as EJ did. I don't trade the break-out as they often prove to be false breakouts. My ideal trading condition is like I posted on my Gold chart yesterday. I like to see the break-out with some momentum, followed by the price returning to the top of the range (even re-entering the range area) and then I will take the next signal in the same direction as the break-out. I believe that this is a very standard and proven method of trading. Of course, it can be frustrating when price zooms off without looking back as I don't get a chance to enter. But as well as missing some good trades, I miss a lot of poor ones.

--- 帖子 #7490 ---
Did anyone bother to do that worthwhile exercise? It wouldn't have worked on EY but CY was nearly textbook. This was posted at the time of the yellow line after we started talking about re-entry in a strong trend (this current trend started at the red line around 84.10) as some traders had been stopped at BE too early and seen the market power up without them. Pullbacks 1-3: 12.1 pips - 23.2 - 16.4 ----&gt; set your TSL at 23.2 + 5 (handful) = at least 28.2 pips below the most recent high. Pullbacks 4-6: 25.5 - 29.2 -29.8 On pure math yes you could have been stopped out but basic PA says that the first steps at the end of an uptrend is a LL (Lower Low) at the very least and we didn't get one (I probably should have mentioned that again but it's not always possible to target every posts to all the traders in here). To recap where to hide your SL (Trailing or not) in a strong uptrend: 1) at least below the most recent low (more important than 2)) 2) calculate the pullbacks in pips and have it at least below that number + a handful of pips. Shallow pullbacks tell you that traders are desperate to join the uptrend and they think/know that if they set their entries too low they might/will not get in.... 150+ pips on a M5 chart ! No Psar, MA ... can replace just a little bit of extra work!

--- 帖子 #7502 ---
Interesting stuff, well done The problem with statistics is that they can always be interpretated in a different way. Looking at your results I can see that When price broke S1, it also broke S2 38.87% of the time When price broke S2, it also broke S3 33.57% of the time When price broke R1, it also broke R2 40.63% of the time When price broke R2, it also broke R3 39.35% of the time So, particularly with the resistance in your results,there is statistically little difference of probable success between taking a long at R1 or R2. Price is likely to hit the next resistance approx 40% of the time in both cases. Using your stistics in another way, I wonder if it strengthens the case for simply setting SL to B/E when R1 is hit and letting the trade run. As an example There is 30 pips between DP and R1 and 30 pips between R1 and R2. You are very unlikely to enter a trade exactly on DP, so assume 10 pips above. If TP at R1 =20 pips profit Price then has a 40% chance of hitting R2 which will increase profit to 50 pips Of course, we have no idea how often price would come back to B/E before continuing on to R2. Also, if R2 is not hit, where/when to exit? Food for thought.

It's a great question &amp; I'm glad you asked it as I'm sure you were not the only one thinking that. . yes, since the 14th November EA is in an uptrend . but you can also argue that since the 8th October EA is in a downtrend . or that since mid August it is in an uptrend ..... Depending on what TF you look at you will get a different answer and that is the core of the problem but also the solution: you need to consider the right period for the TF that you are trading and if you are acting on M5 signals then (in my view) the last 24 hours chart is just about right to give you a good snapshot of where we are: any longer and you'll probably miss out on a lot of trades because you'll only consider long OR short (long in EA's case). This is what greeted me this morning when I got up and looked at the last 24 hours: I saw an uptrend on the left followed by a period of consolidation with a slight down bias (the PA was flat/going lower). As we know, a period of consolidation can mean 2 things: .the market is taking a rest before powering higher? .or the market is building up for a reversal? I didn't know which one, the same as everybody else lol. Then the H1 MTF-Arrow short came (yellow circle - 12 x M5 dots) and if you switch to the H1 TF, you will see that on the same hourly candle, the Genesis Matrix also went short. From that point, it was Genesis indicators (not my biased opinion lol) that were telling me (or at least hinting) that the market had turned Short: this was a great example because PA alone would not have made a convincing case for the Shorts at that time. PA then went up (countertrend) and by the time the next short M5 signal came, you could at least make a case that we might have a failed top (it was a LH - Lower High) and I jumped in because the M5 and M15 positions were both looking really good and we also had a bearish divergence on M5 and M15 + the RRR was ok too (SL just above 2382 with absolute minimum TP at the low of the consolidation (2350 area) with further ones at the DP (2341) &amp; yesterday's highs/lows at 2330 &amp; 2318

--- 帖子 #7534 ---
Ideally, I like to be able to identify a trend in the TF that I am trading, but I will often look at higher tf. If I see a trend in a higher tf, I will be more likely to give a trade a bit more room to breathe. I still like the good old 123 formations to identify possible trend reversals. 1 being a low, 2 a high, 3 a higher low and then a break of 2. Vice versa for possible bear trend reversals. My gold chart shows an example, I know this is basic stuff, but not everyone uses 123's. I like this one especially because level 2 was previous support acting as resistance and when price broke above it again strongly, it can often lead to a strong bull rally. Of course, I'm not what you could call an expert with trading M5 and realise that this type of analysis may not be so reliable as it is in H1 charts.
