In my time at Forex Factory I have seen many, many systems that were solid systems and they all morphed into a complete mess because people (mostly newbies) keep adding more and more indicators and make other changes like including Elliot Waves or Harmonic patterns etc etc etc. Take a look the systems threads and you can see that this is true and it does not need to happen. Imagine, you are a newbie and you come here and read the first 10 - 100 pages and learn the basics of the system. Then you start skipping pages (we all do) until you arrive at the last page and you see a system that bears little resemblance to the original system. Every man and his dog has added an indicator that they think will improve the system (with little or no testing), and have added all sorts of predictive pattern recognition analysis etc etc etc. Poor you.......you came and learned on a solid and profitable system, and what you see at the end of the thread is a complete mongrel of a system that is impossible to trade with and so you lose interest (and maybe money) and off you go to the next system where the cycle repeats. That will not happen here. The system has been thoroughly tested by many experienced traders and found to be reasonably easy to use *provided* the user has some FX knowledge and is prepared to learn. For those who already have a good understanding of the markets, it's a simple system that works very, very well. Any changes or additions to the system will be made my the Genesis Team......and you can rest assured that the team will have tested everything for a good period of time in all market conditions before it is released here, to you. Most of the indicators we see and test just do not measure up to the system at all, and end up in the trash can. Nothing has changed, this is the way it is on this thread. People who come here 12 months from now can and should expect to see the system largely unchanged, and any changes will be documented and added to Post #1. I think that's fair, don't you? So you may see me as too strict and grumpy or whatever, and that's fine. The important thing here is that the system maintains it's integrity, for the good of everyone.....you and me included. Learn the system, trade the system, make money, help others......but......don't attempt to change or modify the system. RJ

If I see a trend in H1 and am trading a trend in the same direction on M15, I will give the trade a bit more breathing space. The bottom line is that the market will go where it wants to go. An experiment for you to do when the market is closed on the weekend. First, read this post Then, download the template attached......you won't need any indicators that you don't already have. The template will look exactly like the attached screenshot. All you'll need to do is to adjust the setting on the Market Open Times indi for Euro Open and London Close.....that's important. Next, run the Trading simulator (Post #1) and load the attached template. Now.....between Frankie open and London close, mark (with a red vertical line) all the high probability entries that you see. Yes, there are no candles.....too bad......we are IFR flying. Enter when the 2 stochs agree with the Matrix. Exits will be tricky, as they are even with candles and pivots etc, but do your best.....you might like to exit when Matrix is all opposite or whatever. DO NOT ADD ANY INDICATORS to this template......don't cheat because you'll just be cheating yourself. When you have 'traded' a few days worth on the simulator......add the candles and total up your good entries and bad entries, and you may as well calculate you nett pippage taken. I think you will be surprised......you won't amass a ton of pips because exits are tricky, but you might surprise yourself on the number of good entries you can take. In my opinion, we (me included) can get too sucked in to what the candles are doing etc etc etc, and this exercise is a good one because you will learn to rely on your instruments (IFR), rather than looking out the window (VFR). Of course there will be shitty days like yesterday....that can't be helped......run a decent and honest test and see what you can learn. This is a good exercise to run a couple of times a month during the weekends. Edit: I just realised....the #mtf stoch may not run with the Trading Sim, so will have to run the standard M5 stoch on the M5 chart etc.....sorry.....I forgot about that. RJ

--- 帖子 #7604 ---
MT4 does not support MTF simulations. If you have data on screen for the MTF indicator/s, the data for it/them has been retrieved from the current history. So the MTF data will be showing you value for the indicator at the close of the candle up to 15 min before the close of the candle. This leads to very favorable results which cannot be reproduced live. One can get an approximate reproduction of the M15 stoch on the M5 time-frame by tweaking the settings of the standard stoch. A setting of 30,6,9 on M5 is probably close enough to show the OB/OS signal of the M15 11,3,3 stoch and should give a truer simulation result.

--- 帖子 #7673 ---
Yeah, there is a lot to take in, but we must do this analysis once a day to help prevent losses. For instance....why did the PA stop at R1?......apart from the fact that it was R1 I mean! So we look back and we see it stopped there just before Tokyo open. Why did it stop there? Lets look at a bigger chart TF. we look at the H1, and we don't see any apparent reason. So we look to the H4. AH HAH!!!!! About Nov 7 the PA also got turned back at the same level. Lets zoom out the chart some more......AH HAH....10th Oct and 15th Oct the PA also got turned around there. Scroll the chart left.....WOW.....got turned around 3 times in Sept (one with a bit of an overshoot). So now we know that this area is a problem for the PA, so we'd better not enter the trade.....in fact, we better make a note of this for next time we are at this level. So only once since since Sept has the PA just smashed through this level, and that was the bears on about 2nd Nov. The PA does what it always does and it came back and retested the level on 7th Sept.....and failed.....so the bears pushed it down another 200 pips. Betcha that when the bulls break this level, the PA will also come back and test the level, and if it holds, the bulls will have full control and it will be safe to enter longs to your hearts content. That's how it's done......it takes 10 minutes and it tells the story in detail of this 2850-ish level of s/r

--- 帖子 #7676 ---
Well it is a valid way to trade, but I think that for new traders it's probably better to avoid using the M1 charts if at all possible. Everything happens so fast on the M1 that it's easy to make mistakes. I do use M1......but only when I'm looking for an entry (or re-entry) during a long slow day long climb or fall of the PA, and the stoch is 'on the roof' on 'on the floor' and Genesis M5 &amp; M15 is not helping. The choices are to forget about the trade because I missed the best entry, or to take the riskier option of drilling down to M1 and looking for a valid entry *with the trend*. Other than that, I try to stay away from M1. M5/M15 or 5-15 gives plenty of opportunities, but you have to be patient and let the trades come to you......don't chase them. It's like trying to jump on a moving train as it's already leaving the station......you might be ok, but it;s a high risk thing to do and you might get hurt. Better to wait for the next train

--- 帖子 #7718 ---
The ratios on 5-15 &amp; 15-60 stategy are 3 &amp; 4 respectively, so ideally you'd want a H12 or H16 TF when trading the H4 charts but that's not available on standard MT so you're stuck with a 6 ratio and the Daily as your HTF (unless you use one of the "still unsatisfactory in my view" Custom TF Generators). We only use 11,3,3 with Genesis &amp; that would be the setting too on H4-D.

--- 帖子 #7719 ---
A couple of things on templates (for those who don't know) and on posting your charts (for those using non-standard Genesis ones): 1- once you have your chart set up exactly the way you want (including non-Genesis indicators if you have) ---&gt; right-click on an empty area of the chart ---&gt; Template ---&gt; Save Template ---&gt; give it the name you want ---&gt; click 'Save' 2- remove the offending (lol) indicators (don't worry you have saved your layout in step 1) &amp; when this is done repeat all the steps decribed in 1- but this time give your template a different name. 3- to switch between your different templates: ---&gt; right-click on an empty area of the chart ---&gt; Template ... and select the one you want from the list. You can now switch between various templates, add any templates to any FX pairs to easily have a uniform view across them all + you can now post your charts in here if you want any query answered.

--- 帖子 #7720 ---
Also, open any new chart (EU for example) and add a chosen template to it. Now click on 'Market Watch' (see picture below) and this will show you ALL the instruments available in your MT; if you can't see them all, right-click on 'Symbols' &amp; select 'Show All'. Drag &amp; drop any instrument (EY for example) from there onto your EU chart and the template will automaticaly change from EU to EY.

--- 帖子 #7721 ---
Note that when switching templates any objects that you have placed manually on the chart since last saving the template will be lost. Objects are trendlines, vertical lines, text etc

--- 帖子 #7743 ---
I place both the M5 stoch and M15 stoch in the same indicator window . Why? Because I believe it gives me very important information. When I'm long I want to see the M5 stoch above the M15 stoch at the time of entry or when I'm short I want to see the M5 stoch below the M15 stoch at the time of entry. Of course, stochastic placement is also always important (i.e., both timeframe stochs rising up from oversold or near oversold for longs and dropping from overbought or near overbought for shorts). I never take a trade without this arrangement. Suffice to say this has worked well for me. Although, I'm not attributing my successful trading only to the above guidelines but it sure does seem to keep me out of some otherwise losing trades.

Hi spark, I have been working to test Genesis system on higer TFs because I am not a full time trader and often I haven't time to follow PA on M5. The preliminary feedbacks are that Genesis works also on M15 very well to spot the entry point but the problem is the room to take profit. Let me explain better this point. When we work intraday pivots lines are our mainly reference levels and we try to jump from one to another. Because we need to have also a good R:R to be sure to make money consistently the ratio between SL (last swing) and TP (pivot level) must be &gt; 1-2 .... and this is the main issue I am facing with the M15 in the intraday activity (this problem is today worst than in the past becuase volatility is lower). Possible solutions to this issue are : Change exit strategy and use #2 or #3 (read 5-15 Genesis pdf) Work on higher TFs swings with tradional S/R analysis plus M15 Genesis to spot the entry Work on higher TFs trend following traditional TA plus Genesi signal The consequences of point 2 and 3 could be to have a trade open overnight (Olivia did it sometimes) and accept a lower win rate but with higher R:R. I am still investigating about possible alternatives. ciao wiz3003

--- 帖子 #7958 ---
This is an outline on how you can setup a strategy on any FX pairs/instruments using Genesis and how my train of thoughts went (yours might/will be different) in designing it. 1) EU H4 chart with basic Genesis template: I picked H4 because it’s the other end of M5/M15 trading and you can fit a full month worth of trades on 1 chart + it might be helpful to those who can’t spend all their time in front of their computer. Also, with any good system, the longer TFs should give more reliable signals and allow for less discretionary trading , which might be welcome by some. 2) Quickly I saw that most signals from the Matrix would have given some pips: this is obviously the basic of what to look for in any strategy (a lot more winners than losers) and it was not a surprise, it’s Genesis after all! These good entries are the yellow lines: the first one is when the Genesis matrix gave a signal and the 2nd one is the candle when the entry actually took place (see point 5) for full entries criteria/reasons). 3) But there were 3 trades (green lines) that instantly looked bad (the market turned the other way straight after the signals). 4) I looked if any of the other Genesis indicators (Stox H4 &amp; HTF Daily, HA candles, Arrow, MA…) could be a good filter to stop entering these trades and the answer was no so I removed them: if something doesn’t help on a chart, then it’s a hindrance and I remove it so it doesn’t take any of my attention away (+ these other Genesis indicators were mainly designed for the small TFs). 5) I then looked at basic PA and realised that on those 3 bad trades/signals, the market only marginally made a new high/low once and only by 2 pips à I had found my filter: don’t enter at the end of that H4 signal candle, but only enter on any of the following candles when the price makes a new high/low by 4 pips (I could have picked 3 really but an extra pip or 2 doesn’t hurt). 6) Then comes the time when I go into more details about all the trades using stats/math: numbers are more reliable than 'I think' or 'in my view' or ... I want to know for each trades how much the market goes against me before showing me a profit (Drawdown) and what is the maximum that the market will ‘show’ me for each trade (Best). This relationship between the 2 will help me decide what leverage to use in my trades (there’s no point trading with 10 lots if the statistics tells you that on each trades you’re likely to have a 50 pips Drawdown lol). 7) Drawdown will tell me what sort of SL I’ll need in future trades: on 7 out of 8 trades, it is between -17 &amp; -32 and that is a nice ‘grouping’: it shows me that there is some good consistency in the signals and that a SL around -35 should take care of nearly 90% (7/8) of the trades. There was 1 drawdown of -47 also so what should one do because you can’t just ignore the result that aren’t good? Increase the SL to -50 on all trades or keep it at -35 and risk 1 losing trade for every 8? The temptation is to go for -50 because the stats says then that you would not have a losing trade but these are only stats and we must remember that there is no such thing as 100% certainty in trading. Over 8 trades we would be risking -400 pips (as opposed to 280 pips) and that is too much because the 120 extra pips risked would cover nearly another 4 extra trades. The math says to stick with -35. 8) Best will tell me where to set my TPs: here we have 3 groups 29/38/42 &amp; 64/69/81 &amp; 157/170. Clearly you need multiple lots (or multiple minilots) to trade this in the best possible statistical way: 1 TP @ 25, 1 TP @ 60 &amp; the last @140/5. Taking all your profits in one go around 25 would barely give you a RRR of 1 and that is a bit low especially on a high TF like H4. All 3 TPs are a few pips short of the lower number in each groupings to trade conservatively and not greedily and make sue that those TPs are actually hit. 9) It will be important to carry on updating the lists of Drawdown &amp; Best because markets are rarely stagnant and if volatility increase/decrease the SLs &amp; TPs might need to be adjusted. There you have it: I know that we have many traders in the background that don’t participate much so here is your chance to add your little bit to Genesis and give something back. I'm always surprised at how few traders are in here at the weekend because a lot of the better &amp; more productive work is done then when there are no open markets to distract you. So ... find a pair that you like or that you trade, get the trade statistics in a similar format and hopefully the numbers will be such (they might not be – maybe H4 EU was lucky but I honestly don’t think so) so that you can devise your own strategy, submit it in the thread, get it discussed and help other traders along. Also feel free to ask any question about the above if I have not been clear enough. Remember this is just a start but I feel you could trade quite well out of it as it is but improvements can come from: .using the Weekly (not Daily) Pivots as help to TPs because these trades can last for a few days .better entry points by using a lower TF to pin point entries after the H4 signal .rather than using 'Best' you can make a note of intermediate TPs for each trades and have a different set of numbers to devise your exit strategy. …. --- 帖子 #7989 ---
You're suggesting well Pete On the subject of differing Stochastic (I know that there are now zillions of versions floating around), please make sure that: .MA Method is set to 0 or Simple .MA PriceField is set to 0 or Low/High .Fixed Minimum &amp; Maximum are set to 0 &amp; 100 respectively (in the 'Common' tab) The last one is sometimes forgotten.... Also during very quiet time in the Oz/Kiwi/Tokyo session, when price is really not moving, it is normal to have a different matrix because of the slightly different prices: very little movement ---&gt; matrix indicators will gravitate towards their median levels (generally the 0 level) ---&gt; it doesn't take much for one to go to +0.01 and give a white square (up) with one broker and one to go to -0.01 for a red square (down) with a different broker. Think of it as a very flat MACD line hovering near 0 and it can easily flip from up to down with each candle and I believe that in this instance, brokers' difference is enough.

--- 帖子 #8008 ---
Hi Silat, For sure 15% is a lot but I think that most traders have smaller spread on the instruments that they trade. Although you're right that it is a 'cost' against you at the end of the day/week/month... you are looking at it the wrong way. Take people who trade indices in the US for example (Dow Jones, S&amp;P...): most don't have a spread at all but they pay comissions on opening and closing trades. Which one is best depends on so many parameters (leverage, frequency of trading...) that I don't think that you can say one is better/cheaper than the other just like that. These costs (spread or comission or both) are just what's called "the cost of doing business" and you got to live with it: trading is a business (for most of us) and all businesses have associated costs in one area or the other (renting office space, buying stocks before selling it, paying staff wages...). If your trading strategy is good enough then these costs won't matter. Just because one is able to make some money with 2 clicks of a mouse, you can't expect everything to be free. The old saying "there's no such thing as a free lunch" also applies in trading. If you don't like paying the spread then set yourself up as a broker and 'earn' the spread from all those trading with you. Of course then, you'll also have to cover yourself against all the winning trades that they have as these will be your losses. See, even on the other side the lunch isn't free...

--- 帖子 #8061 ---
Even if you aim for 10/day......that is still good. It's important to have an achievable goal not a goal that is out of reach because that will have all sorts of negative consequences. If you can get 10/day......then later you can shoot for 15/day, then 20....25.....30....40.....50 etc Of course there will be losses, that's the way this business goes, but you will also get days where you make double your goal, or triple you goal, and that helps offset the losses and keep the 'batting average' in check

--- 帖子 #8148 ---
Hi Scarlet Correct. Sorry for the misunderstanding: I was just posting the stats as they are on the H4 chart rather than the result of yet another great 'after the event' trade (for the record, I didn't take this trade as I was busy elsewhere). The original post was just to outline the potential of a fairly straightforward (with hardly any discretion) strategy because at a glance, Genesis looked profitable on H4 but I'm still collecting data for it as 12 signals aren't enough for a full strategy. Bear in mind that H4 charts do not give the full 'live' picture but they reflect only a possible 'worst case' scenario: when you look at the H4 entry candle (not the signal one), you have no way of knowing if on that H4 candle the entry was activated before the drawdown or vice versa. You have to zoom down to the lower TFs to get the true number and on this occasion the 'real' drawdown was only -3/4 pips and not -46! The point is that if a strategy already looks good on a worst case scenario basis then you're likely to be able to refine it and make it more profitable when you have the full dataset. My mistake Matrix: the last line (in bold) should have read: 06.12 00.00 1.3044 1.3040 -46 +164 (now corrected and correctly stated by Scarlet)

--- 帖子 #8153 ---
They are both fine: when you switch to the Daily chart, the daily stox is now the red/white (it was red/green on H4) and the weekly stox is now the red/green. I've drawn yellow lines to show the same time actually elapsed on both charts and you can see that the shape of the Daily Stox is the same... This must be because you are using one of the MTF Stox that automatically add the higher TF as you switch between TFs: I prefer not to use that feature as it's harder (impossible?) to keep a standard look across TFs (for example, I like my M15 stox to always be 'yellow' in all the TFs I look at). The simplest solution to check any MTF-Stochastic : open a new blank chart and add the standard metatrader Stochastic Oscillator with the right settings (11,3,3-high/low-Simple-0/minimum/100/maximum) and they should match; if they don't match then you have not set the MTF-Stox properly.

--- 帖子 #8222 ---
Jamz, A little clue re fakeouts. About half an hour prior to a significant news events, if you get a sharp move against your HTF stochs, and the stochs dont react, also check your H1 &amp; H4 charts, then with the news, PA then pivots back in the direction of your HTF charts, you will also probably get a Genesis arrow or two. It happened perfectly on last Fridays NFP, EJ had sold off all day, then 30 mins prior to news, you had the exhaustion leg, and the M15 stochs diverged beautifully. I didnt trade it, because it was an especially sensitive news release, but it showed off a perfect fakeout. Earlier on Friday GU did exactly the same, which I got. It is important when stochs move in line with price, and it is just as important when price moves and stochs dont !! Re currencies, I would suggest losing that quickly, have no attachments to any currency or pair, if your signals indicate a trade, enter, no emotions !! Dont question why something is moving, or the the event which triggered it, just trade your signals.

Bear in mind that: .my charts &amp; data are based on the 5PM EST (NY) = UK 22.00 being the end/start of each day, and different brokers around the world will show different stats to mine because they will have different starts/ends to each H4 candles. For anyone of you out there, I'd like to hear from anyone who has different (better or worse) results from the H4 strategy because they are not in the same time zone as me (don't be shy). .it's up to anyone if they want to only trade ETT or look at all the signals: I provided all the signals because a H4 strategy is a high TF strategy and should be less sensitive to signals being generated during any 'quiet' periods (Asian + late US session). .another way to look at the DrawDown is to try to be clever about it and actually enter when the stats suggest that we are near the maximum DD once a full signal has been generated. The danger is that you wait for too good an entry and ends up missing on the trade (as usual, no free lunch in trading....) Please just post all your stats for that period in a similar format to mine if you can so that I can have a look (no point me re-doing the work that you have just done). Markets move all the time and EU's behaviour will change as the weeks pass by and given the choice I will give more validity to the current/recent data rather than older data. Also, remember that the original post was really about how to collect data and devise a possible strategy: traders with different risk appetites will view the same data in a completely different way so I'm always interested in how anyone else would trade it (again, no need to be shy, we're all friends in here)

Hi James, For all the trades, start collecting the "along the way TPs" in stat/excel format and all being well you should start to see some of the numbers 'group' together; use these number areas as TPs or devise an exit strategy around them. See this example for GY (this sort of extra work is needed for most Yen/Sterling/more volatile pairs). http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...03#post6294203 Also, when using the FXI Pivots, in the 'input' tab, set the 'maxWeeks' number to at least 8 or 12 so that you can still have all your pivots showing on the charts 2 or 3 months later/earlier for additional TPs work (there might be a decent strategy around these - which would make sense considering that they are a core part of Genesis, so the TF should not matter). Let me/us know how you get along. Cheers

--- 帖子 #8454 ---
Re: Genesis system on the H4 I have been looking at the H4 charts on other pairs as well. Pairs that trend most of the time seem to do well on H4, such as EURJPY and EURAUD. I have come to realise that on higher time frames, the CCI period 20(2nd row of matrix) is a bit slow. Period CCI 20 seems to work well on lower time frames to keep out of fake entries. Most of the time CCI14 and CCI20 change color on the same candle, but on a few occasions CCI20 is late by one candle to have better entry on H4. I have also played around with Stoch settings for H4 and 14,4,6 seems quite good. The places where the stoch comes from the overbought or the oversold match well the genesis signals. I am posting a screen shot of entries on EURJPY for from Oct 1, 2012 to Jan 3 ,2013. Entries : Solid blue line : BUY entry triggered at +4 pips away from the high of the signal candle. Solid red line : SELL entry triggered at -4 pips away from the low of the signal candle. Dotted blue line : BUY signal that wouldn't have been triggered with a pending order of +4 pips above the high of the signal candle Dotted red line : sell signal that wouldn't have been triggered with a pending order of -4 pips under the low of the signal candle Notes: most signals seem to go into profit right away. Some signals go into a small profit (10 - 20 pips), then retrace, go into drawdown and then go back into profit. I guess it all depends of where the SL is placed if the order is closed in profit or not. Exits : - close trade when TVI changed color and the candle closed. It seems to keep the trade in profit longer and ride the trend when one is in place. - close trade when full matrix closed with opposite color, kind of like a signal to signal trading This is just a visual backtest, without exact data like Oli's, but I hope it can help others

As per your request: In Dollar and in Yen, you can change the daily pip target by adjusting the number in the yellow box below the daily pip target column you will need to adjust your pip value based on your home currency in the yellow box below the pip value column you also will need to adjust your starting capital by changing the number in the first row below the Opening Balance Column The closing balance of the 50th week is in the green box below the closing balance column Hope this helps

Wiz has answered pretty accurately....thanks wiz Generally speaking I enter trades off the M5 chart and I flick between the M5 and M15 to get an idea of what has been/or what is, going on today. The M15 shows the short term trend and it's good to be trading in this direction.....however, I will take counter trend trades when all the indicators say so.....after all.....it can't go in one direction for ever! Mostly these counter trend trades are triggered by a historical support/resistance line or a an important round number etc. If you look back on some of my charts posted you will see where I use the H1, H4, Daily and even Weekly charts to spot strong area's of support and resistance which *might* be a turning point for the market. When I see these area's a plot them on my charts (and sometimes post them here) and keep them ready to see what happens when the PA approaches it. Here is a recent example post.

Hello, Jamz! That is what I was exactly thinking yesterday, after London close. But when I took a look on chart again and made a little "backtesting", I realized that all I had to do to make good green pips is just follow the rules - nothing more.. Let's take a look on yesterday eurusd chart. I've marked all possible entries by vertical blue lines. So, below is what we have (times in GMT): 1. 6.05 am. Buy signal. For me it's perfect signal - both stoch pointed up from OS zone, little stop (about 12 pips, if we would place it below DS1 pivot, or just 8 pips if we would place it below previous low). But it was too early - one hour before Frankfurt open. So we don't take this trade. 2. 7.30 am. Buy signal. m5 stoch has been in OB just before, m15 stoch is still liying there. Signal candle closed right below Daily pivot, so no trade. 3. 8.30 am. Sell signal. Both stoch were in perfect positions. Candle closed below Daily pivot. Arrow appeared at the same time. One thing that would forced to doubt is that the price was going up since pre-Frankfurt open. I would be waiting for LH in that situation, which price did - it was actually just a very little wave, but let's say that we judge it as LH and take the trade. I would place SL above previous high + 2 pips for about 14 pips. 4. 9.05 am. We see buy signal, but m15 stoch is still going down from OB. So I would not do anything and keep waiting. 5. 9.30 am. Ok, now m15 stoch started to point up, m5 stoch is not in perfect position, but it didn't visit OB zone and crossed in a right way. Candle closed above DP, so for me it's enough to reverse at that point. I would close my previous short position with -10 pips loss and open long. Stop loss below previous low for about 16 pips. Starting from this point we would have two possible scenarios: 1) we would take a profit at DR1 (23 pips) or at RN (1,31 - 30 pips) and when the trade is closed - waiting for another opportunities; 2) we would move our SL at BE and let the trade run. Imagine, that we chose first, closed position at DR1 for 23 pips and started waiting for any other signals: 6. 12.10 pm. Sell signal. Stoch m5 is ok, but stoch m15 is still in OB zone. R1 pivot is only 5 pips below, so no trade. 7. 12.45 pm. Buy signal. Stoch m5 is good, but stoch m15 is going down from OB zone. No trade. 8. 13.40 pm. Buy signal. Both stoch pointed up, but already in OB region. Signal candle closed just below R3 (5-7 pips). Stop loss would be very big (about 50 pips), so no trade. 9. 15.20 pm. Buy signal. Stoch m15 still lying in OB zone, stop loss is big enough (35 pips), and the price has already gone around 160 pips since FO, so it's not a good trade anyway. So, my conclusion is: in worst scenario we would took 23-10=13 pips. Not too much, of course, but pips are pips )) Only thing I can say that we don't have anything we need to worry about )) And I'm sure that we would choose better scenario №2, which would bring absolutely another result )) Of course, you are right, that when we see the picture after it's finished - it seems easier. But in my analyses I tried to be objective as much as possible ) As for me, I decided to trade right on this way - follow the rules and my personal plan, keep it as simple as possible and don't complicate anything.. Have a nice weekend to all!!!

OK artem, my 2 cent concerning stoch indi. As RJ already said tons of times trader has to interpret this tool and this is not just an oversold or bought indicator. When we have a strong trend in place it is right to have the stochastic in the overextended area (if you study the stoch formula this is clear) and a possible tactics is just to enter according to the lower TF stoch signal (in our case combined with genesis matrix). So what to do? Personally I like let the PA rules (it is the king) and if the trend is strong (long bars in one direction and small in the opposite way or strong MA5 slope) I don't care much about the M15 stoch position unless I see a divergence , we are close to pivots, S/R or price already run a lot of miles. Obviously not always it is simple to re-enter in a trend and personally I prefer to be first to take the train if I can. ciao wiz

MT4 can be a pain for moving SLs and TPs, however somewhere along the way I picked up these two scripts (attached) that make it so much easier. Once you install the scripts, just drag the script named "ASL Set-Move" onto your chart where you want the Stoploss to be placed and it takes care of it. Same for using "ATP Set-Move" for placing the Take Profit level. I use them both all the time for adjusting my trades. By the way, those are scripts, so place the files in your experts\scripts folder. Be sure to test them in Demo before using them for real.

--- 帖子 #8668 ---
I'm on NY time, and I have a daytime job, so trading the London session can be sleep-depriving. I have devised a means to trade it without staying up in the wee hours watching bars paint (or paint dry, same thing). I keep my trading station running 24x5, on which I have MT4 with the typical Genesis charts for the pair I am currently trading (EURUSD) in the M5, M15 and H1 timeframes. These are the basic steps that allow me to get some sleep and yet not miss all the good trades at the same time: 1) I have my MT4 email link setup to send to my cellular phone, which behaves exactly like a normal text message. I have ATT here in the States, so I setup the MT4 email (Tools-&gt;Options-&gt;Email tab) to send from a freebie Mail.com account (which allows sending emails via SMTP) to my cell-phone-number @ txt.att.net (see the attached image below for setup). 2) I enable email alerts on the M5 Matrix (and disable it on the M15 and H1). This will let The Genesis matrix send me text messages whenever there is a normal M5 matrix signal. Note: those alerts do not account for the current configuration of the M5 and M15 stochastics, and that is the reason for the next piece of the puzzle. 3) I keep an iPad on my nightstand that has a useful app installed: a windows Remote Desktop emulator (I forget the actual name of the app but there are many available for the iPad, and I am using one of the free ones). I have configured that app to connect to and control my trading station, which is located on the other side of my house (not convenient for a quick check of the charts). So, with a couple of taps on the iPad screen, I can see the desktop from my trading station, including Mt4 and all that. Pretty nifty. So, at 3:45 in the morning, when EU is making a run (Genesis matrix signal) I will get a text message on my cell phone, which I keep next to the iPad. The text message sound wakes me up, I grab the iPad, and in about 15 seconds I can see the chart in all its glory, without ever leaving the bed. If it is a bad signal (poorly aligned Stochastics, against a Pivot, etc), the iPad and me just go back to sleep. If it looks like a valid signal, meeting all the criteria for a good trade, only then do I get out of bed and go to the desktop PC. Note: I could install Metatrader onto the iPad, but I doubt the Genesis indicators could be installed. If you wanted, you could trade from iPad based upon the chart you just looked at from the desktop, entirely without leaving the bed. However, I prefer to initiate the trade from the desktop as I am more comfortable with its controls. Enhancements Now I will talk about some ways I have enhanced the above to make it even better. The way I am currently trading Genesis is to focus on only the trades that are in the direction of the main trend (over the last day or two) and only within active trading sessions (LO to LC, mainly). I am a professional software developer since 1985 and I have done a good bit of development in MQL (Metatrader language), so I have made some modifications to the Alerts section of the Genesis Matrix. Before RJ or anyone else erupts, I have not touched the way Genesis works from a signaling standpoint or its appearance on a chart at all - I have only tinkered with filtering the alerts it generates after the signals are computed. First, I added time-of-day limitations to when Alerts could be emailed. I only want to trade London Open to London Close for now (may expand to Frankie later), and I don't want to get alerted to signals that may happen during the early hours before Frankfurt, or late NY. So I added some parameters and a tiny bit of logic that prevents the alerts from being sent via email except during the time periods I specify via the new parameters - basically a From-To arrangement of hours and minutes such as from 07:55 to 18:35. Secondly, I added a trend alignment limitation to when Alerts could be emailed. I use a simple longer-period MA and only allow alerts to be emailed when price is aligned with the trend indicated by the MA (Above/Below). This MA does not display on the chart, it is only used in a calculation to determine if the alert should be allowed. Neither of those mods will affect the core function of Genesis at all - only the email alerts. I will be forwarding my modifications to Xaphod for consideration of inclusion into the official matrix indicator should he and the other core team members decide to do so. I do not plan to share it here myself unless requested to do so by RJ and the other core team members. Here's to more sleep and fewer missed London-session trades! Edit: For the iPad to be able to control your desktop computer, you will need a home network that supports wifi, so the iPad is on the same network as your desktop PC.

*** VISUAL EXPLANATION OF THE STOCH *** I would like to give a little contribution about the stoch behavior (particularly when there is a trend) without any math formula but just in a visual way to help young traders and anyone who doesn't like math. This doesn't want to be an exhaustive explanation and I hope not to offend experienced traders and expecially my friend RJ ... please don't ban me after this We need to make a window with the amount of bars we want to take under control. In genesis model we use a 11 period stoch (see red bubbles in the pic). Then we move these window every time the bar closes and change the height according to the new low or high. In this way at every bar close we can draw a 11 bars wide box with height = (HIGH –LOW). Well .... the stochastic is the position of last bar close in percentage of the box height. Example: Low = 1,3010 High =1,3033 Close =1,3015 ===&gt; Stoch = 21% In this pic we can look at a couple of examples.

--- 帖子 #8710 ---
Another example of stoch calculation without formula.

--- 帖子 #8711 ---
The problem in this way is that the curve we achieved is very nervous … therefore we prefer to smooth it introducing a simple moving average (bold blue line in the pic). The parameter which helps us to smooth the stoch is “slowing”. In the genesis model we use 3 which means a simple MA3 periods.

--- 帖子 #8712 ---
Finally if we remove the original curve we get the smoothed signal curve …

--- 帖子 #8713 ---
At the end Mr.Lane introduced another curve which is a simple MA of this signal (red line in the pic) and developed some entry rules based on these two curves.

--- 帖子 #8714 ---
What happens when the trend is strong? We will find a sequence of windows with long bars in the direction of the trend and some congestion zones (countertrend areas) …… a picture is better than 1000 words

--- 帖子 #8758 ---
Hello, nikz! RN (especially, big RN - *.*1000, *.*2000 etc.) is a reasonable point for exiting. But, if you want to let your trade run or if you have another target for TP, you can take a note of what I usually do. If I have an open trade, already in profit and price went up to the round number - I'm starting to watch closely at what price is doing: 1. If price passed through a RN without hesitation with a good move, I will tighten my SL at 4-5 pips above/below RN. 2. If candle closed right on RN or 1-2 pips below/above it (and candle is not a pinbar and not very small), I will tighten my SL at few pips above/below of 50% of the candle. 3. If candle closed right on RN or 1-2 pips below/above it and it's a pin, I will tighten SL above/below pin, or even close it manually (depends on profit amount and my mood ). You can also find an examples below. Sometimes it works well, sometimes it doesn't, but in general it's working pretty well for me personally. Hope it helps. P.S. Please take a note that I'm using this method only when I'm in good profit already, because if you get out from trades too soon and very often - it's not good for your MM.

I'm just about done for the day, I might not even bother with NY session today as daily target is already reached. However, after reading back on our thread I came across the Currency Strength Meter. Henry Liu has a similar one on his website that runs for the desktop, but this one runs from MT4. As you can see on the screenshot, it lists the strongest currency at the top and the weakest at the bottom. So, in the attached example, you would want to be trading JPY against GPB (which I did hee hee hee), but you would not want to be trading 2 strong currencies against each other like JPY and NZD, or 2 weak currencies against each other like EUR against GPB. Ideally you would watch this indi at various session open times, or at any other time when you see an entry signal. Set the 'inputs' to 35, 35, False Have a play with it.

--- 帖子 #8817 ---
You're welcome. I try and post only the best charts that meet the Genesis criteria, but I do take other trades as well, but I don't and won't post them. I know others do the same. The thing about system trading is that it is not an exact science.....if it was, I would create an EA and retire a rich man!! There was a muppet here a while back who spat the dummy because he couldn't see that this is not, and never will be an exact science. For instance, what is 'overbought?'......is it once the '80' line is crossed?.......what if it only gets to '79?'......does that mean that it isn't overbought?.....technically yes, that's what it means. However, the ebb and flow of the oscillator (and the pa for that matter) does not necessarily adhere to our human rules! That's why we have to use our discretion. If you're uncomfortable doing that, then sit the trade out until a perfect trade comes along, and it will. Eventually, if you keep at it, you will develop this discretion as well, just as we do when we learn to drive, or swim, or anything else.

--- 帖子 #8849 ---
Ok got it working again properly this time. If you have a suffix you need to add it to the chart names under this heading in the mq4 file: string CoppiaValuta[] = there is a long list of chart names just add the suffix to those and recompile and it will work.

--- 帖子 #8851 ---
Often they add a suffix if you are getting a cash rebate. That way they can identify the trades and widen the spread and recapture the cash back piece (in whole or in part). I dont know if this is the case here, however I discovered that a couple of years ago with a broker I was using at that time. They admitted to me that was what they were doing.

If all 7 agree, then the trade is a high probability trade and stands a good chance to succeed. SL is always place above/below the previous swing high/low and it doesn't get hit very often. The system will work for all time frames with no settings that need to be changed. Because it is prudent to see other time frames action, particularly if trading the M5 or m15, it would be extremely annoying to have to change settings to suit the TF. --- 帖子 #8878 ---
Thanks!! Lastingwell, I got it and I have successfully created H12 sochastic and it is working awesome. For, the one who don't know how to do it they should download the indicator provided by lastingwell here. And then just save this indicator to your indicators folder and open a H4 chart and load this indicator by changing the input of this indicator setting of multiplier to 3. Now, a H12 offline chart is created. Now, go to file menu of your mt4 and load this offline chart from file--&gt; Offline chart ----&gt; Eur/Usd H12. Now, open Xaphod's MTF sochastics indicator v2.0 in MetaEditor and enter : case 720: IndicatorName="Period H12"; break; and then compile it. Now go, back to your H4 chart and change the settings of MTF sochastics to 720 timeframe and thus you will get a period H12 sochastics. mazprofx.:nerd:

Pivots are a kind of 'self fulfilling prophesy' ....... because pivots are in such widespread use, the PA often stops at those levels because (collectively) we make it happen. Same sort of thing for fibs. Also, sometimes you look at a correlated cross like (for example) EJ and CJ. One might seem to stall mid stream, and a look at it's correlated pair(s) shows a pivot holding up proceedings. There are a great many pivot trading specialists 'out there' and I was taught by one of them. I know there are the occasional muppet who state as a fact that "pivots don't work", but the facts really are, that they do.....that's why the whole world uses them!!

--- 帖子 #8939 ---
Hi Traders, Last year,after I discovered RJ, I spent few weeks to study Pivot Levels because he continued to tell me that these are very important key levels for a day trader and because I “ need ” to understand what I do or use I tried to figure out why some people made the decision to usethe below formulas to calculate every day these levels. · Central Pivot Point (DP) = (High+ Low + Close) / 3 First level support and resistance: · First Resistance (DR1) =(2*P) - Low · First Support (DS1) =(2*P) - High Likewise,the second level of support and resistance is calculated as follows: · Second Resistance (DR2) = P +(R1-S1) · Second Support (DS2) = P -(R1- S1) Pivot Points in a Nutshell Pivot Pointsare calculated Price Levels that the floor traders, and those who read thetape, like to watch during the trading session. In general, if the day's PriceAction starts above the "Pivot", it will tend to stay above the Pivot(also called the "fulcrum" of the day's activity). On such aday, Resistance will be met at Price Level R1. Should R1 be broken, furtherResistance will be expected at R2. The story is all reversed, of course, if theprice action is below the Pivot. Support will be met at Price Level S1. ShouldS1 be broken, further Support will be expected at S2. If, afterstarting the day above the Pivot, the Price crosses back through the Pivot, thePivot will act as a Resistance area. Pivot Points and Levels are Support and Resistance levels, and behave exactly like any historical Support and Resistance level. That's Pivots in a nutshell ! ( edit by : http://tradingthingys.com/PitPivotPoints.pdf ) Here you can find also a list of interesting sites where to find the usual things about these levels: http://www.investopedia.com/articles/forex/05/fxpivots.asp http://www.babypips.com/school/how-to-calculate-pivot-points.html http://stockcharts.com/help/doku.php?id=chart_school:technical_indicatorspivot_points O K, very interesting … but still I don’t understand why they work and I verify any day they work; is it just “self-prophecy” (like Fibo levels)? But in this case why these formulas and not another way to determine them? Finally light turn on in my mind thinking about the old guys in the Pit without PC or other sophisticated tools to analyze the market, They knew the Fibonacci levels but they couldn’t calculate them easily and quickly without PC …. Hence what to do? The following ideas are original and based on math … you can’t find them in the web IMHO they simply invented a roughly way to estimate the Fibo levels by using just few data: · YesterdayLow · YesterdayHigh · YesterdayClose Without getting you bored with math have a look at the below pic …. What is a dailybar? In general we can say that it is simply the last swing (in the pic I drew a long day bullish).

--- 帖子 #8940 ---
Well if we suppose that Close = High and change this in the pivot formulas you get that DPivot = Low + 66% DR While if Close = ½ High = 50% last swing we get DPivot = Low + 16% DR Therefore we can say that DP is a level moving in a range which depends on the close of the previous day whose boundaries are 34% to 80% from High if Close doesn’t go below the middle of the swing (Bullish bar) Do these numbers remember you something ? …. You are right : Fibonacci levels! Is it helpful to know that? I think yes. Indeed now we can understand better the pivot behavior. Let me say that if YDAY bar was a long bullish bar we should expect to have DP close to 38% fibo and if today will be another bullish bar this could be a good support. But if the YDAY bar was spin (range day) and the momentum is low the power of fibo &amp; pivot is weaker and we could expect some DP breakout …. Does it make sense now? All the considerations done are the same if we have a bearish bar of course. Ah … I forgot! and pivot S/R? I don’t want to get you bored with these topics but if you do the math you will discover that there are also Fibo expansions …. eh eh eh. Have a greatweek end Ciao Wiz P.S. only for math fanatics: If C=H and H=L+DR à DP =(2H+L)/3 = (2L+2DR+L)/3 = 3L+2DR=L+2/3DR = Low+66%DR If C=1/2 DR and H=L+DR à DP =[H+2L-1/2(H-L)]/3 = (1/2L+1/2DR+5/2L)/3 = (3L+1/2DR)/3 = L + 1/6DR = Low + 16%DR

--- 帖子 #9025 ---
For anyone who is interested, some interesting news: We are coming to the end of what has been a pretty dramatic month in FX. Volatility was at multi-year lows towards the end of last year in currency markets as a whole, but what was happening was that correlations were declining, between certain currency pairs and against other asset markets. This has continued this month with a vengeance, but markets have also become a lot more trended (sterling, yen, Swiss franc weakness, euro strength). This could make for a fairly choppy and unpredictable month end as institutional investors look to re-weight cross-currency investments, or reduce exposure to what have been profitable trades. This could make the yen and sterling at risk of some short-covering activity. But in the bigger picture, it’s shown an FX market a lot more sensitive to varying domestic conditions, something which should continue for the coming months. USD: Gave back some of the gains of the previous day, for no good reason other than JPY and GBP short-covering and continued euro-repatriation. That said, if the economic news over coming days is on the stronger side of expectations, then we expect the dollar to make some forward progress. JPY: Trading the yen from the short side seems less simple in recent days, as those pre-disposed to take some money off the table jostle with those late to the game. Looking at the price action this week, there appears to be a greater equilibrium between buyers and sellers right now. That said, still plenty of potential for the yen to slide further next month, with the G20 meeting mid-month sure to stimulate discussion of currency wars. EUR: Breaking above the 1.35 level in early European trade and seems unstoppable right now, boosted by euro-repatriation, month-end flows, and the fact that the ECB’s balance sheet is shrinking (at least for now). Higher levels appear in prospect against most major currencies in the short term. GBP: January has been a shocker for sterling, but yesterday there was some short-covering and month-end flow that steadied things. Right now, it is hard to see where the good news is going to come from, given uncertainty over the UK’s relationship with Europe whilst fiscal policy is not achieving its objectives quickly enough.

Nice analysis wiz......for what it's worth, on decent runs like the one you documented I try to manually trail my SL until eventually I will get knocked out in profit. I know that's not the scientific way to do it, but when I can't find a reason to exit, like s/r, round number etc, that's what I do. As we've discussed before, the exits are always harder than the entry, and I don't believe there is a perfect way to do it. Some set a target and they exit at their target regardless of everything.....and that's ok. Others have other methods. I don't know f there's a right or wrong way, as Kely says, when you have a decent profit, there's nothing wrong with exiting and pocketing your pips

--- 帖子 #9184 ---
As its ok with realjumper I will post it here. Download the attached indicator basket v6 and open in meta editor you will see a list of different baskets (1, 2 etc) up to 14. You can either go with what they have there or choose your own so for instance on the 2-basket I have in there EJ and EU. Then compile it put it on a chart (one from the basket) check allow dll is ticked then under inputs put the amount in your basket so for the 2 basket I have 2 then maxbars 1000 then timeframe 5 do that for every timeframe you want to open. I have done that for every timeframe including monthly because i like to use the pivots indicator with monthly pivot etc so I want it all there. Then go to file -&gt; open offline and you will see Kos#02 (if using the 2 currency basket) and the different timeframe charts. Just open them and load your indicators on as you usually would. To put on a trade I use Tradehedgebuy2 and tradehedgesell2 (install under experts/scripts). The stop loss is taken care of by the MPBM EA (use the same magic number you will be using in the scripts and thats it. For the 5 minute chart I use 40 pips as the stop loss it will close the trades when the 2 pairs between them come to -40. The best way is to try with the 2 basket and then play around on demo. I dont want to clutter the thread though so if you have a problem with any of it send me a pm. It sounds complicated but once youve done it once you will get to know what to do.

--- 帖子 #9199 ---
For anyone who's interested.....you will know how important it is to have accurate pivots, and the lack of uniformity between brokers server times, Sunday candles etc etc makes this a pain in the ass. That is why I have resorted to manually adding the pivots to my charts and I use the data from the actionforex pivot table because I know it's accurate. The downside to that is that I can't go back, even one day, and check yesterdays pivots if I am doing some testing or whatever.....and that's why I used to use the FXiPivots indi in the zip file on Post #1. Anyway, I don't trade off MT4, I just use it for charting. I have now found that FXPro sets their server time correctly and (as far as I know, but I will check next week) they don't use the dreaded Sunday candle. So......when I apply the FXiPivots indi I find that the pivots are absolutely correct in accordance with actionforex table. The only variance is in the 5th digit of the pivot which is of no real consequence anyway. Oh....apparently the demo account never expires either. So....perhaps this will be an end to the Pivot error issue that keeps on popping up.

--- 帖子 #9219 ---
The overall trend is up on EJ and every other Yen cross. Check out an H1 or H4 chart. The bear run was a pull back, or a retrace. The retrace was the counter trend trade, but it was a long slow and steady one, so it was easy to trade. To trade long is to go with the overall trend. Still have to be cautious because we won't know a retrace from a reversal until after it happens, but everything is pointing towards the Yen getting weaker and the Euro getting stronger, so it's fairly safe to assume that the overall bull trend is going to continue. It IS experience, but also it's a matter of checking the other timeframes to see what's going on, as well as knowing a little about each currency of the pair. So I like to know a little about what's driving the Euro, as well as what's driving the Yen. That's the reason why it's good to stick to one or two currency pairs to start with.....so that you can get to know a lot about the 2 currencies and what drives them. For instance, I know virtually nothing about the Canadian dollar, so I won't attempt to trade it.

That's very honest of you to admit that. I agree the concept of Euro strength, is conceptually difficult to get your head around, except the fact that currencies are a zero sum game. So comparatively, if ECB are not undertaking conventional QE, and US and Japan are going full guns blazing, comparatively that makes the Euro strong. QE is the "elephant in the room" at the moment - thats why GBP is weak - QE and a weak economy. What Japan is threatening to do, is a multi-decade game-changer - so after decades of strength, it is now being a lot weaker, QE/trade deficits/weak economy - strength - what strength ?? The trade deficit, has real consequences on demand for Yen. As I stated yesterday, once the strong Euro wreaks havoc on the EU economies, watch the Euro capitulate, but until then whatever logic tells you, just follow your charts. Another example is the number of times Genesis will give a correct signal just prior to or on major news release, that is usually because the buying/selling pressures by big banks taking positions sends us signals. So during trading hours, I switch off my economic mind, and switch on my traders mind - that is absolutely critical. I even "talk" to my "trading persona", going over and over my signals ticking them off prior to a potential setup. My wife is constantly joking with me for talking to myself (she tells me I am mad!! - maybe I am ??), I ignore everything else, just trading signals, over and over again. That is all that matters. We are technical traders (especially on these timeframes), not fundamental traders - so why consider fundamentals during trading ??

I don't know if it's something in the water at the moment, but it seems that everyone on FF wants to see either 'live trades' or a Trade Explorer or else those people think that we are all liars. In fact anyone who makes a profit *without* first showing their trade live or using a Trade Explorer *MUST* be a liar. The question of live trades has been asked and answered already. In fact it used to be on Post #1, and I'm going to put it back there! Lastingwell has hit the nail on the head.......and I have said the same thing myself countless times. When I enter a trade I will not post here, answer emails, answer Skype messages, answer the phone, go to the toilet or anything else. My only interest is to manage my trade. When I have the SL safely in profit I may post my entry....and sometimes I do. As the trade develops, I may post an update, and I may not. I may be looking for another trade.....I may have entered another trade and am watching it because it is not safe yet. I may be looking at a possible exit for my first trade......there are a million reasons why it is just not possible to post live trades all the time. Further, I don't want to see people following each other.....and make no mistake, they will. Whether it is intended or not, people will see it and use it as a signal service. Why?....because trading is not easy, it is difficult and humans are inherently lazy.....if people can see an easy way to make a dollar, they will take it. Also, to help a friend, and he is a lurker here at FF and will verify this for those who don't believe (although I'm sure there are one or two forum surfing lurkers out there who won't believe, and I couldn't care less), I made a live trade, pip by pip last night on the GU short that I took.......yes, the one that I posted here once it was all over. So, I took GU because the signal was good, he took EU because the signal was good. In my experience, the GU trade was a much higher probability trade due to many reasons, and the GU trade paid +52 st S1, which is where I exited. My friend had exited at +2, just before it would have turned negative. Both the above trades met the criteria for an entry, but one was a better option in my opinion......and there are many reasons for this. If I were doing this live here on the forum I would a) get bombarded with posts asking me why GU was better that EU, and b) people who took EU and didn't exit at BE would be crying to me that the entry was good (which it was), so the system must suck!! Every system 'out there' bar none, requires discretion to some degree. Otherwise and EA of Genesis would be made and we would all be very rich people!! Te experience I have gained over thousands of hours of chart watching, trading, losing, winning, testing, demoing etc etc has taught me well. It taught me that my live trade yesterday was more likely to work out than my friends. And so it was. Experience and discretion cannot be built into a system, and it cannot be taught.......and by posting live trades all the time, people will not gain that experience and will forever be dependent on someone else. Finally, this system has been well designed and completely tested under all conditions. The template that I use and the indicators are all available on Post #1. Xaphod has created a thread specifically to create and maintain indicators for Genesis, and we are extremely lucky, and grateful for him sharing his talents with us. Support is given to users of the system and that support comes very quickly, within 24 hours at least. All of this is given for free......is it really too much to ask the people to walk the last mile on their own? Do I (and others) have to hold their hands and spoon feed them as well? Even if we post live trades, and even if we use a Trade Explorer, people will still lose. Why? Because we are all different. This system just doesn't suit some people. Some people expect the system to be like an EA....as long as the entry rules are met then the system MUST make a profit. Sadly that's not the way it works and those people will never make it as traders, no matter the system.....people have to apply their own common sense and discretion to this, and any other system. So, to wrap it up before my coffee goes cold, I will, and do, post live trades from time to time. I always have done so, even in other threads before we created this one. The live trades will come from me, when it suits me, and not when it suits anyone else. I need to make money to put food on the table and I won't be distracted from doing that, for anyone. Be grateful for what you receive, for free, as a result of others hard work and experience. Appreciate the support you are getting , and treasure the occasional 'live trade'. But most of all, test, test, test the system for yourself. You will not get the experience any other way. RJ

I didn't say that the GU trade was 'obvious', I said that "the GU trade was a much higher probability trade due to many reasons". Lets have a look at some of the reasons. * We know that for this year so far, the Euro has strengthened. Yes, Draghi may wish it was lower and is trying to make that happen by flappin his gums, but the market is bigger than he is! * We know that the EU Summit has just been, and is immediately followed by the Eurogroup meetings, so it's reasonable to assume that the market will eagerly await some concrete news before making any decisive moves. Yes, hedge funds and other institutes move the market, but the market was not likely (imo) to make a clear and decisive move while the meeting was going on.....especially in face of no other high impact news on the horizon. * We know that Japan was on holiday, and they are sellers of Yen and buyers of EURO for the moment. So much for the fundamental reasons, I'm sure there are others that I have missed. Lets look at the technical reasons: The EU Chart. You can see the shaded area and you can see how it is and area of strong support/resistance, and in the middle of that area it is kind of like the doldrums.....no direction at all. So in order for the PA to either bounce off and head north, or to take a dive right through this area, we are going to need some considerable power. As we know, last night there was no power for the fundamental reasons above. Also, the stoch wasn't even hinting at turning south, so a short working out for anything other than a small move was unlikely. If the stoch was right up the top and turning over, I would be watching for signals on our Genesis system...for certain!! But all in all.....I didn't see much in the EU pair to get excited about. On to the GU. * Cameron is in a little spot of bother because Fitch and Moodies have both warned that unless the UK gets a grip on it's debt, they stand to lose their AAA rating. If that happens, the GBP will tank! Just the mention of it, and the lack of clear leadership to sort the problem out is affecting the GBP. * UK is spending some 55 million pounds per day on supporting the EZ......much to the dismay of the EU opponents like Nigel Farage. * UK unemployment is a big issue as well, with increasing immigration from Europe, thanks the the open borders of the EZ. Now...the technical stuff. The downtrend is pretty obvious isn't it? Certainly there are pull backs, there has to be....and on our Genesis system on the M5 (and perhaps the M15) these might be trade opportunities. But, the recent pullback has exhausted itself (see the yellow circle) and it was pretty obvious. Moreso when you see the stoch position. We can also see the shaded support area at the bottom, and that serves as a target. As an aside, I didn't let my GU trade run down that far because +52 was worth pocketing in such a thin market as yesterday. I could have (and should have) hung in there, but I didn't.....such is life. So this is exactly what I was talking about in my post above. Genesis does not mention that we should have a basic understanding of the fundamentals. It does not mention using traditional candles and charts for long term searching for s/r and other patterns of interest and many more things. If I were to include everything, it would make Genesis look like and encyclopaedia and it would be boring and unprofitable. These are the things than come with experience and must be applied using our discretion.

--- 帖子 #9556 ---
Thank you very much for your kind words.....it is much appreciated. A lot of work has gone into this system by a lot of people, and we are still looking at ways to make things even easier. As with everything else we do, we do extensive tsting for long periods before we bring it to you. Most things don't work over the long term, or they do work, but offer no improvement. But rest assured, we are always working on improvements. You are exactly right....getting a handle on ones emotions is difficult, and to some extent, it is a constant battle. There is a trader who taught me a lot, you see him at FF occasionally and his nick is 'Atlast.' He is incredible with his Andrews Pitchfork trading, but it doesn't suit me. He introduced me to the book you see on my profile, and he also gave me a gem of an analogy that I have never forgotten. With regard to seeing moves going without you, he would say: 'The train has left the station. It *is* possible to run and try to catch the train and jump on board.....but....the risks of getting on a moving train are just too great and the risk of getting hurt are too real. Why chase the train? Another train will be along later, catch the next train. Don't be silly and get yourself hurt.' I have never forgotten that piece of advice and at times, like last evening, I missed the train (EU) as it left the station at Frankie...but the train called into the S1 station and then backed up to pick up passengers, so I jumped on it there. It then ran on to the S2 station and stopped there to pick up more passengers, so I bought another ticket and we hopped off the train at the S3 station without getting hurt at all. So that's how I think of things.....if I miss the train, I don't run after it.....it's gone without me. Never mind, another one will be along later, and I'll catch that one With Genesis, the signals very much fit the 'train and station' analogy, and I view it in that way....it helps to keep my emotions in check. If we can add pips most days, it doesn't matter whether it's 10 pips or 100pips, if we can end each day slightly ahead of where we started, we are going along perfectly. Of course there are some losing days, but not many. There are days when I don't enter a single trade....and I lose nothing. The important yardstick for me personally is at the end of the month.....have I made a profit this month? The answer is Yes, I have.....every month. Some better than others but always a profit. I get losing days, but not losing weeks or months. So all we have to do is keep chipping away at it and try to achieve consistency. In a way it's like motorcycle racing (which I have done a bit of).....too many people go to a new track and go crazy in practice until they crash before the races actually start. The clever ones go around the new circuit slowly, learning the lines and the breaking markers, learning where the rough patches are, learning where the best overtaking places are etc. Adding speed is easy......just turn the throttle! Those guys are the winners. It's the same with trading......getting consistent is the most important thing.....we can add longer trades once we have the consistent entries sorted out.....we can add larger lot sizes (within reason) at the click of a mouse. Consistency is the key....the rest is easy

Actually I have done my fair share of haymaking....both driving the old Massey Ferguson and following behind chucking the bales onto the truck.... long before round hay bails here invented!! But I don't envy farmers their job either....but the point is that they chose that path knowing full well that, as you say, it is a boom and bust industry to be involved in....and it is very weather dependent. I do get a bit tired of some farmers continued crying though....for instance, we are experiencing a great summer (for us townies), but some of sheep farmers are crying and beginning to mutter about wanting govt assistance. Yet, way back in October/November we were all warned of the likely hot dry summer ahead....but some farmers *still* overstocked their properties with sheep (greed), and now they can't feed them and they want the taxpayer to bail them out. I'm tired of bailing farmers out for too much sun, too much rain, too much wind, world prices falling etc etc. I don't see them paying the taxpayer back for all the handouts when the good times come. The kiwifruit, apples, oranges and other produce are also weather dependent, but they get jack from the govt in the tough times....and rightly so....for that is the nature of the business they chose to be involved with. I know that there are a great many good and honest farmers......by far the majority....but we only ever really hear from the vocal minority.

--- 帖子 #9734 ---
Don't worry, mine are still moving nicely. This is the ATR indie I prefer, you can't change any of the inputs except the colour (which you'll need to do if you have a black chart) If you hover over the lines, you will see when the day starts that above the price is high 2 then above that high1 then below price you have low 2 and low 1 in that order. When price reaches one of the lines for instance, on EJ now, price has reached and gone through Low 2 and Low 1, it then brings the High lines down to show where (if it now turns around) price is likely to reach the other way. I find it very useful, the lines very often act in the same was as S/R do and of course can break through on a good day just as price breaks through s/r. Can Any one explain me it with graphical explanation !

--- 帖子 #9770 ---
The short answer is you cannot eliminate false positives.....or bad trades. Losing and winning is all part of this business, and we have to accept that. We can never be certain that it's safe to get back into the water, we can only enter small trades that meet our entry criteria and see how it goes. Because we are stuck in a ranging market, there is little else we can do. The important thing is to not risk your money needlessly. For instance.....that GU trade I was babysitting went to +20 or something and I moved my SL to BE to eliminate the risk. From there on, I'm playing with the house money, not my capital. Yes, I got stopped out at BE and the news sent the PA my way for more than 100 pips (and that's the second time this has happened to me on this pair recently!), but what did I lose?......nothing!! I'm not worried about 'what could have been'......and I'm not worried that I could have taken a solid +20 if I close the trade before the news. I didn't risk my capital any more than necessary, so I live to try again. Sooner or later, on any one (or more) pairs that I trade, the range will break and I will be there with my little trade.....and I will add more trades as the move (or trend) develops......each time, protecting my capital. This week has been below par for many people, and so we aren't suffering alone, we just have to keep testing the water until it works out for us. Forcing the issue, or trying to force it, will cost you money and confidence. We have to be smarter and more patient than the market!!

--- 帖子 #9841 ---
EA can't work because there is a certain amount of discretion involved in trading, and EA's cannot have this feature! It should be possible to create an EA that would get good entries, but the exits are always the hard part and that's where an EA will fail nearly every time. For the amount of work required to make an EA, and then to have to monitor it, really makes the whole idea not worth exploring. The best way to trade profitably is to put in the time and effort and learn the markets and then pick and choose entries and exits to give yourself the best chance of making consistent profits. There's no easy way.....trading is not easy!

--- 帖子 #9932 ---
FWIW iwan73, I look at the direction of the yellow MA on the chart, be it the M5 or M15, and if it is still rising (for shorts) after the signal bar has completed I let the trade go (just like the trade you took on the EJ - the MA is still rising steeply) - the opposite for longs (of course). Yes, I miss some trades but it seems to filter out those whipsaw/congestion trades. It's just another thing I look at and makes a HPT more likely. I like to see flat, falling or some softening of the MA for short trades. I don't know if anyone else looks at this but this observation alone has kept me out of crappy trades.

--- 帖子 #9995 ---
In a strong trend you need to see another reason for it to go your way not just genesis changing colour. For instance if the M15 stoc was coming down strongly, maybe a pivot above the price or H1 at least printing a bearish candle. None of those happened so to be safe go on the side of the trend. As far as the pivots go you will very often find price will bounce off those so even if there was a strong down signal there is not a lot of room in case it bounces.

--- 帖子 #10101 ---
Understanding stoch is not difficult, but there is much mis-information about stochastic 'out there' perpetuated by muppets who don't know what they are talking about!! I venture to say that you will NEVER see a trade entry with the stochs at the extremes.....it's just doesn't work that way, and if you took a trade at such a time, you would be taking a great risk because, as you can see in that chart, stoch can stay at either extreme for a long time....and that's good if you are in a trade. It's not until they start to drop, and the candles concurr and Genesis concurs that we have an entry.....and by the time the candles and Matric agree, stoch will be halfway down (or up) in it's journey. But where was the stoch (say) 5 candles before the entry?....... Sooner or later the use of the stoch will 'click' in your head!

--- 帖子 #10107 ---
No it's not stupid. Your SL was below the swing low, which was also under the DP, and the price already had a crack at the pivot but got rejected in no uncertain terms. So, your SL was safe. Seeing as your SL was under no threat, there was no valid reason to exit. It's not too often that we can time our entry to perfection and only ever see positive growth, very often the trade has to breath up and down as it progresses. In your case, the price got an outright rejection from the pivot and it went up a bit, which is when you entered. Then, the breathing began.....the price was consolidating, and nothing more. The arrow appeared before the M5 stoch went down a bit, but the M15 stoch wasn't interested in going down. Your blue MA hadn't turned over either. I honestly don't see a valid reason to exit that trade. All I can say, and I say this with respect, is that you got cold feet. You didn't want to have a loss of any size, and so as soon as the trade went negative, you fretted about it and worried until you could exit. This is a common emotion, but you MUST get control of it because otherwise you will close trades with a tiny profit, in case they retrace, which is normal as I just said.....or you will close them with a loss before they even get a chance to get going! This is the classic Fear/Greed scenario and you need to get a grip on this if you are to succeed. How much demo trading have you done? Can you trade for smaller lot sizes so that any loss is 'nickels and dimes' and gradually increase your risk as you settle into it a bit better? And lastly.....trading the GU pair is not advisable for you. GU can be vicious and dangerous at times and I don't recommend it. Stick to EU or maybe EJ. Hope that helps.

--- 帖子 #10142 ---
For me.....if I was already in a trade that was in profit and protected, I certainly would consider adding to the trade where your arrow is. If it was going to be a brand new trade, then no, I wouldn't enter. The reason is that if I already have a trade in profit, the risk of the new trade will be offset by the already in profit trade. So to some extent, I would be playing with the 'house money' not risking my capital. If it is a new trade, then I will be risking my capital, and for that, I want to see a perfect, or near perfect set up first......even if it means I miss the trade completely.....because.....there will always be another train

kosmo, That is a function of the MT4 platform to show you a trade visually on the chart. In the "Terminal" window, select the "Account History" tab. From the list of transactions shown on the "Account History" tab, drag a trade (row) and drop it on a chart window. Greg

If you're already in a trade, then you can either exit, or take the risk of staying in. If your SL is already in profit then you don't have anything to lose, but if your trade is not yet in profit, you have to decide whether to carry the risk or not. I try to stay out at news times....too much of a coin flip for me.

--- 帖子 #10352 ---
If you're considering going against the trend, as a minimum you should at least have higher high / lower low in the direction you intend to trade, and/or a double bounce off of a support line - one bounce off of a support line is generally not enough, as it could easily turn and smash through it next time. You may also consider divergence - but that can be a lot harder to accurately spot when you're starting out.
