--- 帖子 #10408 ---
Well there's 2 schools of thought regarding news trading. One says "don't do it...stay out and trade after the 'dust settles'".......the other says "news it what moves the markets, it's the best time to trade." I don't know which is best of the 2 methods. If the news is a decent event, like interest rates (for example), they have the potential to move the market for days, or to set or reverse trends. So it won't matter if you miss the first 5 minutes of the move. Personally if I am already in a trade, and my trade has a SL in profit then I am usually happy to leave the trade and see what happens. If I'm not yet in a trade, I will wait and see and perhaps pick up some pips after the event. If I was you and I was thinking about trying some news trading, I would do it on demo and see how you go before risking your money. As for Yelena, she used an EA to get into news trades, and I'm not convinced that she was actually doing what she said she was doing. The Genesis team decided (not me alone), that we would ban her from this thread because she was also 'Minako'.....you might have seen some of her posts. Yelena and Minako are the same person.....that's why FF deleted the account of Minako. As you know, we are serious about trading here and we don't want to play games or deal with dishonest people. Was Yelena trading for real? Who knows.....she cannot be trusted so I don't wish to speculate on that. You will find her over at the eur/usd thread so you can ask her yourself.

--- 帖子 #10410 ---
My thoughts on news trading, is you need to be a very experienced trader to trade them. Because of the market's expectations of the news, good news can quickly (without us knowing) suddenly turn and be reassessed as bad, and the market turns. Unfortunately you cant test for this, because the few number of major news events, how the market interpreted it, etc. So unless you have a setup very specifically designed to trade major jumps in price, it is extremely difficult. Yes, at the moment the market is very strongly driven by news, but thats what we have to deal with.

--- 帖子 #10458 ---
OK Simon, let's pass through your questions. Entries: In Genesis there is just one type of entry (see post #2 ) All the entries were in compliance with the standard Genesis rules ( post #2 ). The reference TF was M5. Arrows: Both M5 and M15 arrows are confirmation signals. You can use MTF arrow indi in M5 TF or switch to M15 TF with std arrow indi according to your preferences/habit. 5-15 Variant: In the pdf we simply measured the stats of the arrows (both M5 and M15) when Genesis signal comes on and a right set up is in place. Particularly we verified if M5 and M15 arrows were already on the chart when Genesis signal arose (YES/NO is related to the presence of the arrows). If they weren't we measured how many bars we had to wait in average for seeing the arrows. According to this analysis we can say that if M15 arrow is already on your char and you have a signal in the same direction this is a HPT. Obviously the outcome of the trade depends on the market conditions and the trader can choose among different types of exits in order to get the maximum from the system. I hope this can figure out better your doubts. Here you can find some other clarifications. Let me know if you need more info. ciao wiz

--- 帖子 #10464 ---
If I was going to draw a channel there I would do it differently...see my chart. The trouble with drawing these things, is that you can get sucked into a bias, just as you have done!! I don't pay much, if any attention to these things because they develop a bias in your mind. For instance, if the PA hits the top line you will be thinking "Ok.....I'm looking for a short"......you see?.....now you are biased towards the short side and if the PA goes the other way you will miss the long entry. I look at these things on the Daily chart and the Weekly chart and sometimes the H4, but they are only to keep in the back of my mind.....I don't trade them.....i just observe them, and let our system provide the entry, whether or not it agrees with any trendline. That's why I say that we are system traders here.....not predictive traders!!

--- 帖子 #10522 ---
In some ways what happened is exactly related to the same reason you entered the trade ... that that line had been acting as a strong resistance, so likely there's a lot of orders clustered around there ... but once broken through, there was clear space until the orders balanced out again ... You could think of it like a car trying to drive through a brick wall ... starting from very close, it doesn't break through, it tries and tries again, but finally it reverses a lot, gets up a bit of speed and *boom*, through the wall it goes. Of course, it could have just as easily hit the wall but then bounced downwards harder ... you just never know. But generally, opposite signals is probably a good time to exit.

--- 帖子 #10539 ---
A lot of people don't like HA candles.....and I used to be one of them. You'll hear things like 'oh but HA candles hide the open and close of the candles.' .... They do.....so what?? On these small timeframes that is redundant information.....it is of no use whatsoever! Many people used to 'hate' to use a mac computer, or a Linux computer simply because they were brought up on a Windoze box. Had they been brought up on a Mac, they would have hated Windoze. It's all a matter of what our minds are comfortable with. But we are clever people and we can retrain our minds. The reason the template on Post#1 is the way it is is simple.....white for up and red for down. That goes for the Matrix and the candles......real simple. We have a simple system of the matrix, the stoch, the MA, and the colour of the candles that all need to agree so that we can enter. It is that simple. When we start complicating it with stuff like 'opening' and/or 'closing' prices, doji's, spinning tops, expanding triangles, wedges and more crap, we have more reasons to doubt ourselves and that causes indecision and missed opportunities as well as bias. The whole point of the system is to have our 7 ducks all lined up in row and then we pull the trigger. For longer term analysis, H4, Daily and Weekly charts, Japanese candles and formations become more relevant and act as a 'heads up' to a possible (not probable) event that we may wish to remember for future use.

When you have MTF indicators, backtest using LFH_Trading_Simulator_3 may not work properly. In this case, I recommend you just record your screen using freeware tool CamStudio, which can be downloaded from http://camstudio.org/ . When you use the following setting for video, the recorded video size will be 1.1 GB for 24 hours. Attached Image Be careful not to exceed 2 GB of file size. 2 GB is the max allowed file size of AVI and if it's exceeded, you cannot open the file. (This tool doesn't automatically cut the file within 2 GB limit). When you play the video, you may replay faster in your player if you want. By collecting months of data, you may say if your strategy works. Thanks Justin

--- 帖子 #10706 ---
Regarding stochastics......and this is the last time I'm going to mention this because I have spoken about it countless times and this is common knowledge that is available if you just look for it online. This chart is EJ Daily. You can see the huge bull run we are having....more than 2,000 pips. See the stochastic?.......see how it's sitting up so high? Is there any sign, any sign at all.....anywhere, that the bull run is ending? No......the sign comes at the red line, which was a pull back, or retrace of about 340 pips, and perhaps the bulls are now going to take over again. The point here is, that just because the stoch is up so high, does NOT indicate that a sell trade is forming. That is just stupid thinking and shows a complete lack of understanding of the basics that have been covered many times in this thread....and even in the links provided on Post #1. The time for a trade comes when ALL of our indicators agree, and not before. To set up a bias due to one indicator is simply stupid. Imagine if you were trading this Daily chart and were waiting to enter a short since the first time the stoch hit the roof!!! You'll be sitting there letting 2,000 pips slip right past you because of a silly bias born from not understanding the basics. We do not trade off a single indicator here and we do not engage in bias forming nonsense. Take heed!

Usually when conditions like this happen where opposite arrow appear within 3-6 bars plus genesis signal excluding m15 stoch, its a trend continuation provided that there's a trend happened previously. It is resemblance to elliot wave where wave 1 is trending, 2 is pullback, 3 is fastest and largest pip making wave etc. But that's not the point of wave analysis here and I don't want to wave count the trend because market is dynamic and true enough, its better to stick with trading what we see rather what we think to anticipate the move. The current MTF m15 stoch is good enough to gauge the direction, however there are times when the stoch is heading up for the 1st 2 m5 bar then when the 3rd m5 bar which has a strong reverse turn, MTF m15 stoch will turn or shrink to weaken the direction. I have a long way to go, but thanks to RJ, Olivia, Cody, Oliver, Marty and all of the other contributors, I am getting there. I would like to give a special shout out to RJ. --- 帖子 #10846 ---
Hiya Mickey....this problem has come up before, and the answer is the same in every case. The Matrix is not an indicator, per se......it reads the relevant indicator from your 'experts/indicators' folder and displays the data in the form of one colour or another in the Matrix. If the indicator is not in the 'experts'indicators' folder, then the Matrix cannot read it...obviously, and therefore cannot display it. Go to your 'experts/indicators' folder and make sure that everything in the zip file from Post#1 (except genesis.tpl) is there. It would seem that you are missing TVI and the T3 indicators all of which are in the zip file. When you open a chart....any chart, it doesn't matter, go to your 'Custom Indicators' and look for TVI and T3......you should seem them something like this. If you don't see the indicators in your list, neither can the Matrix.

Jo, Good luck on the scalping. Generally the problem with scalping, is the high risk/reward. You only need a couple of losses to wipe out a lot of hard won profits. --- 帖子 #11018 ---
You need to be aware that scalping quick pips is usually done with higher lot sizes per trade in order to make it worthwhile. after all, there is not much point in scalping 5 pips for 0.10 lot size......you're never going to make much money doing that. So, with larger lot sizes comes larger profits......and larger losses. Also, a good scalper must have a good system and must be absolutely confident with it. I would go as far as to say that you have better be able to string together a 90% win/loss rate (at least) over a period of not less than 100 scalps because the risk/reward ratio is all out of whack. I'm not saying it can't be done, because it certainly can be.....I'm saying it is a method that is fraught with risk unless you are already a profitable and competent trader.

--- 帖子 #11019 ---

Regarding divergence, I like Joe Dinapoli's note in his book: "Don't use an Oscillator to price divergence as an entry technique, unless you have an excellent means of filtering it. Even for the best of Oscillators this can, and often does, spell disaster, particularly for the new participant. Price and Oscillator divergences abound, and the market continues to stop out the divergence players. Looking back in time, you're sure to find divergences that work, but when you're going forward in time, as in real trading, the accuracy of this technique just isn't there."

--- 帖子 #11086 ---
There is nothing deeper. For the first 2 years of trading, I spent in excess of 15 hours a day, 7 days a week observing PA, on weekends going over and over that weeks PA, over and over again (my wife tells me I am obsessed). I still put in minimum 12 hour days. It sounds incredibly boring (and it was), but that is the only way, I now see PA developing recognisable behaviour, and when it follows certain "patterns", I trade (or stay out as the case may be). Sorry, but I cant explain any better than that. In my early days of trading, I used to read about experienced traders, using only PA to trade, and I thought (at the time) what a load of bollocks !! Now I understand what they mean. There is no easy "holy grail" out there. The only thing I personally would add to Genesis was stronger moving averages, but that is just a personal thing, I am a big fan of MAs, as they dont diverge, like all indicators do.

--- 帖子 #11323 ---
It's nothing too complex. Looking at what's going on on the M15 chart is a good guide as to what to do on the M5, as far as direction is concerned. It's just a bigger picture and (imo) the M15 is possible the best guide for Intraday trading. Of course it's good to gave a look at the H1, H4 etc, but maybe I look at them once or twice a day only. The M15 however, is very useful. If we know what the M15 is doing, we can use that information when M5 trading to stay out of bad trades, and to help us enter good trades. Now.....we could (and I still do) switch back and forth between the M5 and M15 charts to gather all the relevant info. Wouldn't it be much more convenient to get a brief peek at the M15 situation without having to switch charts?.....well.....with the help of Xaphods MTF Arrow set to M15, and MTF stoch set to M15, we can get a great picture of what is happening on the M15 chart without ever leaving the M5 chart. Prety cool huh? That's all there is to it......the MTF stoch and Arrow just gives us an idea of what is going on on the M15 chart. If need be, we can then switch to that chart for closer examination.

--- 帖子 #11335 ---
Well, there's a couple of different ways to look at this. One school of thought says stay out at news time because it is so volatile.....the others say that news is what moves the market, so why stay out when the market is moving?? I think that it's best to avoid high impact news for (perhaps) 5 minutes....or until the PA has decided which way it's going. As far as orders not being filled until the worst possible moment, I think that MT4 and the broker may have to share equal blame. I know how damaging to an account this can be, which is why I don't trade with Mt4, and I have no complaints. I will still get slippage at high impact news times, but that's not the brokers fault, that's the speed of the move....and I accept that and avoid those times.

The way I attempt to determine the strength of a move, is with moving averages. The wider they are the stronger the move, say 60 SMA &amp; a shorter one (ie 25 EMA/15EMA). Indicators are less effective for this, as the diverge and get twisted up in big moves

Hi all, finally I could find time to come back here. It is incredible ... just one week away from trading and I had to read more than 30 pages !! In the last pages I read often some people in trouble to identify the end of a trend and the beginning of a range; RJ and Marty gave you some advises very good ... let me add my 2 cents. The enclosed chart is H4 but the internal pattern/behavior of the market behind this is the same in any TFs. I choosed a weak trend to highlight better how I look at the chart to measure the strenght of a trend and potential changes. TREND 1. TOP. 2. First LL 3. First LH. Here is where we know the new bearish movement (potential trend) is starting. 4. LL. Trend still strong - long leg 5. LH. Trend still strong - LH lower than 2 6. LL. Trend still strong - long leg 7. LH. Trend still strong - LH lower than 4 8. LL. Trend stil alive but we are loosing momentum because 6 and 8 are close. Warning! 9. LH Trend is not yet finished and I am still looking for short opportunities BUT NOW I take into account the RANGE option. RANGE 10. Here I have a confirmatin we are in a RANGE because we have no LL. Now I must be careful! 11. here is where many times I lost money ... no trades for me. 12. Good opportunity because fake BO. Now I am looking for long. 13. Typical RANGE BO and re-test I like also to look at H4 chart to spot the levels like 2 and 4 than I move to M5 chart looking for Genesis Signals (points 5,7,9). If you like you can add stocastic to get more info like divergences ... but always my rule is : Price first stocastic later. ciao wiz

If you mean the multi timeframe stoch-tape any multi timeframe indicator will "repaint" until the bar on the timeframe the indicator is reading from closes, that isnt repainting. If you put the 5m stoch tape on the 5m chart then it wont change after the bar closes.

--- 帖子 #11444 ---
The M15 chart is from a simulation in the strategy tester. The M61 time-frame on the chart is an offline chart which is a simulated H1 time-frame. The H1 chart is a live chart from the same time period. The difference in time axis is probably due to the simulations being done on a broker with a different time offset. I have MT4 installations I use exclusively for backtesting. If you compare the bars on the H1 chart to the H1-bars drawn onto the M15 chart you will see that they are the same.

The files you are after are in the : C:\Users\(your account)\AppData\Local\VirtualStore\Program Files\MetaTrader - (your broker)\templates folder. The same applies to experts and the other folders. It a security feature introduced by microsoft with the release of Vista.

--- 帖子 #11798 ---
Its not really any TF is the definitive way to trade, there are many different interpretations. Generally you select a HTF in which you determine a trend (lets call it your "trend" TF) - you may then select the next HTF to ensure if it is a strong trend, you dont trade against it, but if that trend isnt strong, be happy with your "trend" TF. Then you take the next lower TF, in which to time your entries (lets call it your "timing" TF). So Genesis strategy suggests M15 as your "trend" TF, and M5 as your "timing" TF. So checking H1, as your next higher "trend" TF, is a good idea. As you will regularly see fake-outs on M15, ie sharp pullbacks against a strong H1 trend. So checking H1 will keep you on the right side. By not checking multiple TFs (unless you trade H1 or higher) will lead getting chopped up regularly. Then the issue is which TF to trade ????? That is the tough one. That comes down to personal preference;time to you have to sit in front of the screen; and the amount of trading capital. Hope this helps

--- 帖子 #11804 ---
From what I have read, the profitability for TFs, are generally like this: The higher the TF; win/loss ratio is usually lower, but average winners is usually higher, ie your RR is is higher. To take it to the extreme, M1 scalpers can trade below RR of 1:1, but need very high win/loss ratios, with loads of small pips wins, because losses will have a significant impact. Swing traders, ie those holding trades for a few days, will get stopped out a lot, but when they get a big winner it can be 500 pips or more. My old coach (of a few years ago), who was a swing trader, always talked about a trade he made during the early part of the financial crises when he made £80k But I repeat whatever TF you choose, you need a "timing" TF and a "trend" TF. Choosing just 1 TF limits your understanding of what the market is doing.

Struggling with the Pivots ... Using a broker, who has not the 'right' server time to build the correct pivots, is not helpful. First you have to recognize, that pivots are shown wrong, second how to fix? RJ/Kosmo indicated the 'Pivot Manual ActionForex'-EA, you may use to put in the ActionForex H/L/C-Figures manually to get correct pivots. Some times ago I was looking for another solution, because one of my brokers has this problem too. Here is a another solution, the 'Pivot Points - Daily (Shifted)'-EA. You have to check only the time difference GMT to your broker's server and data for the pivots are shift. The pivots remain on the screen each day and are labeled. Look inside the EA, there is a description, how it works. Checking the results I saw, that the pivot always is correct and the R1-3/S1-3 may differ around 1-2 PIPs, especially the R3/S3. For me this is ok. josch

--- 帖子 #11955 ---
Most of the Yen crosses are correlated at the moment because it's the Yen that's doing the major moves, rather than the pairs other half....regardless of whether it's the Swissy, the Aussie, Euro or whatever. Of course there's no point in enetering them all in the same direction if the Yen is the prime mover, but the Aussie is driven by much different forces than is the Swissy and the Euro.....which are somewhat related themselves. So sometimes it's worth trading the AU pair, especially in the Tokyo session which is when the Euro tends to not move too much, but the Aussie might. It just depends on whether the Aussie is moving the price or the Yen is moving it.

--- 帖子 #12047 ---
No. People are free to modify their template within the parameters of the Genesis system, but I think that all new users of the system need to start from the same place. As they get more experienced with the system they will change their template, as you have done, to suit themselves, and that's good. But if we have many templates in the thread, people will skip all over the place trying new templates and that will make it very difficult to keep the thread in order, and then all the new users will lose. As you can see, there are some very, very good traders here using the system, and they are helping others to learn the system as well. Everyone started from the same place, and that helps speed up the learning curve. I don't always make text book Genesis trades, and I know others do the same, but I (we) always post only Genesis system trades here....and the reason is the same....to make sure that all the followers of the system see the same thing and can learn from it.

--- 帖子 #12146 ---
I agree there are reasonable setup confirmation on M5. Just as long you were aware at the time of entry you entering a H1/M30/M15 counter-trend news spike. Probably about as risky as you can get. There is absolutely nothing wrong (ish) with counter-trend trades - PROVIDED - at the time of entry you are aware of it, and only expect a small profit, and a choppy trade. Counter-trend trades very rarely breakout to turn into big winners !! Whereas trend trades have the greater potential to turn into big winners - which after all is what we really want !! Another point, is if you take counter-trend trades and get a nice profit, you can fool yourself into thinking they are a HPT setup, and then when PA turns back to trend, you are so busy patting yourself on the back, you miss the big trend move.

--- 帖子 #12329 ---
Yes it is interesting. I have the greatest respect for Japan and Japanese culture, I worked for the Japanese for 6 years. Having said that, I feel that their whole culture is an impediment to sustained prosperity. They have no original ideas, and the "bold action" that Abe has ordered has been going on for quite some time in the rest of the major economies....but they call it 'Quantitative Easing.' The market is completely ready for this and it comes as no surprise to the market. The market is well versed in how to deal with "bold action" because it has had plenty of practice!! Further, the BOJ, as an independent entity has had all the opportunities in the world to do something....anything....to combat Japans deflation cycle, yet they have never done anything. They all run around like headless chickens. So along comes Abe with his "bold action" idea (which is not his idea at all), and he puts people in the BOJ who will tow the "bold action" line. A couple of months later, every man woman and child is parroting the "bold action"...."2% inflation within 2 years" rhetoric as if it was news of the second coming!!! The people, because of their culture, and this is a fact not a criticism, will say and do whatever Abe and Kuroda say without question, because that is their way. They will believe those two, and parrot the "bold action.....2% within 2 years" dream until the bitter end.....and that's ok......the silly thing is that they also had this belief of Noda who came before, and those that came before him. If we troll back through my posts, I made this very point several years ago: Japan sells it's debt internally....in effect, it's a way of 'saving face' (a cultural thing) from the rest of the world. This can give the illusion that all is (relatively) well in Japan as far as the rating agencies are concerned, but eventually the debt will be too much and will have to be marketed globally.....which we are beginning to see now. Once that gets 'up to speed', we will see the rating agencies downgrade Japan. Of course that will increase interest rates, but it's a double edged sword. Japan has to import all it's raw materials, and there's a cost to that! IMO Japan has missed the boat.....Korea and China (and others) have jumped into the gaps that Japans lack of foresight has created industrially. Whether they can get back that lost ,market share is debatable. Then we have their many other issues like aging workforce etc etc etc In many ways Japan is at the forefront of the 21st century.....but in many ways it is still stuck in the 16th century, and this incompatible mix is costing them dearly......in my humble opinion.

--- 帖子 #12332 ---
I don't think you'll find anywhere in this thread that the reason you closed your trade was a valid reason! I certainly have never suggested that. If you look through your charts you will see many instances of winning trades having small retraces along the way. That's how the price moves. It never, or very rarely goes in a straight line. The price always goes up (or down) in a series of 'stairstep' like movements.....we tend to call this 'breathing'....I guess you can see why. The price taking a 'breath' of -6 is nothing.....it often happens to -20 and if you're going to get scared and exit trades in negative that actually meet the criteria of a good entry (apart for the CT issue), it will slowly but surely eat your account. Also, we have spoken many times about the fact that the price likes to 'test' known s/r lines (like pivots etc) at least once, and this happened on your trade some time after you exited, but your SL was never under any threat. Finally, your SL was well placed and was very cheap..... it was set to -15 pips (more or less) worst case scenario. At the time of writing this, that trade would have given you more than +60 pips, and it's still going....but you got cold feet at -6! I'm not saying that you should necessarily let the price hit your SL, but I am saying that you must allow the price to breath in it's stair step fashion, and you must expect s/r lines to be tested and probably retested. Spend some time this weekend looking at charts and you will see what I mean. RJ

--- 帖子 #12412 ---
Jo, I'll give you a condensed version of how my trading got to where it is now, and hopefully somewhere in there your questions will be answered. Be sure though, that there is much for me to learn still....I don't whether it is possible to ever stop learning in this business and there are far better traders around than me, so I still have a lot of work to do. I started much like anyone else....in complete ignorance! I downloaded a demo account and figured out how it worked and then played with it. I didn't really know too much, but I had a lot of beginners luck and thought that I had discovered my own personal ATM machine!! Of course I was trading a demo account of $50k and I didn't see the value of having a SL....pah....what a stupid idea a SL is!! The inevitable losses came until I wiped out the demo account. After a couple of months I discovered this place (Forex Factory), and a whole new world opened up for me, and I realised that this was not a game, that it should be possible to make money from the FX market. So I subscribed to (guess what? ) the eur/usd thread! I downloaded a new demo and started reading that thread and trying to follow advice and examples and trying to understand TA......as you know, in that thread there are a handful of excellent traders, and a huge number of wannabe traders who we shall refer to as muppets, from here on in! I was making progress, but it was kind of in the 'one step forward, two back' fashion and I was getting very confused by the muppets, who I didn't yet know were muppets. I was inspired by a trader named Atlast, who still posts from time to time in that thread. He was trading before the Internet....trading from the ticker tapes in fact and he seemed to really know his stuff. He was very good with TA and his specialty was the Andrews Pitchfork. We because friends and I asked him about how the pitchfork worked, but he never really explained it to me because he said that I wasn't ready for it yet, instead he got me to buy the book you see on my profile. Reading that book was my first 'Eureka' moment. I realised that what I was going through was the same as everyone else, and that if I stuck with it, I could succeed. Coooool!! The more I read the more I realised who the muppets were and I realised that no one....NO ONE....knows which way the PA will go......and trying to predict it was time consuming, ineffective and unreliable. Never-the-less....after 18 months of demo trading I thought I'd open a small 'live' account. So I did.....with $300. Probably more by good luck than good management I got that account to $2k in about 2 months...all while working full time of course. Then my luck ran out and I entered a steady flow of losses.....all because I was trying to predict which way the price would go, and I was still reading 'advice' from the muppets. So I announced to the eur/usd thread that after making some good progress initially, now it was all turning to custard and I was a) going to leave the thread, and b) going to read my book another few times and then decide whether trading was for me or not. Shortly after that I got an email from another great trader from that thread, Acumen. He said that he understood my frustration with the thread, but he assured me that I was on the brink of a breakout (pardon the pun) and that he could help me, and I could also help him. You see, if you check up on acumen here at FF you will see that he is a great Pivot points and stochastic trader, but he too was getting sick of the ever increasing amount of muppets in that thread. So he decided that he would develop his own system specialising in pivots and stochs, and he would sell it. He would also create a forum from his sytem users and he would offer support. His offer was for me to be his test dummy.....he would give me the system for free, and in return I would give him feedback...good or bad. So I went with acumen and I left FF!! His system did indeed work, and it worked well. It didn't really suit me perfectly but at least I was getting better at entries and also getting better at knowing when to not enter. This was another 'light-bulb' moment for me. I realised that all the predicting in the world amounted to the same thing.....it was guesswork. Educated guess maybe....but still guesswork. What I needed was a system.....I needed to be a system trader if I was going to become consistent, and acumens system, while not perfectly suited to me, taught me the basics of what has stood me in good stead ever since....stochastic and pivots. Eventually I drifted back to FF in search of a system that better suited me, but still I would use stochastic and pivots, no matter what. I settled for a while on the Trading Made Simple thread by (the late) eelfranz, and I learned a great deal.....but the system still didn't suit me. Next, I went to the Symphonie thread, more or less from the start of that thread. The indicators used were shocking repainters, but when used with my stochastic and pivots, it seemed worthy of investing some time. After a bit of a battle I was able to get the non repainting TVi introduced to that sytsem, but I couldn't get and further progress. Never the less.....I was becoming more consistent with the combination of what I had been taught, what I had discovered, and the Symphonie system. Little by little that system morphed into an Elliot wave,and pattern recognition and PA prediction thread and only used the system to enter trades based on the bias born from all this wave counting and pattern recognition mumbo jumbo. I (and others) became frustrated at this and the lack of enthusiasm to make the (basically sound) system a complete non-repainting system and to get back to the roots, which is to become system traders......not counting elliot waves, mexican waves, blow waves or any other kind of wave! A small group of us agreed that we were not going to be like the masses and get into this prediction game, we wanted a system that would show us what the market is doing *now* and how to enter it, *now.* At about this time Xaphod made a set of indicators that didn't repaint and he made them for the Symphonie system. For me......*THIS* was the defining moment. I was as happy as a pig in pile of poo.....and I wanted this to be the system. The Symphonie system however, was not going to embrace this gift from Xaphod, so I thought 'fuck it then', I and a few others spoke to Xaphod and we created the Genesis Matrix System....a system that, at last, see's the market as it is right now, and gives accurate indications of when it is best to enter the market. The rest, as they say, is history. So to come full circle Jo, yes, there were time when I had doubts that I could make it in this business. The lowest point was right before acumen 'rescued' me from the eur/usd thread. If it wasn't for him I might have quit. When I left my full time job (coming up 3 years ago this year), Genesis wasn't born yet.....but I still had a belief that I could make it in this business....but I was never going to make it and hold down a full time job at the same time. I had enough money to not worry (due to previous business ventures) so I 'took the plunge', and I honestly believe that I could not have learned all that I have learned if I did not quit my job. Of course my savings took a huge dive, and my 'income' from FX trading was small. But, the win/loss rate lifted with Symphonie, and it took a much, much steeper climb (and it still gets steeper every day) once we had the Genesis system. This year is the year where in which have already recovered all my losses and my savings account is back to where it was to start with, I have food to eat and roof over head....tequila, Ducati and I am going to make a decent salary as well. So it's been a long haul and a series of ever increasing 'Eureka' moments, and a defining moment when acumen saved me and showed me the power of pivots and stochs. I hope that I am giving something back to the community of traders and learners because I have taken from them too. If we all take and give back.....then there is no limit to what we can accomplish. RJ

RJ, Your trading "life" history was a fascinating read. Mine, was a far more tortuous route. My entire previous career was centred around problem solving, fixing problems for companies I worked for. So I thought it was just a matter of time before I created a trading system, and bang I was away. Fortuitously I was able gradually wind down my consulting business while I studied/testing forex trading. As well as other ventures that were generating an income for me (and running down years of savings). I was very lucky I had a huge exposure to the finance industry throughout my previous career, as well as risk management, in various guises. But the problem was I wasted HUGE amounts of time; testing/evaluated systems, but I stubbornly soldiered on, with unwavering belief in my ability to "solve" this problem. Even my coach, said to me, havent you done enough studying ?? But oh no, not me, and you may have determined by now, I have slightly compulsive tendencies. I was making money, not a lot, but with a poor win/loss ratio which was really sapping for my confidence. But I was chopping and changes indicators all the time. But I was determined (actually I was obsessed about it) to build my own system. Then while searching on another indicator (Gann HiLo indie), low and behold I found the Genesis Matrix system, and this obsessive guy (almost as bad as me), BUT ... Obsessive in a completely different way, obsessive, in that his system does NOT, should NOT be changed ... Yes you guessed him RJ !! Suddenly all that talk that was in my head about finding a system, trading it, not changing, WAS actually working for someone (in fact a group of traders) - MAYBE, just MAYBE, that was the way. Finally I started trading, ONE system, not changing it, sure I kept trying to develop my other systems !! Now what a change, waking up each morning knowing what to expect to see, never changing, week by week, month by month, sure I tweaked a few little bits, but very little, more what was displayed on my screen. As new indies were developed by the GMS team. All of a sudden, this started helping with the development of my other systems, I would lock down certain parts, as I was happy with them, applying that same obsession as RJ, but this time, it was well directed focus. Now I just sit here and trade, no more searching, striving googling this and that indicator, testing this and that, changing, changing, and more changing, crashing metatrader, cause I changed things too much. So here I am at the end of an incredible journey, but at the start of an even better one.

First (more popular) says look at trend in higher TFs and go with the flow. So, if trading M5 , look at trend in higher TFs like M15, M30, H1 etc. 2. Second says, hold on... trends start changing from lower TFs and over time are propagated into the higher TFs. So look at lower TFs- if there is a trend change, say, from M1 to M5 to M15, then logically, there will be propagation into H1, H4 and D1. Thus lower TFs ought to count for trading higher TFs if there is a change setting in from lower TFs. What do your recommend? Regards, Athar.

--- 帖子 #12658 ---
What it's saying is that the stoch and the Matrix are the triggers for any move. The arrow(s) are secondary and we do not necessarily wait for the arrows, but it might be of concern if we do not see them soon after we have entered the trade. If we were going to wait for the arrows, then we may as well just trade the arrows and delete everything else!

--- 帖子 #12659 ---

--- 帖子 #12660 ---
The concept is easy when you think of it like this......the price is bearish in the M15 charts, but on your M5 chart you get a bullish signal to enter. Will you enter? We always pay attention to what's going on in the next timeframe because otherwise we only have 1/2 the picture and we will end up taking trades against the trend of the day. The triple arrows (M15 arrows) are very useful on your M5 charts because if the M5 arrow and the M15 arrows are in agreement, then you have a pretty clear indication of which way the PA is most likely to go.

--- 帖子 #12665 ---
LOL.....I just this minute explained that we do not necessarily wait for the arrow, but we become concerned if we don't see it soon after entry. Unless we're going to delete everything else and just trade the arrows, of course we will have to expect the arrow to come shortly after our entry, in which case 'technically' we would have entered counter to the arrow. In that movie, the previous bull run had completed and a bear run had begun, and this was confirmed by the pivot, the session change, the candle colour, the yellow ma, the stoch and the MTF stoch. That is what our entry rules are....as stated in Post #2. We would have been concerned if the arrows did not appear shortly after the entry (which they did), because that *might* be a warning that the bull run is going to resume.

--- 帖子 #12695 ---
That indeed would be a nightmare..but there is a bit of a difference running a script and using an order manager EA. Using a script, in the context of orders, is somewhat like giving a one-time command to your broker's machine and then walking away...the only party concerned with the command afterwards is your broker's computer..there is no actionable information relating to the order stored on your computer. Using an order manager is like having someone on your computer who is capable of maintaining a conversation with your broker's computer about any orders you instruct your person/manager to oversee. Some managers have the option of retaining the pre-set [or added after execution] SL and or TP to themselves, but most pass that information to the broker's computer by default, except you specify otherwise. The convenience of managers like luktoms' is its modification of SLs, TPs, BEs etc by dragging those lines on one's chart; and having all that data instantly relayed to your broker. Well, you wouldnt really need a VPS to use an order manager safely (perhaps more for trading robots as we know); but if you had to use a VPS, I know of a reliable free one. Amazon provides such a service, its a bit of a convoluted process setting it up though.

--- 帖子 #12696 ---

--- 帖子 #12726 ---
Last year, all of last year, the volatility in the markets was way down on previous years, and certainly way down on this year (so far). There are many pairs which have ATR's of well over 150 pips/day, and we have seen many, many moves of more than 200 pips/day. Last year, and I'm just guessing here, the volatility was way down in the 60 pips/day region on average although there was the odd days (of course) where we got some great runs. Even so, profits still came just the same. HPT's still came, but they may not have run so far as this year, but they were still easy to spot and the exits were the same as now. Everything was pretty much the same as now, just that the price didn't move as far as it has been doing this year. Bearing in mind the above, we don't need 150 pip/day moves in order to be profitable. It's nice to have big moves and bank lots of pips, but you can do very nicely indeed on much, much less than that if you apply lot size compounding. Download the 'Daily Pip Target' spreadsheet from Post #1 and you will see what I mean. As I'm sure you've noticed, the first 3 or 4 hours of London session are where the pips often come from. During this time it should not be difficult to pick up 50 pips....and that's all you need. There's no need to try and force the issue and end up with a loss, if there isn't a HPT set up, then keep your money in your pocket and lose nothing. Tomorrow there might be a set up that gives up 70 pips, the next day 40, the next day 65, the next day 10 etc etc etc. Try not to fall into the trap of aiming for 50/day 'at all costs'........the 50/day target is an average, as I'm sure you can see. If you can end the week/month with an average of 50/day and you apply the compounding method, you'll be very happy. With compounding, as you can see from the spreadsheet, the numbers get very big towards the end....but....the risk doesn't change. The risk is always the same, just the $ amount's change......the risk is the same and the target is the same. As I have said many times before, patience is the holy grail for fx trading, imo. Too many people feel compelled to be in a trade just because they can be.....or because they fear missing out on a move. If you are constantly 'in a trade' just because you can be, then your win:loss rate will suffer. Lets say you enter 100 trades/week...you might only win half of them, and with the right MM you will still be profitable.....but it's pretty stressful doing it that way. Instead if you wait (drinking coffee) for the perfect HPT set up, chances are you will win 85% of your trades. So you might make (say) 10 trades/week, but win 85% of them, for not a lot of stress....or....make 100 trades/week and win 50% of them, for a lot more stress. Have a think about it.....check out the spreadsheet and then make your decision. And by the way, I don't think you're an idiot or arrogant....we all have to take that leap of faith at some stage, and as long as you are patient and let the trades come to you, I think you'll be fine.

The easiest solution is remove all the indicators and add them back one by one. I only use the #MTF Arrow 2.01 and the GenesisArrowMatrix 1.20_2 You dont need to have the double ups (ie arrows in chart and on the matrix at bottom) but that is just a personal preference.

--- 帖子 #12795 ---
- Remove the ASCTrend4TF Matrix. - Add the ASCTrend3TF Matrix instead - Set TimeFrame1.Period to 30; set TimeFrame2.Period to 60; set TimeFrame3.Period to 240 - Close MT4 - Restart MT4 You'll have all the HTF information you wish...and you can read the 5 and 15 minute arrows from the chart directly instead of looking 'down' at another matrix.

So you have identified that the M5 stoch , candle, MA, bounce of pivot are good and that the trend is up.....let me throw the M15 stoch in there as well. The trend is up....you said so yourself.....the PA was bouncing along the DP all day unable to get below it.....which is not surprising in an uptrend. Now, just after Tokyo open the M5 and M15 stochs were very high, and they both dropped to below the 20 line before Frankie came online...yet...the PA still stayed on top of the pivot. So, we have 5 factors in favour the bulls, plus we have the fact that for the previous 24 hours the bulls have been in full control, and I said so at the time. Now we also have the Matrix in agreement. So in total we have 9 solid reasons why a long is worth the VERY SMALL SL.......and one more thing.....the Yen, as I have been saying again and again is being weakened by Abe and his 'bold action'...UJ had gone from 77 to 100 in 2 months!!! So we have all these reasons to enter the trade for a small risk, and you have a problem with it because of the range. Man, I'll take the 9 or 10 reasons to enter a cheap trade rather than 1 reason why not to. I have said many time, that trading is not an exact science...if it was we could create an EA and retire rich people. At some stage you have to apply discretion and go with the probabilities. Sometimes it is prudent to stay out of a range until a breakout.....other times you have 9 or 10 reasons to enter a cheap trade, and a single reason not to. You choose.

The new page numbering is something that you can change. You see, FF in their wisdom changed the default 15 posts per page to 20 posts per page, which is why the numbering is all up the creek. But, if you click on your username, your personal 'Control Panel' will appear at the top left of the page. Click 'User Options'....and at the bottom of the options page is 'Thread Display Options'. Change the default setting to 'Show 15 Posts Per Page', and you will be back to what you've been used to Glad you're getting to grips with the stoch and hope you enjoy the book.....I still do

--- 帖子 #13064 ---
That's essentially a regular bullish divergence.....check out the divergence cheat sheet on Post #1. It doesn't much matter whether the candles are forming a lower low or not....as long as they are not forming higher lows of course. The point is that a divergence exists. Not sure about the 95% rate, but it's always good to watch these divergences because in many cases, especially on the higher TF's, they can be very reliable

--- 帖子 #13065 ---
The majority of the trades I take on m5 are based on divergence from the higher timeframes. You have to be careful though not to jump in until confirmed thats the mistake most people make where divergence is concerned. Take a look at ej h1 chart yesterday well before the big move up thats the reason I was only in longs on m5. Sorry I can't post a chart at the moment as Im on a mobile phone.

--- 帖子 #13066 ---
That is what I did before posting that picture. The main reason why I posted it is that there is a "horizontal" divergence formed there, at least that is how it's explained in the video. It's significant distinction from regular bullish divergence (where price forms LL) is that it will work fast and is highly reliable whereas divergence with LL in PA might work only after PA continues to move in the same direction but with lower speed. RJ, sorry if this is rubbish, will delete if you say so.

--- 帖子 #13070 ---
In that video lecturer emphasizes that divergence on stoch itself is not a signal to enter, but rather notification that PA is likely to reverse. He says it works almost perfect when price is stuck on some horizontal S/R level but stoch is not confirming that move will continue and printing a divergence.

--- 帖子 #13118 ---
I see what you're saying, and you're not wrong, but the voting system plays a part in this mess too. When I was a little boy, we didn't have much money. Yes, Mum was a full time staff nurse at Dad was an aircraft engineer for British Airways (then B.O.A.C), so it's not like there wasn't a reasonable income for the 2 child family. The difference between then and now is (and you touched on this) that in the 21st century, people want everything RIGHT NOW!! And to make that happen, they will borrow as much as they need or can borrow. My parents had a mortgage, and everything else was paid for with cash...ie savings. Not enough money?.....then we can't afford it....period!! But today, young families want the house, the 2 cars, the new computers, the iphones, the overseas holidays etc etc etc etc......right down to the latte on a Saturday morning while shopping.....which goes on the credit card! People don't seem to realise that all this borrowed money that they get from the bank, credit union or wherever, is also borrowed. The banks etc all have to borrow on the open market and this, of course, increases the countries debt....which in turn comes full circle and costs the borrower (and the not borrow) more and more. Now, the welfare system, that you also touched on, is a huge drain on a countries balance sheet. Successive governments have bribed their way into office by offering more welfare.....usually the parties to the left are the main culprits, but they will offer more and more in order to buy votes. A simple example here: In NZ anyone at all can go to university (as long as he/she isn't a complete muppet of course). The course fee's can be borrowed via a government 'Student Loan' and if the student is away from home, he/she will receive a 'living allowance' that is equal to the dole. This living allowance does not need to be repaid. The student loans debt, even for little NZ, is in the billions of dollars.......yet.......when the last Labour govt was running out of votes, they bought the entire student block of votes by stating that if elected, all student loans would be free of any interest ....... It gets worse.......the graduate can just leave NZ and that's the end of the matter! The do not need to worry about their debt because it will be deducted from their salary at the rate of 6%, in the event that they return to NZ. The consequence of this is that graduate doctors, teachers, pilots etc etc etc rack up a pretty big debt (interest free) and then take off overseas to earn bigger salaries than they could here......those of us left here are burdened with this debt. There are many more examples, but you get the idea! Now, we do have a proportional representation system here and this means (in a nutshell) that smaller parties can get a seat or more in parliament....and no ponce party can govern outright. The government is always a coalition. In order for either of the main parties to gain enough seats to govern, they need to negotiate with the smaller parties who have also won seats. During those negotiations the smaller parties state the price of their support.....for example....We have a 'Gold Card' for senior citizens which affords them discounts at various stores, bus rides, movies, ferry tickets and much more. This was sorely needed and it was gained because on of the smaller parties made that the price of their support to both the major parties. Neither of the major parties could form a govt without the support of the minor party(s) and that support costs! Further, if further on during the govts term in office they start 'going off the rails', the smaller parties can walk....and force either a backtrack in policy or they can cross the floor and vote against the govt.....they can even force a new election, which has happened. Like I said before, they system isn't perfect, not by a long shot, but it is more in line with democracy than the FPP system or the American system...imo!

--- 帖子 #13133 ---
ASCTrend1 Matrix/Tape indicators have been updated. Get them on the first post . Should solve the problem one member had over a week ago with the matrix not showing correct data. It was a result of data being downloaded after the indicator was added to the chart. By mistake, the single timeframe newbar function was used in matrix indicators instead of the MTF one. - Fixed updating of bars on all timeframes as new data is being downloaded. - Draw blank dot if there is not data for the bar.

--- 帖子 #13206 ---
The pivot point indi is supplied for you in the zip file on Post #1. Pivots do vary because brokers just will not adhere to a standard which sucks. However, as Jamz has said above, actionforex pivots are correct. So, the pivots drawn on your chart by the supplied indi *must* match (almost exactly) those in the table at actionforex. If they do not, get another broker. Don't be fooled into trying a different indi....the pivot calculation is very simple, and all indi's use the same calc.....it's the data supplied by the broker that can vary, which gives false pivots....iow...rubbish data in = rubbish pivots shown!!

--- 帖子 #13295 ---
Hi, On my monitors I have an M5 and an M15 chart for each pair that I trade, and I'm looking for the 2 TF's to agree on a trade before I enter. Sometimes the trade is more clear to see on the M5, sometimes it's more clear on the M15, the important thing is that both TF's are in agreement . I do look at the H1, H4, Daily and Weekly at least once a day, just to see how the 'big picture' is developing, and if I see anything worth noting, then I jot it down in my dairy and put a sticky on the page. Yes FXI Pivots is very good because you can see past pivot levels as well, rather than just todays pivots, which is the case for many other pivot indies. As I said though, it's essential that the information going into the pivot indi is correct if we expect to see accurate pivot information displayed on the chart. If there brokers server time (or off set) is wrong, then the information will be wrong. Some brokers use a Sunday candle, which also is wrong and gives incorrect information. There are other pivot indies that you can use that have setting you can adjust to compensate for this, but then we have dalylight saving to consider as well. So my advice is to find a broker with the correct server time. My broker has it all wrong, so I do my charting on a demo account of a broker who has it set properly. I find this whole pivot difference extremely annoying and very childish of the brokers......we have an accepted global time standard called 'GMT', so if all brokers used the same offset, GMT + 2, we wouldn't have this issue. I wonder why they persist in such pettiness?.......anyway....that's another story!!

--- 帖子 #13317 ---
If I have the M5 and M15 agree with each other, and our other indicators (Matrix, stochs etc) also agree, then I will take the trade. even if the M30 and H1 ASCTrend say opposite....BUT.....I will be well aware that the larger TF trend (M30 and H1) are opposite, so I know that this trade may not be a big one, and that I should consider exiting in profit at the next pivot, round number or whatever. If I am lucky enough to enter a trade where all 4 ASCTrend TF's agree, and the MAtrix, stoch etc also agree, then the trade may turn into a decent runner and instead of exiting at the next pivot, round number etc, I will move my SL up into (more) profit and look to see if the PA is going to move on to the next pivot etc etc. It's just a matter of experience, but, as I said a while back, all you need to do right now is to get consistent. 20 pips per day is great start. 20 pips per day compounding (as per the spreadsheet on Post #1) is still a very good earn over 6 months. --- 帖子 #13389 ---
I find it quite fascinating that most traders in the early stages, want to constantly want to take the hero trade against the HTF trend. I know for ages, that was exactly how I traded. Constantly getting chopped up. Or the rare occasion I got a reversal, there was massive volatility, and by the time my trade entered profit, I was so relieved, I would close with a small profit. Not very profitable (in fact, losses), but also hugely stressful. Forex markets are renown for their strong trends, which is why we are all here in the first place. There are so many easy trades, trading with HTF trend, I think the mindset should be "I am looking for retracement to enter with HTF trend", NOT "here is a reversal that is going to turn the entire markets, and I am going to get a huge reversal" The later rarely happens, the former happens most of the time !!

--- 帖子 #13498 ---
Padila, I personally consider any signal that does not agree with the Hourly and up(H/D/W) a counter trend trade. Of course a counter trend trade in my book, is not considered a high probability trade. Thus, it can very well go against you very quickly. You have to keep a very tight SL. Some times it works, but often times it doesn't. It's like swimming upstream. Why would you do that? Swim downstream. Don't get me wrong, you can certainly rack up pips just using the 5/15 method to scalp hitting singles all day, while at times you may get lucky and hit it big. It all adds up. I personally prefer to increase my chances of hitting a double, triple or Home run while minimizing any draw down. That's just me. It's like trading a higher TF but instead of entering automatically at the close of their candle, you pinpoint your entry by entering on pullbacks using the lower TF. Analogy - The weekly TF is like the tide. The daily TF is like the wave within the tide, and the hourly is like the ripple within the wave. When all is lined up then it's clear sailing. I apply that methodology to my trading. So if the hourly is lined up with the higher TF, you use the lower TF to line up with the higher TF to optimize your entry. That is what I call a high probability trade. Trade with the ripple, the wave and the tide at your back, and you will rake in the pips. OK Grasshopper? Hope that helps.

Hi Zerrox, This high time frame issue is one I have been trying to tackle for some time and did post earlier about. There have been discussions about HTF confirmation of trend and Marty and RJ have contributed about it more recently again. I accept that it is only with experience one can identify accurately, the higher time frame trends, almost by just eyeballing the chart. However, to make it objective, I am looking at a few things: 1) Day, H4 charts: for levels of support/resistance, candle stick patterns, trend lines. These charts need looking once/twice a day. 2) H1 chart: to look at in the morning and again from time to time, but definitely before major market open times. To note down if there is a trend in H1, if so, the direction. 3) For H1, H4 trends: I have added ASCTrend MTF to my charts recently. I am not going to take any trade against H1 trend as given by the ASCTrend and most of the time not against H4. Any counter-H4 or counter D1 trade is CT for me and if entered, due precaution will be taken. There will be no counter-H1 trade at all. 4) Once H1 trend is identified, actual entry is according to Genesis/stochastics as per post #2. Consider DP/S1/R1 etc as per usual. Not to forget BRN. This is my plan for backtesting during the weekend and to test out next week. Majority of my losing trades were/are the ones taken against the dominant trend. I am hoping that I will be successful in filtering out those losing trades with the above plan. Hopefully, one day I will be able to tell myself confidently that if I am not seeing a setup/trade on the chart, that is because it is not there! Wait until what I need to see appears on the chart. I recognise that what I have just written has been already discussed here multiple times before. I suppose I am writing this post just as a memo for myself. Good weekend to all.

--- 帖子 #13534 ---
By definition nothing repaints before the candle is closed. So of course D1 can change colour 100 times (so to speak) in a day but that is not called repaint. The Asctrend matrix is constructed to look at 4 time frames. Let us consider M5, M15, H1 and H4. After 5 minutes the M5 dot of the matrix is fixed. It will not change (no repaint). All other three can change but that happends only because they are still open. After 15 minutes the M15 dots (three of them) are fixed and so on. Important note. The fact that the higher time frame dots can change at any moment (till they are closed), does not mean that we can not take high probability trades (HPT) by following their signals (even for the still open time frames) The colour alignment of all dots of the standard matrix plus the Asctrend matrix is a very powerfull indication of a HPT. Take into consideration time of day, pivots and stoch as well and SHOOT!

Hi Sio, I'll just add my 5c while MKFXTrade is sleeping. For me, I check the H4 a couple of times a day, and I check the Daily once, and also the Weekly I check just to see how things are progressing. For the actual trades I look at the M15 chart where I can see 2 days worth of movement, so I get a good overall idea of what is going on in the (relatively) short term, and I look for an entry on the M5, as per the setup up criteria we all know. I do use the ASCITrend indi from Xaphod, but I don't show it on the charts for 2 reasons.... 1) I want to keep continuity going for the whole thread for the sake of newcomers to the thread, and the indi is not essential to profitability, it just makes life easier and the charts cleaner. 2) When I enter on the M5 with our usual criteria, I want to see at least the M5 ASCITrend colour match the Genesis Matrix. Without that, I am reluctant to enter.....preferably I want to see the M15 colour match the Matrix too. If I see the H1 and H4 ASCITrend also matching the Matrix, then I know for certain that I am trading with the wind at my back and the trade is (probably) a HPT. If the ASCITrend H1 and H4 are opposite colours, I will still take the trade (because perhaps the trend is changing), but I will be cautious and aware that I need to set a modest target and manually trail my SL. I expect we all do it slightly differently, and MKFXTrade may well have his own variation which will be interesting to see By the way....I know I throw a lot at Abe and Noda and several others in your govt and BOJ, please be sure that it isn't anything personal.....I throw it all the muppets in suits, including that NZ idiot Wheeler who just wasted millions of our dollars intervening into a falling market.....in fact Wheeler is the muppet of the year (so far) for me....although Bernanke is in with chance too!!

--- 帖子 #13735 ---
Sio bel, RJ did a great job of explaining how he uses the HTF to trade. I will add my personal answer as well. High probability trades are the only trades I try to stay discipline in taking. What do I consider a HPT? A HPT is a trade which moves PA on the lower TF, in the direction of the higher TF(Hourly-Daily-Weekly). If all you did was concentrate on this method, and you use Genesis to help pull that trigger on the lower TF, IMO you've already increase your chances of a successful trade. Does that mean the trade is 100% guarantee of success? Of course not. Nothing is guaranteed, but why not try to increase your odds? Put the odds in your favor as to speak. I start the week by analyzing the weekly, then the daily to gauge the trend bias. When both are in agreement then there is a bias in the market(Short or Long). If they are not in agreement then the market is ranging and I try NOT to trade that pair. If there is a bias established by what I just describe, then I use the lower TF to align it in that direction. This is what is termed in the market as a HPT. It prevents over trading, and minimizes the whipsaw by the market. This is how I trade. You must find your way, and what fits your style and personality. GL Hope this answers your question and it's understandable what I am writing. Cheers

--- 帖子 #13779 ---
You have to get out of that habit, because it will do you no good, either for your long term life on this thread, or you long term life on the FX market. When you see that H1 divergence, it's good to bear it in mind as an *additional* reason to enter a short once you have all the other indications in place. If the system tells you to enter short, *and* you have a bearish divergence, then that's great.....but the short is valid with or without the divergence. When you *expect* a move down because you see a divergence, you have a bias. Just about every other thread at FF works on bias, and expectations, and predictions......but *not* this thread, and *not* this system. Bias, expectations, and predictions are not welcome here......we are system traders. End of story. Ok?

--- 帖子 #13780 ---
Understanding what is going to happen on the market after some suit has finished yappin really is a crap shoot. For that reason I don't try to decipher what the suit is yappin about and what it means. It's good that we know that this high impact news is coming because we can get out of the way of the madness and not get (financially) hurt......but trying to trade those events is crazy, imo. Our income comes from the boring day to day movement of the market, and we have a system that is very good at helping us enter at the right time. If we were trading the news, and if we got it right, we would have a nice little bonus. However, if we get it wrong, we can do some serious damage to our accounts because in a sudden move, your SL will suffer terrible slippage and spreads will widen, sometimes considerably. So lets assume that we trade such events, and lets assume that we get it right half the time.......the bonus pips are good, and that would happen what, once or twice a week? Offset that against the ones we get wrong, and suddenly the bonus pips don't look so good. Now have a look at the pips we make every day in the boring market as a result of patience and a good system. The boring pips by far outweigh the 'news' pips. do they not? So.....is the stress and increased blood pressure etc worth it? For me, no......it's not worth it. I would rather have a cup of coffee and see what the charts look like after all the nonsense has died down.

--- 帖子 #13809 ---
Hi RJ - medium term lurker here. I was wondering if you could describe how you see the difference between a bias and trading with the trend? I completely agree that expectations and predications are not helpful, but to me identifying a trend is the same as having a bias - or have I got it wrong. Thanks

--- 帖子 #13810 ---
Interesting question We trade according the entry criteria of the system, plain and simple. We look for high probability trades, which is to say that we want as many indicators as we can have (within the system) to agree......and we would like it to be from a known s/r line or area.....and we would like it to be during the recognised 'good' times of the day for trading......and we would like it to be *with the trend*. Trading with the trend is not so much a bias, it's just a sensible thing to do. A bias is like: 'I see a bearish divergence so I'm looking for a short'....or....'the PA has reached a double top so I'm looking to go short here'......or......'yesterday ended with a shooting start formation so I'm looking for short entries' All of the above examples make the person conditioned to look for short entries...that is his bias.....that is what he wants to see...what he expects to see. When the price goes 15 pips the other way, he thinks 'that's ok...that will give me a better place to enter short'.....then it goes 30 pips the other way, and he thinks, 'I didn't really expect that, but now I should get a short signal soon and what a great place to get in on. But it doesn't happen.....it goes another 20 pips the other way, and he's still looking for a short entry......but.....if he didn't have that short bias, he would have taken the 50 pips on offer for a long trade. That's the danger of a bias.....us humans are conditioned to believe what we think will happen.....to our detriment. If you look around other threads you'll see statements like, 'When EU gets to 1.2700 I will go long there.' So the PA will go to 1.2700 and he will be looking *only* for a long entry, and by the time he concedes that he was wrong in his analysis, it might be too late to go short, and he missed a 100 pip opportunity. That is bias. Trading with the trend is not really a bias, it's just a sensible thing to do

--- 帖子 #13811 ---
In short A trend is something you can see and measure. It is there, on your charts. A bias is just a wishfull thinking concerning future.

--- 帖子 #13821 ---
It's very difficult to pin a trend down to a specific TF. The reality is that trends become apparent on different TF's and if I go out on a limb and say (for example) 'I mean the H4 trend'........there's going to come a time when the H4 is ranging but there is a decent trend on the H1, and even better on M30.....so I will trade that trend, but bearing in mind that it is a relatively weak trend. As soon as I do that, someone is going to jump down my throat and say "but RJ, you siad the trend was on H4 and there is not H4 trend so WTF are you doing?"....lol.....so I'm not going out on that limb. Trends are on many TF's...the larger the TF, the stronger the trend and the longer the trade *may* run for. I spot the trend without thinking, and so do many others here......it's just one of things that will come to everyone over time as they spend more and more hours looking at charts!

--- 帖子 #13842 ---
Hello guys. Just caught up on all post since yesterday evening. I have seen a couple of posters with not such successful trades, even though they THINK they are trading with the higher TF trend. You must realize that after yesterday's very bearish run on most pairs, there would have needed to be some kind of a retrace. The retraces can be best evaluated using the hourly TF stochastics. Once Stochastics reaches it retrace extremes OB/OS, then IMO, one can start looking for trade setups again using the lower TF(per genesis rules) to pull the trigger in the direction of trend again. The main trend is the daily/weekly. The hourly is used to measure the retrace or alignment with the trend. You can't just automatically pull the trigger every time you see an alignment of your matrix with the (daily/weekly). You must align the hourly with the daily and weekly. This is the method of trading using higher TF. Of course if you just want to scalp and pull trigger on every scalp then this doesn't pertain to that trading style. Scalping is a different animal. Hope this is understandable. Happy trading today. Analogy: The hourly- Is the ripple in the water The Daily- Is the wave The weekly - Is the Tide

--- 帖子 #13960 ---
I think you need to take a break. Have a rest from trading and re-think your strategy and apply some logic to it. Also, re-read all the stoch information on Post #1. See the chart below.....the stoch has fallen....yet the price continues to fall. Just because the stoch has fallen that does not necessarily mean that the price is over sold...it can also mean that the bulls are very strong, so a short entry on a pullback is valid. Also, when Cody, Olivia, Wiz3003 and I worked on the 15/5 strategy, we looked first the 60 - 5 strategy developed for the Symphonie system by Yelena. We all agreed that unless we we in a very strong trend, the time difference between M5 and M60 was far too great. There are 12 5 minute 'blocks' per 60 minutes. That is to say that the trend may turn in the first one or two 5 minute blocks, but it won't become apparent until the H1 candle closes......in 50 minutes time!! If that were to happen....and it will happen, the M15 will pick it up within 3 5 minute blocks.......3 x 5 = 15. The 60/5 method can work in a decent trend, but it *will* catch you out sooner or later....and in short trends or choppy markets like EU has been most of this year, you will get killed!! Take some time out man.....calm down.....this is simple, don't make it harder than it is. Have a look at the 5 - 15 PDF and come back next week with a clear head....and read up on stoch

--- 帖子 #13963 ---
And in my chart, the stoch has fallen......yet the PA continues to fall another 80 pips!!! The relationship between M1 and M5 (as in the "how I trade the m5/m1" pdf is much, much different: M1 - M5 relationship: 5 m1 blocks = m5 M5 - M15 relationship: 3 m5 blocks = m15 M5 - H1 relationship: 12 m5 blocks = H1 Do you see the huge difference? Between M1 and M5 there is no other TF available, so we use what we have Between M5 and M15 there is no other TF available, so we use what we have Between M5 and H1 we have the choice of the closest relation which is M15.....we have another choice of M30 as well.....yet you're stretching it out to H1. The relationship is getting too distant, imo.

--- 帖子 #14072 ---
It's difficult to pin it down to exacts because each case differs. If you have a look at the Aussie today, it smashed the DP, but then retested it. Then it smashed R1, and retested it. Currently it's sitting just under R2. Most of the Yen crosses did the same...smashed through and the retested before continuing. The break - retest - continue is probably the most common one we see, but sometimes the level is broken with much power and never retested, and if you're waiting for the retest, you just missed out!! Other time the price creeps the the level and just continues on up, or down as the case may be. So you see it's very hard to pin it down. For sure though, I would not enter a trade right under on right on top of a major S/R level.....at the very least I want the level to break and a new candle open well clear of the level before considering my next move.

--- 帖子 #14073 ---
Thanks - I suspected it was a case of 'each case differs'.

--- 帖子 #14318 ---
Once you download the indicators from post #1, and put the Genesis template, you get the following in M5: 1) Price action in Heiken Ashi candles. 2) 5 MA 3) Pivot Points 4) Genesis Matrix (TVI, CCI, T3, GHL) in M5 time frame 5) Stochastics M5 and M15 at settings 11,3,3 in two different windows. 6) M5 and M15 Arrows on the chart. Upload the template and check that the above are present. These are the indicators you need to trade Genesis. Other indicators are mainly higher time frames of Arrow, Stochastics and Genesis Matrix. You can consider the higher time frames once you are familiar with the basic template. Higher time frame Arrow is available in Matrix form which is Genesis Arrow Matrix. ASCTrend MTF is basically the Arrow indicator in MTF. ASCTrend1i just needs to be present in your indicator folder and works from the background to generate the M5 and M15 arrows on the chart, I would not worry about it separately. I would try out the basic set up first and then add the higher time frame indicators. Look at Xaphod's thread for the Additional indicators. If you read the whole of Xaphod's thread, the additional indicators and their function will be clear. Read post #1 carefully including the links and get familiar with the set up first. Read Marty's posts and look at the charts posted by RJ, MKFXTrader and others to get an idea. Hope it helps. Best wishes.

--- 帖子 #14416 ---
Glad you enjoy. You don't' need to go too deep into fundamentals, but to have your 'finger on the pulse' often helps. For instance, the UJ pair fell back under 100 yesterday because people immediately went to the 'safe' currencies when the poor USA manufacturing data was released. Of course 100.00 is a major 'line in the sand' and it could act as resistance to any further moves north from the UJ pair, especially as that pair hasn't really made much progress even when it was over 100. Then, a few hours ago, Abe said: " that he will push forward with his economic growth strategy despite recent volatile market moves. "The markets have been showing unstable moves recently, but I will firmly shoot the 'three arrows'," Abe said, referring to his growth strategy, at an assembly of Japan's biggest business lobby Keidanren" .....which the market see's as a green light for more moves to weaken the Yen, so they take their money out of the Yen and bingo.....the UJ pair immediately heads north and adds 50 pips in the space of 1 hour. to sit now at 100.30. So, further moves north *might* be on the cards for the UJ pair......at the very least, shorting UJ might be a silly thing to do. So it's just a matter of knowing the basics without too much in depth analysis, and that knowledge should be useful in such situations. As far as the EU pair is concerned, I really am at a loss to understand why EU is not in the 1.20's......so I just trade what Genesis indicates, but I don't expect any 'home runs' on that pair.

--- 帖子 #14482 ---
I think it's more the characteristics of the GU pair. GU is ranked the 4th most actively traded currency in the world ( http://www.therichest.org/business/m...ed-currencies/ data a couple of years old, but still very relevant), and is also the 3rd largest component of the USD Index ( http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Dollar_Index ) . So it's not thin by any means. Certainly more active than say the Aussie which is probably easier to trade. It just takes a lot more work to trade it confidently, as it is more volatile and has more frequent fakeouts.
