--- 帖子 #14850 ---
My 5c on the subject that is troubling you is this......that fear, or anxiety, will never go away completely......and that's a good thing. For example. I have been a skydiver for many years now, and the first time I jumped I was pretty damn scared....but I just put all my faith in my training (this thread) and my equipment (Genesis system), and the jump went well.....so well in fact that I went straight back up and did it again! However, once I got to the door that same fear came back and I wondered why I had just put myself back in the very position that scared the life out of me a couple of hours ago!!! But, I kept the faith and all went well. To cut a long story short.....years and over a thousand jumps later, I STILL get that anxiety as I prepare to exit the aircraft. I wouldn't say that I'm scared like I used to be, but I am certainly very well aware of what it is that I am about to do.....and the consequences of making a mistake. So I check my gear as we near our designated altitude......I ask others to check my gear, and I check theirs. I stick my head out the door to make sure we are in the right piece of sky and to look for other aircraft......I check my gear again and I go through the emergency procedure in my head......I close my eyes and touch my emergency equipment and I rehearse the jump in my head....when I see that we are in the right place in the sky, I call for the pilot to 'Power off' and I have one last look at everyone in the aircraft to make sure that all is as it should be......then we go ahead with the jump. The point to all this is: The anxiety that I feel on 'jump run', is similar to the anxiety that you are feeling until your trade is safe......that feeling may diminish over time, but it won't go away. And it's good that it won't go away because it will keep you safe from making stupid mistakes. It won't work out in your favour every time.....same with skydiving....twice my parachute has not deployed correctly but my reserve parachute (Stop Loss...lol) saved me. Feel the Fear, But Do it Anyway!!

--- 帖子 #14999 ---
Well there's 2 points here..... 1. The arrows are not to be used in isolation. They are an additional indication remember. As we've said on the thread, we don't have to wait for an arrow if everything else lines up. but we would be concerned if an arrow didn't appear shortly afterwards. 2. Any indicator will dance around in this kind of chop. Here is the full chart, with the Genesis Matrix and the stoch. See the Matrix giving false signals?...see the stoch doing the same? That's what happens in choppy markets and that's why we don't use single indicators in isolation. Of course we will still get the occasional false signal, but when we combine all the indicators, we greatly reduce the false signals generated. Note: I have taken the arrows out for this screenshot

--- 帖子 #15035 ---
Some news from the G8 'Meeting' that I found a moment ago might interest some. I'll post the text because the link is full of other crap. US-EU trade agreement back on table The United States and the European Union launched talks on Monday to create one of the world's most ambitious free-trade zones, as France again underscored its determination to protect its movies and culture. A trans-Atlantic free trade agreement was first considered three decades ago but was knocked down by France in the 1990s. Europe has now managed to get Paris onside, opening the way to a deal that could boost the EU and US economies by more than US$100 billion ($125 billion) a year each. "This is a once-in-a-generation prize and we are determined to seize it," said British Prime Minister David Cameron, flanked by US President Barack Obama and leaders of European Union institutions before a Group of Eight summit in Northern Ireland. The United States and Europe account for almost half of the world's total output and a third of its trade. France had threatened to block the start of talks until the EU's other 26 governments accepted its demand to shield movies and online entertainment from competition from Hollywood and Silicon Valley. Paris eventually won at least a temporary exclusion for such industries. Tensions came to a head again on Monday after European Commission President Jose Manuel Barroso told a newspaper that opposition to opening Europe's culture industry to competition was "reactionary" and part of an anti-globalisation agenda. French President Francois Hollande said the comments had been a "bit of a shock, a bit of a surprise" and France would not allow the issue back on the negotiating table. Barroso, aware of the upset in Paris, stressed he believed help was needed for some forms of culture which "are not exactly like other sorts of goods". But, with an eye on Washington, he said audiovisual services could yet be put on the table. "I hope this is understood by our American partners," he said. Obama warned against narrowing the scope of the talks. "It is important that we get it right and that means resisting the temptation to downsize our ambitions or avoid tough issues just for the sake of getting a deal," he said. Those tough issues are likely to include agriculture. The American Farm Bureau Federation, representing big USagricultural interests, urged Washington to do away with the "endless array of non-tariff barriers" in Europe to its exports, including for genetically modified crops. While US and EU negotiators are aware that a final deal will be tough to clinch, they are also conscious of the rising power and influence of China and the need to deepen Western economic integration in order to compete with Asia. 'POLITICAL WILL' The United States and the European Commission, the executive arm of the 27-country European Union, hope for a free-trade deal by the end of 2014 - a tight deadline in complex international trade talks that usually take many years. "We must maintain that political will in the months ahead," Cameron said. The London-based Centre for Economic Policy Research estimates a pact - to be known as the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership - could boost the EU economy by €119b a year, and the US economy by €95b. However, a report commissioned by Germany's non-profit Bertelsmann Foundation said the United States may benefit more than Europe. A deal could increase GDP per capita in the United States by 13 per cent over the long term but by only 5 per cent on average for the European Union, the study found. Businesses on both sides would like an agreement in which a car tested for safety in the United States would not have to be tested again in Europe, and a drug deemed safe by Brussels would not have to be approved as well by the US government. Following the collapse of global trade talks in 2008, both the United States and Europe have sought to strike as many free-trade agreements as possible, and Brussels alone is negotiating with more than 80 countries. The first round of EU-US negotiations will take place in Washington on July 8, the White House said in a statement. - Reuters

--- 帖子 #15044 ---
TradeFinder, Yes they are the same thing, one appears on your price chart ( MTF arrow), the other as an indicator, beneath the price chart (AscTrend matrix). So, yes there is duplication, but (and this is more for the higher TFs), an H1 arrow say, can last quite a period of time. But I like to see (for example a long trade) the green of genesis matrix and genesis arrow matrix all green (or red). With my M15 chart and M5 chart I can easily see multiple TFs confirming by just looking at the last M15 &amp; M5 candles. This is a personal preference of mine. When I see H4 &amp; H1 arrows and Genesis matrix both confirming in the same direction, and you are instantly looking for any M15/M5 trade in that direction. Basically the more TFs you have confirming in the same direction, the greater the probability of the trade. Hope this helps

--- 帖子 #15067 ---
From Post #1 FAQ...which you obviously haven't read....READ IT. No more chances...the door is ajar..... 4. Do these indicators repaint? No, none of the Genesis indicators repaint. It may seem that way if you have (say) an M15 indicator on your M5 chart, but once the period candle has closed, in this case, the M15, then the indicator paints to the chart permanently. Of course while the M15 candle is still in progress, the indicator may *seem* to repaint because the candle is not yet closed. This question has been addressed many times so you can search for more in depth explanation.

The asctrend matrix is not the genesis arrow so it is not the source of the message. Furthermore, the Genesis Matrix and Asctrend matrix will show the symbol as part of the message. The source is most likely the MTF arrow indicator which you still have on one of your charts.

Congratulations on a great day's work. I had a great day too and it's nice to get those big pip days every now and then because it puts a smile on our faces and a bonus in our bank accounts. Having said that, if you download the spreadsheet from Post #1, you can see that with 50 pips/day...in 6 months you will have a very nice sized account if you use the compounding method. Of course the spreadsheet doesn't allow for losses or breakeven days, and it doesn't allow for less that 50 pip days or withdrawals...but.....it also doesn't allow for days (like yesterday) when the pips taken exceed the target 50 pips.....so at the end of the day, it will work our more or less in the right ballpark. Even if you reduce the target to 30 or even 20 pips per day, the total in 6 months is still impressive. The good thing about compounding lot sizes is that the risk never changes.....the 'dollar' amount changes, but the risk is always the same.....no matter what. So enjoy the bonus days, and congratulations to you for a great total.....but remember, is the mundane boring old gathering of pips every day that will swell your bank account more that you might imagine in a relatively short time. Check out the spreadsheet

I have mentioned that I trade only indices (yesterday dow went more than 300 pips straight down, extremely hard to trade it ), but out of respect to this thread I will attach a UJ chart (nothing to do with me) just to make my comments clear. If you ask me what do you trade M5 or M15? I will reply M5. But someone could call it M15. Let us see why: Looking at my tempate you see: 1. M5 matrix 2. Three arrows (M5, M15, M30). As I said before it is not (for me) critical to wait for all of them to close. Even if they are alligned for at least five minutes, I consider the move to be strong enough to be continued. 3. A set of M15 and H1 stochs. That sounds like an M15 template eh? (you use stochs 5 and 15 at M5 time frame, so logically you will use stochs 15 and 60 at a M15 time frame). So what do you finally have? A template where it is almost impossible to be caught in the wrong direction of the market and with enough filters to keep yourself away from market noice (I recall the trader from Italy who posted here that he blowed some significant real money accounts by taking almost every m5 matrix signal). On the other hand a significant difference from a purely M15 system is that I do not have to wait, for a full M15 candlle to close. Just an M5 candlle PROVIDED that at the same time all other boxes tick. So my template might originally seems to be slow (waiting all those things to allign), but I assure you that it is really fast I thought that after the HUGE help I have received from RJ and his amazing team, giving back here some of the things I have learnt and found out is my obligation and the least I can do.

--- 帖子 #15286 ---
Nice question! As I mentioned I want to have fast entries. Fast but (relatively) safe. That is why I do not use the H1 arrow as many here do. Had I used it the correct approach would be to wait for the next M5 signal since the H1 arrow usually appears too late considering the initial signal. Since I want to be "in touch" with the H1 time frame, I did a compromise. I use the three arrows (M5,M15 and M30) AND H1 stoch. The M30 arrow appears many times almost together with the M15 arrow when we are going to have a significant move. So I do not have serious delay problems with it. Moreover in ranging or "dead" periods it is usually opposite to the M15 arrow keeping us out from small false moves. At the same time I keep in touch with H1 not via the slow H1 arrow but via the much faster H1 stoch. So according to the above logic I will enter at a closed M5 candlle when all boxes align no matter which their order is. Be carefull though to what I wrote in post 15,253. Not every signal is a blind entry!

--- 帖子 #15316 ---
I can see why you like the stoch tape on your charts Thomas, and I have spent a lot of time over the weekend testing your method over various currencies. I have to agree with Wiz3003 here though, the original stochastic gives much information that just isn't available via the stoch tape. I've said this many time before, but I will say it again....the stochastic oscillator is more than a simple oversold/overbought indicator, and I feel that a lot of vital information is lost if it's treated in that way, or if it using as a 'rising/falling' indicator. If the #MTF stochs are placed on the chart with the same settings as your stoch tape settings, I believe that you are going to be considerably better off with the #MTF stochs simple because they 'tell the whole story' of what is going on, rather than the 'condensed story.' However.....I do see why you like it, but for me, I don't see it as a step forward....I prefer to see the stoch lines and gauge the market action and strength with the more complete information provided by the traditional stochastic indicator.

--- 帖子 #15350 ---
And that's it, in a nut shell......it simply isn't possible to win every trade. When we lose a trade, then we accept that as part of the deal. The biggest mistake is to start changing things because of a few lost trades. Certainly examine your trades, and document your findings in your journal, but there is no need to add stuff to the charts, or delete stuff, or change TF's etc etc......just accept the loss, enter the details into your journal and move on. That's it!

--- 帖子 #15351 ---
Please allow me to present you one more trading idea concerning EU since everybody agrees that it has becove really difficult to trade it during the last few months. EU is extremelly well correleted (inverse correlation) with UsdChf. Almost a perfect inverse match! So you can avoid some bad trades by just placing the two pairs side by side and check their moves. When for instance you have a valid buy signal at EU, do you have at the same time a valid sell signal at UC? If yes, you have a HPT and you should proceed. If no, wait to see if the correlation will take place during the next few minutes and enter when it happens. Otherwise maybe you should consider skipping the trade. Just my humble opinion based on my correlation experience from indices trading.

What I do is just drop a red vertical line on the chart where I enter the trade.....and that line tool is on your menu above your charts....see the circle in the pic I attached. --- 帖子 #15394 ---
Well using that logic, I may as well use the H4 stoch and that way I'll get even more info!!! There seems to be a bit of a 'feeding frenzy' going here about the H1 stoch....but how many here have actually tested this for any length of time? I know Marty uses it and tonight I see that lastingwell uses it, but to me, it is untested. The whole reason we began using the M15 stoch on the M5 chart is because previously, the H1 was used on the M5....creating 60-5 method......not here, but on the Symphonie thread. When we came up with the 15-5 method, we realised that in anything other than a strong trend the 60 -5 method would slaughter the trader because the difference was too great between 5 and 60. The closest was the 15 so we used that......and you can read all about it in the PDF that Wiz3003 published on the subject. So....I am simply applying the same logic that we used previously......that being that the M30 is the next available TF to use. It could be that the H1 is better......but I will never know if I don't test it to find out! So.....I'm testing the M30 with the M15 and after 4 weeks I will know the answer. Then I will do it again with the H1. That is the way we arrive at the best settings......not by blind faith!! Just before I started typing this I entered 2 trades, one on EU and one on EA.....I'll post the charts in a moment.

To me it's like this, the h1 stoch stays OB longer, because it takes more time and a bigger move to create an hourly trend... My interpretation of the 5-60 method is to just trade in the direction of the hourly trend...and to avoid the pair simply if the move is sideways and not up or down. No hourly stochs involved. Just 5 and 15. However I did notice lately, that whenever I am re-entering based on m5+m15 (the way genesis is meant to be traded), sometimes h1 is already moving out of the extremities... So technically I am going counter the new trend... If you look at my EA trade, all three stox were falling from OB... then when it reached my target, the move died down a little, but the hourly stoch was still falling... A few hours later, there was a pullback to the daily pivot and then a drop to the daily support... I personally am beginning to acknowledge the use of h1 stochs as an addition to the regular 5-15 method... Just for some of those trades. It is still way more important to me to actually get an arrow on m15... Because when I carefully analyse my charts, I can see MTF arrows and all signals going opposite of the arrows have been fakeys. So it should be enough to trade with m15...

Sometimes when there's enough buyers the fact that it is close to a resistance means very little. It all depends on the strength that a currency has. I've been trading without taking this into account for the past few weeks (ever since I went back on live), even though when I demoed I was zealously respecting my one rule "not to trade equally strong(or weak) currencies", and I realize now that nothing is more important than being able to make the right choice when picking the pair you are going to take a trade on. I monitor most (all major) jpy crosses and also aussie dollar crosses. On the side I have EU which I follow together with UF (simply because of the - correlation) and GU completely apart. When I asked earlier today what had made the jpy crosses drop, I realized (thanks to RJ's post) that it didn't matter what made them drop, but that they did in fact drop. Which meant a strong yen, from here on out I merely had to pick another currency that is being sold off (using the same method, pretty much), and pair it against the yen. Of course, you can also simply check out the CSM provided in post #1, as it does the job for you and is more visual. I almost got frustrated when I took the last 5 to 10 genesis signals... textbook signals on EU (among others) and trades simply did not work... And I began to suspect that it is because I pair currencies that are equally strong (or weak), and guess what I was right. Doesn't matter the reason, the point is that the people are buying the euro... Once again, I have RJ to thank for opening my eyes to that. Glad you're enjoying my posts and charts, keep in mind I am still very new and not very confident (if confident at all)... Which is why I try never to affirm something, even if I am pretty darn sure about what I am saying. I like it better when any of the more experienced traders can correct me at any time.

People are interesting creatures, as I'm sure you'll agree. Some people just accept things the way they are for some reason whether it be complacency, laziness or blind faith or whatever. Some people like to investigate, test, question etc etc in order to understand the very reason why things are the way they are. I fall into the latter category, probably because my father was an aircraft engineer and my Mum was a nurse. I was the little boy who pulled apart his toy train the day after Christmas in order to see how it worked.....and yes...I did put it back together again. The point is this.....2 people have said that they use the H1 stoch on their M5 charts with considerable success, and I have no reason to doubt them. However, I cannot simply accept that that the H1 stoch is the 'best thing since sliced bread' without testing it or seeing tests that have been conducted over a decent period of time. Some of you just accept it and throw it on your charts and happily put your money on the line without giving it a second thought. If it works....great. If not.....those same people will throw something else on their charts and risk their money with that etc etc. I've seen it a thousand times before and at the end of the day, really I couldn't care less. They say that a fool and his money are easily parted! I post 'live' trades here from time to time. Sometimes I lose a trade....I lost one yesterday. Sometimes I have to take a manual exit at BE....sometimes I can show you a decent 'win' by manually trailing my trades until I get knocked out in a decent profit or I reach my target. Who else here has EVER posted even 1 'live' trade? That's right, in nearly 12 months and more than 15,000 posts, no one other than me has posted any 'live' trades. It's not easy to do, especially as I depend on my trades to keep food on the table, and it sometimes comes at a personal cost of missing another opportunity because I'm posting and not looking for a new trade to add to my existing trade. That's the price I pay sometimes, and I'm ok with that. I know how people like to sit back and watch a 'live' trade on the small TF's because they are concluded in a matter of minutes or hours, but certainly in that day......but no one other than me does it, yet we have a lot of armchair experts and critics here. Plenty seem to be able to 'talk the talk'.....different story when it comes to 'walking the walk' though isn't it? I was going to post the majority of my M15 test as 'live' trades for the next 4 weeks, as time allows, so that we could all watch and learn together. I chose to use the M30 stcoh for reasons that I have explained previously, yet, for the very first trade...lol....the FIRST trade in 4 weeks of testing.....I get to field a barrage of questions, developing into (almost) arguments as to why I should be using the H1 stoch!!! Not only do I receive many posts of the like, I also receive PM's and emails!!....Unbelievable!!! Let me be absolutely crystal clear here......This test is something that I decided to do FOR ME. I'm not doing it for you.....I want to know the results of M15 trading with the M30 stoch and I will share the results with you...both in the 'live' trading and in the analysis and conclusion at the end pf the 4 weeks of trading. You don't get to tell me what to do, or how to run my own tests. It might have been more helpful if you had said something like 'Hey RJ....I'll help you out, you test with M30 stoch and I'll do the test too but I'll use the H1 stoch and we can compare data in 4 weeks time.' But no.....most of you don't want to actually do anything to help out, most of you 'armchair experts' just want to reap the rewards of someone else's efforts. You might even be able to throw in some criticism as well......but remember this.....only fools and politicians criticise a half finished job......and I'm sure that we don't have any politicians in the house. It's easy to sit back and post 'after the fact' trades and never have to 'walk the walk' isn't it? It's easy to sit back and let someone else do the testing and you just enjoy the results...for free isn't it? No effort required. So that's it for me.....I don't need this distraction and I don't need this aggravation. I'm a reasonable trader and there is nothing much for me here. I can probably do better if I don't have to come here and deal with this crap every day. I have given thousands of hours to you all here and I am not going to give any more.....especially when I see a group of vocal critics who have the audacity to tell me how to run my own tests, yet can't even post a 'live' trade of their own, let alone actually roll up their sleeves and help out. So go throw all sorts of indicators at your charts.....do whatever you want...I don't care any more.

--- 帖子 #15522 ---
I feel I need to add something here, and I hope it is not me that caused any issues with RJ. But, perhaps my comments have been misconstrued. I have said I dont trade against H1 stoch, but that doesn't I will trade every time H1 stoch crosses. And here is the beauty of Genesis, we have: - Stoch (momentum) - Genesis matrix (I refer to it as overall strength of move) - Asc Arrows (I refer to the arrows, as a change of direction/trend - MAs (my own preference) So all above in 1 TF aligning is a good sign, the more TFs that agree the better. So to pick out 1 indie, even on just 1 or 2 or 3 TFs, cannot be a good signal. So, what do I like to see to enter a trade ? Well a full Genesis dash/matrix and all TF MAs aligned, is a great start, and all Asc arrows aligning, is better, all that and all stochs crossed in the same direction, is perfect. Are you patient enough to wait for all that to align across H4,H1,M15,M5 ? Is it unrealistic to expect all to ever align, OR is it when all align, that is when the biggest moves occur ? A compromise, OK H1/M15/M5 all agreeing. Oh and dont forget pivots S&amp;R and trading hours and news. So that is why trading is so tough, finding a combination of all above agreeing. But all of the above has been address (adinfinitum) on this thread as crucial aspects to be considered, when entering a trade. Will a setup you decide on always give a positive result - NO ! But that is a decision each and every one has to decide on. Sorry for the babbling post.

--- 帖子 #15533 ---
Yes, it is the one here I believe they work pretty much the same way, except the CSM sort of rates currencies from 0 to 9 (0 being weak 9 being strong), and allows for various analyzes on that basis, whereas the 1000pip indi just organizes currencies from strongest to weakest. Henry has a tutorial of ways you can use the CSM, because it is more sophisticated than the 1000pip indi for instance. For example, the strength measurement uses ATR in its calculation, which means that a blue (rated 0-2) currency has probably reached its range to the downside... if you pair it with a red one (rated 7-9) which has reached its top range too, you're in danger of entering at the top or bottom of the daily range of the pair... It's the same as entering short on a pair if ATR is reached. And so on... There is a video tutorial you can check out here .

My scalping is a lot of market "feel" should you say, with defined trigger points, but a lot of market reading on a tick chart. However, EU isn't quite the instrument it used to be I believe, and often allows me down time during my sessions so I started perusing FF. Noticed RJ's name attached to this thread and of course was interested to see what he had come up with. So I have kept up 4 markets in a separate MT4 and have been monitoring it through my sessions (NY/London overlap) as well as continuing my scalping on EU for about 2.5/3 weeks or so. I might just over manage my trades (i.e. even earlier exits)! Long story short, I'm comfortable doing what I'm doing now, and have an excellent mentor whom I can continue to work with when I need some help, but Genesis provides a slightly more mechanical (and therefore less stressful for me) approach, as well as a full support team here in this thread. So current plans are to continue doing both and see which method ultimately creates a great % return in 3-6 months time - its about making money and whatever makes me more is ultimately the logical thing to choose. Perhaps I continue both, although both feels a little too chaotic. Long post, I apologize....

Posting Charts As has been said, many of us have charts that use variations of Genesis, maybe with some extra MA's or whatever. We can't all post different charts because it makes a mess of the thread and it makes it harder of others to follow who are new to the system. So, below I have posted a basic Genesis chart. It doesn't matter whether you use the Arrows or the ASCTrend......whichever you prefer. This is the way I would like to see charts posted please.......colours are completely up to you of course!! There is no need to have lots and lots of templates, or even change templates to achieve this. I have one template (the one you see below) named 'posting template' and it is always open, but minimised at the bottom of the screen. When I want to post a chart I maximise my 'posting template' and go to the Market Watch menu of MT4, and simply drag and drop the currency pair I want to post onto the template. The dragged currency pair will take on the properties of the template and then I make my screenshot......post it to the thread and then minimise the 'posting template' again and carry on. It's that simple.....just one chart set up as per the rules....then drag and drop from Market Watch when you want to make a screenshot to post.

FOM - great trades. Closing trades early.....something that works for me - ask yourself when you are in a trade.... 1. The reason or reasons I'm still in this trade are still valid . ( Be it bounce of S/R, Pivot, BRN, whatever) 2. Is there another valid Genesis trade/signal starting to develop?? Is PA still favouring you.....(yes, sideways PA is no fun but the market does need to breathe.......is it ready to turnover or continue its original trend.......well you need to wait(the hardest thing to conquer) 4. If all above are good - and you have a SL in place or even better moved SL to BE - sit on your hands!! PM1

--- 帖子 #15941 ---
The 'early exit syndrome' (lol) is a difficult one to overcome.....and you have the answer already...imo. The entry! If the entry is a little bit suspect....ie that you aren't quite sure if you should have entered or not, then that can lead to an early exit because you might be thinking to get out because you possibly shouldn't have entered to start with. Another reason could be that you are over leveraged. Another reason could be lack of confidence following several losses. Another reason could be the thinking that '10 pips is better than nothing".......which could be true if the PA goes back......but could also lead to a further problem if the PA takes off for +60 right after you exit for +10!! There are many possible reasons, but I think (imo) they all boil to to the classic 'fear and greed' problem that affects us all at some stage. In your example, you needed to exit before to sleep....and that's fair enough...I would do the same thing....unless I was in a decent profit and then I might just lock in my target plus some profit and let it do it's thing while I sleep. But....I think it boils down to the entry. If the entry is text book perfect, then I won't close the trade unless it *clearly* is going to reverse, which does happen every once in a while. Other than that though, I generally don't sit there watching it. I can't do anything, I have an emergency SL in place that am comfortable with, so I just try to forget about it and look for something else to trade....read this thread or something, go make coffee or whatever. I can't influence the PA, so let it be..... Easier said than done I know!!

--- 帖子 #16007 ---
16,000 posts......wow.....with that much yappin we could probably get membership on the EU speaking circuit!! You raise some good points regarding 'live' trades etc and the answer is going to be a little more in depth to explain what I mean. But before I start, the short answer is, yes, I would like to see more live trades *where possible*, and it doesn't matter if they are winners or not. There is much to be learned by seeing live trading, but there is also much to be learned by seeing completed trades....good or bad outcome. Sometimes it's just not possible to post a live trade, especially in the M5 TF because it's not only the actual time it takes to make a screenshot, post it together with analysis, update the analysis etc etc....it is also placing more pressure on the trader and limits their ability to look for other potential trades. So I'm under no illusion that live trading is just a simple matter of posting a chart, it's more than that and I would never expect anyone to make a habit of doing it....I certainly don't, but I do it when I can. So that's the short answer Now, if you surf around FF you will see people who scoff at a system or method because a) there are no live trades posted, and b) because they see no attached Trade Explorer from the thread starter. Such comments are made mostly by muppets looking for the holy grail and actually putting in zero effort to explore and test the system. Muppetdom is not limited to newcomers......I have kicked out several 10v+ muppets because they have obviously skim-read Post #1, seen that there is no Trade Explorer (TE) attached and then condescended to pass judgement on the system......which is an act of extreme arrogance and disrespect! So....I think I have pretty much covered the 'live trade' issue above. So lets talk about the TE issue. Firstly, I can't attach a TE to this thread even if I wanted to because my broker's platform is not compatible with the TE application. Second....the TE application is a great tool for examining my own trades and performance because it covers so many variable at the click of the mouse. It is certainly an amazing tool to examine one's own performance. However, the senior muppets will say that 'if the system really is as good as it claims to be then why not have a TE?'. The inherent danger in that is that I can trade this system very well. There are a few who can trade it better than I, but the point is that I can trade this system which I present to you all......of course I can trade it....why else would I bring it?!?!?! Now......if I could attach a TE, it would show some very good results.....and I say that as a matter of fact, not as a show of arrogance. If a relative newcomer happens along and see's the TE, his first reaction is going to be. "wow...look at this....yippee, I'm going to subscribe and make shit loads of money!!" You can see that happening, right? Yet from experience we know that he will read the first post, and few others, and then download the indicators, ask a zillion questions that have been answered countless times before......lose money.....diss the system......and quit!!! Why did he quit? He saw the excellent results for the TE.....yet he lost money, said that the system was all crap and then left. Why? Simply because he didn't take the time to read through most of the thread, and he didn't spend time testing and learning from other people. So what did the TE do for this guy?.......it did nothing except assist in him burning his account. It didn't burn his account for him, he did that himself, but it certainly didn't help! The TE would prove that *I* can trade this system.....and that's all it would prove. Some guy just walked across the Grand Canyon on a tightrope.......that proves it can be done, but does that mean that we can all do the same??? Of course not.....yet that is what happens with a TE.......and I have no wish to be complicit in someone losing their account!! The best thing is, as we keep saying, read and understand Post #1 and it's various links, read the thread, and test the system. There are no short cuts!! Soooooooooo..................to come full circle, yes, live trades are welcome.....yes, past trades are welcome.......yes, winners and losers are welcome. We can learn from each of these thing RJ

Well....we have everyone looking closer at the stoch...yipee!! I have added the '80' line (as close as I can get it) with the yellow horizontal line. This line is the 'line in the sand' that says whether the PA is overbought or not. Now, given that we know that the stoch can stay overbought and the price can still climb hundreds more pips to the north, it is not wise to short in an uptrend while the stoch is still not yet clear of the '80' line. I must admit to doing exactly that myself on occasion, but I do try to stop myself from doing it. Until the stoch is clear of the 80 line, the uptrend may not yet be over, and so it might pay to hold on a little while to see what happens next.....Nothing is guaranteed, but it helps...fwiw

--- 帖子 #16055 ---
Here, I'll just post it with my explanation and you tell me if it's ok. I have modified a pivot indicator that can be adjusted for a different GMT setting. I started with some very good code from Elton Treloar, and then added some code from the Pivot Manual ActionForex and a few other things. My current broker is GMT +0 so I set the Start Hour to 21. If you choose to Show Comments, you will see the High, Low and Close being used to calculate the pivots. If these numbers are not close enough to Action Forex, or what ever source you use, you can edit them in the settings, although usually the only one I have seen that may need adjusting is the Close value. At the end of the forex day, or if you restart MT4, these values will reset internally to Zero which will then reset the high, low and close, even though you may see a different value in the settings if you changed it. Also there is an option to show yesterday's high and low values. There are also options to shift labels left or right of the current bar. If the shift right value is greater than zero it will always use that regardless of what is in the shift left value, so make sure that is set to zero if you want to shift the labels to the left. Hope it helps someone besides me. I have not tried it on brokers other than +0 and +3. I'm still working on trying to shift my ADR values back 3 hours.

On the M5 chart, the entry would have been much earlier than on the M15....about 16 - 18 pips higher in fact. But look at the same pullback we were just looking at on the M15. So we get shaken out of the trade for +8. There is a re-entry opportunity, which I might have taken, and that would have given me another +34......for a grand total of +42! So.....forget about the 1 pip difference, lets call it even. What about if I had entered on the M5 and exited on the M15?? Lets see...... The entry would have been about .980 and the exit would have been the same...at the pivot. Total pips using the M5 entry and the same exit.....but managing the trade on the M15.....total pips would have been about +57. So, by entering on the M5 and managing and exiting on the M15, we would have an extra 17 pips (more or less) and not got shaken out of the trade, or had any anxious moments. Plus we could have scaled in another trade and added another 30 pips to the deal. Scaling in at that level from such a nice entry was much more likley because the first trade would already be at BE......whereas on the M15 it would not have been. Interesting?

I'm not going to comment on your setups because that is not how I trade, or how the system is meant to be traded. I never just look at the M5 chart and make a judgement on it......which is what you're asking me to do here. The Genesis system won't trade for you.....you have to understand how PA behaves on the currency pair you trade....this thread has got so much information in it.....I can't do anything other than repeat that everything is here that you need...you have to find the answers for yourself.

I know my post sounds harsh, but that's the way it is really...there is no easy fix, no magic bullet, no holy grail, and I know that you know that. This testing I'm doing on the M15 TF.....it shows that there are many, many questions that I have no answers for, so I set about testing the theory to see if it's true or not. Other discoveries along the way are added bonuses.....like the possibility that entering on the M5 and managing the trade and exiting on the M15 might be a great thing. This is what testing is all about....and learning along the way. I honestly do believe that trading a single currency pair will teach you a lot. It's like learning language. You might need to speak 4 different languages, but you have to learn them one at a time.....only adding a new language when you have one already well and truly understood. If you try and learn all 4 at the same time, you'll never make it happen!! On any of the popular pairs, there will be a 30 - 60 pip move every day....or almost every day. That's all you need!!! There was a beautiful move on EJ today...Tokyo session that was worth 45 pips (in fact the move is still going). That's all you need. If you are switching between 4 or more currency pairs, you will never 'get a feel' for any of them. Spend 4 months on EJ alone.....not worry about what other analysts say because they are full of shit......forget about what other threads say.....forget about everything.0 Just set up an M5 and an M15 chart of EJ and give them 1/2 the screen each (if you only have a single screen). When you see the 2 TF's agree...take the trade. If they don't agree....grab some coffee and watch. If they don't agree but still move 40 pips....forget about it....smile....you lost nothing and it wasn't a high probability trade anyway. Learn all about how EJ moves...it has a personality.....learn it....profit for what you learn. If you can take 30 -50 pips a day *average*, and you compound the lot size......the risk stays the same, but the dollars add up.....quicker than you might imagine. If you can manage even 20 pips/day, that's a good start. Check out the spreadsheet. It wasn't the Hare that won the race...it was the Tortoise!!!

--- 帖子 #16109 ---
Yeah....someone else on this thread trades only a single pair and does very, very well at it. When you get to know a particular pair, you get to understand how it moves, and eventually you'll understand how it reacts to certain circumstances like news etc. You'll be watching it creeping along and you know that it's going to breakout.....it hasn't happened yet....Genesis is looking good blah, blah, blah.....and then it breaks out just as you expected. That sort of familiarity is invaluable and eventually it makes your trading life much easier. Trading, or rather, watching many pairs is a double edged sword. You get to see more opportunities, but how many of them do you stop at and analyse to see whether it really is a good opportunity?.......eventually you decide, 'nah...better not' (because you don't know that pair too well), only to come back to see your favourite pair, and bloody hell....you missed a perfect opportunity!!! It happens.....it happens to me too.....and that's yet another benefit of doing this M15 test. Because I'm trying to give the test the best chance of decent amount of trades, I'm limiting the pairs I watch to just 3.....and the pips are coming easier than ever.....although that could be the TF, hard to be certain. If you want (say) 50 pips/day as your target, then there's no point in watching 10 pairs. Any of the majors will give you an opportunity to grab 50 on average. Some days less, some days considerably more. So it's a 'swings and roundabouts' thing, but getting to know a single pair intimately can only be a good thing....imo!

--- 帖子 #16193 ---
Any positive trade is a good trade...that's for sure! Personally I don't like trading GU, but that's just me. When I trade, I always have a target, and in your trade it would have been S1. Now, right before you entered that trade, if it was me I would say to myself, 'So RJ, you have made no pips today (for example) and this trade looks good.' So I enter the trade and set my target at S1. When I contemplate an exit, I have to have a reason to exit, just as I had to have a reason to enter. Where you exited, I see no valid reason to exit at all. If I was concerned that the PA might reverse, and there is no sign of that in your trade, but if I was concerned I would go the BE +1 pip......but still target S1. If the PA does reverse and knock me out for +1, well that's still one more pip than I started with, so I still win. If I *do* see a valid reason to exit, I will do so, but in your trade, there was no reason to exit so I would have gone to BE +1 to remove all risk, and then stood my ground until S1 arrives, or a valid reason to exit early. I got knocked out of 2 trades last week, at BE +10 each time......if I had have exited early I could have had +25 on each of them but there was no reason to exit that I could see. The news knocked me out, but I still had more pips than when I entered, so it was still a win. My targets were about +45 each (more or less), so if the trades had worked they would have paid well......they didn't work, but they still paid..........win/win

--- 帖子 #16212 ---
Just an FYI post The China quarterly GDP release today was forecast at 7.7% on Forex Factory's calendar, but 7.5% on FXStreet's calendar. So I learnt my lesson to take a look at a couple of websites to compare the expected data, as this did have an impact for today's trading (if anyone was here for the Tokyo open). The actual number came in at 7.5%, which if you used the forecast of 7.5% you may have leaned towards poor data as expected out, potentially sequentially low met, and eg AUD may have some up leg. Which is probably what happened, except of course the data was leaked early and the AUD started to move 5 minutes early. If you had used Forex Factory's 7.7%, then you may have thought it was a reasonably significant miss (given how China manages its data release), with the potential for downside on AUD. Not that we're trying to introduce bias or trade purely on data release, or say one calendar is better than the other, but it's worth having a look at a couple of calendars just to be sure.

--- 帖子 #16231 ---
Firstly, thanks for sharing your trades - I agree it is good to share losing trades too. Unless I'm missing something, your entries appear to be quite late ... on your losing trade for example, your entry is on the last row (11th row) of white dots on the Genesis matrix ... with your winning one it's the 17th row of red dots ... generally the idea is to enter on the second set of red/white dots ... i.e., once the first row has lined up and "locked in", then you'd enter ... If you'd done this on your first trade, you probably would've made at least a small profit ... and if you'd entered on the second set on your down trade, you would've got a much higher reward. By entering so late, you run the risk that the momentum has finished. Have marked in green lines where I think the entries should've been. Just my 2c.

--- 帖子 #16313 ---
So the update on this is that I've only focused on the one pair for the last 9 or so days - EJ. Included in that was the weekend where I spent some time on the simulator and ran through about 20 or so days of trading. I have to say, for someone like me that was a huge benefit in terms of getting "instant" feedback. Sure you might not quite have the same level of information / tools as you would in live trading, but in terms of seeing how the pair's price action flowed, was a good way to learn. Most of you probably already know this, but in case there's anyone trying to chase 10 pairs at once, here's some insight on one pair. The big advantage is that, if you're watching a lot of pairs, you don't have a mental picture of what's happening on each pair. With only one pair you do - when you hear an alert, you pretty much already know what you're going to see. In other words, you pretty much already know whether it's likely to be worthwhile or not. Also, because you're only getting one alert at a time, you have time to have a proper look at the screen and make your decision. You're not making a 5 second decision so that you can go and quickly check the next pair that also just alerted. You have time to be thorough. In other words, better decision making. Better decision making = better trades. Better trades = better profits. Of course the disadvantage is if you're looking for near-perfect setups, and you have limited trading hours, and family distractions, you can very easily miss the 1 or 2 opportunities that come your way in a night. So I think for next week I will extend it to a second pair, probably EA although obviously I want to try and find something that moves at different times than EJ. We shall see. But yeah, just wanted to say that those that are overloading themselves with too many pairs, you really should consider giving this a try, even just for a week.

--- 帖子 #16317 ---
That's exactly what I mean If you have a look at EA now, you can see on the M5 that you may have exited the short on the pullback fearing a reversal. But again, the M15 is not even remotely interested. Same for the GJ long.....on the M5 there has been 2 occasions where we may have exited following the M5......but the M15 is not interested!! Of course there comes a time where the reversal IS going to happen, and we have to be aware of that, but it's unlikely that a reversal will begin 'mid stream'......it usually happens at a pivot or other s/r area.....or a sudden news event. But generally speaking, when a pullback on the M5 happens.....check the M15 as well because it might save you from getting shaken out of the trade. There's a little bit more to it than that, but not much more. The rule (in a nut shell), as far as I can see before analysing the last 4 weeks data is to 'enter on the M5, manage on the M15, exit at the chosen target.

--- 帖子 #16341 ---
Everyone was waiting for the big gap in UJ on Asian session Open. Didn't happen. I DO trade the Asian session. But as a general rule, everything of any significance that's going to happen, happens before lunchtime in Tokyo. I waited an hour after the Open to let the dust settle. In yesterday's Upper House election, Abe's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its partner, the New Komeito party, won at least 74 of the 121 seats up for grabs in the 242-seat upper house. With the coalition's uncontested 59 seats, that ensures it a comfortable majority, tightening Abe's grip on power and raising the chances of a long-term Japanese leader for the first time since Junichiro Koizumi's rare five-year term ended in 2006. I have seen and read English language news releases describing the election results as Abe's re-election. That is erroneous. This was an election for one of the two chambers of the legislative branch of Japan's government. While it's newsworthy that the LDP now has a voting majority in both chambers of The Diet, other factors like trade balance, investor's confidence, relations with China.....etc., also have to be included when it comes to UJ. While the election may give the Nikkei some confidence, foreign investors haven't exactly been snapping up Japanese securities. And in the end, it will be the foreign market that determines the direction of UJ in reaction to what the LDP does. The LDP has another agenda besides the value of the yen in relation to the $US. Watch for Japan to start discussing amendments to the post-war Constitution and to be more aggressive on the political and diplomatic fronts. How will this affect UJ? Who knows. As they say, for every Bull there's a Bear. All we can do is watch and react to what the market does. As speculators, that's our job. Many people are taking a bias on what direction the yen will go and how far. Try not to be influenced by one group or the other. Just trade your charts and you should be OK. One other thing to keep in mind, for the newer traders. From now until September you're going to see the action in the markets slow down considerably. This has nothing to do with currency values. It's simply the fact that in August, most of the free world is on vacation. In September, it's back to business. So if you don't trade in August, you're not missing a whole lot. Hope everyone has a great trading week.

--- 帖子 #16435 ---
I'm no economist, but here's my thought. China's growth over the last 20 years resembles Japan's from the 1960s to 1990s, except on a grander scale. Most noteworthy, is that it is a growth based on Fixed Asset Investments and Net Exports. Right now, FAI as % of China's GDP resembles what Japan's was when it's growth peaked (as has China's, the growth rate that is), hence continued FAI growth by say ~20% pa not only isn't possible, it will have less incremental impact. Kind of like Japan's highway to nowhere, China has expressways to limited populations and high speed rail investments over the last few years funded by debt that not only cannot pay pack principal, is having difficulties paying back just interest. And net export is having a smaller net impact on GDP growth due to the Rmb appreciation, and government spending isn't likely to increase suddenly given the last splurge, the $4trn stimulus that occurred in 2009-11 that is one of the root causes of China's current imbalances. So you're left with domestic consumption to drive growth, and while most of us have seen/heard of the Chinese's spending power overseas, it is by the portion that is better-off, and does not represent the whole country. As a whole, the biggest danger for China is that it hits the fate of Japan (ie little economic growth, ie either deflation in the case of Japan or stagflation), WITHOUT ITS MIDDLE CLASS BEING DEVELOPED . Whereas Japan had one of the highest per capital GDPs when it FAI and export driven model started to have limited/marginal impact to growth, China is still so far away from there that it seems it is unlikely to get there. And this is why China's government/PBOC are so intent on keeping money supply tight this round, regardless of any crisis in Europe and or Japan (later, if), because they know another round of stimulus will probably shorten the time it has to help develop its middle class prosperity before the inevitable is reached (the last round made the rich richer, and marginalized a good portion of the middle class poorer by inflating away their real spending power). Having said that, there are plenty of times left. While the official debt to GDP is understated due to the shadow economy, the Renminbi is managed, outflow is restricted and the yuan government debt is mostly local currency, so there's time for growth to gradually slow down before a crisis is more evident. Now is just the formation stage, and it could probably last 5- 10 years or more. But it will eventually come. Not our problem to worry about for a while yet, I would think.

--- 帖子 #16438 ---
The holding by China of US debt is down to 2 factors, the US trade deficit/China trade surplus, and China's pegging of Yuan to the dollar. So the excessive trade imbalances are a massive problem for both countries, but it is the pegging of the yuan, that is the main factor is driving dollar holdings by China, which forces china to hold more and more dollars to maintain the peg. But the bigger issues as I said are the imbalances within the Chinese economy that are the bigger problems, the points Rainyday made, are the key issues. The imbalances between domestic consumption as % of GDP and public investment. Public investment is over 50% and domestic consumption is down to around 32%. These extremes have never been recorded in the entire economic history, of the world ever, ever, ever. Vastly greater than Japan, or any other economy has ever recorded. So the greater the reliance on investment (particularly in a state controlled country) the greater chance mal-investments and it requires more Yuan for an incremental rise in investment, which causes non-performing loans, which if allowed to run, causes liquidity issues in the banking sector. This is why China has such a large shadow banking sector, it the only way to continue their state controlled investments. This has to blow up at some stage, as liquidity for investment disappears. Slowing world growth will reduce imports (we are seeing this already), which will put more pressure on state investment to drive growth. There is the problem.

Here's a reasonable example of what I'm doing in this current test. This isn't the best example, but it will do. As it happens the PA broke down while I was Photoshopping, but that's by-the-by. I'm trading the EJ pair and I entered on the M5 chart. You can see that it gives a better entry than a straight M15 entry. Having entered on M5, I now manage my trade on the M15 chart.....and here's why: See how the PA halted for some time on the M5 chart? The candles didn't know which way to go, and the Matrix was starting to have thoughts about changing too. Also, the M5 stoch was looking a bit bullish, although the M15 stoch wasn't. Hands up those who might have taken the profit and exited right there on the M5? If your hand is up.....that's fair enough....no one ever went broke from taking profits!! However, if we look at that same area on the M15 chart, there is nothing there that even remotely suggests that an exit is in order.....so I go and get coffee and don't worry about it. Then, as I said, I'm making the screenshots and S1 gets hit...SMACK....according to the plan So, I got the earliest entry I could get by using the M5, and I didn't get shaken out of the trade because I managed it on the M15. That's what I'm doing on this test.

--- 帖子 #16448 ---
As Jamz mentioned, there is a link on Post #1 about this : IFR. Trading. A Trading Exercise posted here by RJ I still do this IFR Trading exercise on the weekends because it is invaluable. Now I will let you and everyone into a secret. On my personal trading charts I have the candles set to be very very dark colours, and the reasoning is this. If you sit on a chair and get instructed to watch the floor and do not take your eyes off the floor , just like in school. For a while you'll be ok, but soon an ant will happen along and that ant will capture your attention, and you will watch it until it is no longer in sight. What you weren't doing is watching the floor as instructed!!! We are human, we cannot help ourselves from watching things that move.....even when we're told not to!! So, seeing as IFR trading works really well (apart from the exits), I decided to dim my candles so that they almost blend into the background of the chart, which stops me from staring at the candles and missing good entries or even entire trades!! I need the candles to manage the exit, but I don't really need then to enter. Entry is what Genesis excels at......and the candles watching that we can't help but do, is just a costly distraction, imo. It seems you have reached the same conclusion

--- 帖子 #16459 ---
The only time you would be in danger of a visit from mister margin call is if you don't pay attention to the basic safe trading rules of life.....and they apply to us all no matter what the system. If you're going to open multiple trades and they all turn sour, then you may be right. However, you'd be crazy to open multiple trades that would or could threaten your account. Personally, as I've said before, I never have more than 2 trades running at the same time unless they are protected by (at least) a BE SL. If I have 2 unprotected trades open and they both turn sour, the damage to the account is minimal....provided of course that the SL is not outrageous!! Once 1 of the 2 trades achieves BE, then I am free to open another trade, but still within my personal rules of 'no more that 2 unprotected trades open at the same time.' As per the spreadsheet, the risk percentage is the same from the start.....the $ numbers change, but the risk is the same, so there is no more chance of a visit from mister margin call from the first trade to the last trade.

Finally back home... I would have stayed in vacation longer but I can't do that... for now! I would like to share a piece of advice for the newcomers who come into the thread. When you begin, it is hard to catch what is the top priority over your long journey into this forex world. Is it the trading system? Is it the pivots? Do everything is in the money management? How much should I risk per trade? And so on... I personally think that having a trading journal and a plan is a MUST. Note everything you do! Bad or good! You can review your mistake later. With experience, you can go back into the past, and you will be GLAD to say to yourself that with your current knowledge, you would have AVOID this trade for X reasons. At the beginning, I was reading the thread and said to myself : "Well... Thats kind of easy. Blue / Red / White / Arrow up or Down. Stochastics blablabla... I can do that! Why should I pratice?!" Reality is another story. Knowledge don't appear like a bunny into a magician hat. You must pratice if you eventually want to beat the market. I did begin my trading journal around beginning of june. I did upload an exemple of my trading journal. As you will see, it is a mix of french and english language, so don't be surprise. --- 帖子 #16495 ---
Hi all, at the beginning of this year I developed a customizable trading journal which works in Excel and I would like sharing it with you. I spent time on this tool because one of my accounts doesn't work on MT4 and I can't interface it with Myfxbook or similar softwares; besides I needed a tool to simulate trades in backtest and analyze data. The usage should be pretty easy (sorry if I didn't spend time to develop the usability and readability of this tool). Once you have customized the lists in the "tracking &amp; analysis" folder (3) you have just to fill in the cells in the "trade journal" folder where the top label is yellow (1). By clicking the cell a list menu (2) you can select the field. The journal calculates on behalf of you some statistics which can help to monitor your good/bad trades and understand where to work to improve. For the time being I am working on other projects therefore I am available to answer your questions but please don't ask me to improve or modify it I hope this can help you to improve your performances. Enjoy it! wiz

--- 帖子 #16599 ---
Dear RJ I have a question concerning your experiment with M15 exits. Let's suppose that you took a long entry targeting R1. PA indeed reached R1 but M15 matrix looks quite good. I guess that you keep your position open. Is that so?

--- 帖子 #16600 ---
It's not so much 'exiting' with M15...it's more managing the trade with M15. The exits are the same as I have always done, target pivots, round numbers or historic s/r lines. But to answer your question, assuming that R1 was my target: I generally manually trail my trades as you may have seen, and if the Matrix looks good, stochs still look good etc etc, then I will bring my SL up to a suitable spot between the pivot and R1, and then target R2. If the pa successfully moves on from R1, then I will bring my SL up to just under R1 and then watch as the PA continues, and manually trail the PA as usual. On the other hand, if the PA/matrix/stochs are looking a bit exhausted at R1, I will take the money and run. If the PA later takes off to R2 without me, so be it! Does that help?

Hi all Been away for a while on holiday . Good to be back trading and back to this thread. Took this trade earlier today. It turned out to be a winner with a good risk reward, but I wanted to check that it was a valid High Probability Trade (pretty sure it was valid, but not sure about being a HPT), as most of the trades I see posted seem to be when price has just turned and the stochs are midway, rather than when price has been trending and the stochs are firmly stuck above 80 or below 20. I started the day at LO and took the trade after price had broken the previous days high (white dashed line). Price had been trending up on M5 and M15, so both stochs were above 80 and the Genesis Matrix was all white. I then entered on the first candle that opened both above the previous days high and above the 5MA. Maybe should have waited for a retest of the previous days high, which would have given me an entry 3 candles later, but a slightly higher price? TP was R1. I think the trade was a valid, but could it be considered a HPT or not? (I'm trying to only take HPT!) Thanks

--- 帖子 #16657 ---
Good analysis. HPT trade?......yes and no...lol! The perfect entry would have been when I have placed the blue line......but I'm not sure what time that was as I don't have the GU chart set up at present. Having said that.....the move that you participated in was all one big long and strong move which started at the blue line. Where you entered the Matrix was perfect, the stochs were solidly bullish and you had an arrow and momentum......so from that standpoint, it was a good trade. The risk was that the move could have ended at any time and you may have been left 'high and dry.' Of course the PA can always reverse 'at any time', but the odds increase as the move continues....we don't know where it will exhaust itself. When we get into the trade at the perfect point, or close to it, we (mostly) have the benefit of being 'in at the ground floor' and as such we can expect a reasonable chance of a decent ride. Your entry would be a perfect re-entry, or scaling in another long to compliment an existing and 'in profit' long, but I can't say that it was a HPT...imo

--- 帖子 #16847 ---
Yep....there's plenty of people around who would scoff at such a statement PM1, but those same people will almost certainly be the ones who are losing (mostly) due to the fact that their emotions get the better of them...lol...the hypocrisy!! I have a friend who says he get's nervous every time he enters the market and he wishes that this feeling would go away. My view is that this will never go away....call it nerves or apprehension or fear or anything else, but I don't think it will go away ever.....it might diminish as we get better and better, but it will never go away.....and to me, this is a good thing because: When I jumped out of an airplane for the first time, I was well trained, had faith in my equipment, but I was scared.....really scared. But I did it anyway! I don't remember too much of that first jump, they call it 'sensory overload.' Anyway, once I landed I assumed that I had conquered my fear and so I immediately went up again for jump number 2. As we approached the right altitude my fear came back, just as strong as before...I even remember thinking 'what a dick I must be....I just was in this same position and I was (pardon me but..) shitting myself, and here I am again.....why did I place myself in this same situation again? To cut a long story short.....years later and more than 1,000 jumps completed, I *still* get those butterflies as we approach altitude. I'm not scared like I was in the beginning, but I definitely have those butterflies. I think those butterflies are there for a reason......they make me check my equipment (again), I check other peoples equipment and I get them to check mine....I close my eyes and rehearse the jump in my head.....I check that the aircraft is in the right piece of sky.....I check that no other aircraft are close.....I check my equipment again and rehearse my emergency procedure.....then the jump proceeds. The point is that those nerves make me check and double everything that it's possible to check because when I exit the aircraft, in a little over a minute my life will end, unless I act to save it!! I think a very similar thing happens in trading. When we are preparing to enter a trade, we know what the consequences of the trade going bad can be, and we have an emergency procedure (SL) for that. We check our equipment (Matrix, stoch etc etc), we rehearse our trade (S/R, BRN,TP etc) and when everything is done, we enter the trade. Those nerves that keep me safe in the sky, also keep me safe when I trade. If I enter a trade in a slap-happy manner without a care in the world, I will probably lose....and as long as I have that attitude, I will lose! So for sure I think that emotions play a part in trading, but we need to use them to our advantage, not let them get the better of us. And yes, as you say, visualise (or rehearse) the trade, including the emergency exit. Any muppet can click the mouse to enter a trade, but if our head is not in the right place, we may regret that click!!! IMO...of course! RJ

--- 帖子 #17032 ---
There will be some charts in the PDF, but the purpose of the test is not to show specific entries and exits, but more to show where just watching and M5 chart would very likely have caused you and I to exit the trade, when looking at the M15 chart, there was no reason to exit. So the test is really about how to stay in the trade rather than entries and exits. We know how to enter, and exits depend to a degree on the style the trader chooses. I like pivots, s/r, round numbers etc, and they serve me well, but there is no 'hard and fast' rule for exits. On another note, it's very pleasing to see people here posting their trades as they happen. I will be the first to say that posting a trade the instant you enter is neither practical or sensible, but once some measure of profit is locked in, it's good to analyse the trade in 'real time' and discuss possible exit points etc etc. Far, far too many threads here at FF specialise in (supposed) closed trades, some even hours later, and this is worth very little imo. Of course it's good to review past trades, but it does stretch ones belief when all they EVER post are winning trades that closed ages ago.....even trades that took several hours to complete, and there was ample time to show it live. Those threads and those posters are not worth the paper they write on imo, so I am very pleased that people here post live trades as and when they can. Like I say, it is not always possible or practical to post live trades, but when we can (and do), everyone learns a lot. There is not much to be learned from constant winning trades that are posted after the fact, imo

--- 帖子 #17062 ---
I said I would have a look at the scenario of the ARROW signalling BEFORE the MATRIX is complete. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) I reviewed the EU,AU and EJ, but the sample results were very few, and as such it's hard to make a definitive statistical conclusion for the exercise. The conclusion I did come up with over the 3 pairs and 5 occurences was that the PA did not go very far (i.e. 10-15 pips MAX) before stalling on all 5. Quickly looking at the EA did produce mixed results - some stalled but others did have some good results......so, what do we get from that??? Not much really except..... the message that is very clear is that the arrow must occur within 3-4 bars (preferably 2 bars) after the matrix has completed and entry taken otherwise the PA generally stalls and/or stops you out. Just keep in mind that that arrow has to be there soon after entry or the movement you want is potentially weak. Remember you want HPTrades. So no arrow within that timeframe - reduce position size, just get out or hope (just remember hope is not an action that protects your capital...no capital = no play!). Whatever you decide it should be documented in your trade plan/rules.....do your homework on the pairs you trade. End of the day, get a feel for the pairs you trade, know their nuances and how they react around the open line, the daily PV, Resis/support lines, yesterday's H/L and always look left..... PM1

Personally I like to wait for the whole set...Matrix, at least the M5 arrow (ASCTrend actually, but the signals are the same), stochs, pivots etc etc....I just want to see everything line up or else I don't enter. Perhaps I'm not as aggressive as other traders, but we all have our own style

--- 帖子 #17082 ---
I'm sure you would have read in the High Probability Trading book about this Jamz. I remember Marcel speaking about traders he had met on the 'floor' and how there was one trader who took few trades, but his win/loss rate was astounding. So much so that people tried to be like him, but they failed because they couldn't stick to the rules! I recall him saying that most profitable traders had a method where they would advance in the '2 steps forward and one back' fashion, but this guy had a very steady advance curve. For sure, some trades slipped right by him, and others would scoff because this guy missed out on the trade......but......when he DID enter a trade, he nearly always won. This is the way I'm trying to do it too. The trades that I see but don't take because they didn't meet my criteria, can go without me.....even if they turned into 100 pip winners for some. I'm happy for them, and I'm happy for me, because I stood firm against any knee jerk entry. Now, the times that those situations turn into 100 pip winners is not many...and most of them I would be in on anyway if they met my criteria. More often than not, those trades may run for a while before they either reverse or stall.....either way, they give few pips, maybe a BE exit, maybe even a loss.....but one thing they will give ME.....is stress!! When I enter a trade I am pretty sure that it will go my way, because I have done my homework and the trade meets my criteria. If I'm wrong, that's fine...I'm wrong and I deal with the loss easily because it was an accepted part of the plan. But 7 or 8 out of 10 trades will go my way. I might only enter a few trades, but if they are 80% winners, then (to me) that is better than entering 25 trades and having a win/loss rate of 50:50 or less. So don't be grumpy....just keep working on your criteria to better cope with these situations. I *could* have entered EA, AU and NU and got all 3 correct. My bias was correct based on what I knew these Aussie and Kiwi idiots in suits would say.....but that's not part of my plan.....that's gambling. And......now you owe me coffee

--- 帖子 #17129 ---
There's a few issues here, some of them are a little confusing but most are not. Yes, your short attempt was certainly with the main trend, but the little bull run, or pullback, had been going on since London open, or shortly after LO. Given that this pullback seemed quite determined at the time, you need to be sure that it is indeed complete and the main (bear) trend is now going to resume. You chose the moment that you thought the bears were going to resume control, but how deep did you look into this before pulling the trigger? There are some differences between your chart and mine, and that is clearly an issue, but lets move on for the moment. Looking at your M5 chart, the entry looks pretty good......but......we need to be as sure as possible that that this pullback is over and we are entering the resumption of the bear run. How to do that? One way to see if this is possibly genuine or not is to just take a quick look at the m15 chart. Now we see a very different picture....the resumption of the bear run does not look at all likely, even the Matrix is not complete. If you were trading *only* on the M15, I'm sure you wouldn't have entertained going short where you did on the M5. So, a quick look at the M15 and you most likely would never have entered that trade. True? But going back to your M5 chart your S1 line and mine are out by about 7 pips, which is not huge, but it is of concern. perhaps you might like to check your pivot levels against the table in actionforex? Also, I see that you had an M5 'down' arrow.....which no doubt was of some influence to your decision to enter short. You can see on my chart that there is no arrow present. I use the ASCTrend indi, but the indication is exactly the same......and I have none. That is of concern to me too. So, to wrap it up, I think your thought process and analysis was fine, but if you had just checked the M15 chart for confirmation before you pulled the trigger, you may have decided to not enter. No doubt though, there is an issue with the charts because your pivots and mine are different, your arrows and my ASCTrend are different. We need to investigate what is the cause of these differences.

--- 帖子 #17167 ---
That's right.....another thing to look out for, and this is the same for many brokers and often gets overlooked, is that at market close each day (NY close that it) the spreads will widen considerably and if you have an open trade with a tight SL, you may get stopped out, even though the price never actually went that way, or that far. It's to do with the brokers resetting their servers and (I assume) the banks where the brokers get their feeds from have to reset their servers too. Anyway, it does happen and that is another reason why I don't like leaving trades running overnight unless they are in a healthy profit. I think that with Pepperstone, as well as the above, you cannot trade for 5 minutes during this 'server reset' period.

--- 帖子 #17183 ---
The attached indicator should shed some light on the matter. For those who might be interested in the difference between the AscTrend and the WPR, you can put a WPR indicator on top of it to compare. Risk=6 is equivalent to a WPR period of 13. WPR Period=Risk*2+1, High level=67+Risk, Low level=33-Risk. @To whom it may concern If one suspects that there are differences in the data from the brokers, it is quite an easy matter to compare the candle data from the various brokers.

--- 帖子 #17243 ---
Is your ASCTrend matrix set up the same as jalkok? (Can't tell from your image). i.e. Jalkok's shows m5, m15 , h1 , h4 If it is, then it's only the h4 that is different. h4 candles vary because it is all dependent on the server time. i.e. Jalkok's 4 hour candle appears to have started at 16:00 on his server time, which appears to be 17:00 on your server time ... i.e. when his candle finished and changed, you were already 1 hour into a new 4 hour candle ... hence, it didn't change on yours until that h4 candle finished As regards to the Genesis Matrix - I only see one box different on the CCI line around that time. Jalkok got a white - red - white where you got a red - red - white. Granted that could have let you enter 10 minutes earlier, but for the most part it is the same. Given you are obviously on different brokers, I'd say it's once again just due to a small difference in the pricing feed. Others may have other thoughts, but that's my 2c.
