--- 帖子 #17255 ---
Hi, again. I just wanted to post this if it might help someone studying this method (as I still am). Look for reasons NOT to take the trade! I spent many hours this weekend analyzing the prior week's signals, as I am doing every week now (funny, I'm starting to become profitable since I started doing that , probably because I'm building confidence in the signals.) It's great when I'm looking for setups and see a trade on the chart that I took; that means I'm doing it right. I'm looking at times I COULD be trading: Asia/NY or London, but I can't trade them all (and don't want to). I trade the first 4 hours of Tokyo plus the 2 hours before, except Sunday/Monday, and the first 4 hours of NY, minus the first hour because I'm not up yet. I also analyzed the first 4 hours of London plus Frankie. I found 85 Genesis signals in all, well, minus 7 or 8 for NY lunch that I was considering, but NOoooo. All these REQUIRE the M15 stoch to be above 80 or below 20 and this is the FIRST signal ONLY, until it is above 80 or below 20 again; I'm not ready to try re-entry signals yet. A few more can be removed because the M15 Stoch didn't break below 80 or above 20. Then there are those that BARELY broke the line(s); not a strong signal. I also decided to restrict the Max and Min SL I would accept, because I use a set TP. Other restrictions like HL or LH matching M15 Stoch OR M15 Stoch divergence. After eliminating all those, I ended up with 16 trades out of 59 signals in Asia/NY and 11 out of 26 in London. I also saw one post from RJ talking about waiting for pullback, and I have been testing that for a while now and trading it live. I decided the best for me was a 25% pullback from the signal toward SL. This reduces my Asia/NY trades to 9 and London to 7! AND the pullback has always tested equal or more profitable with less trades. And the best part is you don't have to rush to place the trade or worry about missing it. I only wait the next 4 bars and if it doesn't pullback, I cancel the order. A large majority of the time, if it pulls back after that, it will lose. So my REAL results from last week? I posted one trade earlier. Out of 9 possible trade I only took 4: 3 winners and 1 loser. I missed several because I was driving to work or home but the end result was the same... 5% for the week based on 1% risk per trade. Am I happy? YOU BET! I know people that make more but this kind of result will let me leave my job in 6 months, and I can live with that. (more would be quicker ) If I had taken all 85 signals? Besides losing sleep I would be down between -6 and -11% for the week. Look for reasons NOT to take the trade! Looking forward to studying your 515 test, RJ. Thanks! Now if EJ can only break below the BRN of 132 for my short trade from 132.155

--- 帖子 #17256 ---
* Will you take a setup when target at next pivot line is smaller in pips than the SL using previous swing high/low (in other word reward:risk is less than 1:1)? Generally speaking, no, I wouldn't. * after a range day with small daily range the pivot lines are close one another, will you still consider next pivot lines as target? Yes I would, simply because the rest of the pivot trades probably do as well! Having said that though, I might not exit so easily at each pivot line if the move appears to be a strong one. An example being that GU *might* not move much tonight because the is a UK bank holiday today, but the next day things *might* be back to normal. So it's possible that tomorrow, GU pivots might be all bunched up....and if that was the case, I will still aim for each pivot line as it comes, but I might hold the trade for longer if the trade is still within the usual ATR range.

When using the 5 15 method at what point do are you moving your SL to BE? Is it any different from when you managed the trade on M5? Thanks Trekker

--- 帖子 #17357 ---
Moving the SL to BE is just the same. The point of the M15 is to keep me in the trade by not get shaken out by a false counter move. Essentially the trade is entered on M5 as per normal, and once the trade is protected by the SL @ BE, then I watch the m5 and M15 charts side-by-side. If I see the price trying to pullback, I focus only on the M15 chart....I minimise the M5 chart sometimes to stop myself being influenced by it. When (and if) the move resumes, I go back to watching both charts

Hmmm.....you need to decide before you enter, what possible effect the news could have, and then decide whether you want to wait for the news, or enter before it, as you did. Seeing as you entered before the news, with a relatively cheap 20 pips SL, you really should have let that run. You must accept that the 20 pip SL being hit is a possibility, and it is acceptable to your pocket. If it's too expensive for your pocket, you have the choice of finding another trade or reducing your lot size/leverage. As you know, your SL was never under any threat, and I have to suggest that the dreaded "fear &amp; greed" syndrome has got it's hooks into you. Perhaps trading a very small account or else go back to demo for a while might help.....and don't forget the IFR trading, it WILL help.

Cold W - you need to trust the signal. That stoch setup on the M5 and M15 is about as good as it gets. There was some 4-5hrs after the sell off and then sideways trading before the signal, to me, this isn't a CT. So looking at your chart my thought process is as follows - 1. Not CT trade because of the big lag in time and PA 2. The M5 is trending up from &lt; 20 3. The M15 is also trending up from &lt; 20 and has formed what I call the "mouth". (See the stoch MA (signal line)and stoch spread apart (like a mouth) as the signal takes place. Look at the 1030 timeframe and the M15 doesn't form the mouth - not a good trade. A good trade will have the mouth start to form straight away. I know the M15 only updates every 3 bars but you will get in sync with PA and the potential of the M15 to make the mouth). 4. The stop is nicely placed with 20 pips and under support line 5. The signal HA candle has a nice push from the 5 SMA 6. The time is good - just after NY open My comments FWIW. PM1

--- 帖子 #17440 ---

--- 帖子 #17441 ---
Yes that's correct. There is no need to be tax registered as a 'company', but to be registered as a 'Sole Trader' instead. A 'Sole Trader' covers any owner-operated business that does not have employees.....much like a truck owner-driver, ar a owner-operator plumbing contractor etc etc. We have to be GST (same as the UK's VAT but cheaper) registered as well, and this comes in handy because as a 'Sole Trader' working from home I can claim a percentage of my homes power cost, heating costs, 100% of my 'plant and equipment' (in other words, my computer, printer etc etc), a percentage of coffee and food etc etc etc....depending on how good the accountant is!! My 'Sole Trader' company is taxed on any profits it shows, which is why it's good to not show profits on the books, and I am personally taxed on any money I withdraw (drawings) as my salary. The grey area is that NZ wants to tax the money that sits in the brokers account, but I contend that this money is not yet in the 'company' bank account, and so is not yet taxable. It only becomes taxable when it actually enters the bank account of the 'Sole Trading' company, from which the 'company' can disburse the money for costs like my salary, repairs and maintenance, other costs (like power etc ) etc etc. This is an ongoing battle with IRD, and I will probably lose that one in the end, but by the time that happens, hopefully I will have come up with another idea to keep IRD off my back!! I don't mind paying taxes because that's how the country moves ahead, I just want to pay my fair share and not a cent more!!

Looking at your chart there RJ...................for a good valid trade what about adding to the trade when you get those spikes up towards the last Swing High, where your stop is?? The R:R works out to something like at a minumum 4:1............something to think about for testing later?? PM1

Politically, there are bigger ramifications that may not have an immediate impact for markets, but could change the interplay between nations and we may get a sense of this as G20 leaders gather in St. Petersburg tomorrow and Friday. Near-term, expect markets to remain on edge and if there is a strike on Syria, for the dollar to gain, as well as oil and gold, with likely erosion of moves in the coming days.

--- 帖子 #17703 ---
Ok.....I have seen a few people forget the BRN's lately, so here is an indi for you. It can handle up to 6 different round numbers, but all we are interested in is the BRN. The default settings has 'FirstLineOn = true' and 'SecondLineOn = true' and the other 4 lines on set to false. Change 'SecondLineOn = true', to 'SecondLineOn = false' and then you will get a line (you choose whatever colour you want) for every BRN on your chart.

--- 帖子 #17801 ---
Glad you enjoyed the book I used to post longer term Japanese candlestick charts here to show patterns that might affect the trend, but I stopped doing it some time ago. The danger is that people indeed DO form a bias, and this can be costly. For instance, I have seen many H &amp; S patterns fail......I'm not sure of the exact number but it must be close to 50/50 for successful H &amp; S to unsuccessful H &amp; S patterns. When people see this pattern, to DO form a bias and they hold off taking what is an otherwise obvious trade (according to the system), because it seems counter to what *might* happen *if* the H &amp; S pattern comes true! The reality is that if that pattern does come trues, the system will see it and post the entry anyway, so it's not like we're going to miss the trade because we didn't see the H&amp; S pattern. If people want to incorporate pattern recognition into their own trading, then that's up to them. But it can't be on this thread because this thread is unique at FF in that we trade the system.....we are system traders. Any trade that meets the criteria will be an opportunity. Any pattern that is watched and bears fruit, will also give an entry on our system without us ever seeing the pattern, so we won't miss out on anything.....but the pattern recognition people might well miss out due to their bias. There are countless pattern recognition threads here at FF, and the main reason for creating this thread was to keep well away from that pattern recognition stuff because it is so subjective. If we allow it here, then soon there will be patterns all over peoples charts, trendlines, flags, hammers, morning stars, Elliot waves, harmonic patterns etc etc......and this thread will be just the same as all the others here!! So your question is fine.....but we need to keep true to the system and trade what the system shows us. If you wish to use patterns in your own trading, that's fine......just not on this thread please

much appreciated is your personal opinion that M5 despite providing more false signals, provides more signals and therefore more swings can be taken advantage of and potentially more pips? i can definitely see how that could be argued

--- 帖子 #17806 ---
Well, yes and no.....it depends very much on the type of PA we are experiencing at the time, and experience with the system. Right after that M15 test, I ran another 4 week test where entries were taken on the M5 chart, but the trades were managed on the M15 charts to help eliminate getting shaken out of a trade by small pullbacks. The pullbacks on the M5 looked as if an exit was a good idea, but upon checking the M15, there was no valid reason to exit....it was just the normal 'breathing' of any decent move. So the entire were on M5 and the trade was then managed on the M15....and to me, this is the best way to maximise profits, other than scaling in trades, which I have yet to cover. You can find the M5 entry/M15 manage study right after that link I gave you. The study goes for 4 weeks and a PDF is there after the end of the test. As far as false entries go on the M5, they are few and far between once the trader really gets the hang of the system and of reading the stochastics.......the stochs are the key to good entries.

--- 帖子 #17815 ---
Ok....I don't want to get into this too much right now because there is 4 weeks of testing ahead of me...but....the basics of my plan are: M1 chart with standard 5MA Yellow Standard Genesis Matrix Standard ASCTrend-4TF Standard 11,3,3 M1 Stoch &lt;----- this might change to M5 stoch...not sure yet MTF M15 stoch 11,3,3 MTF M30 stoch 11,3,3 Now you can't see the M30 stoch but it IS there......see the Yellow arrow....just drag the divider up and you will see the M30 stoch. I've done it like this because we don't need to see it all the time....just a quick check of it every 10 - 15 minutes will do. So....the trade between the 2 green lines is one I will take *because* quite apart from the standard Genesis rules of entry....we have all 3 stochs in agreement. The trade between the 2 red lines I am not interested in AT ALL!! The 3 stochs do not agree, so this trade is not going to happen. In essence...we are ensuring that we are trading with the trend. That's the basics of what I'm doing, but it's very early days as PM1 said, so this is not something I would encourage you to do, this is just to let you know where my 4 weeks of testing starts from.

So here I am, 8.30pm Saturday night, posting to our thread......lol....what does that tell you?!?! :nerd: Fridays M1 live test worked ok.....I ended in the green and suffered no losses. I have been backtesting and simulator testing for much of today and I just want to post a screenshot (chf/jpy) for you to explain something. As I said before, I'm not going to get into a deep discussion about this, that can wait for the PDF at the end of the test. However, the layout of my charts has changed a little bit as you can see. There is a very good reason for this which we will discuss later, and this layour may well work for the m5 as well and even the M15 charts. The things to notice is (remember, this is an M1 chart): 1. M5 stoch (11,3,3) 2. M15 stoch (11,3,3) 3. Standard Genesis Matrix The ASCTrend_4TF is gone. There is simply too much to keep an eye on in the fast moving M1 charts, and it really isn't needed. I have changed the actual layout because, from top to bottom, this is the sequence of confirmation for entry. In essence....I want to see (in a bear move): 1. Bear candle open under Yellow MA 2. M5 stoch crossed down ( in a perfect world, from the top of the window) 3. M15 stoch crossed down ( in a perfect world, from the top of the window) 4. Full bear Genesis Matrix. If all those conditions are met *in that order*, then enter.....or else, forgetaboutit!! I have a way to stay in trades as well, but that's all you need to know for now, because this might not work so I don't want to fill you up with stuff that might all turn to shit! lol. Oh, one more thing....I have taken away the 80 &amp; 20 lines from both stochs.......this is M1 trading and 'oversold/overbought' doesn't really exist, so the lines are gone. This may be the way forward in all TF's, but it's MUCH too early to go down that road yet, I just wanted to show you what the charts will look like for the next 4 weeks. I'll post as many trade examples as I can, and I'll post as many live trades as I can too.....but cut me some slack please....M1 trading can get fast and furious!!

--- 帖子 #17859 ---
Yes, you're quite right Marty....I'm not advocating anyone follow what I'm doing at this stage....I'm just investigating whether it can be done safely or not. For instance, I know that you won't trade against the H1 stoch. If a similar safety 'valve' can be incorporated into the M1 chart to gain a good entry with the trend, then it could be advantageous. As I mentioned in that link I posted above, I'm sure that many newer traders lost a lot of money over the past couple of weeks trying to trade the PA that actually offered no trade at all......you and I and other more experienced traders just sit out the doldrums and wait for the volatility to return. But what if, as we saw last week, the PA is going up and down 20-30 pips all day? If offers no entry on the M5 charts, but it offers good entries on the M1 charts. With SL placed above the swings as per normal, the risk is minimal.....10 pips at most and the SL is just as safe as in the M5 chart, because it is place in the same spot. So....if the overall trend is (say) down, but the swings are too small to trade on the M5, but are trade-able on the M1, then the trader can simply 'sell the rallies'.......same as he/she would do on any other TF. The SL is less, the risk is small, the profits are small, but potentially good........and the trader who feels he/she must trade (and we have all been there), can at least do it with safety. It might not work out that way Marty....but it's worth investigating, imo.

Bear in mind that I didn't trade on Tuesday, but I still took all 5 days into consideration regardless, because this is real life! If you compare this week with an average week on the 515 test, you can see that the Nett profit and average pips/day is similar. Yes, the total is helped by the FOMC generated +168, but that is offset by 0 pips on Tuesday. The trades taken have been similar to a 'common' M5 trade, just that I am getting into the trade much sooner, hence the smaller SL.....but....the SL is located in almost the same place as it would be on an M5 trade, so the risk is actually less (smaller SL) that would be the case on the M5. In some cases, the trade would never be entered if I was just using the M5 TF. I haven't worked out the average R:R but just looking at the trades, I would guess it is better than 1:2. I'm not going to get too deep into the exact method I'm using, but it is very close to what I outlined before...very close. All will be revealed at the end of the test. It's fair to say that most people regard M1 as 'noise' and impossible to trade safely. Well, so far I have not found that to be the case. Those people probably do not have a robust system which we have, but whatever the case....*so far* I see this as a possible way to trade in market conditions where it is impossible to trade on M5 and above. --- 帖子 #18156 ---
I don't think you have to get pissed off or be frustated because you missed a huge move; in realty you didn't because you were in and you made the right decision to exit @ your target. Noboy can know if a move will become a home-run or not and eventually reverse. We know that the exit (and position size) is where the good traders make the difference but this is also the dark side of the game. So what is the best exit strategy for a day trader (a trader who closes all his/her trades at the end of the day) ? The Genesis users know that we can use many different exit strategies based on pivots, RN, M15 arrow etc. but there is also the human beings' inner side which doesn't like miss home runs ... therefore what to do? take profit at target or try to let them run? I tried to answer this question building a model which simulates double or triple exits and compare the "ALL in ONE" exit (when we close all our units at target) with other strategies based on close unit1 at target (like ALL in ONE strategy) and let the unit2 runs ... the outcome is very interesting I suggest who wants to improve his/her exit skills to play with the attached model but in few words we can say that if you are a day trader and you take your profit @ your target (whatever R-multiple is) you have many more chances to maximize your profit than let it run ... even if sometime when you close the trade it takes off to the moon. Just as example in a streak of 20 winning trades if you want to beat the "two units 2R exit" you need to take more than 4 home runs &gt; 10 R or in other words 20% of your trades must be &gt; than 10R; if your avg. risk is 20 pips it means to have 20% of 200 pips days ! I hope this can help you to forget quickly the EA trade and have a great week end BTW impressive results RJ ... Congratulations !!

I have a completely unscientific method I'm afraid. To some extent it depends on the pair I'm trading and the session I'm trading, as well as the type of PA we are experiencing at that time. Sometimes, for example, I won't go to BE until +20 or maybe +25....especially when trading GJ in the early London session. Much less than that and the SL will get hit leaving me with a small profit and no chance of re-entry. But the same time on (say) NU or UJ and I might feel good moving to BE at +15. Once I have got to BE, I trail the SL according to the movement in the PA. If it's having 'mini swings' of 10 pips, then I won't trail closer than 15-20 pips. If it's just creeping along slowly, I might trail it every 10 pips. So it depends on many things and in the end it's just having a 'feel' for it. Very unscientific, and sometimes my SL in profit will just get tripped, before the PA takes off....it happened last week in fact, but such is life...can't get it right all the time!! I guess none of the above is much help....it's just a matter of experience I guess

--- 帖子 #18255 ---
Sl's are one of those tools that I think are under-used by many in trading. Obviously their most important job is like you say, an insurance policy, or emergency brake for those time when we are wrong and the market moves too fast to effect a reasonable exit without too much damage to the account. I always manually trail my SL's and my trade, once in profit, will either reach my target or get stopped in profit. Again, it depends on the nature of the PA.....sometimes having go to (say) S1, I will bring the SL within about 20 pips and aim for S2, and trail the SL in the same way as I described before. If I get to S2 and the move still looks good, I will do the same again and shoot for S3, and so on. Sometimes I can go all the way, but most often I get stopped in profit when I trade like that. One could always bitch that I left 20 pips on the table (with hindsight), but that's the compromise with trailing stops. Either take the profit at the target and bitch when the PA continues without you.....or trail the SL and bitch that you get stopped in profit and left 20 on the table...lol. For me, leaving 20 on the table is not the end of the world because it doesn't happen too often. Either the target is reached and I exit, or I manually exit when the PA stalls....like I did today, before the trailed SL is hit. As we were saying before....many ways to skin a cat!!

Just very briefly....GU, when it turns (which might be soon, check out the Daily and Weekly charts), is likely to fall 1,000 pips back to the major support. If you were to short that and hold your trade, you might make 1,000 pips. But think of this, when your trade gets to +100, move your SL to +50, and then enter another short. When the first trade gets to +200, move the SL to +100, and move the 2nd trade SL to +50 and enter a third short.....etc etc etc. As the move 'breathes', you may get a trade knocked out at +50 (so what?), and you can re-enter that trade when the bear run resumes......same rules as before. Doing it like this there is very limited losses possible, but potential to turn that 1,000 pip drop into something much more eyewateringly profitable!! The same can be done on intraday trades but it's a bit more tricky to do.....same principal applies though

--- 帖子 #18277 ---
I am amazed how people want to make money trading, without understanding some basic "game theory" principles. Many people use martingale or similar schemes in their trading or in rulette etc. What they do not understand is that in order to make money you need a positive EV strategy (EV=expected value). Casinos are happy to see as many people as possible playing rulette with a "system" or not. Because the game is designed to have a positive EV for the house thus negative for the customer . No reason to analyze it here more. All casino games are designed to have a positive EV for the house (apart from blackjack but thats another story). The more you play the better for them. What each trader is trying to do consiously or unconsiously is to set up a positive EV system. (Not the guy in RJ's comment though). He who manages this, can live from trading. Not only that but HE CAN CALCULATE WITH GREAT ACCURACY how much he can take out of the market. Lets see an example: Suppose we have a system which can produce say 70% winning trades (note: we all here know that genesis can do better than that, but I will stick to 70% for this example). Each losing trade will be between -10 to -20 (the average stop loss of the system per trade) depending on the particular setup. Say -15 on average. Each winning trade should be between +15 (if TP is less than 15 why enter...) to +??? ( many times could be 50 plus pips) say +20 on average. So lets calculate the EV of such a system: Per 100 trades we win 70X20=1400 and we lose 30X(-15)=-450. We win 1050 pips overall or 10.5 pips per trade. The EV of our system is thus 10.5 The trader with such a system KNOWS that on average, every time he pulls the trigger FOLLOWING HIS SYSTEM RULES makes 10plus pips. Every single time...

--- 帖子 #18278 ---
That's an interesting way to put it, but you're right...that's how it works.

--- 帖子 #18291 ---
Depends on the: - importance of the news - was it normal release news, or unexpected news - how close or far away from expectations the news was - other intraday trends, ie is H4 &amp; H1 trends alligned or opposite. - how far the immediate candles after the news stretched from MAs - etc, etc News trading is probably the most difficult, therefore there cannot be any prescribed time. caveat emptor !!

--- 帖子 #18306 ---
Great post thomasK. This is what most traders don't get, if your system has a positive expectancy, you become the "house". Now all you have to do is to keep following your trading plan. Genesis is the BEST trading system I've ever used, because of its high win rate - which allows you to be more agressive with money management without incurring in large drawdowns because you'll have fewer consecutive losers - and the RR ratio is surprisingly good for a high win rate system. Frequently we see systems with high win rate but the average winner is smaller than average loser. Trading is a statistics game in the end.

--- 帖子 #18339 ---
Relating more specifically to blackjack and investing, is the interesting concept of Kelly's Formula (or Kelly's Criterion), which is basically the optimal bet size giving your win-odds, that maximizes your risk-adjusted returns over a period of time. Bet higher, and the volatility of your returns actually lower your overall returns, and bet lower you're not maximizing it. Can google it if you're interested. There's an interesting book called Fortune's Formula ( http://www.amazon.com/Fortunes-Formu...ne%27s+formula ) that discusses this. Lots of other books and resources available on the web also.

--- 帖子 #18340 ---

--- 帖子 #18519 ---
I think so too. I'll get more into this later, but during the test I observed that when the PA is leaving a known s/r line (Pivot, BRN etc), on the M1 it was easy to catch the move very, very early and with a SL of (say) 10 - 15 pips, it was easy to get the SL to BE very early, with no more risk than on the M5 chart. The difference being that on the M5 chart, we may have to wait 5 or 10 minutes (2 candles) to be comfortable that the PA was going to do what we expect it to do, and by then, the SL (which would be in the exact same spot as for the M1 entry), might now be 25 pips or more (depending on the PA), and this may make the trade too expensive to enter. But during that initial 5 to 10 minute period (2 candles on the M5), we would have watched 5 to 10 candles on the M1 instead of 1 or 2 on the M5, and so we often see a much clearer picture, much earlier. I hope that makes sense, it will be much easier to show on a chart on the PDF. On that note, I might have to make 2 PDF's......one to review the M1 test in the same way as I did for the other tests, and the other to show in more detail how the M1 could be traded. The method I used for M1 trading is very, very similar to what I have always done, but I found a better way to view the charts that makes things cleaner and easier to view....and the way I have found for M1, may also be better for M5......but I'm not going to test that, everyone can choose for themselves!! The changes to the charts are very small as we will see in due course, which shows that the system is really very strong, and the changes may just be a personal thing Now....coffee time

--- 帖子 #18563 ---
After looking funny photos of sheeps all over the thread I decided to google ' Trade like a Sheep''.. then the result was Investopedia explains 'Sheep' Like a sheep, this type of investor is a follower, relying on a shepherd for guidance. These shepherds can come in the form of financial pundits or the latest trend or market story. Sheep-like investors are often the last to get in on a major market move, such as the tech boom of the late '90s, because they base their investments on what is being talked about the most. Many experts believe that sheep-like investors are the most likely to sustain investment losses because they have no clear investment strategy. This thread fails this theory because here sheeps rule the world

For all those that trade Auzzie crosses, here is a little news, that you may find interesting: We wrote yesterday about the Aussie and looking at the reasons why it has seemed to defy gravity in the past couple of weeks (see “Explaining the Aussie”) and this has continued overnight on the back of the latest RBA minutes, which scaled back on mentioning a weaker currency as a means to boosting the economy. This had been a theme for some time from the RBA, so combining this with the more neutral stance to policy taken at the September meeting, the Aussie received further support pushing it to a 4 month high against the US dollar. We wrote yesterday about how the Aussie is no longer a carry currency, stacks up well on sovereign risk analysis and has been supported by momentum and changes in positioning (as long-term shorts have bailed out). All this means recent gains could well be sustained.

--- 帖子 #18746 ---
Ok...regarding the +10 pips poll.... Yes = 13 No = 1 I haven't included those who PM'd me.....you guys and girls can have you say when you are members of the thread...with all due respect Now, the reason I asked the question is this...there are many people who may think 'others are making 40 - 70 and I can't do that'. Well neither could I, or Marty or anyone else without doing the 'hard yards' first. It's the same when you learn to walk...you learn to crawl, then you take a few steps, and gradually build up to running. No one can show you how to run the 100 in under 10 seconds.....that takes time and practice and practice and practice. Same for riding a bike, swimming or anything else. Trading is the same.....once you understand the system, you have taken your first (very wobbly) step......and that's all. You haven't 'cracked' FX trading at all (if that's possible).....all you have done is take the first step. You ARE GOING TO FALL OVER...and skin your hands and knees.....that I can promise you. When we started to walk, we had bruises and grazes on our hands and knees all the time! Same with trading.....our accounts may go 2 steps forward and one back......one step forward and two back.....three steps forward and two back etc etc. That's the learning process in action!! That's also the painful reality, and that's why we trade with a small percentage of our account balance....because we want to try again tomorrow, and the next day, and the next day. If we blow all our money on a few trades, we have lost our 'stake', and now we can't trade.....or continue the learning process. So....as we have been saying, preservation of capital is of paramount importance. But all's not lost, there is a way to become modestly profitable and all it takes is 10 pips per day and....the holy grail of trading....*patience*. A while back I was given a spreadsheet to work from, but it didn't quite suit my project. PM1 has kindly modified this for me earlier on this year, and I was going to start on the project in August. However....the best laid plans and all that....due to many factors (changing brokers, Mums eyes etc) I have been unable to start it until now...and now I'm not going to start it until January so that I can make this next test for the calendar year. So in January I will start the project and give updates on progress from time to time. However, I want to share with you some 'do-able' facts and figures....firstly revolving around our +10 pips/day. * The project will start on January 12 2014. * The daily target is 10 pips. * These figures allow for weekends, but not public holidays. * These figures do not allow for withdrawals * These figures do not allow for negative days (or less than 10 pips) * These figures do not allow for bonus days (more than 10 pips) The 'lot size' is determined by the account balance. So eg Account balance = $500 then lot size = 0.05 Account balance = $600 then lot size = 0.06 Account balance = $700 then lot size = 0.07 Account balance = $1000 then lot size = 0.10 Account balance = $1200 then lot size = 0.12 Account balance = $1800 then lot size = 0.18 Account balance = $3500 then lot size = 0.35 Account balance = $6000 then lot size = 0.60 etc etc etc ======================================== Example 1 12-Jan-2014 Opening Balance = $500 Daily Target = 10 pips 17-Jan-2014 Closing Balance = $530 28-Feb-2014 Closing Balance = $696 30-April-2014 Closing Balance = $1,043 30-June-2014 Closing Balance = $1,573 29-Aug-2014 Closing Balance = $2,410 31-Oct-2014 Closing Balance = $3,745 31-Dec-2014 Closing Balance = $5,716 In this example (10 pips/day), we turned $500 into $5,716. Show me another way of making that kind of a return on $500 in 12 months!! ============================================ ============================================ Example 2 12-Jan-2014 Opening Balance = $1,000 Daily Target = 10 pips 17-Jan-2014 Closing Balance = $1,060 28-Feb-2014 Closing Balance = $1,410 30-April-2014 Closing Balance = $2,136 30-June-2014 Closing Balance = $3,249 29-Aug-2014 Closing Balance = $5,007 31-Oct-2014 Closing Balance = $7,811 31-Dec-2014 Closing Balance = $11,961 ============================================ So there you have it.....this is based on just 10 pips / day.......and most people can do 10 pips / day! Yes, the figures don't allow for losses or withdrawal......but they also don't allow for days when you exceed 10 pips......and that can happen easily as you have seen Cold_W do recently We don't need to feel sad if all we made is 10 pips......and we don't need to feel like losers because some people got 130 pips and we only got 30. Some non-farm payrolls trading strategy from RBS Here’s the gameplan from the currency strategists at RBS. The consensus for NFP is 180K after a 169K reading for August A rise of 200K or more with upward revisions to July and August would be needed to resurrect talk of a December taper Fade any US strength on a number between 170K and 180K especially vs EUR, AUD and NZD A reading of 130-160K would solidify views of no taper until 2014, would boost EUR/USD and NZD/USD AUD/USD longs would benefit most from a reading of 100-125K 90K or lower would cause a round of risk aversion with USD outperforming except vs JPY Love it when someone lays out a clear strategy.

--- 帖子 #18803 ---
I'll try to answer. Probably not the best answer, but let's keep the game going. To me it is price being above or below a moving average line. Eg the 60 day SMA that Marty has suggested before. If we put it on a 30min and/or 60 min chart and look back a few days, usually it is pretty clear where the trend is. When it's hovering close to the 60d SMA on either 30min or 60 min chart, then I'd like to combine this with a look at the corresponding stoch position (M30 Stoch on M30 chart and M60 Stoch on M60 chart). If the trend is up, ie prices above the 60d SMA, then I'd like to see the stoch making its retracement to OS position (ie below 20) while prices remain above or near the 60d SMA. Then when the stoch exit OS and moves towards OB, prices will move in the direction of trend and away from the moving average. Of course, at some point price will cross the moving average with enough momentum that prices will then be below the 60d SMA and to an extent such that (perhaps not first retracement, but soon enough) when the stoch retraces back up OB position price no longer crosses above the 60d SMA and a down trend is confirmed once the stoch exits OB and price moves down below the moving average.

--- 帖子 #18809 ---
So getting back to my point. When M30 trend and M30 stochs heading in same direction, you get a stronger move, than when M30 stoch cross against M30 trend, ie a CT move. So if you time your M1/M5 entry when M30 trend and M30 stochs allign, you get a higher probability move. As RD said, I define an M30 trend, eg uptrend when price is above M30-SMA60 and M30-EMA30 is above M30-SMA60. Or if you just want to use M30-SMA60, but the 2 together is stronger. RE CT moves, the further price is away from SMA60, the greater the probability of a tradeable move; the closer price gets to the SMA60, the smaller the move

Yeah....Andre-Jacques Garnerin is like a god in skydiving circles! In fact Leonardo Da Vinci invented the first parachute much earlier...in the late 1400's I think, and it was constructed out of wood and canvas. Some people, British I think, made the parachute (quite recently) as per Leonardo's drawings and jumped it. Not out of an airplane, but suspended beneath a balloon. At a suitable altitude the parachute was released from the balloon, complete with a man suspended under it (brave man) and the wooden parachute descended at a rate that was in control and would have given a survivable landing. The 'test jumper' didn't attempt the landing because the heavy wooden parachute would have landed on his head!!!.....so he cut away from the wooden parachute and deployed a modern parachute and landed safely. But the point was proved, Da Vinci's parachute worked!! Clever guy that Leonardo!!

Say for example you enter a trade following all the rules correctly and the stop loss is above/below the most recent high/low. Now the unfortunate happens and the PA turns around before you were able to move to B.E., but PA doesnt retrace so far back that the stop is hit. So we are in limbo. As we have been taught the stop loss is just there as more of an emergency back up, rather than sitting there waiting for it to be hit. So we have to decide what to do, either: exit for a small loss now OR ride it out and assume the pullback is noise and the trend will continue in the direction of your trade. I only enter trades with the HTF stochastic being on my side (moving in the direction I am trading and the D&amp;K values spreading nicely apart i.e PM1's "mouth") so I dont get too worried when the M5/M15 stochs pullback and move against me. However I DO look to exit when the HTF (usually 60min or 240min if swing trading) stochs cross and turn against the trade. Ok so lets forget about situations which cause spikes or immediate reversals (e.g. news releases) they are a bit different. This is relevant to regular everyday market movements. What does everyone think of this HTF stochastic exit logic? What other indications (not indicators) does everyone/anyone look for? Im sure there is a confluence. Everyone in this thread is extremely helpful, but two answers I am not looking for are: 1) "You can see it when the PA changes behavior" or 2) "Its a gut feeling" Reasons for this are, everything is driven by PA and PA gets expressed through all the other filters (indicators) we have on our screen. So it obvious that its all about PA. If you can identify something specific, you have my complete attention. Secondly gut instincts are actually your subconscious identifying patterns that your conscious mind hasn't registered yet. What I want to dig into is, what are these patterns so my conscious mind can see them? (Of note I have spent plenty of time in front of the screen and have got a reasonably good 'feeling' for PA. I want to change my feeling into an understanding.) I appreciate how dynamic the market is, so I am not expecting a hard and fast answer. I just want to start discussing it so we can identify key items that we can use. Thanks.

So many questions to answer............. What does everyone think of this HTF stochastic exit logic? You are trading M5 so what happens if the H1/H4 turn against you?? Well if the H1 turns against you the M5 should have well and truly turned against you. Does the HTF's look like they are about to turn? Don't trade. Trade the M5 in the direction of the HTF's by all means but manage on the M15 or the M5. "You can see it when the PA changes behaviour" You should have a good reason to enter the trade initially..............what is the deal breaker?? Stoch? Matrix? BRN? DP? S1/R1??? What is this pairs personality? Just remember if you exit and the trade then turns around and goes the "correct" direction.............you are allowed to hop back on again!! "Its a gut feeling" You want a definitive answer...............screen time will give you that. Find what the indicators do under certain PA conditions then you will know how to react. What the PA does around BRN/DP/ Open/ yHigh / yLow....is the previous move fast or slow? Does it have momentum? What is the previous PA? Are the candles wicky? etc etc. All these observations are taken in by the subconscious and they form the BIG PICTURE that you cannot consciously account. --- 帖子 #18885 ---
What does everyone think of this HTF stochastic exit logic? When trading the M5 TF, I wouldn't have entered (generally speaking) against the M30, H1 stoch but I can't confess to ever watching the H4 stoch because it's not relevant to M5 short term trading. So assuming that the M5, M15, M30 and (mostly) the H1 stochs are in my favour, then the first indication of a change of direction against you will become apparent in the M5, M15, M30 H1 stochs in that order!! As PM1 says, if the H1 stoch has turned against you, your trade is already dead....probably an hour or two ago! You would have seen my GU trade from last night.....I took the manual exit at +9, but if my SL wasn't already at BE but still at the swing high, the SL was not under threat and the trade went on to make more than 35 pips. However, that was a CT trade so the rules don't really apply.....the exit was to secure +9 rather than +0. When the trade is WITH the trend and the SL is placed above/below the swing high/low, and the trade is not yet at BE, the forgetting about about news spikes etc, I will close the trade early if the (apparent) reversal is strong......like say 3 large candles striding their way to the SL! In that case I will try to take a manual exit before the SL is hit, but if that is not possible then I'm ok to take the loss of the SL being hit....because....that was always part of my plan. I can afford that SL to be hit if that's what the PA is going to do. I'm ok with that. If the SL is going to be too expensive for my taste, then I wouldn't have entered the trade in the first place! So to recap.....If the trade is not at BE and the pa seems intent on reversing, as determined by powerful candles, I will try to exit with a small profit or a small loss. If that's not possible and my SL is hit, that's ok with me because I factored that in when I entered the trade.

A few points here.... M1 trading for sure won't be everyone's cup of tea...different strokes for different folks!! The reason I began the M1 testing was to see whether Genesis could trade the M1 when we are in a tight range for days on end, and the answer is 'yes it can, but with a couple of subtle changes'. Of course we have the option to just sit out those days and wait for the market to return to 'normal', but going down to M1 is also an option. The setup you describe will certainly be stressful and perhaps even unreliable on M1 although I couldn't say for sure because I don't trade in that way. I'd have to embark on another 4 week test, and I think I'm all 'tested out' for this year!! Speaking of testing, it's good that you had a crack at M1, but (with respect), 1 day doesn't show anything really. That's the reason that I go for 4 weeks for each test, to try and see if the system can handle all market conditions (well, most market conditions), and to see if any 'tweaks' are required. One thing I see mentioned often is that M1 trading is too intense, stressful...and requires 'massive screentime', takes many losses as well as wins...blah, blah, blah.....and I can say, hand on heart, that this is may all be true if you don't have the right system, goals, attitude etc etc......and I am not point a finger at you Marty, or me or anyone else.....I see those comments often and I think it was/is a trader here at FF named Turvey (or similar), who has traded M1 for a long time and has had to endure all that kind of talk!! An example....'M1 trading requires too much screentime'. I submit that this is not true....because....If I trade (say) the opening of Tokyo, London and NY I will get more setups that I know what to do with on the M1...for certain. Now, referring back to the spreadsheep (slip of the tongue...I mean 'spreadsheet'... ) example I made a few days ago here , I gave 2 samples of pips/day goal....each had an example of a starting balance of $500 and $1,000. Let me do one more example, and I'll split the difference and instead of making it 10 pips/day or 30 pips/day......I'll go 20 pips/day Example 1 12-Jan-2014 Opening Balance = $500 Daily Target = 20 pips Risk = 2% 17-Jan-2014 Closing Balance = $560 28-Feb-2014 Closing Balance = $974 30-April-2014 Closing Balance = $2,210 30-June-2014 Closing Balance = $5,108 29-Aug-2014 Closing Balance = $12,138 31-Oct-2014 Closing Balance = $29,512 31-Dec-2014 Closing Balance = $69,092 ============================================ Example 2 12-Jan-2014 Opening Balance = $1,000 Daily Target = 20 pips Risk = 2% 17-Jan-2014 Closing Balance = $1,122 28-Feb-2014 Closing Balance = $1,994 30-April-2014 Closing Balance = $4,606 30-June-2014 Closing Balance = $10,718 29-Aug-2014 Closing Balance = $25,548 31-Oct-2014 Closing Balance = $62,208 31-Dec-2014 Closing Balance = $145,702 ============================================ Now, both examples require only 20 pips/day. On the M1 chart, on the 4 pairs that I monitor, I am sure that I can get those 20 pips in the first 3 hours (if not sooner) of any of the above market openings. So.....that blows the 'too much screentime' myth out of the water! Also, there is no stress or intensity involved, and the reason there isn't, is the same reason that the 20 pips will come fairly easily and quickly...the system is tweaked to suit M1 specifically, and it works well. The 'many losses as well as wins' argument also holds no water, for the exact same reason. The ultimate goal (for me) is to make that 20 or 30 within the first few hours of Tokyo session, then I'm done trading for the day because I have a nice income from just that small amount of pips. That's where I want to be.....and will be, by this time next year. There will be, I am certain of this, people who are going to be saying 'yeah, yeah, yeah RJ...that's all fine and dandy, but it's theory only.....show me the money.' Those people are correct.....I have not been trading in the above fashion and I don't have a 6 figure bank account so far this year. Why not? Because a) I haven't followed this method of lot size compounding, and b) because I have to live and pay my expenses! So to come full circle.....M1 trading won't be for everyone, and Genesis on the M5 is excellent....and the same method of lot size compounding will work there too. I don't want to spend time making in depth analysis, waiting for setups to start forming, check multiple timeframes and then wait patiently for the setup to complete and give me an entry. I've been there....and it doesn't 'float my boat' any longer......I would like to spend a few hours with little stress to make a good income and then I can have the time to do what I want to do......and to me, time is the most important commodity!

Hi to all A thought re M1 trading and debunking the myths that surround it......even though Im an M5 trader. We can trade the system on any TF, as has been proved and documented. The difference is in personal preference and trading style. I often open up my Marcel Link book to a random page and read a bit, for relaxation/revision, and he makes a relevant observation that if you looked at an M1 chart and a Daily chart, and the TF wasn't on the chart, you wouldn't be able to tell them apart. The only obvious difference is that, of course, M1 moves at a much faster pace, but it makes the same moves. One of the things I really like about the system we trade and the lower TFs is that the draw down is very small. 10, 15, 25 pip stop losses for 10, 15, 25, 50, 70+ pip gains. This means we can make much better progress and be more in control of our trades, and what is happening to our money. The thought of taking trades where you set a 150 - 300 pip stop loss on H4/D1 TF seems absurd compared to how we at Genesis Matrix trade. Surely there is as much noise on M1 as D1 or Monthly, which is really no noise at all.............the noise is in the candles, hence the reason we use HA candles (or in my case no candles). Just a Sunday evening ponder before the trading week begins. J.

Probably better starting higher and then gradually working lower (if necessary), that way you gain in exercising disciline (waiting for a trade)

--- 帖子 #18962 ---
Getting the most out of your trades. After my GU short today, which got me to my weekly target, I thought to myself, what should I do now?.....what would a professional in control of his game do? In the past, I would usually have kept trading. Nothing wrong w that. The last thing I wanted to do was give anything back to the market. I really wanted to milk that trade. So I took myself out for lunch, and spent the rest of the day feeling nothing but positive and confident thoughts about trading. If you have read the Dr Maltz book 'Psycho Cybernetics', you will know that feeding yourself this kind of information is very powerful. The trade itself was a good re-entry to the bigger previous bear move, but I was also in the right place at the right time. In saying that, fishing for a good time starts w throwing in your line! My point is, I think it might be very useful to really let trades sink in properly, bad trades too. Im thinking maybe there is a lot of value in taking a break after a trade, to re calibrate, process, digest...................and then resume trading, w patience and discipline. As I moved around in the afternoon I replayed the trade over and over again in my mind, not by looking back at the charts, etching into my mind all the correct things I did prior to the trade, which was nothing more than doing the basics well. Im sure this wont suit everyone here, but for me it feels like a good discipline strategy. J

All brokers, as far as I know, reset their servers at the end of NY session/beginning of Sydney session. Pepperstone is no different in this regard, and the spreads will widen.....and at that time you won't be able to trade for 30 minutes ( I think ). That's not an issue for me because I don't wish to enter/exit trades at that time, and I never...well....very rarely, leave trades open overnight. This is not 'broker stop hunting' (which is rubbish anyway), this is usual practice at the end of the trading day and the broker has to pass on the wide spreads it receives from it's suppliers. I think it's good that Pepperstone doesn't let us trade at that time because if we did, and we weren't aware of the wide spreads, we would cry!!

Hi RJ Im w you on this one.................in my own way of course. When I started in 4x everything I read prescribed that you needed 100k capital, trade/risk 1% and you would need 500 pips per week to make 5k profit per week. Thats a lot of pips, and a long road for working people who have limited time to trade, little capital and little experience. I have adjusted my MM model to: (after I restore my account balance to even) risk 3% Average S/L 15 pips Average profit 20 pips Win rate 60% Weekly target (only if the opportunities fall in line) net 30 pips after commissions etc. (thats 6 pips per day profit) Now, w 10k capital and 200 trading days for the year you have a compounding profit of over 108k. That over 1000% ROI. The key, is stick to the stop loss. (manage your losses properly and the gains will come) If everyone here only took good Genesis Matrix signals and stuck to the S/L, I know the results would actually be much better than my model. The sticky part for some I think will be when you get into dealing w larger sums of money per trade. There are simple ways around this, like when you get up to say 4 lot trades you trade 4 lots per trade for a month even if your going great guns. Im lucky to have had 3 start up businesses of my own (1 good, 2 bad) and dealt w money up to the $1M mark, so when its money time Im ok because Ive had experience making and losing money. Remember none of the money you make doing this was yours to begin with, so the odd loss here and there doesnt matter. This week I have made 2 trades for a net gain of 50 pips. More importantly, I have maintained discipline and patience and not taken any bad trades. I let 3 other trades go because there was something about them that didn't smell quite right..................they all went on to be good trades of course. The point is, 2 straight forward trades and Im way ahead of target. I dont need masses of pips, and I dont need to squeeze every last pip out of each trade. The 2 wins this week I only took the meat out of the trade. I didnt bother w the 3 veg, and kept pressure off the entry and the exit. When Im up river, fly fishing, I only bring back what I need .......a couple for the family, 1 for the solicitor and 1 for the dentist............thats all I need , the rest I put back. J

I am far from forming a bias on the basis of such analysis, though. Instead, once I've spotted a potential setup, Genesis steps in to confirm the entry. Some might disagree, but for me this is what constitutes smart, stress free and effective high probability trading with optimal risk management. A holistic yet simple approach to trading, where the big picture meets precision, and in which Genesis plays an important role. What I really love about this approach, is that because I monitor the H4+ charts for setups, I have plenty of time to analyse 15+ pairs, which makes up for the inherent lower frequency of trades on the HTFs. I certainly do not want to go against the thread rules, so I will only post this once to illustrate how I look at the HTFs. I will delete the post should you wish, RJ. The example below is my last short trade on CHFJPY. The screenshot should be self-explanatory, but I will just add that (if well managed) the trade could give 165 pip profit for 35 pip SL, i.e. 4.7:1 RR. --- 帖子 #19059 ---
Point taken!! Actually I don't disagree with much of what you said because clearly you are a) learning to trade the larger TF's, and b) have recognised that 'reversal patterns' can be unreliable.....but tend to be more reliable as the TF gets larger. Personally I don't like 'reversal patterns' any more than I like H &amp; S type patterns because I have seen them fail more often than succeed, and they always look good in hindsight, which is what most analysts ever show! But....having said that, there's nothing wrong with taking note of these patterns and other area's of s/r to keep in the back of your mind for future reference. I do this too. What really winds me up though, and I saw this earlier on in the week.....some person (on another thread) stating that when the currency pair 'gets to x level, he was going to short it.'.....'x' level being 160 pips further north! So he/she is going to sit and watch the PA travel 160 pips north, and then short it, just because that is the plan that he/she has convinced himself of. To me.....one word fit's that trader...MUPPET!!! Why not trade the 160 pips north if the trader is so certain that it's going to get there? And why pre-determine that if/when it gets there that it will reverse?......because it did in the past?......because it is a historic s/r area? So it's simply impossible for the PA to carry on even further north?? Those are the sorts of things that lead a trader into losses...... I have no objection to your charts Jo, at all. They are long term 'possibilities' and I have posted plenty of those sorts of charts here in the past. It's when people close their minds (as the trader above) to anything other than their bias that I get upset, because it's foolish and WILL lose a trader money!!

Dear RJ great stuff and I am sure many people will find it usefull. There is a problem though which you may want to correct in order not having younger members being confused. I dont know how it happened but on a closed M5 arrow -as you already mentioned- you must have squares (red or whire) which are multiple of 5. So 6 or 8 white squares can not be followed by red ones on the M5 arrow matrix. We can have say 8 white squares at the end of the matrix, meaning that a block of 5 is closed and a second block is being formed (having already 3 of them), but not as in your presentation. Thanks again for a great job from you and Wiz

--- 帖子 #19118 ---
If I can chime in here....... Many traders on the other threads I browse from time to time believe a stoch in an OB/OS position is a signal to enter/exit, and that a turn in PA is iminent. This isnt what stochs were designed for, but they can be of great help when preparing to enter/exit, as we know. Ive had alot of trades and seen many more where a stoch getting into OB/OS is when the momentum releases and PA really takes off. If you look at any chart and spot M5 stoch flat lining high or low you will see that behind it is a strong, open mouthed M15 or M30 or H1 stoch move, and often all of the HTF stochs together. I read an interesting thread the other day where the trader didnt enter the trade until the stoch was OB/OS! It was quite a good looking system, not a patch on ours of course. [Probably stating the obvious here] Cheers J. EDIT: case in point below. Missed this trade as I was 'yappin'.

Not sure I understand your question, but here goes: Lets say my SL was at (say) 99.00 and my short trade was at (say) 98.70 and the PA, due to unexpected news instantly went up to 100.00, then by the time SL was tripped and processed, the price would already have shot way past my SL. So instead of my SL closing the trade at it's designated level of 99.00....it might not have been able to close the trade until much later...maybe 99.50 or worse. It takes time for the SL to get tripped and close the trade, and in a super fast moving market, it might not be possible for the server to process the SL at the designated level...hence....slippage. Is that what you mean?

--- 帖子 #19282 ---
Interesting post JJ. I believe it helps opening up, as looking inwards, may only compound the problem. One of my biggest break-throughs happened while chatting to my brother-in-law. But I was lucky as his job, is coaching Phd students in simulation project/scenerios. So while he didnt understand the subject, he knew the right question to ask. Re getting shaken out of trades, this is where, I believe looking at HTFs helps. Someone posted here awhile ago, H4 had no relevance to M5/M1 trading; but I disagree. It may not effect your entry signal, but it SHOULD affect your exit. For me if H1 and H4 trends/stochs are alligned, I am more likely to scale into a trade at a pivot point, where as if H1 &amp; H4 are in opposite trends, I will more likely close at a pivot point. Big Difference. On big breakouts I see many LTF traders, close out, at the time I am either entering or scaling in. AND that is where the money is. IMHO

A couple of points.....one is to not risk any money at all! Start a demo account with (say) $1,000 and trade that account wisely. When you have doubled that account, open a real account, but only for (say) $200. When you can turn that account into $400, then you might want to consider trading slightly larger lots as per the spreadsheet that you will find on the thread. Another point is to focus on the job in hand...unless you get to know the system (any system) intimately, you will never succeed.

--- 帖子 #19449 ---
Hey all. Slow day for my trading the longer TF's as most of today's action seems to be against the longer trends. Thought I might take the opportunity to share what I'm working on for longer term trades. RJ thought some might be interested. You all have been doing fantastic with the 1 and 5 min, buy I find that difficult to fit into my schedule. Anyways here's the first chart using the E/J as an example. Attached Image (click to enlarge) So I first look at the daily. I've cobbled up Xaphod's genesis dashboard to show all time frames from 15M to weekly. Once I have the daily and weekly in sync on the matrix then I wait for the lower time frames to sync up. To do this I monitor the 15m charts for signals in line with the D1/WK. I'm looking for all TF's to be in agreement. When that happens I have a very good shot at a good trade. If other factors line up...S&amp;R, pivots, etc. I enter the trade. This allows me to get on board the long term trend with a shorter TF entry trigger and smaller s/l. Might sound confusing but it's really not. Next time I have a live one I'll post that up.

Hi Goldminer, It looks like it is me to help you out as I recognize something similar here.... At lease you know you're wrong. If I may talk generally, yes, we need the money NOW hurry up!!! but actually, money is not like that with trading. Money is the tool, the lever that we can use in forex and money may be the result but other than that, it has nothing to do with trading. That is something else and why on this thread we talk about pips. Mr Market doesn't care or know your circumstances. It is frustrating learning but that is all you can do. Play with very small sums or on Demo and gain the ability to recognize a consistent entry and trade management. There will still be spikes that take you out and price reversals and ooops, forgot the news so you have to get used to that. Please excuse my speech and just be grateful your not here in my office where I could go on and on and on for a couple of hours....... Yes, happy trading Goldminer!

Yes, the wide open mouths are lovely on the stochastic prior to entry but I see it as a trade off. The wider the mouth the higher the probability of strong move but it also means the move has started which in turn opened the stochs mouth to begin with and with that the SL is becoming more and more expensive and further to that the higher probability of a retrace toward the SL. Like everything in life its a trade off. Anybody with any thoughts on how to tackle this one? Regards Anthm

What you are saying Anthm is quite true. The wider the mouth the greater the SL but I have also found if that M15 mouth gets wide quite quickly the trade is not that good to ride. How to tackle this - don't trade and wait for something else to come along. Go back in the charts and look at M15 with mega mouths and see how they turned out............look at mouths that are just right and see how the turn out..........while you are at it look at the steepness of the M5 stoch...........if mega steep and against the trend - stay away!! The only time this doesn't work is at news event times. PM1

--- 帖子 #19510 ---
Regarding this I'm firmly a disciple of Marty (now, and much later to the party than I should have been). Look as far up the higher TFs as you can. I now look up as far as H4. The wide mouths on the higher TFs are the juicy trades, eg if you get wide mouth and agreement on the H1/H4 Stochs, you can almost inevitably wait and get a good re-entry using M5/M15 Stoch and Genesis/ASCTrend that'll give you a good risk reward and not an exceedingly large stop loss as you'll be able to use the period of consolidation before it as your last high/low. Be cautious when the H1/H4 Stochs don't line up, it will be unlikely you can get a very sustained trade. It's ok if one is strong and the other is neutral, but you don't want a case where one of the H1/H4 Stochs has a wide mouth against the trade direction you're taking. Or at least you'll need to be very swift and monitor it very carefully. Some trades, as you mentioned, you'll get a good signal and M5/M15/M30 Stochs to line up before you get a good confirmation that their stoch mouths will open wide. That's part of what makes trading difficult. In these cases, at least I want to make sure the H1/H4 Stochs don't have wide mouths against this trend. If it was as easy as getting a few TF Stochs to line up, then we'd all be robbing the banks. Luckily we have Genesis so that hope is still alive

Hey, I'm back after some time off forex. I had to fix some bad mistakes I was doing back about end of july, beginning of august. I had pretty decent success, but I should had listen to the old saying "Don't try to fix something which is already working". I did try to play with the TF, Arrow and stoch to find better entry and better exit. I also had a bad habit to overtrade when the price hitted my SL, which is a shame actually. No worry about my balance though ; I did quit because I was disappointed with myself and not because I burn myself. So the good point now, is that I can start back where I left, with a brand new mindset!!! Here's my AU trade yesterday. I did go in because of Stoch pointing down, Matrix and Arrows on my side (the W1 was red at that time). My RR was 1:1 at first. One of my past problem was that I was getting out of good trade prematurely. For my return, I did prepare myself to let the winner run. So once my trade did hit DP, I did ask myself "Do I have a reason to get out of that trade?" The answer was no, which mean : Move SL to BE +1. Next target, S1. When the price did hit S1, I did ask myself the same question. From my point of view, I didn't see any threat, so I did move my SL to DP, which was about +18. Once again, I did the same thing when the price did reach S2, same question again, same answer. I did close my trade when the matrix all turned white and stoch was pointing up. That was my signal. The result was a wonderful +86 pips! Attached Image (click to enlarge) Thanks Genesis! I'm back home

--- 帖子 #19642 ---
The Matrix-Signals will only give you alerts on one timeframe and you can only use one instance in MT4 (ie. you can only run it on one chart.) Which timeframe is entirely up to you and depends on the timeframe you are trading off. The alerts it gives are the same as you can set in the Genesis Matrix indicator so it is not giving you any special signals you do not already have access to. It is useful if one wants to monitor many charts or if one needs a call to get back to the cahrts after being distracted. If you want alerts for when multiple timeframes line up, the GMTS-Dash can give you that.

I disagree. That's definitely NOT right (it's either a deviation from a trading plan or lack of management specs) which is not such a big deal to fix BUT in order to fix something you have to know what that something is, so here are my suggestions: 1) Dissect the trade once again (feelings, thoughts, actions) 2) What was good (according to the plan), keep on with that 3) What was bad (late entry - why?; impatient - what's the cause? - normally you should NEVER be impatient or feel nervous while trading, otherwise your judgement is clouDED which is almost DEAD), think about how to get rid of that crap 4) Act according to your resolutions Seems to me you don't have a detailed plan for this kind of situation - think about it and write it down so that the next time you see a signal a little late you either stay out having YOUR reasons for that or get in and know exactly what to do without any impatient/nervous/dunno-when-to-exit-and-why-not-now/whatever kind of sh*t

--- 帖子 #19821 ---
Interesting observation One thing I always take note of is the top line of the Genesis Matrix....the TVI. Quite often it is the first to change colour. Sometimes it changes back and the move continues, but because it's usually the first to change colour, it can be a heads up that the move may be running out of steam. It's not a trade exit signal per se...but it is something to keep an eye on and maybe to bring the SL into profit......

--- 帖子 #19920 ---
Hmmm...the incorrect pivot issue surfaces yet again!! For the record and those who may not have seen the previous discussions about this issue: I asked for a table of pivots to be included here at ff just like the actionforex table more than a year ago. I guess it wasn't as important as 'subscriptions' and 'impact users' for this place though......what a shame..... The actionforex.com pivot table is here .... don't forget to select the 'Daily' tab. If your pivots are within 5 pips....that's probably as far as you should be from 'true'.....if you pivots are off by more than that, then the server offset is wrong and you will need another Pivot indi where you can change the offset. There's some info about this on Post 1

--- 帖子 #19957 ---
If I may show something that may help with this - and I will quickly remove this if I am moving too far "off piste"...... Trading off the 1m chart enables us to take advantage of the many short intra-day swings in our chosen pair or cross and IMO it is important to bank frequently, as this great system gives us plenty of opportunities to enter in each trading session, especially if we can monitor 2 or 3 contracts. I look for an increase in (tick) volume (aka activity), in a wider ranged bar around "a level" and - providing I have at least 15 pips profit - I will either bank half or all. My pre market prep has aleady shown me the nearest S&amp;R levels which I keep on my 15m chart for easy reference. To help show this I use one of Sonic's volume indicators that has an alert and the ATR indicator that I set to show the length of each bar - when I post I minimise these......

--- 帖子 #20049 ---
So I wanted to put this up in case anybody finds it useful~ Basically it's a mod of Jinchu's 'do-able-auto' spreadsheet from page 1. I based the model off of the risk formula from the 5-15 manual, and added input fields for risk percentage, average stoploss, and pip value. This lets you try out more conservative estimates....but damn if I wasn't sad that I won't be a multi-millionaire by next Christmas as the original promised It's set up in a split screen with the model on the left and a blank worksheet on the right. So what you would do, is input your starting balance on the model and set risk, SL, and daily pip target to your liking. It then populates a years work of accurately hitting your pip target every day. Then, you can keep track of your actual progress on the blank log. Each line is 1 week worth of Genesis trading, where you enter your lot size (using the model on the left as a guide) and pip counts, so when you finish up Friday you can see how everything played out. There's also a column for withdrawals if you regularly take funds out. I tried to make it auto populate as much as possible, so only the colored fields need manual input. Anyway, if anybody wants to look it over, please let me know if there are any bugs or big issues. Hope it helps!

--- 帖子 #20052 ---
Hey Marty, I completely get what you're saying and agree that "what if" spreadsheets can give you a 'pie in the sky' disposition to trading that is negative. But for my purposes at least, in this particular document, the focus isn't to give an unrealistic goal as much as it's to help me combat my biggest enemy in currency trading, which is over-trading. People struggle with different hurdles when they trade and my personal downfall in the past has been giving earned pips back to the bank because I over-traded or didn't take profit when it was offered to me. I use this spreadsheet for two main purposes, 1. quickly calculating my lots based on my account (with realistic, conservative estimates that are achievable) and 2. keeping myself on track with an attainable profit target so when it's achieved, I don't get greedy and ultimately give it all back. But again, I do fully agree with your post. In actuality it's probably the #1 reason why I modified the original document in the first place

--- 帖子 #20060 ---
Myself, I use a script ("Easy Order") that calculates my lot size based on my SL. It means I'm always risking the same % per trade, no matter whether the SL is cheap or expensive. Even though the risk is always the same, cheap or expensive SLs are still a factor though, as the more expensive the SL, potentially the harder it is to get a good risk / reward. The script has the option to set a TP as well at time of entry, but I modified it so it doesn't for me, as I often observe how the trade starts off and then determine the best TP (or just let it run with a jumping stop EA taking care of things).

--- 帖子 #20061 ---
Morning all I would like to raise a discussion on how to manage a trade and look for best exit if in the unlikely event that price reverses form original entry direction before SL can be placed at BE. As we know a premature exit here may be costly as the reversal may just be noise and we may have not given price enough opportunity to develop for the move in our direction. Then again waiting too long may be costly in the event that we let price recede too far towards SL and incur a bigger loss. This topic has been raised in the past but for me personally it requires more examination. I trade M1 and when I am in this situation the things that I find that allow me to exit with hopefully a cheap loss are. ♦ M5 matrix has had a full color change, (this is often way to late as price has receded along way towards SL) ♦ M15 Stochastic crosses, once again it is often way too late. ♦ M5 Stochastic cross if price has been rejected from recent Highs or lows (this one often too early and may mean that the move is missed. Any thoughts, comments or ideas on this would be appreciated Kind Regards Anthm

--- 帖子 #20062 ---
Hi anthm When Genesis is traded correctly, false entry signals are few and far between. Exits are always the hard part. RJ looks for 3 strong candles against the trade, and you might have picked up in recent posts that TVI changing colour first is a heads up as well. Personally, Ive interfered w so many trades in the past that have gone on to be very good winners and not even challenge my SL that I just dont do it anymore. I accept that Im going to loose the odd trade, within my risk tolerance...............so be it. Every trade has pull backs at some stage, some early, some late, but the system and the stochs will tell you the most likely outcome. Most Importantly, if you are doubting your trades, and doubting your signals [assuming you are entering on good signals], then you are probably always going to make the wrong decision about an early exit. And, if youre losing a lot of trades early, there can only be 2 reasons: 1. entering on poor signals and/or against rules [eg. news, S/R, DP, BRN, Friday 13th etc etc] 2. interfering w trades and/or getting shaken out just because price is moving against you for a few pips. When you are trading M1, you have to trust the system more than any other TF, I reckon. Trust the system, Trade the system, and take profits when youre happy. I hope this helps. Cheers J. EDIT: I also accept that on M1, against the trend, profit potential might be modest.

--- 帖子 #20064 ---
I don't think it's destructive Marty, I think it's encouraging. The earlier examples I gave of 10 pips/day, 20 pips/day and 30 pips/day I see as encouraging because they are realistic goals with our system. I think that people (to a degree) get hung up on trying to score the 'home runs'......trades in the 60's, 70's and more, when the reality is that a goal of just 20 pips/day, at the end of the year is going to make a very nice sized account. 20 pips/day is easily achievable and people can go to sleep at night with their 20 pips feeling great and content......rather than going to bed with 'just' 20 pips when they see others taking in 75 pips or more! It's kind of like the carrot and donkey thing....it's an incentive...and it's encouraging. I don't see it as destructive. Destructive (imo) would be to say that 'you're wasting your time if the best you can is 20 pips/day' I guess it's a matter of perspective......

Morning All Would anybody be able to tell me If when scrolling back on a chart to check something in the past lets say two weeks ago, is it possible that one of the 4 squares that make up the Genesis Matrix may have changed color from what it was on that particular day. I suspect it would be a memory issue with the MT4. Has anybody experienced this? Kind Regards

--- 帖子 #20168 ---
Yup! Here's how to solve this problem [that's what I did]: 1) Go to 'Indicator list' 2) Click 'Genesis Matrix' 3) Click 'Edit' 4) Click 'Inputs' 5) Find 'T3 Bar count' - paste 50000 [my input] or something near that 6) Enjoy!

--- 帖子 #20169 ---
Yup...that's correct. I think the default bar count for the T3 part of the Matrix is 1500 bars.....so if you are going back several days on a low TF chart (say M5 or M1) then the T3 row will go completely all one colour. As you say....change the bar count if you want to go back further and you'll be fine.

--- 帖子 #20250 ---
You exited with +15.....and that is profit, which is good. No one can deny that. If you can do 20 - 30 every day for a year, you're going to have a BIG account!! Having said that, why DID you exit??? Because the stoch 'started to cross?'.....not a valid reason. If this move drops another 200 pips.....and it could.....the stochs will all cross several times, as the PA 'breathes'. The Stochs are not like ping pong balls.....they don't HAVE to go up just because the reach the bottom....they could stay on the bottom for another 200 pips...easily. The stochs staying riveted to the floor is showing that the bears have a lot of power. What I do in these situations, and I have done it live here many times, is to put the SL into profit....say +1. Then....you simply can not lose! the risk is removed...gone...forever. Worst case is your SL gets hit for +1....and so what if it does.....that's 1 more than you started with, right? When the move has gone (say) 20 pips.....SL to +5. When the move gets to +30 bring SL to +10 or +15 (you choose)...etc etc. When the PA hit's the next S/R which in this case is the BRN, take your exit and profit.....or.....bring your SL into more profit and see if the move goes down more. When you exit like you did, it is the bad old 'fear and greed' getting the better of you. Afraid that if you don't TP now, you might only get +1 instead of +15.....and greed that +15 is better than +1. But the reality is that even +1 is better than what you had (0) before you started the trade. So, manually trail the SL until the PA either hits the next s/r, or it stops you out in profit......either way....profit is yours!!
