--- 帖子 #20326 ---
Hi Acroix, My feedback is more just something to look out for ... it doesn't always apply, but sometimes does ... if you look at a trend as higher high or lower low, then your entry point is following a lower low, and there is not yet a higher high. You are entering just below the most recent lower high (well, more of a pause really) , but before price has gone above that lower high. So by that definition of trend, you're against trend. What happens? Price reaches the point of the previous lower high, and then promptly turns around. I've added green lines that may help make it a little clearer. I must stress, many a time, your entry like that could work ... this is just something else to factor in - i.e. the previous lower high becomes a resistance point.

--- 帖子 #20341 ---
Patterns and system cycles Maybe someone will find this interesting. It's end of week; I will entertain you with some observations about systems and cycles. You may need more coffee to go through this….. I usually start watching markets after FO, and never trade before LO and this has kept me safe for quite a long time. However I have noticed that recently I am missing quite a few good trades as the move starts at FO and is rarely reversed at LO. Well, apart from today, where there were some good re-entry points at least. I should wake up earlier perhaps (by the way, what time do you start Islander?), but one never knows if this change in pattern is going to be permanent or not. It is a typical dilemma for all systems. Each system goes through cycles and sometimes seems that it can't give a single wrong signal and sometimes it seems to be broken only to resume a few days or weeks later (hey, just for the record, I am not implying that Genesis is broken in any shape or form!) . For instance, I do not seem to be able to make any money on my DAX trading recently, which was one my star performers until some time ago. EU could be another example. This is another reason why discipline, risk and money management (and, if you can, diversification) is so vital to keep you afloat during these cycles. This is also why itchy feet (or minds!) people like RJ try to devise new ways to keep the pips coming in different market conditions, by looking at different time frames, for instance, and giving us another great system in the process….. Another way could be to keep track of other pairs or markets even if one does not trade them. This is what I did with Oil, for instance. I did not trade it for ages, but I kept looking and testing it in the background, so that, if the time comes for some diversification, I know how it behaves….well, with the warnings above. Where DAX is currently threading water, Oil has given some good trades this week. I should add that this should apply to more experienced and disciplined traders, though, as it is easy to get lost juggling too many balls. Enough lecturing and patronising. I am off to pre-Xmas socialising (drinks and gossip). Have a nice weekend everyone.

--- 帖子 #20343 ---
You're definitely right about the ASCT. You need a full 5 minute segment to finish before your color is 'locked in', so the time to act would be on the 6th bar open if conservative is your approach. On the stoch, I personally have been paying more attention to making sure the 15M stoch looks perfect (clean cut move right out of OB/OS with the open mouth heading in the right direction), and using the 5M stoch as more of a dis qualifier. Meaning, I recognize that the move is underway, so it's natural that the 5M stoch might have 'left the station' a little already, so I won't shy away from a mostly traveled, or even pinned 5M stoch as long as it originally came from OB/OS and wasn't just floating around in the middle. Also, on both of RJ's examples in the M1 pdf I think the M5 stoch had moved at least to the 50 level if not more by the time a conservative entry was ready. Anyway, just my thoughts. I am not an expert and yield to the more experienced

@ yesIknow &amp; RJ I start my day at 6:30 am GMT - half an hour before FO with a review of the overnight (for me) action and updating my higher TF charts - I print out 4hr charts of four contracts and have them on the wall above my monitors. Every morning I update them by hand. I also read the news comments, both in FF and elsewhere. I have an A4 day book with the pages divided vertically in half and I update each of my four contracts with yesterdays H,L &amp; C with times and +/- pips and the range. I also add the overnight H, L &amp; R and then I am ready to put in the FO reading of price, the M30 stock reading and slope and the 5m Matrix and range so far for each contract - I update this every hour and will also have note important news times and then that info. - I leave space for the 30 min if needed. If a contract has Aud or Jpy in it, I will consider trading it immediatly on a signal as these are IMO the still active contracts whilst Tokyo, Singapore etc are still open - the obvious ones are AudUsd, EurAud, EurJpy and GbpJpy. I also trade GbpUsd and prefer not to trade it until nearer LO - so 7:30 gmt at minimum and this may be why RJ does not like cable - its best moves are when he's thinking of bed - or already there I make good use of the matrix pop up alerts and I have changed the sound file to mke them more noticable. These are generalisations for range-bound times - thus the most of the time! Once a market starts trending and there is a noticable slope on the 5m 25ema into FO then it becomes worthwhile to consider earlier entries on the appropriate signal - I'm talking about EurUsd and GbpUsd PS I also have trade entry and exit check list which covers my entry and exit rules, comments and conclusion etc etc for each trade taken - I will share this if there is any interest...

--- 帖子 #20350 ---
Regarding the stochs &amp; ASCT..... When the PA has (for example) gone up and hit a BRN and then reversed, yes, ASCT (conservative entry) might be late in the move. But when the PA is wandering along minding it's own business in no particular direction, and then set's it's direction (by way of news or some other event), you'll find that everything (incl stoch) lines up nicely. Remember that stoch is not just a simple oversold/overbought indi, in a short situation, if the M5 stoch has come down from up high but is now getting pretty low, but the M15 stoch looks good and everything else looks good, take the trade. The stoch can stay low (or high) for a considerable amount of time which shows the strength of the move. There's a lot of info on Post #1 about the stoch and there is a little movie as well that illustrates this very well

We....that is *us humans* are the weakest part of any system...and that's a fact. That goes for all things in life too. In skydiving (for instance) the odds of hitting the ground and dieing are about 60,000:1. Yet people die every year. The bottom line is that the equipment (the system) is 10 times more reliable that the person operating it!! It's just the way we are...we see something and act upon it, when we should just trust the system. I'm no different....every time I think I know better than the system I get slapped!!! Having said that, I wouldn't have been very keen to enter your trade because entering a Sell trade just above the DP is not something that I would do.

All I can suggest, is not changing anything, keep your written trading rules beside you, even tick them off prior to entering every trade (thats what I do) . Before your trading day starts, close your eyes, and reiterate them. Then at the end of the day, write down for each trade, did you follow your rules, how did it feel, when you did enter a disciplined trade, and how you felt, when you didnt. Prove to yourself, you can follow your rules, and gradually you will turn the corner.

--- 帖子 #20419 ---
Good advice indeed and in case this helps others here to develope their own set of Trading Rules, here are mine for my personal way of trading off the 1 minute charts - actually my third update since I started using Genesis..... 27 Nov 2013 3D + Genesis Trading Rules When the GM 1m Alert pops up 1. On the 5m chart first confirm that the 30m stoch green line is sloping in the direction of the trade and that a minimum of three components of the G Matrix are the same colour as the direction of the trade. If this stoch is &gt;70 or &lt;30 ignore it as it is OB or OS and just consider the Matrix 2. Do the red and green 60m stoch lines agree with the entry - if NOT then consider reducing the size of the trade. An entry against is considered a CT trade, thus has less potential 3. On the 1 min chart, the 5m stoch must be crossed and "opening" in the direction of the trade and the G Matrix have all four colours in agreement. 4. On the 1 min chart, the 15m stoch must be at least flat and preferably sloping in the direction of the trade 5. When 1,3 and 4 "allow" a trade, enter after the first closed 1m candle that crosses the 1m 25ema in the direction of the trade - provided that the entry is within 4 pips of the 25ema If &gt; 4pips wait for a pull back towards the 25ema 5. Exit part or all after a Wide Ranged Bar with higher volume around a level provided that more than 20 pips are available - less during FH 8 Do NOT overtrade. If in doubt, wait for a pull back or for the next 30m Time Line. 9. Hard Stop Loss is a maximum of 15 pips. Mental SL 25ema / band NB These rules are for entering the more volatile contracts for 2 hours after LO and from NYO 1 for three hours with the objective of banking a minimum average of 30 pips a day - 600 / month. The entries are aggressive. Yen crosses may be entered from FO.

Hi When youre trading pullbacks/CTs on M1 you have to have a modest profit expectation, especially when the DP is coming back into play. I you look at the matrix and the ASCT you can see there were some good indications that price might not continue north. Watching the system signals during the trade is more important than watching price in my view. I know this sounds a bit odd, but on obvious CTs or pullback trades I often take an aggressive entry because I know that there may not be many pips on offer, as long as the SL is manageable. --- 帖子 #20424 ---
I always have a 'split screen' with the M1 chart on the left, and the M5 chart on the right. Half a screen each is plenty to see what's going on. that way on the M5 I can see the immediate trend at all times, and on the M1 I can find a trade that agrees with the M5 immediate trend. In the case of your trade, you were going against the immediate trend. IOW, since LO the trend had been going south, so your trade was certainly a CT trade. Given that it was CT, and even though the signal looked good, the choices are, take a small profit as J said, or treat this CT opportunity as a minor pullback, which it was, and ignore it. Had you done that, and had some more coffee of course , there was a conservative sell signal at around 16.62 (pepperstone time) that would have given you about 30 pips. You 'got out of jail' at BE, and so the broker got nothing from you, which is good. But (to me) having the split screen is essential when M1 trading......

I am defending the "could've, would've, should've and if only" syndrome. These comments usually come out like an expletive - or with a few expletives but if you slow it down a little and review the currency you're talking about it can be more useful than just dismissing those terms as useless. I 'could've' entered just there, where the stochastics are both trending up, both arrows have formed and with my stoploss below - although there was that pullback where I closed out, price then went on up for 200 pips and my "should've" and "if only" would've worked out. Don't just ban these terms, make good use of them for your future trades. I'm always saying, "how can I do better next time?" to myself.

--- 帖子 #20496 ---
Fair enough Jamz For me, those words/phrases only lead to frustration and emotional responses, which harms my trading. I review my trades to look for improvement on exits entries etc, but in a pragmatic way, not wishing I had done something differently or hoping that I will do something differently in the future. If I take +20 and price goes on for +200 I dont care. My style is conservative. I would rather take profits and wait for a re-entry opportunity and pay the spread/commission, than wait through pullbacks...........because thats when I make mistakes. Im at fault when I dont manage trades on a HTF, which I am correcting. Thats my trading style. Those words/phrases aren't banned or useless, theyre just not for me. Hope your trading is going well. I also thought some time ago that Dax is a beast. Now is one of my best friends.... Here is a small trick if you dont use it already. Usually Dow, Dax and Ftse move together. Have the discipline to take trades when all three point to the same direction AND of course all other usual trading rules apply. The beast will become a loyal servant this way. For instance RJ mentioned a few messages back that someone he knows destroyed his account on yesterday's FOMC. In 2-3 minutes after FOMC announcement all the above three indices were pointing north. For such kind of events use M15 matrix as well BUT NO NEED TO WAIT till a full close. When all is white, chose the best setup (low SL possible, etc) and enjoy...

The way I see it jimi, you are taking too many risks. I was dropping hints to you yesterday that the market is quiet, that the market is digesting FOMC, that the end of the year is nearly here etc etc, but you were still taking trades that many of us would not take. The market is not going anywhere, it will be here tomorrow. You don't need to try and score all the goals of the season in a single game!! Even on a small TF like M1, on any given currency pair I see perhaps 1 perfect setup per session. The other set ups look pretty good, but not perfect. Take only the perfect set up. Also, as ExcessFX says, you might want to consider going to the M5 method. One more thing, don't be surfing around different charts all day scanning for a setup....you might find something, but more likely you will miss most entries and you will never get a 'feel' for the personality of any given pair. I used to watch many pairs, but since I started focusing on just 2 (EA and GJ), I have come to know them quite well and I can 'feel' when a set up looks suspicious and when it looks obvious. I may change one, or both of those pairs if the volatility of either (or both) gets too small, and find substitutes......but monitoring 2 pairs closely is something that my account thanks me for! Lastly, the 'glue' that binds all of the above together is the 'holy grail' of trading.....PATIENCE!

I can't recall who showed the following to me, so I cannot take credit for finding this little gem of a tool. Please get in touch with me (you know who you are) and I will add this to Post#1 and credit you with it's discovery. Anyway...on this page you will find the coolest of volatility tools. It will show you which pairs are returning the best amount of pips over a given period, so that you can perhaps review the pairs you trade. 1. So, go to the page 2. In the 'Volatility calculated over the last Weeks' text box, enter '2' and 'Submit Query' 3. Click the word 'Pips' at the top of the table and this will order the table by Pips Ascending. 4. Click it again and this will order the table by Pips Descending. 5. Have coffee and enjoy

--- 帖子 #20596 ---
It can be due to various reasons; important news, strong S/R level of certain pair, period of the day....Mostly those are the things that you need to do/examine by yourself and that is the "discrete" part. No system or EA will do this for you. Combined with mechanical parts of the system (eg. same direction of matrix, stochs, ASCT) genesis will give you the edge. If you have more HTFs aligned, you will be with the trend and your chances for HPT will increase. If I have everything above, and still price hit my SL, I will take my loss with no problem. Nothing is 100% (except death and taxes ). So my advice is, if you decide to continue with genesis, leave M1 trading to more experienced/versatile traders, where "discrete" part plays bigger role and focus on M5 or M15.

It could well be that volume does show an exit that coincides with pivots etc, but I think that when entering on the M1 and managing on the M5, the pivots, BRN's, etc that have served us well in the past, do a great job. --- 帖子 #20686 ---
Well, I'm an aggressive trader when it comes to MM. The longer term TF I'm still running on Genesis I risk 10% of the balance. Most of my equity is "floating" by nature of the strategy, so figuring on balance isn't really that high. On the M1 &amp; M5, I'll be risking 5% based on stoploss. Based on an average s/l of 10 pips that would obviously give a return of 5% on a 10 pip move. My goal is going to be 20 pips a day. If I can reach that it would double account about every 8 trading days (don't trade every day) with compounding. I know that's pie in the sky...but a man's gotta dream.

--- 帖子 #20687 ---

--- 帖子 #20688 ---
Hi FoM, good question ... I think the TS is just a piece of the puzzle and IMHO not the most important. Of course you need to have a TS with an edge otherwise you loose time and money but even if there are many good systems many traders can't win. I think one has to follow the following step in each trade : SET UP 1) Market HTFs analysis and understanding 2) Game plan ( what if analysis ) EXECUTION 3) Entry signal 4) MM 5) Management (what do I do at the first traffic area? BE, scaling, TP) --&gt; if you didn't make a good setup phase it is more difficult to manage your trades 6) Exit (SL or TP) MM is another very important piece of the puzzle and in some way strongly correlated to psychological side of the game and a lack of trading/business plan

--- 帖子 #20691 ---
Lol...not really. I just feel that if whatever strategy I'm implementing is solid then I'll be okay. Risking a lower percentage won't make my trades any more or less successful. If my strategy is flawed, with a lower % risk, the account will just bleed to death more slowly. Conversely, if I have a strategy that is successful, I'd just as soon risk a bit more for a more rapid growth rate. As account balance increases I would scale back the percentage accordingly.

--- 帖子 #20692 ---
Yes s/l is a bit bigger. But remember (if you've looked at my other LTF posts). I'm actually entering on the M15 but using the other TF's to establish direction. All TF's must be in sync...from M15 to W1. So the stops aren't really that much bigger on M15...maybe 25 to 40 pips. I move my stop to BE when profit is equal to original stop, then trail until profit is locked at the level of the original stop. After that I switch to the 4H, D1 &amp; W1 as discussed earlier.

--- 帖子 #21083 ---
Can I give some suggestions? Try to get really good at Genesis first, and then add the other stuff. Speaking from my own experience. I always like to try new indicators out, but what I've found is I needed to have a system that I've traded on and know inside out, and then gradually add the other indicators. Other wise it can be confusing and counterproductive. How long does it take to know a system inside out? It depends. Some people are fast, I'm probably on the slow side (haha). And I didn't have much experience before coming across Genesis. And I can't think of a better 'core' system than Genesis + Moving Averages. So perhaps it is better that you know Genesis so well so that when you add or try out each new indicator you can pretty quickly gauge whether this indicator adds to Genesis or not. And 'how' it adds. MTF Stochs, Genesis/ASCTrend tapes and MTF Moving Averages are the core of my entries. If these don't line up properly, I won't trade. However, nowadays I've added a few other indicators to help me filter these trades for even better win-loss ratio. But these took a lot of time and don't work unless my core entry signal is correct. Regarding moving averages, I think they help straight away. Helps you gauge trend, and you'd want to trade on the right side of trend until you get really good at Genesis. Whereas RJ doesn't need moving averages because he's had so much chart time and is such a great trader, I think most traders could do with some form of MA to filter CounterTrend trades (at least until they get really good).

--- 帖子 #21085 ---
I feel like now is a good time to repost a post that I consider "gold" from back in the early days of the thread ... done by OlivierForex who is no longer on the thread but has some great posts if you're ever digging around the thread ... basically it covers how he figures out whether adding a new indicator actually makes him any better off or worse off ... I'm copying and pasting rather than quoting as quoting would cut it off. Original post is here : http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...9&amp;#post6016049 ########################## That is so true....The 'problem' with people's perception of Genesis is that its graphical &amp; visual simplicity hides the complexity behind it. I'm sure that most people look at the matrix and count it as 1 indicator (4 dots either blue or red - easy) when in fact it is none of that. If I'm correct, bar the CCI line, the 3 other matrix lines (TVI/GHL/T3) are 'made' of at least 2 indicators (if not more) running in the background. So at a stroke you already have a minimum of 7 'decision makers', add the Stox (5 &amp; 15) + the Yellow MA + the Arrow &amp; the odd Pivot line &amp; you are talking about at least 12 different indicators all needing to be pointing in the same direction to give you valid signal. How many more do you really need? But having said that, yes you can add more indicators as extra 'filters' and for sure they will stop you entering some Genesis bad trades but the flipside of that is they will also keep you out &amp; make you miss some good trades. It's a balancing act and I decide to include something extra in my trading only by doing a lot of backtesting and this is my method: .on the M5 TF I will mark down on my chart all the Genesis trades for a minimum of 1 month. .for each of these trades I will write down what my Potential New Filter (PNF) was telling me and you have 4 possible scenarios: 1) PNF agrees with a Genesis good trade: that will be marked as +0 (the PNF didn't add anything). 2) PNF agrees with a Genesis bad trade &amp; that trade would have been a 20 pips loss: that will be marked also as +0 (the PNF didn't add anything). 3) PNF disagrees with a Genesis good trade and it would have stopped me from entering a good/valid trade: if that trade 'showed' me a 'realistic' 30 pips, I mark this as -30. 4) PNF disagrees with a Genesis bad trade and that trade would have been a 20 pips loss: that will become +20 (the PNF stopped me from entering a bad trade). I then add it all up and if: .it is a negative (-) total or very close to zero then the PNF gets discarded as it hasn't added anything of value: it's only taking some of my attention away from the other stuff. .it is a big positive number &amp; I will include it in my forward live trading for a month and see if the backtesting results match the live difference in outcome. It's only then that I decide to keep it or not. So if you have anything 'new' to add to Genesis' core rules and you have done some proper (and I really mean proper lol) backtesting to backup your claims then I'll happily listen. ##########################

--- 帖子 #21110 ---
Spyderman Thanks for your charts. I also use the M30 Stoch like Marty, and I need both M15 and M30 Stoch aligned (crossed in the same direction at the very least) to trade. I cheat a little though. I use the settings of 8,3,3 for the M30 Stoch (just the M30 Stoch and timeframes higher than M30) just so I can get the HTF crossover a little faster. This rarely hurts as we're not timing the entry based on M30 Stoch, rather the M5/M15 stoch, but getting the crossover confirmation a little faster on M30 with this setting helps to miss less trades. See if you like this better than 11,3,3 for M30. For M5/M15 Stochs, RJ's tried and true 11,3,3 settings work wonderfully. Also, I think you'll find it helpful for have your stoch panes larger, and it actually doesn't hurt to have the price action panes smaller. Which is kind of against common sense. But then again, RJ darkens the HA candles, so he focuses more on the indicators. Personally, I have M5 and M15 stochs in one pane, and M30 stochs in another. The wider panes allows you to see the stoch mouths in M15/M30 more clearly. For me, my tapes and stoch panes take up &gt;2/3 of my chart, with prices &lt;1/3.

--- 帖子 #21112 ---
Regarding trying to get M5 stoch coming straight down from OB vs hooking, took me a long time to get through on this point also. RJ gave us the simple M5/M15 stoch coming from OB/OS, which is the ideal setup for strength. But trying to get this without looking at M30 Stoch will lead to mistakes (unless you have a lot of price action knowldege and experience trading genesis) because often, when M5/M15 stoch are just exiting from OB/OS, M30 stoch is still in OB/OS and may not exit or the exit may be weak and prices/M30 stoch will hook up again. But when you wait for M30 stoch to come down and agree, usually you've missed the trade as SL is higher and prices have moved. One alternative is to have another indicator to help you filter the strength of the price action. That is hard and less reliable. The other alternative is to wait for M30 stoch to come down, confirm, and wait for a retracement in the LTF stoch (M5/M15) and try to get in on that (and if you don't get it, well, you've missed a trade but haven't lost anything). Like Marty implied, once M30 stoch crosses 50 strongly (ie with wide mouth), you can go back historical charts and see how long it takes for M30 stoch to hit the opposite OB/OS and for %K to cross over %D in OB/OS. That's how much time (opportunity) you have time to your entry on the M5 timeframe. The M5 stoch hook up/down on strong M30 stoch (with wide mouth) simply means that the M30 stoch has such overriding strength that M5 stoch cannot make a full retracement to the originating OB/OS.

--- 帖子 #21130 ---
If you can improve your entry to an extent that your win-loss ratio gets very good, then the R:R (whether it is 1:1 or 0.8:1) isn't that big of an issue, in my opinion, as you'll get enough winners that run pass your initial target prices. What matters is your overall R-multiple, or roughly a combination of your risk reward + win-loss ratio. One impacts the other, so you can never really look at it separately. You can have a strategy that has low R:R but high win-loss ratio that works, or the other way around a low win-loss ratio but high R:R (but you'll need very strong mental strength for this). So the ultimate goal is to get so good at Genesis that you improve the win-loss ratio and risk:reward at the same time, to get a high R-multiple strategy.

--- 帖子 #21155 ---
Different parts of the world but in our summer I feel that I'm missing out a lot of the "best trading time" too. I feel bad about missing the US session, and I guess you feel bad about missing the London session. One thing I do everyday is go through the charts for the day before and mark out the good strong entries that occurred during my trading hours - generally ones that would've made 20 pips or more. Now each pair usually has 1 or 2 of those strong entries every day in the 3 - 4 hours that I can trade. That is, each pair usually has at least 1 - 2 strong setups that generated a good profit during the time that I traded. This eases my frustration levels because it reinforces everyday that the strong setups are there, and that there's really no need to jump into less than optimal trades.

--- 帖子 #21160 ---
The thing to bear in mind here, is that back testing will always show fantastic entry and exit points. Forward testing, or testing live, is very different. Genesis doesnt repaint, we know that, BUT, the matrix, ASCT, and stochs will always re-form themselves within their set time frames. RJs PDF on M1 trading shows perfect examples of this. I went a long time looking back at sessions the day before and found 90% + examples of great set ups. Lets not forget that those set ups only confirm themselves after 'periods' finish. To quote....'trading from the right side of the chart is much harder than the left'..................or something to that nature............PM1 I think. J

--- 帖子 #21243 ---
If you use Xaphod's stoch-mtf, then it will give you the stoch the whole way through. For example, if you are 45 minutes into the hour, then the last 45 minutes will show as a different colour (in my case orange) because it's not yet locked in, but, it gives you an indication of where it's likely to finish. Diagram below shows you what I mean ... the bits between the pink lines aren't "locked in", and on a normal stoch you wouldn't see them. But the stoch-mtf interprets where the stoch is at the present moment and paints that as orange until it's "locked in"

Firstly....Happy New Year to you all, I hope everyone had a great Christmas/New Year and that you're all ready for another year of trading. Thanks to those that contributed to the thread over the holiday period, and congratulations to those that took the banks money! There are a couple of points I need to raise though......and to start with I will paste below what I posted just 3 months ago: "The reason why no other indicators will be allowed is simple. The system works, and it works well as it is. If someone with a year or two of struggling to be consistently profitable comes here and uses the system as is, they will be on the path to consistent profitability. However, if I wasn't so strict on the indi issue, by now people would see charts with various THV indicators, Coral, all manner of MA crosses, SAR, Inchimoku clouds, harmonic patterns etc etc etc......and then this thread would look like any other here at FF.....and the very people we are trying to help would see this thread as just another mongrel system that is complicated and open to all sorts of predictions and interpretations. Who will win?......the brokers, that's who!!! When people become consistently profitable with Genesis, they may well add their own indies to make the system even more profitable....and that's great....I love it. But hopefully, by then, they will realise that others who are joining our thread are in the same position that they once were themselves. And what do they need? They need a consistent, easy(ish) system with pages and pages of examples with all the same charts, and a group of profitable Genesis traders to help them to become profitable. And that's the reason why outside indicators have to be kept off the thread." If you want to talk about 'bundles' of MA's or anything other than the core Genesis System, please do it via PM or start another thread. The very people I see discussing these things are the same people who needed, and benefited from, the nice clean Genesis thread that we have. Please show some discipline and allow those people who are waiting to join our thread to see the same thing you saw when you came here so that they too can benefit from the system without the confusion that is creeping into the thread. Comments such as 'I didn't enter because the MA's suggested not to enter" (for example) are way off topic and have no place here. We do not trade based on what any MA's may or may not indicate......in the same way that we do not discuss Elliot Waves, micro waves, Mexican waves or any other kind of wave!! It's true that I have my own personal version of Genesis, same as Fame of Me does, same as Martyfish does and others no doubt do as well. But I do not discuss that on the thread, and the trades I show and all the testing I have done for the various TF's traded conform to the standard Genesis system. On Post #1 it is explained how to very easily post charts that conform to the rules, without so much as raising a bead of sweat on your brow. For the sake of those people yet to come, PLEASE respect the rules and keep this thread clean. Thank you. The second point I want to raise is that I may not be around as much this year as I have been previously. I will still keep an eye on the thread, but it's very tiring (and annoying) to have to keep repeating the same things over and over, when the onus should not be on me to keep going over the same ground just because someone is too lazy to read Post #1 and it's links, and/or to use the threads 'Search' function!! For instance, I see some SL placement questions being asked and various answers given. The placement of SL is clearly explained in Post #2 and it has been gone over several times in this thread!! So I won't be answering such questions in the future, I will simple tell the poster to 'get off his ass and find the answer in the thread"......it's that simple. People who are too lazy to find the answer and expect others to spent *their time* answering them might just find themselves being shown the door. Lastly.....if a person expects to learn how to trade with this (or any) system, they HAVE to have the discipline to immerse themselves completely in that system.....and not jump around from thread to thread, system to system and expect to learn much.....because it won't happen!! It is impossible to glance over a system and expect to be trading it successfully in a short period of time, more so if that person is going to have a dabble at several other systems at the same time. Find a system, and focus on it completely if you expect to learn it! So.....to finish on some positives.... I have all the tools necessary for us to 'take up residence' elsewhere if FF behave towards me and this thread in the way they did at the end of last year. --- 帖子 #21313 ---
Firstly, trading news events is far higher risk, and should only be traded by experienced traders, and start with small trade sizes. Secondly, I dont follow FF rating of news, to me the industry standard rating is more relevant, Retail sales are tier 2 news, I very rarely trade tier 1 news, ie jobs/CB announcements/CPI. Tier 2 is less volatile, and more predictable. There is nothing wrong closing just prior to news events, if you are in a trade. Its all about the setup, if PA goes through a stalling process prior to news, and my MAs line up, then just prior to the news, ie within 5 mins, you start getting loads of asc arrows in the direction of my MAs, that turns it into a good trade setup, if there wasnt going to be a news event, I am trusting a Genesis signal is all I am doing here. In my chart setup, I think I forgot to say, on my M5 chart I have M5/M15/M30 asc arrows, and on M15 chart I have M15/M30/H1 arrows all have alerts. But you need to do loads of back-testing seeing those news events, and the Genesis setup - dont ry it unless you are completely comfortable recognising those Genesis setups.

--- 帖子 #21469 ---
You MUST watch it closely....there's no other way on the M1-M5 method. My advice would be to pick a single pair only....and i would choose *either* EA of GJ...perhaps even EJ....but only one of those pairs. They each give pretty good ATR and they are consistent. If Tokyo market is best for your location, then perhaps one of the Yen crosses (GJ or EJ) would suit. If London market is easier for you, perhaps EA would suit. No matter which pair....stick with that pair. Get to know it well....get to understand how it reacts to news and it reacts to different times of the day. Find out what an average move might be (not a news event). Perhaps it moves it steps of 15 pips....perhaps more, or less. The only way you will know this is if you focus on the job in front of you. You won't do it by glancing at several pairs, reading the thread, checking up on Facebook (or whatever) when you think nothing is happening...because....when you're not concentrating....it will happen, and you will miss it!! Tokyo market hasn't offered anything today on the pairs I mention, and given that we are 4 hours into the session, perhaps nothing will happen until Frankie/London market. We can never be sure, but from my own observations, mostly if it hasn't happened by now, then it probably isn't going to!! I will cook dinner and see what happens at Frankie/London. I have in the past. Main fix within MT4 is to go Tools -&gt; Options -&gt; Charts and decrease the Max bars in history and Max bars in chart. I have one setup with 10,000 and one with 20,000 - which is heaps less than the default setting and means you use a lot less memory and hence your computer handles it better. Other factors are obviously number of charts / indicators ... and also what else your computer may be doing. My experience anyway.

Maybe you could try with some harder rules when it comes to money management. If you are afraid that green trade will become red, you can set BE+1 after 15 or even 10 pips on M1 for example. Right after you enter the trade, BE is set so if your trade goes 10 or 15 pips in profit, depending on your settings, your trade would be a safe ride from that point, no need to worry anymore. That way you can eliminate over-thinking and save your self from getting exhausted. If a trade goes in your direction, great, try figuring your TP or bring your SL down/up. If not, you're BE on that trade so no loss, concentrate on finding another entry. We will beat this creature! Cheers!

--- 帖子 #21643 ---
One thing to be aware of in situations such as this spydi is where the previous supply and demand area was. During the Asian session the market reached a high of 169.77 before selling off into the start of the euro session. As the PA edged towards this level again shortly after NY open, it started to falter, as you yourself mentioned earlier. This uncertainty together with the price now sitting at the Asian high level was a warning sign to either close out fully or close partially and leave the rest on the table. The euro session topped out at 169.77 just like the Asian session did. Doesn't always fall into place like it did today but it's nice when it does!

--- 帖子 #21664 ---
All economic news releases are categorised by their respective level of importance. Broken down into Tier 1, 2, and 3. Tier 1 - Central bank announcements, GDP, CPI, jobs. Tier 2 - Retail sales, PMIs, some CB speakers, etc Tier 3 - all other

--- 帖子 #21665 ---
Its not mentioned here much, maybe because the southern hemishere traders dont have to deal with multiple tier 1/2 news releases. On trading days where UK, EZ, and US have multiple news releases like today, trading on these days is incredibly difficult. Pre-news pops, moves suddenly stop, as the market prepares for the next news event, make trading exceptionally difficult. Today we have US ADP at 13:15, then US Services PMI at arounf 14:00, then more PMI at 15:00. In all 7 tier 1/2 news releases.

Metaquotes bears sole responsibility for the results of their update latest . If you need help, your broker and Metaquotes should provide it. Contact info: http://forum.mql4.com/60555 support@metaquotes.net Metaquotes service desk One could reasonably expect the update to perform the following procedure correctly. Apparently, it does not. To run old indicators that do not compile successfully in the new version: Find the MT4 data folder: http://forum.mql4.com/60555 See point 3. Locate the 'oldindi*.ex4' files in where ever MT4 stores them: " ..\experts\indicators\ ". The file date stamps will be prior to the update. Locate the newly compiled files in the new " ..\MQL4\indicators\ " folder. Make a backup copy and delete both the 'oldindi*.mq4' and 'oldindi*.ex4' files. Copy the old *.ex4 to the new " ..\MQL4\indicators\ " folder. Do not copy the *.mq4 files . Make sure to get any other required indicators/files. Restart MT4 Programs that generate offline charts will not work without being rewritten and recompiled: http://articles.mql4.com/1140 Some programs that call dll's with string parameters may not work correctly without rewriting. MT4 now uses unicode strings. It previously used ANSI strings.

--- 帖子 #21725 ---
Xaphod, Order processing was supposed to be improved! Quoting from their notes: Terminal: Changed the algorithm of placing trade requests. In previous builds, an additional network connection has been created when placing trade requests. This connection has remained active for some time after a last trade request was sent in order to provide fast sending of a large number of trade requests. Now, when placing trade requests, all of them are passed via the main connection with the trade server. Thus, the time of processing the trade requests (especially the first one) has been considerably reduced as there is no need to wait for connection to the trade server being established any more. In order for the new request sending algorithm to be operable, the trade server should also be updated - requests are still set in a separate connection on older trade servers. Due to transition to the new model of requests processing, the ability to cancel the trade requests not yet accepted by the server (Cancel button in the trade request status dialog) has been disabled. I no longer use MetaTrader for orders for several reasons, including platform issues. Let me just say watching the price from an ECN broker along side a typical retail broker has been eye-opening. I hope that the issues smooth out quickly. Which broker do you use, if you don't mind me asking?

--- 帖子 #21732 ---
Hello everybody, I have been on the sidelines for a while, but I’ve been trying Genesis on H4 for the last month and there are some points I’d like to share with you all… Trying to use the standard Genesis 5-15 on H4-D I’ve come across some interesting things: 1. Obviously due to the huge SL required I had to drastically reduce the position size 2. I had the (wrong) idea that H4 was extremely slow, I would have to wait for ages to get a valid signal and in the end it wouldn’t be profitable unless you had a very good amount of money to start with. 3. Trailing and TP has always been an issue for me, due to the nature of H4, what to do now with H4 candles that fly through RNs? what to do at pivot points? How can I assess if I have “room” for a trade since RNs seem so “close” in H4? What I’ve found: 1. Reducing the position size to the absolute minimum allowed me to open trades in different pairs and sometimes if I’m caught on the wrong side on one pair that position can be balanced with profits from other pairs. Not exactly basket trading, but some sort of. Another interesting thing is that obviously the spread in money terms becomes quite irrelevant. 2. Due to lotsize and ample SL used I can check the charts two or three times a day without the fear of finding a massive bleeding of the account. Small positions, small losses… (Small profit? Not sure). Quite ok sailing through non extremely important news, too, and more driven by fundamentals. I have the matrix indi with immediate alert, not the default alert on bar close, this way the alert is not a proper trigger, but more of a “kind advice” that I will assess whenever I have the opportunity to have a look at the charts in the next 4 hours. If I get several Daily matrix alerts that could indicate trend weakness too. 3. This part has been tricky. “Moving to BE too soon is a sign of a nervous trader” (thanks kosmo), but I have to protect my profit… To work around the problem I tried this, borrowed from Nanningbob: Signal. Matrix + stoch will give a signal letting you know a potential trade set up is happening (kind advice). When this happens, you can then look at the chart and decide whether or not to take the trade, the important thing here is that there is time to assess the situation, for instance if price is behind the DP I will set a pending order after de pivot, if not I could take the trade immediately or set a pending order at the next RN or after an evident S/D area. I don’t usually wait for the candle to close (we’re in H4!) Take Profit To protect profits what works best (for me, also borrowed from Nanningbob) is to use standard TP just before the next RN and a series of pending orders immediately after the RN. This way, without moving the SL, I can give the trade enough room to move banking profits at the same time and follow the whole move (since I use minimum lotsize I cannot take partial profits, and the spread influence per trade is minimal). One of the orders will probably be triggered and become a loser, well I will have banked a few of them by that time and will have time to close it manually if the matrix shows signs of exhaustion. It’s very early days yet but the results have been very, very promising, hit ratio of over 70% and 19.86% gain in two weeks. Those 40 - 45 pips orders really stack on top of each other! (Yes, considering the SL, the RR per trade is horrible, but once you have taken the profit who cares where was the SL?) Sorry for the long post. I'm not sure it's completely Genesis, I had to tweak a bit the exit strategy and timing in order to make it fit in my daily schedule, any thoughts are welcomed.

--- 帖子 #21748 ---
Some people seem to have problems with Build 600, and not others. I have had no issues at all. but one thing I have done is to delete all the .mq4 files from the new 'Indicators' folder (see pic) to just leave the .ex4 files there. I did this because Build 600 cannot compile the .mq4 files correctly, so you end up with a corrupt .ex4 file that will not work. Therefore, there is no reason to leave the .mq4 files there as one day they may cause a problem. Before you go deleting them though, make sure you have backups......you can get these from the old 'experts/indicators' folder, and you should store them somewhere other than on the same machine.....windoze being not crashproof etc etc...lol. I talked to Xaphod here about deleting the .mq4 files from the new indicators folder, and he agrees.

--- 帖子 #21749 ---
Yup, that's exactly what I did also. Works fine for me, and my upgrade took only a couple of hours. Just make sure to keep a copy of all your indicators and templates somewhere safe first. I had some trouble with the stoch-mtf.ex4 file on higher timeframes initially, sometime it just disappears. But seems to be working better now. It would be great if we eventually have a thread for Genesis tools .mq4 files for build 600 and higher

--- 帖子 #21752 ---
That's right...that's exactly what that pop up will do. I too said 'No', but I got sick of it and thought, 'what the hell...lets do it'...and clicked 'Yes'. The next thing that happened was the platform opened for a split second and then shut down. After about 2 or 3 seconds it opened again, momentarily, and then shut down again. 2 or 3 seconds later, it opened and stayed open so I checked the version and it said 'Build 600'.....so I opened some charts, and all was well. After finding where the templates and indicators now reside I was ok.....I really don't care where they reside, as long as I know where they are!! During my research on Build 600, I found out that if you place an .mq4 file in the new location, the platform will try to create (compile) an .ex4 file, which is what Build 509 used to do as well. But now the programming language has changed and MT4 (Build 600) can no longer read the old language properly, so it tries to create and .ex4 file, but it can't do it. What you end up with is a corrupt .ex4 file, which is the indi, and it won't work! So....to prevent any chance of an .mq4 file automatically trying to compile into a .ex4 file (which won't work), better to delete the .mq4 files completely from the new location because they are redundant......no point in them even being there. Whether build 600 is better than 509. I don't know. You'd have to ask Xaphod about that. But if I was you, when the markets are quiet, I'd bite the bullet and upgrade......provided you have already made backups of you 'experts/indicators' folder, as well as your templates folder. In the event that it all turns to shit, you can uninstall MT4 and download a fresh one from your broker......replace the indicators and templates from your back up, and you should be good to go

--- 帖子 #21757 ---
The updated programming language has more functionality which will make writing more advanced indicators and EAs easier. They have added their App and Signal Market which is probably one of the main reasons for the update. Metaquotes takes a 20% cut of sales. Build 600+ is supposed to open market orders faster. About 400ms faster. Previous builds required re-authentication after 30s of trade inactivity which caused the longer processing time. However, the new build is still riddled with bugs and should really be still in beta. They released 4 updates (600, 602,603,604) the first week of the initial release which should give you some idea of the quality of the software.

--- 帖子 #21771 ---
Over the past couple of days I have been testing another economic calendar. The one here lacks many events which could be important and it's kind of irritating (to me) to have to sit there clicking a little green ball and watching it spin round and round to actually get the data!! So I am now using the very good calendar of FX Street. The calendar is full of useful events and it updates as the event is released.....with no input from you required. It also sounds a chime when each event is released. I have been impressed with it's speed and accuracy and it's great to not have to click and wait for the update. Of course it can be configured to suit your time zone. There are other features there too, but you can find them all in a video tutorial which is at the top of the calendar. The website has some useful stuff elsewhere on it too. You need to sign up to FX Street, but that's a 2 minute operation and is quite painless. I love the calendar and will use it all the time from now on. Check it out at: http://www.fxstreet.com/economic-calendar/

I’ve been finding this week difficult to trade. So i thought i’d put this post up, it may or may not help anyone, this is more of a diary for myself that i will refer back on. I have finished the week with a profit, but it hasn’t necessarily been from well placed trades. I should mention, i can only trade from Tokyo open until two hours after London open. This is because i live in New Zealand. I have a specific set of rules for entering trades, this has evolved over time and basically it is: M5 Chart, M5 Matrix, M5, 15 stochs dropping or rising from OB/OS, H1 Stochs lining up, and i try to get the H4 on board as well. Exit when M5 Matrix discolours. The above entry setup has not occurred very often this week, which left me second guessing my trading setup, and that perhaps i was doing something wrong. Yesterday i added trend indicators, stoch tapes, etc etc. Then i arrived at the conclusion, the market simply wasn’t offering the pips, there was absolutely nothing wrong with my original trading setup. I have reverted back to my original setup, and did a IFR type scan over the weeks data, to the hours i trade. All i could find was 3 trades that match my entry requirements. I only trade GJ and EA. I have attached the examples. 3 trades, (10, 40 &amp; 45 pis over 5 days) This is 19 pips per day (and its a bad week in my book). 19 pips per day put into the spreadsheet is still a great deal of money by the end of the year. The point of this post is more about phycology. It doesn’t matter if a few days go by and there are no trades that suit your entry requirements. As RJ would say, patience is the holy grail in FX trading. Making “knee jerk reactions” to fake-outs will only lead to an empty account. Have a great weekend everyone ExcessFX *Credit to RJ, Martyfish &amp; jjre65 for their influences

--- 帖子 #21878 ---
We probably have all gone through making a similar mistakes in our learning curve. Yes, you MUST follow the trend. Taking counter trend (CT) trades is not for the inexperienced. I don't know of a single trader who is successful who doesn't make him/herself aware of the overall trend. I trade mainly M1 charts, sometimes M5...but every day when I sit down in the morning, I check the H1 situation as well as the H4 and sometimes the Daily charts too. I take notes of the trend...direction, when the trend started, what level it started at and how strong I think it is. You can do this really easily by starting on the Daily chart and in your notebook, just enter the currency pair and in the margin, enter DAILY and beside it, just draw an up or down arrow. Then, under that, enter H4 and beside that, enter your up or down arrow.....then H1, then M30, then m15. Now you should have a good idea of which way we're going. If all the arrows seem up and down, perhaps we are in a consolidating phase, which makes it more difficult. If all the arrows are the same way, then only take trades in that direction

Welcome to our new members....more of us to take the banks money!! There will be a few more joining shortly too. Just one point, I received a PM concerning the new Build 600 zip file of the Post #1. The concern was that it wasn't set us as per the M1 trading set up. That's true, it isn't!! It's set up as per the standard M5 trading that Genesis is based around. The M5 set up originally used only the M5 stoch (11,3,3), but over time we discovered that is handy to also have the M15 stoch setup on the same chart. This is how the new zip file is set up. All the standard stuff, but also including the MTF Stoch set to M15 time. If you want to change that template to a specific M1 set up, you'll have to swap that standard stoch for another instance of the MTF stoch and set it to M5. So to recap the stoch settings.... M1 trading stochs are: MTF set to 5 period...11,3,3 and also MTF stoch set to 15 period....11,3,3 M5 trading stochs settings...... Standard stoch (5 period)....11,3,3 and also MTF stoch set to 15 period....11,3,3

--- 帖子 #21939 ---
It certainly can be confusing....but if you spend some time on the weekend going back over some of the senior members charts, you might see that the trades they pick are very often really good ones. Also, you have to go back over your own charts and fine the absolute perfect trades that meet the requirements to a tee. In any given day, you might see (say) 8 pretty good set ups. Of those 8, perhaps 6 win and 2 lose. Of the 6 winners, perhaps 4 are small winners and the other 2 are reasonable. That's not a bad ratio at all.....but.....there is quite a bit of stress in managing 8 trades in a day, especially when the 8 setups are just, pretty good . More often then not, I will just let those pretty good set ups go. I might take the trade if I think there's a few pips in in it, but I try to wait for the perfect set up......one where everything is aligned about as good as it's possible to get, and I take that trade. Often, that single trade will yield more pips than the 6 pretty good setups. Now, none of the above is going to be too much help to you, so the best way, imo, is to do something that Olivia used to talk about when she was here.....she would say, 'immediately after you enter the trade, take a screenshot of it. If you would be proud to post that screenshot here as a great example of a great entry......then it probably is!!......if you see your screenshot and think...hmmm....this one may or may not fly, probably shouldn't have entered......then you probably shouldn't have entered!!!' As the saying goes.....it's better (for your pocket) to be out, wishing in....than it is to be in, wishing out!!!

--- 帖子 #21945 ---
When I enter a trade, I already know where the SL will be placed, and how expensive it will be if it gets hit. If it's going to be too expensive, then I can reduce the lots size traded to make the SL cost acceptable, or else I will just skip the trade completely. No point in having a 40 pip SL when the profit is going to be 20 pips!! Also, we have to remember that the SL is there more as an emergency measure, rather than something that we will allow to be hit. It's there in case some idiot like Draghi says something wrong and causes a big spike at the wrong moment!! Once the trade is entered and the SL is placed, if the trade starts looking bad.....ie the candles go the other way, the stochs turn over etc etc and everything is generally turning bad, then I will just cut the trade manually. No point in sitting there like a zombie watching your SL get hit.....if you've made a mistake and the trade turns around, take a manual exit and re-think the whole plan...over a cup of coffee I generally do monitor my trade very closely, until I can get the SL into profit, so that the trade is safe....no matter what happens. Once that's done, then I can look for other opportunities. As the trade progresses, I will manually move my SL further into profit, and then go back to looking for other opportunities. Remember...I already have a target in mind (S1, R1, BRN or something), so I don't need to worry too much about it. Either it gets to my target or it stops me out in profit.....either way, I win!!

--- 帖子 #21972 ---
Hi to you both. Aswell as manual trailing the stop, it is important to focus on the system indicators during the trade, not the candles, as you do in watching for set ups. The Matrix, ASCT and stochs will tell you when price is running out of steam. If you both look at your exit point you will see there is no sign of weakness in the move according to the system indicators. Trading M1 I take notice when the TVI and T3 change colour on the M1 Matrix, and usually take action when they change colour on my M5 chart, unless it is a big trade and I am managing the trade on M15, or price is due for a pullback or a rest before moving on.......anyway the point being the indicators are there as much for trade management as they are for trade identification. We all leave pips on the table sometimes. Dont worry about it, just learn from it. Nothing wrong with taking profits. You dont need to squeeze every last pip out of every trade. With good MM, 10 - 30 pips a day is plenty enough to make a lot of money if you compound your account. If youre not using PM1's trade calculator xls I would strongly recommend it. Cheers J.

Sorry to labour the point. But I find it absolutely fascinating why new/beginner traders try CT trades ? So, take today, fabulous volatility, many, many big trend trades, that are yielding big 20 - 40 + pips per move. All HPT trades with solid Genesis signals. Why would anyone consider a CT trade ? I know from my own experience early in my trading career, I tried for months and months, thinking, I could be clever and pinch CT pips, because I knew all about trading, and my system was awesome and capable of picking up pips all over the place, BUT never took the big trend trades. So I would pick up a few pips here and a few pips there, then a big stopped out loss (exits are tough for experienced traders, VERY tough for new traders). Not quite sure why I wouldn't take the big trend move, might be the volatility, might be questioning is this the trend move or a fake out, unsure of my system, because I changed it every other day ?? Determining trend seems an easy thing to do, but when, where, and more importantly why did the move start ? and when to get in ?? Also, the key aspect of "laws of probability". When you already have a great system like Genesis, once you have spent a considerable amount of time studying setups that yield decent trend moves, just keeping hitting the button, and rewards will come. Then you will have completely forgotten about CT trades !! I promise !!

--- 帖子 #22059 ---
Hi mazp The reverse order adds up to the same result, which is getting all the ducks in a row and pulling the trigger, whether you are waiting for signals on LTFs and confirming on HTFs or the other way around. However, I will take LTF stochs coming from OB/OS with HTF stochs in a high or low position every time over HTF stochs coming from OB/OS and LTF stochs above/below 80/20. I know from my trading, that LTF stochs coming from high/low w HTF stochs in the same general direction when they are high/low usually gives me a 15-20 pip head start in trades, which gets me into very good positions. Strong HTF stochs do carry a lot of influence over long term price action, but they do not in any way prevent price from doing whatever it wants, when it wants. Strong M15 stoch is not the key for me, it is a piece of the puzzle. For sure it was an HPT, but not merely because the HTFs were in line. No trade is an HPT just because the HTF stochs agree, there are many other considerations, at least for me. Cheers J.

--- 帖子 #22070 ---
Yes - the value of GbpJpy is calculated by multiplying the values of its two components....viz: GbpUsd X UsdJpy = GbpJpy I recently explained this here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...90#post7319990 Thus a 1 pip`move in UsdJpy moves GbpJpy by 1.67 pips, whereas a 1 pip move in GbpUsd only moves GbpJpy by 1.03 pips. Therefore, IMO, to obtain the trades with the most potential it is important to monitor both of the base pairs and look to take entries when BOTH are moving in the same direction. If they are moving in opposite directions then only trade one of the base pairs.

--- 帖子 #22101 ---
Hi You will find 2 schools of thought concerning these trades on the thread. Some believe that some market movers know the news well before it is released, and large positions are being built up to an hour out from news release. I have taken some news trades where Genesis has provided good entry signals, and where I thought there was enough room to build a 20 ish pip profit before the news break. You can now set your SL say 15pips in profit 5mins out from the release, which on my broker will usually absorb slippage if the news goes against the trade. You will be surprised how many signals Genesis generates that conform w news releases. However, I agree w you to a certain extent, the news is unknown to us, and it has a 50% chance of going against you, the same as any other trade, but far more viscious. So, I would still take a news trade if the conditions were right, for me, but I dont make it a priority. Its a personal thing. One piece of advice I would give........be extra careful when High Impact News is in multiple lots, eg there are 2 or 3 red flag releases all at 1 time for 1 currency. Here there is a big risk that price will whipsaw wildly and you will get knocked out, even if you have traded in the right direction. Cheers J.

So i want to explain my take on the stochastic oscillator. The correct explanation can be found here: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_oscillator Its been said here on the thread 100 times before, it is more than a simple OB/OS indicator. I see it kind of like a "magnetic force", either bullish or bearish. So when entering a trade, i like to see them getting all "pulled" together by whatever force. I use a M5,15 &amp; 30 Stoch on the same window, when the M15 &amp; 30 are heading in a certain direction, and the M5 has a good pullback, then turns around to agree with the M15 &amp; 30 stoch, i will enter once the Matrix confirms. Attached is a picture to make my point clearer, i have marked a few yellow lines where i see stochs aligned. ExcessFX

I only takes Trade in the Direction of Trend, i.e Continuation Trades. And, we can consider them all HPT's if the Setup is Perfect. Note:- No CT Trades. No Reversals. No Picking of High/Low, Top/Bottom etc. My Setup:- At First, I always looks for Strong M30 and H1 Stochs (i.e both crossed up/down sharply and above/below 50). Note:- Just use Marty's Theory, for considering the M5 Stoch..i.e M30 Stoch should be crossed heavily up/down &amp; above/below 50..And, M5 Stoch hooking back against M30 Stoch and then recrossing back in the Same Direction. M30 &amp; H1 Stoch quite Strong. 2.) M15 Stoch also Strong. 3.) M5-H1 Matrix all Red. 4.) AscTrend upto H1 all Bearish. So, the pair was strong Bearish, no doubt. Reason to take such a low Stoch was....all Stoch''s were Strong and in Alignment and more importantly H4 Stoch was quite Strong and you will see each HTF Stochs were backing LTF Stoch's. So, in such a Strong Setup, it will hardly give M5 Stoch a chance to retrace back and recross back in the same direction. But, for the one's that considers CT Trades, then for them it was a very profitable trade to miss.. For Exit:- Here, I exited my trade on S2..Because it was behind my mind..LO can either boost your move or it can reverse it all..So was happy to close it out at S2 because was getting 50+ pips..But, if i would have used system for exit (Mostly, that I do) then I would have exited at the green circle shown in M1 chart. My Criteria For Exit:- M5 TVI giving opposite signal and M5 ,M15 stoch crossing and moving in the same direction of M5 TVI. (Again, this was invented by Marty, u will see it if u search Marty's posts of this year,..it's working for me..and my exits has improved dramatically by following this). But, Note :- This works only if you are in a Strong Trend move..I would not recommend this exit criteria for a CT Trade.. mazprofx.

EA trade from earlier, perhaps a slightly lucky one ... Entry reasons : Signal and arrow already in play Good HTF stochs (m15 / m30) Evidence of a lower high (weak evidence, but, still evidence) More of a "re-entry" type trade, as best place to enter would have been earlier Trade : Was aware of the French news at 7:45 London Time, but was not aware of the 8:00 Spanish news (wasn't and still isn't on FF calendar). Strong reaction downwards on news. Good for me this time, but could've also gone bad. As it was a sudden move, took half of trade off once it's initial push down was starting to slow. But, moral of the story - Don't rely too much on the FF Calendar, there's better calendars out there!

--- 帖子 #22253 ---
Thanks for the post, Mazpro, What it shows is that, Genesis entries, whether M1 or M5, shows where momentum is just right. Hence, an entry taken with Genesis being "all systems go," goes into profit almost immediately. The problem is, without the bigger picture in mind, one could be entering counter trend trades. It is ok to do CT, as long as one recognises that it is counter trend and money manages that accordingly. Marty's version incorporates the higher time frame trend and higher time frame momentum very well. So we have a system, where we can identify a set up that is in the direction of the higher time frame and the lower time frame momentum is in the right direction. Hence the chances of the trade going right increases tremendously. I think, those of us who are still posting here, if we keep this in mind and keep on discussing trades, all of us will be benefited. We will be able to discuss the trades that went well as well as the ones that did not and come up with a way of selecting out the good ones. Padila

--- 帖子 #22254 ---
Once we get a Genesis set up, two questions need to be asked: Is the higher time frame momentum in our direction? Is the higher time frame trend in our favour? If the answers are yes, probability of winning goes up. Incorporating Marty's method, like Mazprofx has done, achieves just that.

--- 帖子 #20046 ---
Two things that would have kept me from this trade Padila. Firstly, I incorporate EMA25 and EMA75 on my M5 chart (EMA75 is basically the EMA25 off the M15 chart). At the point you entered PA was just below the EMA 75 but the EMA's had not crossed downwards(they were still quite wide). Secondly, the TVI on both M30 and H1 was still rising. I like to see the M30 red (falling) and ideally, the same with the H1 but I will occasionally ignore H1 TVI if the stochs look good, ie, HTF stochs leaving the 20/80 levels together. Hope this helps.
